author: simple-agent-manager[bot]
body:
Task: F-4 `01M6A7WK5PQSM0HN1FRCVGZHBN` (platform spaces mission, QA1-09, gates STAFF). Owner decision 2026-11-01, SAM policy 4bcc461e: institutional Discover shows only members with a saved community profile. This supersedes the 24 Oct demo decision ("all members, no opt-in").

## What changes

- **One predicate.** `discoverableMember(column, callerId)` in `web/src/lib/community/eligibility.ts` returns a parenthesised SQL condition: a `communityProfile` row exists, the person has no MENTOR or ADMIN role, and the person isn't the caller. INSTITUTION is deliberately not excluded. The column must be a qualified internal name (anything else throws). The caller's id is bound, never interpolated.
- **Every institutional surface uses it:**
  - REST `GET /api/community/profiles` and `POST /profiles/discover` (`searchProfiles`, `discoveryEvidence`);
  - chat `search_profiles` / `get_profile` / selected profile, and MCP `search_profiles` / `get_profile` / `list_journey` / `assess_profile`. Both go through the same service methods, which is what removes the drift;
  - platform search (B-1.4) for institution and admin callers: the people group, and other owners' projects. Other callers still see the public talent directory unchanged. The caller's own shared projects stay findable as their own (`/dashboard/community`).
- **By-id reads fail closed with no existence oracle.** `getProfile`, `listJourney`, and therefore assessment, chat and MCP reads, return the same `404 Profile not found.` for an ineligible person as for an id that never existed. Non-institutions still get 403 before any lookup. Your own profile is always readable.
- **Unchanged:** visibility of private contributions, recordings and transcripts; the MENTOR/ADMIN exclusions; the mixed-role rule; caller authorization (MCP still requires the INSTITUTION role, REST and chat accept institution or admin, as before).
- **Copy.** Member-facing sentences now say exactly "Approved institutions can discover your saved community profile and the contributions you share." This covers the members page (3 places), the Journey workspace "Who can discover this?", `/community` and CommunityIntro. Institution-facing equivalent: "Approved institutions can discover saved community profiles and the contributions members share." (partner page, intro step). This is QA1-18's copy; F-3 excludes QA1-18, and F-3 has no open PR touching these files.
- **Seeds and fixtures**, so demo and preview institutions still find eligible synthetic members:
  - preview: `agent-preview-auth.mjs` upserts a saved profile for the synthetic Amina Fixture;
  - staging personas: `otherMember` is provisioned with a saved profile (the member still saves theirs during verification), and user deletion cascades it away;
  - local QA: `e2e/platform-personas.local.sql` gives Achieng a saved profile, while Wanjiku and Lucy stay without one;
  - the retained staging demo dataset already saves profiles for its members.

**No migration.** A "saved profile" is an existing `communityProfile` row, written only by the member's own save (`updateOwnProfile`). The `communityProfile.userId` primary key and the `UserRoles` user index serve the new EXISTS checks. This applies in production regardless of the spaces flag (owner-approved): it changes existing pre-spaces endpoints, not flagged ones.

## Acceptance criteria and evidence

`web/src/lib/community/eligibility.test.ts` is one parameterized test with real migrations on node:sqlite. Six fictional people: Joseph (institution, saved), Achieng (saved), Lucy (no profile), David (mentor), Amina (admin), Kevin (institution, saved). Every one of them would match "Webhook" on every surface if eligibility allowed it.

| Case | Evidence |
|---|---|
| No-profile user excluded | Lists: REST search, REST Discover, chat search tool, MCP `search_profiles`, platform search (people + projects). Joseph sees exactly Achieng and Kevin. |
| Institution self excluded | Same matrix, for both Joseph and Kevin. |
| Mentor/admin excluded | Same matrix. |
| Eligible member included | Same matrix. Reads of Achieng and Kevin are `allowed` on every read surface. |
| By-id read of an ineligible person denied | Read surfaces: REST profile, REST assessment, chat selected profile, chat `get_profile` tool, MCP `get_profile` / `list_journey` / `assess_profile`. Reads of Lucy, David and Amina are `toEqual` the read of a never-existing id. |
| Mixed-role member with the institution role and a saved profile stays searchable by other institutions | Kevin is listed for Joseph, and Joseph for Kevin. |
| The test guards the fix | Run against `main`'s `service.ts` and `search/service.ts`: 28 of 50 cases fail. |

Also covered:
- A saved empty profile counts as saved.
- You can read your own profile without saving one.
- Non-institutions get 403 before any lookup.
- The public talent directory is unchanged for other callers.
- `discoverableMember` rejects unqualified or injected column names.

Existing suites were updated to the new rule: `service.test.ts`, `staging-boundary.test.ts`, search `test-support` and the >500-row test, staging demo, persona cleanup and preview seed tests. The copy assertions now pin the exact sentences.

## Commands run (in `web/`)

- `npm ci --legacy-peer-deps`: ok.
- Baseline on `main` (`ee06215`): `npx vitest run` gave 268 files and 4166 tests passed.
- `npx vitest run`: 269 files, **4216 tests passed**.
- `npm run lint` (oxlint + eslint): clean.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx astro check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 60 hints (same as main).
- No dependency changes, so no `audit:ci` is needed.

Migrations added: none.

author: hashin9973-ux
body:
## Root cause

The worker discovers immutable request files through the Git Trees / recent-commit paths, but `loadMailboxRequest()` then rereads the request by branch-scoped Contents path. `readRemoteFile()` converts HTTP 404 to `null`, and `processRequestInner()` previously returned silently on that null value. This leaves a request visible in `bridge/requests` but without a claim, result, or useful widget entry.

## Fix

- Retain the immutable blob SHA supplied by both request-tree reconciliation and recent commit details.
- Read the discovered request through GitHub's Git Blobs API first; fall back to the Contents path when the blob read is unavailable.
- Do not silently return when a request discovered in the tree cannot be read. Surface a `REQUEST_FILE_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic so it remains visible and can be retried on reconciliation.
- Preserve the existing malformed-request rejection behavior.
- Release the per-request SHA cache after dispatch settles.

## Regression tests

- Reproduces a request that is present in the request tree while the Contents endpoint returns 404; verifies that the immutable blob is read, the command executes once, and the agent widget contains matching request, claim and result details.
- Verifies a request that cannot be read through either route is surfaced as a failed diagnostic instead of disappearing silently.

No workspace source files, safety settings, or network configuration are changed by this PR.

author: minev-dev
body: ## Why? Redelivering a persisted approval after restart could start implementation without explicit resume. Concurrent database writes could also invalidate workflow eligibility snapshots, causing launch or cancellation to fail. ## What? - Return a receipt for matching persisted plan acceptance without starting a workflow driver, including recorded approval redelivery. - Use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for workflow launch and cancellation so writer ownership precedes eligibility reads. ## Project impact Implementation left unclaimed after restart requires explicit resume; replaying an old approval no longer starts it. Workflow launch and cancellation acquire the writer lock before reading eligibility, preventing concurrent commits from invalidating those snapshots. Co-Authored-By: [Agentty](https://github.com/agentty-xyz/agentty) > [!NOTE] > ### Fix task-chain relaunch and locking on approval redelivery > - Fixes a workflow relaunch bug: repeated acceptance of the same plan attempt now returns `false` from `App.accept_api_task_chain_plan` without calling `ensure_task_chain_driver`. Redelivered approval replies leave the driver, transcript, and execution state unchanged; explicit resume still dispatches the Implementer. > - Adds WAL-mode concurrency tests in [task_chain_concurrency_test.rs](https://github.com/agentty-xyz/agentty/pull/969/files#diff-dca396d0bb7f59af8cd0c620e1410fdbdd6978dafe7cb7597a9dc92ea1681f97) showing that workflow admission and cancellation acquire the writer reservation before their eligibility reads, blocking a concurrent writer until the workflow operation finishes. > - Adds a test in [task_chain_reply_test.rs](https://github.com/agentty-xyz/agentty/pull/969/files#diff-e5b6275848e74729dbbe4d2f79f5ce7b88b48866117a4e0fa12ee2d168176c27) covering approval redelivery plus explicit resume completing the workflow. > - Risk: `save_task_chain` and `cancel_one_execution` in [task_chain.rs](https://github.com/agentty-xyz/agentty/pull/969/files#diff-8883dfaf082049c022c9006b25047186d3b2a4090df0c1e315288f0a88acd921) now open with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so a concurrent non-workflow write during these reads fails with SQLite error 5 until the transaction commits. > > > > Macroscope summarized 26bf044. > >

author: mynameistrez
body: The rule defined a full run as one with the universal job, which a push to main has, but a push runs 17 jobs and skips the installed, smoke, coexistence and Windows jobs. A green push was therefore treated as the check when it is not the full pipeline. The check now looks only at the newest dispatch of build.yml on main, which is the shape that runs every job, and says explicitly that a green push does not satisfy it.

author: leofinanceai
body:
## Problem

After the merge of #4, the `e2e-test` job on `main` failed: all 6 questionnaire specs failed on desktop and mobile, while the other 15 passed. CI serves `dist` with `serve -s`, whose single-page fallback answers `/cuestionario/` with the app shell, so the form never rendered. Cloudflare Pages serves existing files first, which is why the page works in production.

## Solution

- **`makefile`:** drop `-s` from `start-app-e2e-ci`. The app routes by hash, and every spec visits `/` or a hash route, so nothing needs the fallback.
- **`public/cuestionario/index.html`:** use absolute asset paths (`/cuestionario/...`), so the page also works at `/cuestionario` without the trailing slash. A server can serve it there, and the relative paths then resolved to the site root.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** point to the questionnaire on the Amai Mochi site; the claude.ai version was deleted.

## How To Test

Reproduced in the dev container against the CI server command. Each scenario checked the progress count, the WhatsApp message, the optional section and the draft after a reload:
- `npx serve -l 5175 -L -s dist` (before): `/cuestionario/` returns the app (`<title>Amai Mochi</title>`) and the form is not rendered, the same failure as on CI.
- `npx serve -l 5175 -L dist` (after): all spec scenarios pass at both `/cuestionario/` and `/cuestionario`, with fonts loaded and no failed requests.

The Playwright suite itself is blocked in the dev container by the harness, so the `e2e-test` job on this PR is the confirmation.

## Additional Checks

- [x] The **documentation** is up to date
- [ ] Tested with **fakerest** provider (not applicable)
- [x] Tested with **Mobile** resolution

## Summary

Unblocks #106 (spec 062, configuration step of the `.statecraft/derived/` move). Revision 22's `secret-scan` job failed there: gitleaks' `generic-api-key` rule matched three registry shards (020, 025, 045), each a section anchor mapped to its SHA-256 digest. Preserve checkpoints while columns stay unchanged and height remains within the current backing pages. Keep recovery for width changes and height growth that exposes older pages to live edits, including resize round trips. The daemon compatibility grid probe now collects the external command's result before printing its complete marker. A shell job-control diagnostic previously split the marker and size; a regression covers that failure without weakening the grid assertion.

author: christopherowen
body:
## Summary
Builds directly on top of **PR #821** (`exp/dsv41-mhc-multitoken-finalize-aux-post-collapse-norm`) to ensure extending `mhc` single-launch fusion (`project_and_finalize_streams`) to multi-token decode (`M <= 16`, covering DSpark speculative verify/draft batches `M = 6, 8, 12, 16`) has **zero negative consequences** on SM occupancy, PDL overlap, or `M = 1` latency:

1. **Split Lock-Free `mhc_claim` + `mhc_wait_splits` (`nanosleep.u32 32` Backoff)**:
   - Splits `mhc_claim_and_wait` into `mhc_claim` (1 `atomicAdd` per split CTA) and `mhc_wait_splits` (executed only by the `live_m` finalizer CTAs).
   - Because all 40 split CTAs (`splits = 10` $\times$ `4` streams, `246` regs/thread) fit in a single wave across GB10's 48 SMs, every split CTA reaches `mhc_claim` without waiting on any other CTA, and the `40 - live_m` non-finalizer CTAs exit immediately to free their SMs.
2. **Zero-Spin `M = 1` Fastpath**:
   - When `live_m == 1` (`M = 1`), the single finalizer CTA (`arrived == splits - 1`) resets `counter` to `0` immediately on the first atomic without executing `ld.global.acquire`, a second `__threadfence()`, or a second `atomicAdd`.
3. **Late `pdl.trigger()` After Stage 1 (`mhc_claim`)**:
   - Replaces early `pdl.chain()` at kernel entry with `pdl.wait()` at entry and `pdl.trigger()` after Stage 1 completes and `mhc_claim` finishes.
   - Downstream kernels (`attention_front`, `gemm_mxfp8`, `moe_topk_gate_forward`) begin their CTA launch right as the `40 - live_m` non-finalizer CTAs exit, overlapping Stage 2 (`mhc_finalize_row`) without competing for SMs during Stage 1's 40-CTA TF32 GEMM.
4. **Pre-Barrier `weight` / `scale` / `base` Preload Overlapped with `mhc_wait_splits`**:
   - While Thread 0 in the `live_m` finalizer CTAs waits in `mhc_wait_splits`, Warp 0 (`tx < 24`) preloads `scale` and `base` and Warps 1–3 (`tx >= 32`) preload all `5,120` BF16 elements (`10.24 KB`) of `weight` into shared memory before the Stage 2 `T.sync_threads()`.

## Verification & Benchmarks on `dgx4` (`GB10` / `SM121`, `spark-ds41f:19f2c20ed4d6-next-21`)
- `pytest tests/kernels/test_deepseek_v41_tilelang_mhc.py`: **163 passed, 0 PDL source violations**

- `ptxas` compilation stats (`sm_121a`): `0 bytes spill stores, 0 bytes spill loads, 246 registers`
- Full-layer CUDA Graph replay (`LayerChain`, 2 `mhc` calls/layer):

| Decode Rows (`M`) | 2-Launch (`project_streams` + `finalize`) | 1-Launch (Late Trigger + Pre-Wait Preload) | Per-Layer Delta | 61-Layer Step Delta |

author: tmac1973
body:
## The problem

A split model is one download, started from its first shard, and the downloader only gets the total size of all shards. Since #501 it checks a finished file's size, but only for single-file downloads, because the total says nothing about any one shard. So a shard of the wrong size (cut short, or from another revision) was still kept. The fork handler had its own workaround for this (#503 trimmed it to shard groups).

## What changes

**`Downloader.ExpectSize(finalPath, size)`** (`internal/huggingface/downloader.go`). It works like `ExpectSHA256`: a map from a file's final path to its size, set before the download starts. When `downloadFile` reaches that file, the size replaces the caller's size, so the checks from #501 and #504 apply to that one shard:

- a finished shard of another size is downloaded again into `.part` and replaces the old one only when complete;
- a download that ends at another size is discarded;
- a complete `.part` of that size is put in place without a request.

An entry is removed when its file is done: skipped as already in place, or checked by `finishPart` (put in place or rejected). An entry whose download fails partway stays, so a retry still has the size. Without `ExpectSize`, shards behave as before.

**Callers that know each shard's size now set it:**

- **Fork model sets** (`internal/api/fork_models.go`): each file in a group gets its `ModelFile.Bytes`. The workaround that deleted wrong-sized shards before the download is removed. One small difference: a wrong-sized shard is no longer deleted up front; it stays until its replacement is complete, as for every other download since #501.
- **Models tab Update** (`internal/api/model_update.go`): each changed file gets its size from the repository, next to its SHA-256.

## Left unchanged

- **Browse, Autoconfigure and other downloads started from `POST /api/hf/download`.** The request only carries the file name and the combined size. The file list does have each shard's size (`File.ShardSizes`), so the page could send them, but that is a change to the request and the templates; I left it for a separate PR if it is wanted.
- **HEAD sizes.** I did not use the per-shard HEAD requests in `fetchCombinedSize` as a source of sizes. A wrong length from a HEAD would make every download of that shard fail, so sizes come only from file lists.

## Tests

- `TestExpectSizeChecksEachShard`: with sizes set, a shard of the wrong size is downloaded again, a good shard is not requested, the callback gets the total, and no sizes are left in the map afterwards.
- `TestForkModelResumeKeepsGoodFiles` (from #503) puts a wrong-sized shard on disk. It failed when the fork workaround was switched off; it now passes with the workaround removed, through `ExpectSize`.
- `make build`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `make js-test` pass locally.

author: topoconsultoria
body:
## Fase 6 — Operação e entrega

Closes #9

> **Dependência / ordem de merge:** este PR tem como base `claude/ajustes-issue-20` (PR [#25](https://github.com/faonovais/freenfse/pull/25)) e **depende dele** (que depende de [#23](https://github.com/faonovais/freenfse/pull/23) → [#19](https://github.com/faonovais/freenfse/pull/19) → [#17](https://github.com/faonovais/freenfse/pull/17)). Ordem na `main`: #17 → #19 → #23 → #25 → este. Depois que o #25 for integrado, reaponte a base deste PR. A troca de base e o merge ficam com o usuário.

### O que entra

1. **Instalador CLI** (`instalador/`, só biblioteca padrão do Python) — Docker Compose **ou** nativo (systemd + Nginx + Gunicorn + worker + beat). Pergunta ou recebe domínio, e-mail do certificado, porta e pasta de dados; gera o `.env` (permissão **600**) com `SECRET_KEY`, `FREENFSE_CHAVES` e senhas aleatórias, **sem imprimir segredo** nem passá-lo na linha de comando; é **idempotente** (nunca troca um segredo existente nem apaga dado); HTTPS por Let's Encrypt (certbot) ou certificado próprio, ligando `COOKIES_SEGUROS`/`PROXY_TLS`/HSTS; páginas de erro do Nginx em linguagem simples (JSON na API); verificação final de saúde e da cifragem; modo `--simular`. Compose com rotação de logs, `/tmp` em tmpfs, volume de backups e sonda do beat.
2. **Backup e restauração** — `pg_dump -Fc` de todos os *schemas* sob instantâneo consistente, cifrado em fluxo com **`age` para uma chave pública** (a privada fica **fora do servidor**, separada da `FREENFSE_CHAVES`). Retenção configurável (nunca apaga o mais recente, só roda após sucesso), tarefa diária 02:30. **Restauração só em banco novo e com conferência:** SHA-256 do arquivo, linhas por tabela contra o manifesto e abertura de uma amostra dos campos cifrados; banco marcado como verificado/NÃO VERIFICADO.
3. **Criptografia em repouso** ([ADR 0008](docs/adr/0008-criptografia-em-repouso-backup-e-retencao.md)) — XML da DPS/NFS-e, eventos e evidências cifrados na aplicação (AES-256-GCM da Fase 1, 7 colunas), hash sobre o XML em claro (e o download o **confere**: valor cifrado trocado por outro válido não é entregue), migração dos dados existentes (idempotente, reversível, falha sem chaves), `verificar_cifragem` que lê a coluna **bruta**.
4. **LGPD e retenção** — registros de envio de e-mail: **5 anos + expurgo automático**; XML ≥ 5 anos **sem expurgo automático** (provado com o relógio 10 anos à frente); [política de privacidade](docs/privacidade.md) (dados, finalidade, base legal, prazo, direitos).
5. **Observabilidade** — logs JSON de uma linha com **máscara de segredos, CPF e e-mail** (formatador + filtro); `GET /api/saude/` (banco, Redis, worker, agendador, backup); **healthcheck do beat** (pendência da #10); alertas por e-mail: emissão sem resposta da Sefin > 2 h, falhas permanentes de e-mail/Drive, backup que falhou/atrasou.
6. **Views para BI** — schema `bi` (`empresas`, `notas`, `servicos`, `retencoes`, `eventos`) consolidando as empresas, **usuário de banco somente leitura** (senha como verificador SCRAM), sem XML nem credenciais; [grão e chaves](docs/bi.md).
7. **Documentação** — [manual de instalação](docs/instalacao.md) (inclui **SMTP com senha de app numa caixa dedicada** e o **alerta sobre a delegação do Gmail**, issue #18), [chaves e backup](docs/chaves-e-backup.md) (guarda fora do servidor, restauração, rotação), [manual do usuário](docs/manual-do-usuario.md), [checklist de produção](docs/checklist-producao.md), [ADR 0009](docs/adr/0009-operacao-instalador-observabilidade-e-bi.md).

### Decisões em aberto para o usuário

* **CPF e nome de pessoa física no BI:** por padrão o CPF sai **mascarado** e o nome **não sai** (minimização). Mudar é uma linha na view, mas amplia a exposição de dado pessoal — decisão sua.
* **Trilha de auditoria:** proposta de **5 anos, sem expurgo automático** (trilha imutável); registros de e-mail seguem a decisão da #18.
* **Dados cadastrais em claro** (nome/documento do tomador, `Pessoa`, *snapshots*): continuam legíveis no banco porque o sistema precisa buscar/ordenar/exibir; mitigados por backups cifrados, controle de acesso e **criptografia de disco recomendada** (ADR 0008). Cifrar só o *snapshot* sem cifrar o cadastro daria falsa segurança.
* **Alerta de backup** sai por um **SMTP do sistema** (`ALERTAS_SMTP_*`), não pelo e-mail da empresa (Fase 4), porque não pertence a nenhuma empresa.

### Segurança

* Nada confidencial versionado: valores falsos nos testes (montados em pedaços para o gitleaks não confundir com segredo), `.env.example` só com campos vazios. gitleaks (histórico completo e árvore): **nenhum vazamento**; o job de gitleaks do CI também.
* Zero menções ao repositório privado no diff. Segredos fora da saída e da linha de comando do instalador (testado, com mutação).
* A restauração **exige as duas chaves** (a privada do backup e a `FREENFSE_CHAVES`) — perder uma delas é grave; o procedimento de guarda é bloqueante no checklist.

### Roteiro para o usuário (VPS de teste)

**Não foi feita verificação real em VPS.** O roteiro de instalação limpa, idempotência, erros em linguagem simples, dados cifrados em repouso, backup/restauração (incluindo as falhas esperadas), alertas, BI, renovação do certificado e reinício está em [`docs/verificacao-fase-6.md`](docs/verificacao-fase-6.md) (parte 1). Use VPS descartável, produção restrita e dados fictícios.

### Testes

* **Backend:** **1395** testes passando na suíte completa (agendamentos 196, cadastros 98, core 249, documentos 222, fiscal 527, **operacao 103**); `ruff`, `ruff format --check` e `makemigrations --check` limpos. `operacao` entrou nos `testpaths` (sem isso o CI não rodaria os testes do app novo).
* **Instalador:** 66 testes (`cd instalador && python -m pytest`), com o `nginx -t` real; rodam no CI como usuário comum e como root localmente.
* **Por critério:** restauração de backup (`operacao/tests/test_backup.py`, 25) · coluna de XML cifrada lida em bruto (`fiscal/tests/test_xml_cifrado.py` 11 + migração 4 + lote/Drive/e-mail 3) · expurgo de 5 anos com relógio controlado (`documentos/tests/test_retencao.py`, 6) · logs sem segredo (22) · saúde/beat (27) · alertas (21) · BI (18). Detalhe em `docs/verificacao-fase-6.md`.
* **Mutações:** 76 — **75 detectadas** e 1 equivalente (sem efeito observável). Pontos obrigatórios cobertos: backup sem cifrar (B1), restauração sem conferência (B3–B5), XML em claro (X1–X4), expurgo apagando documento fiscal (R1–R2), log com segredo (L1–L7). Duas **sobreviveram na primeira rodada** (B11: retenção rodando antes do dump; N16: `--dados` informado de novo ignorado) e viraram testes. A primeira rodada do instalador foi **invalidada** por um *bytecode* velho no meu runner (todas "falhavam" no mesmo teste) e **refeita**; tabela completa no documento.
* **CI** (SHA `ad35f54`, run [41265304725](https://github.com/faonovais/freenfse/actions/runs/41265304725)): **os 4 jobs verdes** — Backend (ruff, pytest 1395 e testes do instalador 66), Frontend, gitleaks e Docker Compose (aplicação vazia sobe). O job do Compose constrói a imagem (`pg_dump` 18 + `age`), sobe a pilha com `--wait` (sonda do beat) e confere `/api/saude/` pelo Nginx, `verificar_cifragem` e a página de erro com o backend parado.
  * A rodada anterior (`02e052f`) ficou vermelha em **um** teste do instalador: o `nginx -t` fazia `bind()` na porta 80 e o runner do CI não é root. Corrigido em `ad35f54` trocando as portas 80/443 por portas altas **apenas na cópia usada pelo teste** (templates de produção intactos); reproduzido como usuário `nobody` antes de corrigir.

### Limitações

* Neste ambiente não há daemon Docker nem systemd. O build da imagem e a subida do Compose foram provados **no CI** (job verde); a **instalação nativa (systemd)** e a **VPS real** só são exercitadas pelo roteiro.
* Sem teste de escrita concorrente durante o backup (o instantâneo consistente é usado, não provado sob carga).
* A máscara de logs é heurística (regex); o alerta de falhas permanentes não chega

body:
# WO-020 records

This branch files the instance records of WO-020, the first concept-study batch: twenty movement studies in DotLn-Angular's AI for Games, with the study record, its check, the `motion` and `timeline` families, the addressable readings and the summary-driven Tools home that WO-021 to WO-024 reuse. The change was reviewed and published to `DylanBWood/DotLn-Angular` as the pull request `feat: add concept studies for the movement tools and the study record` (#11) on `feat/movement-concept-studies`, opened as a draft at the verification pass and marked ready by the final publish with the reviewed commit and the records commit. No code of this instance changes. The branch carries the control segment, the order's evidence, the profile and workstream write-backs, the host observations of the publish calls and the final review's publication bodies.

## What a reviewer gets

- The order's [evidence](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/README.md): the [fan-out](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/fan-out.md) with the three briefs and every worker's statement and tokens; the [critics' findings](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/review.md) and their dispositions; the [self-review](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/self-review.md) of three independent reviewers (17 found, 16 fixed, 1 recorded); the [twenty-one comparison rounds](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/design/comparisons.md) and the [rejected implementations](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/design/rejected-implementations.md); the executor [walkthrough](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/walkthrough.md) and 96 screenshots; the [host qualification](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/host-qualification.md) of the Claude Code execution, the Codex workers, the verification's draft publish and this review's publish calls; and the [preview record](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/evidence/WO-020/preview-pr.json) of the draft pull request, its checks and this review's reading of it.
- Decisions D001 to D020: the base and the publishing rule, the Codex route the operator directed, the fan-out's stop figure and its lift, the record kept as specified, the engine's added exports, the comparison rounds and the word that ended them, the critics' findings, the bundle attribution, the three reviewers' findings with one deferral, the verification, and this review's acceptance with three boarded repairs. The decisions, VER-001 (pass) and FINAL-001 (pass) are filed under `docs/dotln/` in the target branch by the records commit. The publication bodies [PR.md](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/final-reviews/WO-020/PR.md), [RELEASE-NOTES.md](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/final-reviews/WO-020/RELEASE-NOTES.md) and this file stay beside the report path here.
- The [repository profile](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/repositories/dotln-angular.md), whose implementation map now names the study record, the families, the check and the addressable reading, and the [workstream](https://github.com/dylanwoodconsulting/DotLn-Enterprise-Starter/blob/6a4e95651f9523aafd766daa731e29c072e35ce1/docs/workstreams/WS-001-dotln-angular.md) delivery states.
- The control segment `docs/control/orders/WO-020.jsonl`, the current-state projection, the work-order index, the decisions index and the follow-up register, with two new rows: the family-discriminated model before `marbles` (D018) and the three small repairs the final review boarded (D020).

## Validation

- The target's declared review gate (install, lint, e2e type check, unit tests, format, build, e2e and visual) passed at tree `4e6b3e4b93d6c5226e31f2e819006d0723911dbf` with no tracked-byte mutation, after the Preflight line. CI's `checks`, `visual` and `title` passed on that tree from a clean checkout on the draft. The reviewed commit `77dc9e545e5310ea6e20af6da0b445f754960e9e` has that tree, so the gate was not rerun.
- VER-001 performed the Objective's session independently in the production build at three widths, ran all twenty models over 168 input cases, the Tools, Catalog and Core suites uncached, the tooling tests with sixteen more malformed variations, the browser failure paths and axe; this review reran the literal criterion commands and greps, compared the migrated Arrive assertions with the deleted spec, and read the whole diff.
- All nine criteria are met; no waiver, correction or override was recorded. Criterion 1, the verifier's, is met on VER-001's walkthrough; the executor's ledger entry for it predates that session.
- Gates in this worktree: `npm run test:docs` passed after the review's last record edit, before the result, and again after the records moved and the publish observations were written. No launchpad complete run is owed, because no launchpad code changed and the criteria name the target gate and the document gate.

## Limits and follow-ups

- Registered and left with their owners: the family-discriminated study model before the `marbles` family (D018, for WO-021); the study check's raw error on a named file that does not parse, the unused computed in the explanation component and the root README's menu row (D020, for the first batch that edits those files); the scene's "read the study" link, which reopens when this order merges.
- The verifying session opened the draft without filing its publish call; the host-qualification record and the preview record now carry what the forge and the object store show, and the invocation itself stays unknown.
- After both merges, the operator fast-forwards `main` and dispatches `resume: release close` there. That closes the target worktree with the no-release outcome for the launchpad and cuts the target's minor release with the reviewed notes. This branch starts at `main`'s current head, so the pull request carries only WO-020's own records.

Based on `feat/ui-shell` (#14); the orchestrator rebases onto `main` once #14 merges.

## What it does

- **Platform** ([android D60](https://github.com/Astroreen/AstroTime/blob/feat/accounts-sync/docs/plans/android.md#D60)): the UI's root takes one `Platform` — `store`, `http`, `secrets`, `openExternal`, `preferences`. `SecretStore` is an interface in `@astrotime/core`; the web's adapters are in `apps/web/src/platform.ts`: HTTP through `/dav-proxy/` on the app's own origin (D39, the same URL space in the dev server and the image), credentials in IndexedDB (`secrets.ts`), Login Flow's page in a new tab.
- **`syncAll(context, { fresh })`** in `@astrotime/sync` (D90): every account in turn, a report per account (`synced`, `signed-out`, `refused`, `offline`, `failed`), never throws for an account; a call during a sync joins it, `fresh` gets one more sync after it, shared. `saveAccount`/`removeAccount` are the one place that spells the credentials' key and JSON; credentials never touch the store. Migration 5 keeps each account's calendar home (`homeUrl`), so a sync does not discover first.
- **Adding an account** (D19, D92), EN/RU: Nextcloud by Login Flow v2 (opens Nextcloud's page, shows that it waits, can open the page again, Cancel, gives up after 20 minutes, polls every 2 s and at once when the tab is visible again, as android D65), or any CalDAV server by address, user name and password (`/.well-known/caldav`). Errors told apart: wrong password, unreachable, no CalDAV server, no Nextcloud, **not allowed by this AstroTime's administrator** (the proxy now marks its own refusals with `x-astrotime-refused`, which `fetchClient` turns into `ProxyRefusedError`), and a **redirect to another server**, named so the user signs in there (D39). An empty app shows a first-run screen with both ways in.
- **The shell** (design D46): the account button at the end of the top bar opens the accounts dialog (each account's status and menu, "Sync now", "Add account"), as Google's account button opens its account sheet. The drawer lists each account with its status and a menu (sync now, sign in again, remove) above its calendars (colour, visibility checkbox from #14), and "Add account". Removing asks first; syncs that start later skip the account, the running and queued ones end first; then the secret goes, then the account's local data.
- **When the UI syncs** (D91): on start; back in front of the user (tab visible, window focused) when the last sync started over a minute ago; **every 5 minutes while visible** and online; on `online`; 2 s after a burst of local changes (`SyncScheduler.changed()`, wired for PR 5b/6); "Sync now". Status without getting in the way: a ring on the account button while syncing, a dot when something needs the user; per account "Syncing…", "Synced at 10:40", offline, signed out (with "Sign in again"), refused, failed, the report's `problem` codes and dropped changes in words (D37, D38), and the count of conflicts (D6).

## Decisions

Implements foundation D19 (the web's credentials, updated in place), D20/D39 (the proxy's refusals reach the user), D37/D38 (problems worded), design D46 (accounts in the drawer, the account button), android D60 (the shape that landed is noted in D60, as it asks). New, in [foundation.md § Accounts and syncing](https://github.com/Astroreen/AstroTime/blob/feat/accounts-sync/docs/plans/foundation.md#accounts-and-syncing):

- **D89 — credentials on the web: IndexedDB, sealed.** AES-GCM under a 256-bit key made with `extractable: false`, kept in the same database. Recorded honestly: it keeps the password out of plain sight (storage inspector, a search through the profile, a copy of the site's data); it does **not** stop script in the page (it can use the key) nor a determined reader of the disk (the key's bytes are in the same profile). A passphrase at every start was rejected (background syncs could not answer it either). A secret that no longer decrypts reads as none → "sign in again".
- **D90 — one sync entry; the accounts' credentials in one place.** `@astrotime/sync` now depends on `@astrotime/caldav` (it opens the providers). Signing in to an account already here (same calendar home and user) replaces its password instead of adding a duplicate. The demo's account has `provider: "demo"` and is never synced. Reminders join `syncAll` with PR 6.
- **D91 — when the UI syncs** (above). 5 minutes because a visible app is one the user is looking at, and a sync that finds nothing new is one PROPFIND plus one `sync-collection` per calendar. Android (D67) and the desktop (D75) add their own triggers through `syncAll`.
- **D92 — signing in on the web, and the accounts in the shell** (above). "Sync now" syncs every account (it is `syncAll`). Login Flow's poll waits through a moment offline, a 429 or a passing 5xx; five server errors in a row end it with an error naming the status.

## Deferred

- Closed: **Scheduling syncs** (the web's part is D91; the Android and desktop links live in D91).
- Added to foundation: **The Conflicts list** (the count shows in the accounts dialog; the list with "apply mine again" comes with editing, PR 6); **naming a redirecting server on Android and the desktop** (they drop `Authorization` across origins, so discovery ends in a refused password there; with PR A2/D2).
- Added to android: **One redirect loop for the native shells** — a shared redirect loop in `@astrotime/caldav` over a one-hop `HttpClient`, so Android's plugin and the desktop's `net.request` follow one implementation of the redirect rule of android D62 / desktop D72.
- Unchanged: **Login Flow v2 end to end** (the other PR's disposable Nextcloud); see the real-server check below.

## Review of the first push

The automated review read the placeholder description; the evidence is above and below now. Fixed in 47c0a3b, with tests: `removeAccount` racing a queued `fresh` sync (an account being removed is skipped by any later sync; the running and queued ones end first); re-sign-in matched by the calendar home alone (now home and user, so another user of a shared home is added, never handed the first one's account; only the password is replaced); the web secret store swallowing every error when it stores its key (now only the two-tab `ConstraintError`), reading a null transaction error, and an unhandled rejection in `inStore`. The PR-plan line is reflowed. Changed after a later review: a poll that keeps answering 5xx (five in a row) now ends the sign-in with the status, instead of waiting out the 20 minutes.

## Merging with 5a-2

Outside the view components. Shared files touched: `drawer.tsx` (only the accounts part, now `AccountSection`), `calendar-screen.tsx` (the account button, the first-run branch, `onLeave`), the catalogs (a block after `store.*`; `drawer.noCalendars` became `accounts.noCalendars`), `styles.css` (three `danger` tokens), the demo's `provider: "demo"`, `AstroTime`'s props (`platform` instead of `store` + `preferences`; the browser test's `render()` keeps its signature).

## Real-server check (manual)

Against a real **Nextcloud 34** (34.0.5), the dedicated test user, dev server on 5183 with the server on `ASTROTIME_PROXY_ALLOW`; a calendar with two events and a task was created through CalDAV first and deleted afterwards.

- **Password sign-in worked**: discovery and the first sync through the proxy; the seeded event appeared in the Week view 2.2 s after "Sign in", the account's three calendars in the drawer.
- **Login Flow v2** started through the proxy, the app showed its waiting step and opened Nextcloud's login page, but the server's own rate limit in front of Nextcloud (Cloudflare error 1015) stopped the automated approval on its login pages, twice; I stopped there rather than extend the ban. T

author: ignusvm
body:
## Summary

Weed processing and Boundless Inspiration up to Rip, for release 0.15.0. Spec, plan and tasks are in `specs/001-weed-processing/`.

- **Pipeline:** mature crops give Rough Buds. Trimming gives Trimmed Buds and seeds, at a chance by strain family: Landrace 50%, Neutrals 25%, Warm 15%, Green 10%, Cool 5%. Curing gives Cured Buds. `weed_bud` stays the finished item (display name only changes), so every recipe and the Terpinator and Budtender keep working. The strain stays with the bud throughout.
- **Tier 1:** the Trim Tray and Curing Rack need no power and are fed by hand. The tray places on the floor or as a top slab.
- **Tiers 2-4:** Snip Station, Bud Barber, Trim Reaper; Dry Box, Cure Closet, The Humidor. Hoppers and pipes feed the top and sides and empty the bottom.
- **Boundless Inspiration:** the existing Hookah burns coal and a cured bud for a minute and makes 4,200 BI, upgrading to the Double Hose (8,400) and Big Bertha (16,800), the same block with the same session. A burn runs four machines of its tier for the minute, batteries match a Hookah, and a Wick carries two Hookahs; Stash Jar, Stash Box, Mother Stash; Hemp, Rolled and Glass Wicks; the Hit Box. Only wire burns out, into ash. A block on too high a tier overloads and stops, with a green, smoky screen, and never breaks.
- **Shared power rule:** free while a high player is within 21 blocks, otherwise BI, otherwise paused with progress kept. Bongs, the Hookah and edibles now count as being high, as joints and pipes already did.
- **Style:** every tech block shares a custom screen with an animated BI gauge, and has animated textures and synthesized sound effects (`tools/generate_tech_ui.py`, `tools/generate_sounds.py`).
- **Existing machines:** the Terpinator and Infuser move onto that rule, with recipes and outputs unchanged. The Terpinator is top tier so it can't overload. The Infuser has no running job, so catching a colour and infusing a seed each cost one payment, and a refusal keeps the pool.

**Behaviour changes to note:** Hookahs take coal only, and a Budtender loads one session per 10 minutes. A sober player with no BI can no longer run the Terpinator or Infuser. Colonies now need cured buds supplied by a player until the Bud Barn, because farmers bring in rough buds.

## Testing

- Unit tests pass, including a 1,000-trim seed rate check for every strain.
- Game tests pass except `malformedAndFutureSavesFailClosed`, which fails on `main` too. New coverage: drops, strain through both steps, lit Hookah to machine, upgraded Hookahs, pause and resume, free running while high, wire burnout, wire limits, block overload, Hit Box step-down, Stashes settling, hopper in and out with two strains, side rules on the item capability, batch curing.
- `tools/check_block_assets.py` confirms all 17 new blocks have complete models, textures, names and loot.
- **In game so far:** tier 1, a machine, Wicks and a Stash Box were placed and run on an earlier build. **Not yet seen or heard on a client:** the new screens, overload effect, animated textures, sounds and upgraded Hookah models. The 10-minute Budtender limit has unit tests only, and the checks in `specs/001-weed-processing/quickstart.md` are still to do.

body: Two small transcript CSS fixes Leo asked for on 2026-10-31. **1. The turn footer sits in the middle of its gap.** Leo: "when i hover this little whatever time ago copy sound ellipsis thing should be centered in between the two things you're saying in between / so padding after == padding before that kinda thing all around" Before: the footer's 24px line (time, Copy, Read aloud, More) was 7px under the reply's last text line and 16px over the next prompt's bubble. Now the line moves down inside its own row by `--cv-footer-drop` (4px, or 2px over the same agent's next reply, whose first line has the same half-leading). That amount comes off the row's bottom padding. Room above and below is now about 11px and 12px, and over the composer it is the same. **Every footer row keeps its height**, so model.ts's estimates still match and the running-turn line the footer replaces doesn't jump. **2. Tables are less faint.** Leo: "at least the left side of our table if we're gonna have it should be more distinctly there it's all almost a bit too faint" - Row rules go from 4.5% to 9% of the text colour. - Every table's first column, which names its rows, takes the label weight (500). Labeled tables already used it. - The header keeps its strong rule. **Test:** `webviews/test/agent-pane-transcript-spacing.test.ts` now measures the room above and below the first and last footer: from the reply's last line box to the footer line, and from the footer line to the next bubble or the composer. It requires the two to be within 1.5px. On base they are 7 and 16. **Risk:** CSS only, in `conversation.css`. No footer or table geometry outside the agent-pane transcript changes; Chief views keep their own `.cv-table`. Not covered here: - Tool rows crammed against prose: #29124, open. - The hover-revealed controls of an empty footer stay pinned at its row top, as on base. Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- ## Summary by cubic Centers the transcript turn footer between the reply's last line and the next row, and makes markdown tables read more distinctly. - The footer (time, Copy, Read aloud, More) moves down inside its own row so the room above and below is balanced (~11px/12px). The drop is 4px, 2px over the same agent's next reply, and 0px for the footer that ends the chat, which still rests the turn gap over the composer. author: aozaki-kuro
body:
## Problem

On phones the keyword browse sheet (the "All" popover below 48rem):

1. let the home listing behind it scroll — a native popover never locks page scroll, so a drag on the backdrop strip, or one that chains out of a list too short to scroll, moved the page;
2. had no visible way to close it — the only light-dismiss target is the 2.5rem backdrop strip above the sheet.

## Fix (CSS/markup only, `CommissionSearchIsland.astro`)

- `html:has(#search-browse-popover:popover-open)` gets `overflow: hidden; touch-action: none` (same lock as the hamburger menu), scoped to the sheet breakpoint. Keyed on the open state, so every close path (X, Esc, light dismiss, term click) releases it.
- A sticky, zero-height close row with a round X button (`popovertargetaction="hide"`, `md:hidden`) that floats over the list and stays reachable while it scrolls.
- `height: auto` on the sheet: the UA popover height is `fit-content`, so a short list hung from the top instead of reaching the bottom.

Desktop popover is unchanged.

## Verification

- Mobile preview (375×812, fixture data): sheet fills 40px→bottom; `html` overflow is `hidden` while open, `visible` after closing via X, real Esc, tap on the dimmed strip, and a term click.
- `pnpm run lint`, `astro check`, `pnpm run test` (537 passed).
- Not verified on a real iOS device (touch scrolling inside the sheet with the `touch-action` lock relies on the same behavior as the hamburger menu).

author: nextwebspark
body:
Closes #1142

## What

Three parts: research into how other products handle connecting your own OAuth app (client ID and secret), a redesigned Settings → Integrations mockup, and fixes for the security review's findings 1, 2 and 4–7.

**1. Mockup and research** (`claude-design/Settings.dc.html`, knob `integrationsState`; `docs/integrations/settings-page-ux.md`)
- Each provider is a closed card with a status pill.
- Setting up your own app follows the order of the provider's console, using the console's own field names.
- The secret is masked while typed, with a Show toggle.
- Save and verify asks the provider first.
- A saved app is shown as read-only rows. The secret appears masked, with Replace; it is never revealed.

**2. Changing app now retires the connections made through the old one** (findings 1 and 2)

The problems:
- A refresh token belongs to the OAuth client it was issued to, and nothing recorded which app a mailbox or Zoom account was connected through.
- After a switch of app, each refresh presented an old token with the new app's keys. If the provider answered `invalid_client`, the mailbox stayed ACTIVE and its sends were deferred every hour, forever.
- Recall.ai only received keys on a connect. A rotated secret broke every Recall calendar once the old secret was deleted. "Return to the shared app" left the firm's own secret at Recall.

The fix:
- **V168** adds `app_client_id` to `app_lm_mailbox_connection` and `app_lm_zoom_connection`. It is backfilled from the workspace's own app; null means "the app used until now".
- A change of app (including a return to the shared app) withdraws every live connection made through the old one, in the same transaction (`ReplacedAppConnections`):
  - the connection goes to ERROR, so it reads as "reconnect";
  - its access token is dropped from memory;
  - its Recall calendar is released;
  - the audit line records `connectionsWithdrawn`.
- The read carries `connectionsThroughApp`. The form warns before a save that changes app, and the return dialog states the count.
- New keys for the same app (a new secret or tenant) publish `ProviderAppKeysReplaced`. `RecallCalendars` then hands each calendar the new keys after commit.

**3. Own-app keys are checked against each provider's format, on client and server** (findings 4–7)
- A secret containing a space, tab, line break or control character is refused. It is not trimmed, following the codebase rule that whitespace inside a secret is part of the secret.
- Entra's Secret ID pasted where the value belongs is refused.
- Google client IDs must end in `.apps.googleusercontent.com`; Microsoft client IDs must be GUIDs.
- The Microsoft tenant must be a GUID or a domain; `common`, `organizations` and `consumers` are refused.
- The expiry date is asked for Microsoft only, and must fall between today and 24 months out. A date already on record stays valid, even once past.
- The secret field has autofill off: no generated-password suggestion, and no saving to password managers.
- Microsoft's fields use Entra's own names.
- `docs/validation-matrix.md` rows updated; the ☐ own-app row is closed.

Still open, and recorded in the doc: Save and verify (finding 3, needs a verify endpoint), the secret's last-4 hint, and the replayable admin-consent `state` (finding 8, informational only).

## Verification

- **API, full suite against a local Postgres 16** (Docker is unavailable in this session, so I ran the suite against a throwaway local instance and reverted the temporary test wiring):
  - Flyway applied V1–V168 cleanly.
  - 2,503 tests: 2,492 passed, 0 failed.
  - 11 errors, all migration tests that start their own Testcontainers database ("Could not find a valid Docker environment"). CI's Docker will run them.
  - The changed integration classes all pass: `WorkspaceIntegrationIntegrationTest` (12), `RecallCalendarIntegrationTest` (13), `ZoomIntegrationTest` (10), `MailboxConnectionIntegrationTest` (14).
  - New unit tests pass: `WorkspaceIntegrationServiceTest` (21) and `ReplacedAppConnectionsTest` (3).
- **Web**: `npx vitest run` passes (2,653 tests in 256 files, including the style ratchet and copy guard), and `npm run build` is clean. Settings tests rerun after merging `main`.
- `/verify`'s live app run was not possible: it needs Docker's Postgres.

author: sebastianfoerste
body:
Branch `improve/2026-10-31-ci-hygiene` at `213e753614c28b3bc449137fe147306d2db7a678` (one commit on top of `main` `fe98b47baa3d6aac9447ff5bcc62fe73f3fd6e5a`). Files: `.github/workflows/micar-lint.yml`, new `.github/dependabot.yml`. `whitepaper.json`, `README.md` and `LICENSE` are untouched.

## What

- Top-level `permissions: contents: read`. The job only reads the repository and writes to the log and the step summary; the linter Action's SARIF upload is off by default (it would need `security-events: write`, which the owner can add if they ever turn it on).
- `actions/checkout@v4` → `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1` with `persist-credentials: false`. No step pushes or calls the API, so the token has no reason to stay in `.git/config`.
- `timeout-minutes: 10` on the job (a run takes about half a minute).
- `sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter@v1`, its two inputs and the strict-mode comment are unchanged. A two-line comment above the `uses:` line says why that tag floats: it is the template owner's own Action and the tag moves with each linter release, so repositories created from this template receive linter updates without editing the file.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: weekly grouped `github-actions` version updates, at most two open pull requests, with a two-line comment that Dependabot only opens pull requests, that a repository created from this template inherits the file and can delete it, and that it also proposes the linter Action's next major (`v2`).

## Why

- Every current run on `main` prints `##[warning]Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4` (run 41118419312, 2026-10-30). checkout v7.0.1 runs on `node24`.
- `uvx zizmor --offline .github/workflows/` on `main`: `error[unpinned-uses]` ×2, `warning[excessive-permissions]`, `warning[artipacked]`: "7 findings (3 suppressed, 1 unsafe fixes): 0 informational, 0 low, 2 medium, 2 high". After this change: "3 findings (2 suppressed): 0 informational, 0 low, 0 medium, 1 high", the one remaining `unpinned-uses` being the linter's own `@v1` line, which stays floating by design (see below).
- This is the house style of the linter repository, the same owner's work: its `ci.yml` has `permissions: contents: read`, `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7` with `persist-credentials: false`, and a weekly grouped `github-actions` Dependabot config. The template should match its own source of truth.
- A pin is only safe while something keeps it current, hence Dependabot. Dependabot alerts are disabled for this repository (API: "Dependabot alerts are disabled for this repository"); version updates do not need them.

## Why the linter Action stays on `@v1`

The linter repository's `scripts/check_whitepaper_starter.py` (`make template-check`, part of `make check`) requires the workflow to contain the exact fragments `uses: sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter@v1`, `whitepaper: whitepaper.json` and `strict: 'false'`; the README documents that the tag moves with each release so that template users get new rules without editing their copy. Pinning it to a commit would break that contract and freeze every downstream copy at one release. zizmor therefore keeps one `unpinned-uses` finding for that line; this is accepted, not suppressed.

## Evidence

Tag resolved read-only on 2026-10-31: `gh api repos/actions/checkout/git/ref/tags/v7.0.1 --jq .object.sha` → `3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1` (lightweight tag; `v7` points at the same commit; released 2026-07-20). The `action.yml` at that commit declares the `persist-credentials` input and `runs.using: node24`. GitHub Advisory Database (ecosystem `actions`): no advisory for `actions/checkout` or for the linter Action.

## How verified

```
$ uvx zizmor --offline .github/workflows/        # main, before
warning[artipacked]: credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts
warning[excessive-permissions]: overly broad permissions
error[unpinned-uses]: unpinned action reference
error[unpinned-uses]: unpinned action reference
7 findings (3 suppressed, 1 unsafe fixes): 0 informational, 0 low, 2 medium, 2 high

$ uvx zizmor --offline .github/workflows/        # this branch
error[unpinned-uses]: unpinned action reference
  --> .github/workflows/micar-lint.yml:21:15     # sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter@v1, by design
3 findings (2 suppressed): 0 informational, 0 low, 0 medium, 1 high

$ uvx --from actionlint-py actionlint; echo exit=$?
exit=0
$ uv run --no-project --with pyyaml python -I -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(".github/workflows/micar-lint.yml")); yaml.safe_load(open(".github/dependabot.yml")); print("yaml ok")'
yaml ok
$ for f in "uses: sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter@v1" "whitepaper: whitepaper.json" "strict: 'false'"; do grep -qF -- "$f" .github/workflows/micar-lint.yml && echo "contract ok: $f"; done
contract ok: uses: sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter@v1
contract ok: whitepaper: whitepaper.json
contract ok: strict: 'false'
$ git diff --stat main -- whitepaper.json LICENSE README.md
(empty)
$ uvx --no-cache --from "git+https://github.com/sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter@v1.2.1" micar-lint whitepaper.json | sed -n '4p'; echo exit=$?
Pass: 2  |  Review: 15  |  Missing: 3  |  Blockers: 15
exit=0
```

The GitHub run on this branch cannot be observed from the job that produced it (no PR is opened here); the `micar-lint` check on the pull request is the final proof that the pinned checkout and the `permissions` block work on the runner.

## Landing the change at the source

The owner's release process edits `templates/whitepaper-starter/` in `sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter` and exports it with `make template-export` (`docs/WHITEPAPER_STARTER_RELEASE.md`); a commit merged here makes that export's next push non-fast-forward. Recipe for a linter clone:

```
git -C <template-clone> diff main..improve/2026-10-31-ci-hygiene | git apply --directory=templates/whitepaper-starter
make template-check
```

then commit there and let the normal export carry it back. Merging here first is also fine if the owner then reconciles the export branch by merging rather than pushing.

body:
Driver: the Lean pipeline inside cmd/compile (refs #12).

- `gofv-ssa-opt` (`GoFVTest/Driver/{Pipeline,Main}.lean`): runs the registered ports in `compile.go` pass order (required/optimize/disabled as `ssa.Compile`), stops at the first unported pass with `status unported "<pass>"`; `--from/--to/--partial`, `--list`; `--check` whole-pipeline parity (chained Lean results vs every stock section; `--mixed`, `--whole-file-env`). Comparison helpers moved to `GoFVTest/Parity/Compare.lean`; renumber mismatch reports now print both definitions.
- `patches/go/0002-gofv-driver.patch`: `GOFV_SSA_DRIVER=<gofv-ssa-opt>` exports each function in process (0001's exporter), runs the Lean pipeline, imports the result into the `ssa.Func` (values, blocks, IDs, free lists, caches, names, consts; types/aux/slots by table number into the compiler's objects, new ones via the compiler's constructors / `fe.SplitSlot` / `fe.Syslook` / `TypeLinksym`), re-exports and requires byte equality, falls back to the stock passes on any error; `GOFV_SSA_DRIVER_MODE=full|mixed`, `_STATS`, `_DUMP`, `_PKG`, `_FUNC`. `scripts/build-go.sh` applies it only with `GOFV_GO_DRIVER=1` (the oracle stays 0001-only).
- `scripts/driver-e2e.sh`, `docs/DRIVER.md`.

## Checks
- `lake build gofv-ssa-opt pass-parity`: OK.
- `gofv-ssa-opt --check --jobs 4` on gofv-corpus/2aae1000ea1d/plain (9,297 functions): whole pipeline identical 9,269; first divergence at `decompose builtin` 9 (#79), at `writebarrier` 19 (new symbol contents from the driver's narrower frontend view; the importer only requires name+ABI for new symbols).
- `scripts/driver-e2e.sh --mode full` (std + 183 corpus programs, linux/arm64): 44,189 functions compiled, 44,181 entirely through Lean, 8 fallbacks (6 `writebarrier` error: size not in export, 1 `early phielim` same cause, 1 import: frontend struct copy); 183/183 programs same output+exit under qemu-aarch64-static; std archives byte-identical 191/372; linked binaries identical 0/183 (known gap, see DRIVER.md: state outside the exported SSA).
- No theorems.

author: leemour
body:
## Task
Make mail-cli ready for the next stages (local search 0.2.0, organise 0.3.0, server search 0.4.0, SMTP 0.5.0, OAuth 0.6.0) so each adds data and an adapter, not a branch in every command, and fix what the review of 0.1.1 found. No release: that comes after the cli-core wiring of Gmail labels, stored rules and mailProgress.

## What
- **Port and one way in** (RISK-2071, WC-ARCH-3, WC-ARCH-10, WC-LIFE-3, WC-LIFE-5): `src/mail/backend.ts` names `MailBackend` (cli-core's `MailSource` plus `folderList`, `check`, `close`). `openMail(context, {endpoint?, password?, canRetry?})` in `src/commands/context.ts` is the only way a command reaches the server; `session start` and `session status --check` now get the deadline and abort too. Tests replace the backend through the environment's `backend`. `close` sets a flag that `connect` refuses, so nothing reconnects after close.
- **Adapter split** (DEBT-205, WC-LAY-8): `src/mail/imap.ts` becomes `src/mail/imap/` with `connection.ts`, `read.ts`, `account.ts`, `messages.ts`, `errors.ts`.
- **Retries** (DEBT-204, DEBT-206, WC-TEST-5): cli-base `realSleep` and full-jitter `backoffMs`; a command's timer is injectable, so the timeout test no longer waits for real time.
- **Body batches** (PERF-70): at most 20 MB of RFC822.SIZE per body FETCH as well as 15 messages; no array copy per item.
- **Threads and headers** (RISK-2072, DEBT-202): a listing reads In-Reply-To and References; without a server thread id the thread is the first id in References, else In-Reply-To. Gmail's X-GM-MSGID and X-GM-THRID are unchanged. Header fields come from cli-core's `HEADER_FIELDS` and `headersOf`.
- **Provider registry** (RISK-2073): one `PROVIDERS` entry per provider (domains, MX, IMAP, SMTP, auth, note, sync folders, steps) in place of two tables. A new profile saves `auth`; a profile with only the flat `imap_*` keys keeps working, with nothing to migrate (a test pins it). Gmail syncs the `\All` folder (All Mail, in any language) by default.
- **session start** (FIND-2089): in its own file, and prints host, port, security and login before the password is sent. The stale comment on `discover` is fixed.
- **Password sources** (BUG-469, WC-OUT-12): one `PASSWORD_SOURCES` constant; the schemas now include `file`.
- **--limit** (BUG-470, WC-LIFE-16, WC-OUT-9): the reported "partial with no next step" did not reproduce, and a test pins the next step. The answer now says `stopped: "limit"` and the next step names `--limit`. `remaining` stays 0 for such a run because cli-core does not count what `max` left; that is a cli-core fix.

## Not in this PR
- Gmail labels, stored rules and mailProgress: they wait for the cli-core version a parallel agent is preparing.
- SMTP servers in the registry are not used yet, and were not checked against the providers' pages.

## Testing
- `pnpm release:check` passes locally: 148 tests; coverage statements 96.16%, branches 82.38%, functions 95.23%, lines 97.06%.
- The Windows and macOS run: `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref refactor/mail-backend` (result linked in a comment below).

body:
## Summary / 概要

Chat reading can now use VRCT-VOX's own chatbox detector. It is a YOLOX-Tiny trained only from frames captured in the chatbox lab (#21), published under MIT at [kein5/vrct-vox-chatbox-detector](https://huggingface.co/kein5/vrct-vox-chatbox-detector). It is not derived from the upstream model or its outputs.

- **Catalog.** New entry `vrct-vox-chatbox-detector` (target `ocr`, role `detector`, MIT), pinned to revision `d3f89ea1` with size and SHA-256. Nothing ships in builds. The file downloads only after the user agrees, and the hash is checked before it loads. `CATALOG_VERSION` is bumped, so earlier consent no longer counts.
- **Pipeline.** The detector is used only when the verified download exists and the new switch is on. Otherwise reading works as before, without a detector. The loader accepts only this entry's file name and hash, and rejects the upstream file name and anything in the bundled folder.
- **UI.** Config → Chat reading → Reading area adds:
  - a switch "Use the chatbox detector (recommended when installed)"
  - its state (in use / downloaded but off / not downloaded)
  - the consented download

  Text is in `locales/en.yml` and `locales/ja.yml`.
- **NOTICE.md** names the Hugging Face repository and the Megvii COCO base weights (Apache-2.0).

VRCT-VOX 独自の吹き出し検出モデル（MIT、Hugging Face で公開）を、同意付きで取得して、チャットの読み取りに使えるようにしました。

## Verification / 確認したこと

- Downloaded the published file anonymously from the pinned URL. Its SHA-256 matches the catalog.
- Opt-in real-model tests with the published file:
  - 39/40 labelled chatboxes found, 0 extra (the previous upload found 40/40 on these early lab frames).
  - With PP-OCR: 10 of 12 chatboxes read exactly as sent (the same as before).
- On frames neither version trained on (validation parts of two captures on VRChat's servers, and a separate 10-minute capture): 205 of 214 chatboxes found with 7 false detections; the previous upload `475e92e0` found 197 with 13. The lab had saved earlier frames with red and blue swapped; this version is trained on corrected frames.
- Earlier, the backend pipeline (`OcrPipeline` with the app's defaults, the X11 capture and the consented download) read a live lab VRChat window: of 30 messages, 22 exactly and 27 nearly as sent, and no world text. The misses were by design: one repeat within the 30-second dedup window and a one-character message. The Tauri UI was not part of that run.
- `tools/dev.py check`:
  - backend, ui, quick (lint, node, tooling) and commits: passed
  - voice: 1423 passed. The 6 failures in `test_capture_pipewire.py` happen because the native capture helper is not built in this worktree; they are unrelated to this change.
- **Not verified:**
  - a live VRChat window with the detector on
  - the opt-in browser suites after the last commit, which changes no UI
  - a Windows build

- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:` ...); checked by CI.
- [x] Tests added or updated for behavior changes.
- [x] No secrets, API keys, voice recordings or private model files are included.

author: hwacookie
body:
Fixes #39

## What changed

- Parking: delete the entry-angle limit - the owner ruled it is not a constraint (issue 39)

## Verdicts / measurements

## What

Deletes the reverse solver's entry-angle limit. The owner ruled on 2026-10-30 that the parking
constraints are contacts / road edge / oncoming occupancy and that no intermediate angle is
prohibited. I kept a 20 deg limit anyway through three rounds (hard refusal -> named constant ->
re-set-up *trigger*), each time justifying it with measurements. Those measurements were real but
they were evidence about a different thing: our two-arc family cannot sweep from a steep pose
without a straight reverse leg, so the limit was standing in for a planner gap. Keeping an
invented number as the decision input was the wrong trade, and the user called it.

Now nothing in the solver asks "how steep is the nose". The only refusal is the candidate
search: no path that clears both neighbours, the kerb, the centreline and the run-out. When that
happens the job re-sets up - bounded forward run, then the same search from the new pose - and
when the re-set-ups run out the straight backup and the visible hazard give-up still apply, so
the issue 39 invariant (no parking job ends without a verdict) is untouched.

Removed: PARK_ENTRY_MAX_RAD / PARK_ENTRY_MAX_DEG and the REFUSED record that quoted them, and the
old angle-based EXTRA STAGE condition (it tested |psi0| > 10 deg, i.e. the same invented number in
another place). Added at that site: re-set-up armed by the geometry verdict, with the pose and the
lateral gap in the record so the refusal can be checked against the bay, not against a threshold.

## Verdict lines

    unit               Failed: 0, Passed: 165, Skipped: 2, Total: 167
    canary             PARK_SHIMMY_TRIES=0 -> Failed: 1, exactly BayReverseInTests(clearanceM: 1.5)
    e2e, WATCH MODE (--watch --realtime, maximized window, staged frozen)
      bay 2.5 m        PASSED  lane guard clean, kerb 8 cm front / 10 cm rear (limit 30 cm)
      bay 1.0 m        timed out (see below)
      bay 0.5 m        timed out (see below)
      park_block_priority  timed out (see below)

## The one thing I will not paper over

Watch mode exposed a harness defect my warped runs had hidden: on this same code at --warp 4 the
tight bays reach verdicts (155/77 cm, and 17.1 deg / 0.57 m give-up), while at real time three of
five scenarios end "timed out". A verdict that depends on pacing cannot judge parking, and it is
very likely the same effect behind issue 47's supposedly order-dependent row (which passes alone
and fails in long runs). So this PR claims the constraint removal and the unit gates, and makes no
e2e claim about the tight bays until the scenario window is pinned to sim time.

author: tagban
body:
The Twin Adder's fifth recruit mission, "Their Finest Hour" (111605).

- **Accept:** Fulke gives you the ceremony invitation.
- **Ceremony:** walking into Mih Khetto's Amphitheatre (trigger 1090279, shared with Man2g0) plays Kan-E-Senna's address (com0g610). The cutscene ends on a warp, so the server sets you down on the benches.
- **Thancred** stands on the stage. He gives you the Earthbreaker and sends you to the Rootslake.
- **The crowd** after the ceremony: a Wood Wailer, a Serpent captain, a conjurer, a mother and a child, each with their own line.
- **Rootslake** (South Shroud): Thancred talks first, then Urianger reads the sixth verse and closes the quest. The reward is 1,541 EXP and 300 Serpent Seals.
- Seed 129 holds the cast. Four of the crowd classes shipped stripped, so they get PopulaceStandard.

## Notes

- The client names no classes for the crowd, so generic Gridanians that match each line stand in.
- Thancred at the amphitheatre also shows a "!" while you're on your way to the Rootslake, because the flag is per class. Talking to him there just ends the event.
- The Rootslake pair stands on the gully path down to the lake's west shore. Urianger's first spot was inside the rock, so it was moved.

## Tested in the client

The whole quest was played end to end: accept, the ceremony cutscene and warp, Thancred and the Earthbreaker, a crowd talk, then the Rootslake. The reward window showed 1,541 experience points and 300 Serpent Seals, and the quest completed.

author: sebastianfoerste
body:
Branch `improve/2026-10-31-readme` at `d5dfbd515589fd3856c2ef889c832ac8c613c835` (one commit on top of `main` `fe98b47baa3d6aac9447ff5bcc62fe73f3fd6e5a`). Only `README.md` changes: 822 → 349 words.

## What

The same five parts in the same order, each cut to what a template user needs:

- What it is and how the check behaves: report mode (`strict: 'false'`), open findings do not fail the check, a file the linter cannot load (invalid JSON, unknown `"type"`) does, `strict: 'true'` fails on any open (Review or Missing) BLOCKER. The browser playground sentence stays ("nothing you paste leaves the page").
- How to use it: four steps (use the template; replace every `REPLACE:` placeholder, the linter reads an untouched placeholder as text, not as a gap; set `"type"`, the placeholders describe an asset-referenced token under Art. 19 and Annex II MiCAR, for `emt`/`other` the linter warns about keys it does not read and names the sections it lacks, add those and rewrite the existing placeholders for your type; push, work the findings down, hand the draft to counsel).
- What the linter checks: deterministic checks (keywords, minimum length and structure per required section and annex item, LEI check digits, file format); no judgement of accuracy or adequacy; the two never-passing BLOCKERs with the deposit-floor citation kept character for character ("Art. 35(4), 36(4)(d), 45(3) and 45(7)(b) MiCAR"), so a strict build always fails; the workflow follows the linter's `@v1` tag, which moves with each v1 release; its changelog says what changed.
- Scope and honesty (not legal advice; "A green check never means the white paper is lawful, complete or ready to notify or submit for approval. That judgment stays with your lawyer."; content requirements only; synthetic text) and License.

Dropped: every sentence tied to one linter release ("in 1.2.1 the notification-date and language checks do", "the two LEI checks still report the `issuer` section Missing", "`@v1` runs v1.2.1, which does not yet run …", "once a linter release includes the first-page statement check", the `not_approved_statement` sentence), the list of exactly which sections `emt` and `other` report as Missing (the Actions log names them), the duplicated explanation of strict mode, and "A draft can pass every check that can pass and still be misleading" (the green-check sentence next to it says the same for the CI reader). Style: one citation form (EU form, as the linter prints by default): "Anhang II" → "Annex II"; "Art. 6 Abs. 3" went with its sentence. `whitepaper.json` keeps its German form; whether both should match is the owner's call.

## Why

- `wc -w README.md` on `main` is 822, more than twice the 350-word limit. More than half of the text describes the behaviour of linter 1.2.1 specifically.
- The linter's unreleased `main` (`0722a85`, 2026-10-31) already contradicts those sentences: on the untouched template it reports `Pass: 0 | Review: 19 | Missing: 1` (the date and language checks go to Review, the two LEI rules go to Review with a note on other national identifiers, `ANNEX_II.G.VALUATION_AUDIT` reads the rights section). A README that describes one release goes wrong on the day `@v1` moves; one that describes the mechanism does not. The owner's release gate (`docs/WHITEPAPER_STARTER_RELEASE.md`, step 2) already re-runs the untouched template at release time; after this change there is no release-specific README sentence left to update.
- The linter repository's `tests/test_doc_claims.py` fails if the starter README contains "pinpoint"; it does not.

## Evidence for every behavioural sentence (linter v1.2.1 = what `@v1` runs, reproduced locally on 2026-10-31 with `uvx --no-cache --from "git+https://github.com/sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter@v1.2.1" micar-lint …`)

```
# untouched whitepaper.json (type art), report mode, exit 0; with --strict the same report and exit 1
Pass: 2  |  Review: 15  |  Missing: 3  |  Blockers: 15
[MISS  ] [BLOCKER] COMMON.IXBRL_TAGGING  Inline XBRL (iXBRL) compliance and ESMA metadata tagging
           -  Draft format: notification requires XHTML with Inline XBRL tagging. This format cannot satisfy that requirement; the content checks still apply.
[MISS  ] [MAJOR  ] COMMON.LEI_CHECK_DIGITS  Legal Entity Identifier format and check digits (ISO 17442, ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 97-10)     ("LEI check digits, file format")
[REVIEW] [BLOCKER] ANNEX_II.G.DEPOSIT_FLOOR_REVIEW  Candidate deposit floor for the reserve (30 % under Art. 36(4)(d); 60 % under Art. 45(7)(b) for significant ARTs, or for non-significant ARTs via Arts. 35(4) and 45(3) MiCAR) - lawyer review required
           -  Draft characterisation assertion missing or invalid (references_official_currency, art_significant); the applicable minimum share cannot be determined. The assertion remains pending lawyer confirmation.
# every other rule: [REVIEW] with "Section is thin" and/or "Missing review terms" ("reads an untouched placeholder as text, not as a gap"); a Review BLOCKER counts as open: --strict exits 1 on this report ("open (Review or Missing) BLOCKER")

# "type": "emt" → Pass: 2 | Review: 9 | Missing: 5 | Blockers: 11 ; "type": "other" → Pass: 2 | Review: 9 | Missing: 7 | Blockers: 11 ; both print:
  -  Unrecognized section key 'art' in draft sections. Ensure it matches required section keys.
  -  Unrecognized section key 'reserve_of_assets' in draft sections. Ensure it matches required section keys.
  -  Unrecognized section key 'redemption' in draft sections. Ensure it matches required section keys.
# emt: [MISS] ANNEX_III.B (section 'emt'), ANNEX_III.SAFEGUARDING ('safeguarding'); other: [MISS] ANNEX_I.A ('offeror'), ANNEX_I.C ('trading_platform_operator'), ANNEX_I.D ('project'), ANNEX_I.F ('crypto_asset')  ("names the sections it lacks")

# "a file the linter cannot load (invalid JSON, unknown "type") does [fail the check]" (report mode):
$ micar-lint wp-badtype.json ; echo exit=$?
Unknown whitepaper type 'bogus'. Expected one of: other, art, emt
exit=1
$ micar-lint wp-invalid.json ; echo exit=$?
Invalid JSON in wp-invalid.json: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 3 (char 2)
exit=1
```

"The workflow follows the linter's `@v1` tag, which moves with each v1 release": `gh api repos/sebastianfoerste/micar-whitepaper-linter/git/tags/009458fd…` → tag `v1`, message "v1 -> v1.2.1", object `02e7467ccb9f0150da9967352d45c06bef3f2852` = tag `v1.2.1` (2026-10-27); linter CHANGELOG 1.2.0: "The tag `v1.2.0` marks both, and `v1` moves to it." The deposit-floor rule is Review-only in the v1.2.1 source (`_deposit_floor_finding` never returns pass), so "never pass … a strict build therefore always fails" is literal, not just true for this draft.

## Legal statements, verified on 2026-10-31

Sources: ESMA Interactive Single Rulebook (an official ESMA publication of the consolidated MiCAR text; EUR-Lex answered every request from this sandbox with an empty HTTP 202 challenge page, and the Publications Office CELLAR resolver with HTTP 500 at the time of this run) and, for Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2984, the Official Journal text (OJ L, 2024/2984, 3.12.2024; ELI `http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2024/2984/oj`) as served by CELLAR earlier the same day into this sandbox (`/tmp/eurlex/its-eng.txt`, 12:06 CET).

|---|---|---|---|
| "the deposit floor of the reserve of assets (Art. 35(4), 36(4)(d), 45(3) and 45(7)(b) MiCAR), left to a lawyer" (before: "… always stays open for a lawyer") | Art. 36(4), second subparagraph, point (d): deposits in credit institutions "cannot be lower than 30 %"; Art. 45(7), first subparagraph, point (b): "cannot be lower than 60 %"; Art. 45(3): liquidity management policy of significant-ART issuers; Art. 35(4): the competent authority may require a non-significant issuer "to comply with any requirement set out in Article 45" | https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-and-data/interactive-sin
