body:
Refs #276 — Communications Hub R2 completion. **Draft; owner approval gates closure and merge. Do not merge.**

## Purpose
Complete ARTEMIS Communications Hub R2 on the existing preview branch: hardened two-way messaging intake, durable pilot capture, an authenticated operator inbox with replies, a retry worker, and signed webhook recording — with an honest status taxonomy that never presents provider acceptance as delivery.

Ownership: division UNREVIEWED (no PRODUCT_REGISTRY entry), product Communications Hub R2, lifecycle noindex preview/pilot, visibility public form + authenticated operator inbox, data mode live intake with private data in Supabase only.

## Scope
- `lib/comms/` pure helpers (validation/sanitization incl. CR/LF stripping, status taxonomy + legacy mapping, retry backoff, Svix + GitHub HMAC verification) + server REST/Resend helpers; unit tests (12 new).
- Intake hardening: ip-hash rate limit (5/h, 20/day, ADR-014), client idempotency (header or submissionId, unique index, deduplicated response), Resend provider id captured, notification_error/attempts/next_retry_at recorded, outbox-honest status PATCH (a failed PATCH reports notification_queued, never provider_accepted).
- Migration v2 (new file; v1 untouched): new columns + replies table + GitHub events table; RLS enabled, no policies.
- Retry route gated by ARTEMIS_COMMS_CRON_SECRET (fail closed); Resend webhook (Svix) for delivered/bounced/complained; GitHub webhook ledger storing summaries only.
- Operator inbox at /communications/inbox (requireAuth, ADR-011) with thread view and replies recorded before sending.
- Pilot requests: full payload persisted to Supabase before the Squarespace sync; durable capture wins on sync failure; legacy behaviour unchanged when Supabase is not configured.
- Public console: real honeypot field, per-mount submissionId, corrected status copy. Middleware matcher adds the inbox.

## What is NOT changed
- No production deployment, no merge, no Vercel env changes, no Supabase SQL executed (migrations are files + instructions only).
- WhatsApp/SMS is not implemented (no provider/consent) — page still says "not activated in this preview".
- v1 migration is not rewritten. No secrets, phone numbers, or private inquiry content in source.

## Verification
- Baseline (6491fb21): typecheck PASS, lint PASS, tests 258 passed / 3 failed (pre-existing standalone-isolation failures), build compiles then stops at an auth-page prerender with "Supabase is not configured" (no env in sandbox).
- Final (this head): typecheck PASS, lint PASS, tests 270 passed / 3 failed (same 3 pre-existing failures, unrelated HVAC standalone files), no-env build behaves identically in kind; with dummy non-secret Supabase placeholders the full build completes (postbuild validators OK) — baseline does the same with the same placeholders.
- Live preview probes are recorded in the Issue #276 comment.

## Env prerequisites (names only — owner action)
SUPABASE_URL (or NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL), SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, RESEND_API_KEY, ARTEMIS_COMMS_FROM, ARTEMIS_COMMS_TO, ARTEMIS_IP_SALT, ARTEMIS_INTERNAL_ALLOWLIST; optional ARTEMIS_COMMS_CRON_SECRET, RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Then run migrations v1, then v2, in the Supabase SQL editor.

## Risks / not yet verified
Live delivery, replies, webhooks, and the retry worker are NOT verified — they require the env above. Until then POST /api/communications correctly returns 503 "not configured". Full record: docs/history/artemis-comms-r2-plan-2026-10-31.md

author: kratosdatagod
body:
Before: no browser test opened an entity's drift, quarantine or freshness cards, or Home's late tables. Nothing checked that Replay sends only the rows that were fixed, or that Discard asks before it writes.

After: `app/tests/browser/entity-drift-quarantine.test.cjs` (12 tests) covers them. Test only, with no app code changed. Discard already asks in a danger confirm.

How: engine answers are mocked in the shapes `dataops_service.py`, `meta/drift.py`, `meta/freshness.py`, `meta/engine.py` and `meta/project.py` return; the file names them in a comment.

Fixes #1374

## What it checks
- Drift shows added, dropped and retyped columns. When nothing changed, the card says the source matches the contract; there is no "no drift" text, so the test checks that wording.
- Quarantine lists each held row and its reason. Replay sends exactly the rows fixed, with exactly the fixed values.
- Discard asks first in a danger confirm. Cancel sends nothing, and Discard sends the picked rows.
- Freshness shows each environment as Fresh, Late or Never loaded. The engine's `never` status is the story's "unknown".
- The freshness dialog saves the promise as entered. The Teams alerts dialog sends the address and test choice picked, and Cancel sends nothing.
- Home lists late tables, or says every promise is kept.
- An engine error shows a plain message, and the card stays as it was (drift, replay and freshness save).
- Opening the page and Home sends no write.
- axe finds nothing serious on the cards and dialogs, using `settleForAxe`. The test also fails on any page error.

## Runs
- The new file passed 12/12 on three runs in a row, and 12/12 with two `ui.test.cjs` processes running alongside.
- I re-ran it once more before opening this PR: 12/12.
- `ui.test.cjs`: 314/314.

## Mutation checks
Each mutation was made in `app/ui/dataops.js` and then restored.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| Replay sends every row's id | Replay test |
| Replay sends edits for rows that weren't fixed | Replay test |
| Discard confirm removed | Discard test, axe test |
| Confirm not danger | Discard test |
| Discard write sent before the confirm | Discard test |
| Dropped drift rows not drawn | Drift test |
| Late drawn as Fresh | Freshness test |
| Freshness save sends every environment, not the ones ticked | Freshness dialog test |
| "Send a test and save" sends `test: false` | Alerts test |
| Card redrawn after a replay error | Error test |
| A write sent while the page loads | Replay, Discard, Freshness dialog and read-only tests |

## Not covered
Drift's "Save to config" (`meta_drift_apply`) is only checked to stay disabled until something is picked. The story didn't ask for more.

## Handoff
Ready for quality. Only Release management merges.

author: bobliuuu
body:
## What
- `vcs-server --backend s3://bucket/prefix?endpoint=...` (S3 mode; refuses stores that ignore conditional writes) next to `--root`.
- Lock validator (#125): lease expiry computed by the server clock (client `expires_at` only conveys the requested lease), `--max-lease-secs` cap, replica skew epsilon (`--skew-epsilon-ms`, `Publisher::with_skew_epsilon`; #130).
- Per-zone path-glob policy (#123, `--policy`): allow/deny/require-lock, deny by default, deny beats allow, admin skips allow/deny but not require-lock.
- `model_locks.rs`: replica clock offsets + skew epsilon, new invariant L-SKEW, two mutation checks.
- `deploy/` (Dockerfile, systemd unit, tokens and policy samples) and `docs/deploy.md`.

## Why
Makes vcs-server usable by a team without touching the request-handling code owned by the security work (only a small hunk in `object_put` and `Config`).

## QA (run on the Linux box)
- `cargo test --workspace`: 517 passed, 0 failed; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean.
- `vcs-cli/tests/server_e2e.rs`: real `vcs-server` on an ephemeral port, real `vcs`: remote set, publish, clone, fetch, sync, lock/unlock, publish refused under another user's lock, 401 on wrong token, 403 for read-only token. Passes against a directory backend and against S3 (`VCS_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT`).
- S3 backend was exercised against **moto** (`moto_server`), not MinIO: docker is not usable on the box and MinIO's binaries are gone (410). The fake server in the vcs-store-s3 tests is canned-response only and cannot do CAS. moto passes the existing gated MinIO suite too.
- `crates/vcs-server/tests/validator.rs`: server-computed expiry, forged expiry, lease cap, future client clock, two replicas with skew, policy, require-lock.

## Caveats
- The S3 e2e test skips unless `VCS_TEST_S3_ENDPOINT` is set (CI needs an S3-compatible server).
- Dockerfile and systemd unit were not built or started. The CLI still only opens `http://` remotes.
- Read access is role-only; policy filters writes. The skew model uses two replicas and a 2-tick horizon.

## Problem

`tests/e2e/specs/pdf-text.spec.ts` proxies `fonts.gstatic.com` through `page.route` with `route.fetch()`. A fetch still in flight when the test ends rejects with "Request context disposed". The `expect` inside the handler then failed the test after its body had already passed (run 41240846813).

body:
Closes #18

## Summary

```text
src/app/
├── layout.tsx              # <html lang="es">, <body class="dcc-root">, @dcc/ui/css (CSS only)
├── page.tsx                # "Wise Wizard" placeholder, dcc- classes only
└── api/health/route.ts     # Prisma SELECT 1 → 200 | 503
prisma/schema.prisma        # Postgres datasource, no models (#11)
Dockerfile, compose.yaml    # Bun build on node:26 → standalone on Node as `node`; app + postgres:18, volumes db + sources
.github/workflows/ci.yml    # bun install --frozen-lockfile → check → build → playwright
.claude/                    # plugins (settings.json), skills, fallow + graphify hooks
```

```text
bun run check
  lint → typecheck (next typegen + tsc) → format:check → test (vitest)
  → fallow → react-doctor --no-telemetry --no-supply-chain → impeccable detect src
bun run setup   # once per clone
  graphify hook install
  claude plugin install {ponytail, impeccable, mattpocock-skills} --scope project
```

Decisions taken during the work (each one asked or forced by the tools):

- **Versions:** Next 16.4.3, Node 26 (Active LTS since 2026-10-28), Bun 1.4.4, Prisma 7.10.1 + `@prisma/adapter-pg` (npm `latest` for `prisma` is `8.0.0-rc.29`, so I took the last stable), Agent SDK 0.3.316 + peers, ts-fsrs 6.0.0, dcc-ui-kit `#v2.8.1` (still the latest tag), ESLint 10.
- **`trustedDependencies: []`:** no installed package needs a lifecycle script. Prisma's preinstall only checks the Node version, and the CLI downloads its schema engine on demand (verified by deleting it). An empty list also overrides Bun's default trust list. `prisma generate` runs from the root `postinstall`.
- **`prisma` CLI is a devDependency** (fallow flagged it; Prisma's docs install it with `--save-dev`). `@prisma/client` + the adapter stay runtime.
- **dcc-ui-kit fonts:** Turbopack resolves the relative `url(fonts/…)` from `node_modules` into `/_next/static/media/…`. No copy into `public/` was needed.
- **Next agent rules:** the managed block `next dev` writes into `AGENTS.md` is kept (your call).
- **react-doctor supply-chain scan off** (`--no-supply-chain`, your call): `check` stays offline and deterministic.
- **Plugins need a per-clone install.** The Claude Code docs (`plugins/loading.md` → "Enabled in project settings but not installed") say a plugin enabled only in the project `.claude/settings.json` isn't fetched onto a new machine. So `bun run setup` runs `claude plugin install … --scope project` for each one (your call).
- **fallow's commit/push gate** from `fallow agent install` is a Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook, committed in `.claude/`, not a `.git/hooks` script. The only per-clone git hooks are graphify's.
- **react-doctor skill:** `react-doctor install --yes` would also install skills for Codex and Copilot, a `doctor` script, a pre-commit hook and a `react-doctor.yml` workflow. The interactive mode is the only way to opt out, so I copied `node_modules/react-doctor/dist/skills/react-doctor` into `.claude/skills/`, which is what its Claude Code step does (`mode: "copy"`).
- **Installer output pruned** (`writing-for-agents`):
  - fallow's `AGENTS.md` block (task map, which duplicates the fallow skill and `--help`) is replaced by a short `### Quality gates` note under Conventions.
  - graphify's `CLAUDE.md` section no longer claims the graph exists and drops the committed-graph rule, since `graphify-out/` is gitignored.
  - graphify's stray `.claude/CLAUDE.md` pointer is deleted.
  - graphify's hooks used `/Users/<me>/.local/bin/graphify` and now resolve `graphify` from `PATH`; they exit 0 when it's missing.
- **Prettier ignores** `docs/research/` (it rewrote quoted code fragments in these dated snapshots) and tool-written files (`.claude/skills/`, `.claude/hooks/`, `.mcp.json`, `skills-lock.json`, `.impeccable/`).
- **compose:** `db` publishes on `127.0.0.1:${DB_PORT:-5432}`, because my host already runs a Postgres on 5432.

## Evidence

**Fresh clone** of this branch (`git clone` into a temp dir → `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run check && bun run build && bun run test:e2e`). The first attempt went **red** on `tsc` (`Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'`: `.next/types` doesn't exist before a build). `typecheck` now runs `next typegen` first, and the second fresh clone is green with a clean `git status`.

`bun run check` (condensed; full output has fallow's health table):

```text
$ eslint
$ next typegen && tsc --noEmit
✓ Types generated successfully
$ prettier --check .
All matched files use Prettier code style!
$ vitest run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
✓ No issues found            # fallow dead-code
✓ No code duplication found  # fallow dupes
✓ 0 above threshold · 16 analyzed · maintainability 97.5 (good)
✔ No issues found!           # react-doctor
4 files scanned with regex matching only (.ts, .tsx).   # impeccable: 0 findings
```

Every gate exits non-zero on a finding. I checked fallow without its config (exit 1), and impeccable/react-doctor use `--blocking warning` / exit 2.

`bun run test:e2e`:

```text
  ✓  1 [desktop] › e2e/home.spec.ts:3:5 › home renders in Spanish with dcc-ui-kit CSS only
  ✓  2 [mobile] › e2e/home.spec.ts:3:5 › home renders in Spanish with dcc-ui-kit CSS only
  2 passed (2.1s)
```

The e2e test checks: `lang="es"`, `body.dcc-root`, a computed body font that starts with Inter and an Inter `FontFace` with status `loaded`, no `window.DCCUI` and no dcc-ui-kit `<script>`, and no failed or ≥400 request. To confirm it isn't vacuous, I removed the CSS import and it failed with `Expected pattern: /^"?Inter"?/ Received string: "Times"`.

`docker compose up --build`:

```text
$ curl -i localhost:3000/api/health   # db up
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","db":"up"}

$ docker compose stop db
$ curl -i localhost:3000/api/health   # db stopped
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"status":"error","db":"down"}

$ docker compose start db
$ curl -i localhost:3000/api/health   # db back
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","db":"up"}
```

The app container runs as `uid=1000(node)`, and `/data/sources` is owned by `node`. The CSS and the 6 woff2 files return 200 from the container.

Plugins enabled (`claude plugin list`) and committed skills:

```text
ponytail@ponytail                           5.3.3  scope: project  ✔ enabled
impeccable@impeccable                       4.8.0  scope: project  ✔ enabled
mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official   1.3.1  scope: project  ✔ enabled

.claude/skills/: fallow  fallow-setup  graphify  react-doctor  vercel-react-best-practices
```

Out of scope: nothing installed for #14 (no headless library or icons), #17/#11 (no PDF toolchain, no models), #15 (no SDK wiring, no token) or #10 (no `PRODUCT.md`/`DESIGN.md`). `.env` is gitignored; `.env.example` has example values and an empty `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive bootstrap on an app-less repo; reverting the merge removes it. The `.git/hooks` and the plugin installs live per clone and are removed with `graphify hook uninstall` / `claude plugin uninstall`.

**Blast Radius:** tooling

- Every later issue inherits `bun run check` as its gate, along with the fallow, impeccable and graphify hooks in Claude Code sessions.
- The AC "a clone gets them without any user-level install" holds for the skills. The three plugins need `bun run setup` once per clone, after trusting the folder in Claude Code. I couldn't test that on a machine that has never seen these marketplaces.
- Re-running `graphify claude install` rewrites its `CLAUDE.md` section and puts the absolute path back in its hooks. `bun run setup` doesn't call it.
- The react-doctor skill's text still says `npx react-doctor@latest` (vendored as shipped).
- Your user-level graphify skill is 0.9.50 against the 0.9.99 CLI. I left it untouched; `graphify install --platform claude` updates it.

author: ahmedikram05
body:
## Summary

Three leftover P2s from the six-repo deep-dive review. 2 commits.

- **Baseline-cache filenames embedded the raw `instance_id`** (`evaluation/test_runner.py`), so an id containing a path separator or `..` could traverse or overwrite files in the shared cache volume. The name is now a SHA-256 of the id, and read/write share one helper so hits stay deterministic. New test uses the hostile id `"../../../etc/instance..id"` and asserts the file lands inside the cache dir and round-trips.
- **Fabricated `once_per_repo` ground truth was persisted.** A repo skipped under `once_per_repo` recorded `f2p=1.0` with an empty `tests_head` and wrote it to the baseline cache, so a later run at the same `base_sha` (e.g. `verify_mode="all"`) could load it as real ground truth. Fabricated results are no longer written at the source. *Correction to the review:* the reported cross-`base_sha` reuse isn't reachable — `_load_baseline_cache` already rejects a mismatched `base_sha`; the real defect is persistence at the *same* sha.
- **`vllm`/`peft`/`trl` were open-ended in a production path.** `vllm` is imported by the eval inference and serving code, `peft` by `registry/cli.py`, `trl` by the eval image — a minor release could silently change sampling or adapter behaviour between deploys. Bounds are the next minor past the resolved lock versions (`vllm>=0.26.0,<0.29.0`, `peft>=0.19.0,<0.20.0`, `trl>=1.9.0,<1.10.0`) so `uv.lock` stays satisfiable. `bitsandbytes`/`accelerate` deliberately left unbounded: training-only, not on the serving/eval path.

## Evidence

- `UV_FROZEN=1 uv run pytest tests/evaluation/test_eval_unit.py tests/evaluation/test_eval_test_runner_coverage.py -q` → **216 passed, 1 skipped**
- `UV_FROZEN=1 uv run ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy evaluation/test_runner.py` → no issues
- `pyproject.toml` parsed offline (tomllib) with the new bounds
- `git status --short -- uv.lock` → **unmodified**

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** eval cache hygiene, dependency resolution

- Pre-existing poisoned v3 cache entries in a shared volume are **not** regenerated — the fix is refuse-to-write going forward. Bumping `_BASELINE_CACHE_VERSION` would purge them but invalidates every cached baseline; flagged, not done.
- The Modal image specs (`evaluation/inference.py`, `inference/modal_serve.py`) still pin `vllm>=0.26.0` at *build* time, which bypasses the new `pyproject.toml` bound — worth a follow-up.
- Pinning only narrows the window to the next minor; it is not a full freeze.

author: adlermrf
body:
## O que foi feito

Implementação da tela de listagem de tarefas, com busca por título, filtros por status e prioridade, ordenação e paginação, todos executados no backend. Também inclui ajustes globais de idioma e ícones.

### Tela de listagem (`features/tasks/task-list`)
- Tabela com título, prioridade, status, vencimento, data de criação e ações
- Prioridade e status com cores e rótulos em português
- Busca por título com espera de 400 ms depois da digitação
- Filtros por status e prioridade, combináveis com a busca, e botão "Limpar filtros"
- Ordenação por título, vencimento e data de criação, os mesmos campos aceitos pela API
- Paginador com o total vindo de `totalItems` da API, e não do tamanho da lista
- Ações por linha: ver detalhes, editar, concluir ou reabrir, e excluir
- Barra de progresso durante a busca
- Mensagens para lista vazia e para erro da API
- Em telas estreitas, os filtros quebram em linhas e a tabela ganha rolagem horizontal própria

### Ajustes globais
- `PtBrPaginatorIntl`: textos do paginador em português, como "Itens por página" e "1 – 10 de 12"
- `LOCALE_ID` `pt-BR`: datas no formato brasileiro
- `MAT_ICON_DEFAULT_OPTIONS`: os `<mat-icon>` passam a usar a fonte Material Symbols, a mesma carregada no `index.html`
- `index.html` com `lang="pt-BR"` e título "To-Do List"

### Testes
- `TaskList` com 3 cenários, usando `HttpTestingController`:
  - A primeira busca pede a página 0, 10 itens, ordenada por `CREATED_AT` em ordem `DESC`, e a tabela mostra os rótulos em português
  - Lista vazia mostra "Nenhuma tarefa encontrada."
  - Erro da API aparece na faixa de alerta

## Decisões de projeto

- **Sem `MatTableDataSource`:** ele ordena e pagina em memória, no navegador. Aqui a tabela recebe só a página devolvida pela API, e o paginador e a ordenação geram uma nova chamada.
- **Estado em signals:** o projeto é zoneless, então a tela só se atualiza quando um signal muda. Tarefas, total, carregamento e erro ficam em signals.
- **Um signal `query` para a busca:** filtros, paginador e ordenação atualizam o mesmo `query`, e cada mudança dispara uma busca. O `switchMap` cancela a busca anterior se a resposta ainda não chegou.
- **Página volta para 0** ao mudar filtro ou ordenação, porque a página atual pode não existir no novo resultado.
- **Rótulos tipados como `Record<string, string>` no componente:** a linha da tabela chega ao template sem tipo, e o modo estrito recusaria a indexação.

## Limitações conhecidas

- A exclusão usa o `confirm()` do navegador por enquanto; será trocada por um diálogo do Material.
- Em telas de cerca de 420 px, a barra superior com os três botões não cabe, e a página passa a rolar para o lado. A 500 px, cabe.
- O build de produção avisa que o pacote inicial (cerca de 720 kB) passa do orçamento padrão de 500 kB. Não é erro; o tamanho vem do Angular Material.

## Como testar

Testes do frontend:

```bash
cd frontend
ng test --watch=false
```

O resultado deve mostrar `Test Files 6 passed (6)` e `Tests 14 passed (14)`.

Na tela, com o backend rodando num terminal e `ng serve` no outro, abra `http://localhost:4200/tasks`. Para testar a paginação, crie pelo menos 11 tarefas pelo Swagger.

| O que testar | Esperado |
|---|---|
| Barra superior | Ícones de verdade, não palavras |
| Abrir a página | Tarefas mais recentes primeiro, com prioridade e status coloridos e em português |
| Digitar "estu" na busca | Depois de uma pausa, só as tarefas com "estu" no título |
| Status e Prioridade | Os filtros se combinam com a busca |
| "Limpar filtros" | Volta à lista completa |
| Cabeçalho "Título" | Ordem alfabética; de novo inverte; um terceiro clique volta ao padrão |
| Paginador | "Itens por página" e "1 – 10 de N"; a próxima página mostra o resto |
| Ícone ✓ numa tarefa | Vira "Concluída", e o ícone muda para reabrir |
| Ícone de lixeira | Pede confirmação; ao confirmar, a tarefa some |
| Filtro sem resultado | "Nenhuma tarefa encontrada." |
| Backend parado | Faixa vermelha: "Não foi possível conectar ao servidor..." |

Prova de que o servidor pagina, ordena e filtra: abra a aba Network (F12) e mude a página, a ordenação ou um filtro. Cada ação gera uma chamada nova a `tasks?page=...&sort=...`.

body:
## Pourquoi
Les statuts du classeur donnaient CX-01, CX-04 et AM-02 « Partiel » faute de tests sur plusieurs critères. Cette PR **n'ajoute que des tests** : aucun code applicatif ni test existant n'est modifié. (Classeur v3 introuvable : v2 utilisée.)

## Contenu
**API** (vrai routeur, vrai JWT, SQLite en mémoire) — jeu de données écrit **à la main** (`tests/_jeu_donnees_cx.py`, valeurs attendues calculées à la main, jamais par du code applicatif) :
- `test_cx01_indicateurs_siege.py` (24) : CSAT global et son évolution en points, nombre d'avis et évolution en %, nombre d'avis critiques et son évolution (plus = défavorable), répartition des sentiments (comptes et pourcentages, repli sur les notes sans analyse), alertes critiques par agence, classement, période sélectionnable (7, 30, 60, 90 jours, par défaut, bornes 422), filtre d'agence, isolation (autre organisation, agence désactivée, avis hors période), rôles, et concordance de `/dashboard/siege` avec `/dashboard/statistics/cx`.
- `test_cx04_combinaison_filtres.py` (18) : chaque filtre seul, bornes de période, discordance, **les 128 combinaisons des 7 filtres** (agence, période, note, ton, gravité, thème, discordance) comparées à un modèle de référence (liste, total `X-Total-Count`, ordre), pagination et tri sous filtres, cas vides, isolation par organisation et par agence.
- `test_am02_indicateurs_agence.py` (24) : CSAT, nombre d'avis, évolution vs période précédente de même durée, négatifs, critiques, discordances, sentiments, cycle de traitement, thèmes, périodes (7/30/60/90), avis hors période, période sans avis (jamais 0), isolation entre agences/organisations/rôles, concordance avec `/dashboard/statistics/agency`.

**Dashboard** (+46 tests) :
- `siegeData.test.ts`, `SiegeKpis.valeurs.test.tsx` (CX-01) : formatage (virgule, signe −, milliers), évolutions et leur valence, « Pas d'avis », états vides et indisponibles.
- `avisFiltresRetrait.test.ts`, `FeedbacksPage.filtresActifs.test.tsx` (CX-04) : les huit filtres actifs listés avec leur libellé, retrait un par un (liste affichée et paramètres de la requête), « Tout réinitialiser », agence imposée non retirable, boutons « Retirer le filtre … » rendus par la page.
- `AgencyDecisionKpis.valeurs.test.tsx` (AM-02) : valeurs affichées, contexte, évolution, états vides, ordre de lecture des blocs (garde-fou statique).

## Défaut constaté (non corrigé)
Sur la vue d'ensemble de l'agence, le CSAT et la prise en charge s'affichent avec un **point** décimal (« 61.5 % », « 33.3 % pris en charge ») alors que leurs évolutions (« −16,7 pts ») et la vue siège (« 61,5 % ») utilisent la virgule. Gravité : présentation. Preuve : test `it.fails` dans `AgencyDecisionKpis.valeurs.test.tsx` (réussit tant que le défaut existe, échouera à la correction : retirer alors `.fails`).

## Vérifications
- **Mutations : 25 casses du code, toutes détectées** (CSAT, filtre d'organisation, agences désactivées, valence des critiques, période précédente, arrondi des pourcentages, définition des critiques, filtre de gravité inversé, organisation, thème, borne de fin, tri, discordance, agence, période, accès…). Deux ont d'abord révélé des trous du jeu (avis sans analyse absent) : corrigés.
- API **1 984 réussis / 6 ignorés** (1 918 + 66 nouveaux), dashboard **467** (421 + 46), `tsc --noEmit` OK. Durée ajoutée : ≈ 11 s côté API, < 1 s de tests côté dashboard.

## Non vérifié
PostgreSQL (SQLite uniquement), rendu dans un navigateur, délais, critères visuels (ordre d'affichage, lisibilité).

author: milkclouds
body:
## Summary

This PR checks that vla-eval's **live** mode reproduces the RTC paper's **sync**, step-counted-delay protocol on Kinetix (arXiv:2506.07339, Fig. 5). There is no core change.

**Code**
- `model_servers/rtc.py`: the server is now `KinetixRTCServer(DaemonModelServer)`.
  - It imports the official `FlowPolicy.action` / `realtime_action` / `bid_action`; nothing is reimplemented.
  - It runs `eval_flow.py`'s chunk schedule (inference every `horizon` steps, the previous chunk covering `delay` steps, chunk 0 exempt).
  - Each observation gets its step's slot: `reply` in sync, `publish` in live. The step is the benchmark's `env_step`.
  - Latency is set by `latency`: `steps`, `wall` = (d−½)/hz, or `wall_exact`. It is slept in the episode task, never on the model thread.
  - Each step's intended action and chunk index/age go to `StepRecorder`.
  - Warm-up happens in `reset_episodes`, and the server uses `row.step` / `admitted_at`, so it is already compatible with the #97 cleanup.
- `benchmarks/kinetix`:
  - **`start_on_first_action`** (default true): a hold before the first policy action does not step the env. Kinetix's sim t=0 is an artifact, and the first action "releases the scene". Pre-start ticks are recorded.
  - The **hold is zero**. Motors take a velocity target and are off at 0; thrusters take a force. Zero is Kinetix's `noop_action`.
  - Per step, it records the applied action and its wall time.
  - `step()` is pre-compiled, so no live tick stalls on JIT.
  - Its specs now match what it sends.
- Configs: `rtc/{naive,rtc,rtc_hard,bid}.yaml` use `bc/31` (BID weak `bc/7`). The Kinetix README now says 12 tasks.
- Reproduction report: `docs/reproductions/rtc.md`. Data are in `docs/reproductions/data/rtc-kinetix/`, with `ref_eval.py` (arms R/R′: the official script, optionally scored like v3) and `report.py` (`analyze` one recording DB; `tables` regenerates every table in the doc).
- No host tests: the server is model code, and host `tests/` is for model-independent harness logic. The chunk schedule is validated by the real C-vs-R′ and L-vs-C runs.
- Size vs `main`: `src/` +329/−278, configs +29/−13, docs +247/−10, scripts +407, data +987 (31 files).

**Results** (paper Fig. 5 layout: solve rate averaged over the 12 levels, by method and inference delay d, execution horizon s = max(d, 1))

Fig. 5 is a plot; its values are read from the vector PDF (±0.003). R is the official `eval_flow.py` run by us (2048 rollouts per level).

*Paper metric* — each cell is **Fig. 5 / R**:

| method | d=0 | d=1 | d=2 | d=3 | d=4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTC | .922 / .922 | .893 / .896 | .843 / .847 | .747 / .743 | .618 / .612 |
| RTC (hard) | .916 / .917 | .849 / .844 | .817 / .817 | .732 / .732 | .619 / .612 |
| BID | .921 / .916 | .877 / .883 | .801 / .817 | .673 / .692 | .552 / .558 |
| naive | .915 / .916 | .753 / .754 | .708 / .709 | .584 / .585 | .493 / .490 |

*Kinetix v3 success metric* (vla-eval pins Kinetix v3, which reads success differently, see below) — each cell is **R′ / C / L**: R′ = the official script scored like v3, C = vla-eval sync (delay counted in steps, 2048/level), L = vla-eval live (10 Hz wall clock, injected latency (d − ½)/10 s, 512/level). `*` = a cell failing a pre-registered criterion against R′.

| method | d=0 | d=1 | d=2 | d=3 | d=4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTC | .967 / .963\* / .965 | .940 / .937 / .937 | .887 / .882 / .881 | .781 / .779 / .787 | .642 / .640 / .633 |
| RTC (hard) | .961 / .956\* / — | .890 / .890 / — | .857 / .853 / — | .770 / .765 / — | .643 / .637 / — |
| BID | .965 / — / — | .927 / — / — | .858 / — / — | .729 / — / — | .585 / — / — |
| naive | .961 / .955\* / .957 | .795 / .804\* / .807\* | .746 / .748 / .751 | .613 / .612 / .605 | .515 / .513 / .516 |

Reading it: R reproduces Fig. 5 (≤ 0.7 pp; BID ≤ 1.9 pp). C and L both track R′, and L tracks C on all 10 live conditions (\|diff\| ≤ 0.84 pp; criteria: the level-average difference within its 95% CI, and at most 2 of 12 levels outside their per-level CI). The `*` cells are either d = 0 averages near the ceiling (CI about ±0.3 pp) or naive d = 1, which is the trampoline level only (+15–17 pp in both C and L, env-side). Per-condition CIs, per-level tables and the s sweep are in `docs/reproductions/rtc.md`.

- **Kinetix v3 vs `cf7453e`.** The two read a step's `GoalR` from different frame-skip substeps: v3 from the first terminal substep, `cf7453e` from the last. The physics is identical. R′ is the official script with v3's reading of success; it is about 4 pp above the paper's metric.
- **Failures.** The C failures are d = 0 averages near the ceiling (CI about ±0.3 pp) and trampoline at naive d = 1. That cell is +15 to +17 pp in both C and L, so it is env-side; it is the open item.
- **Live instruments.** Effective delay = d for ≥ 99.96% of boundaries. Stale ticks ≤ 0.003%. One pre-start tick per episode. In 0.2–1.6% of episodes one env step exceeds Δt/2 (node jitter).
- **Gated start.** An earlier sync check that replayed one zero-action step before step 0 (instead of gating) was run and dropped.

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the relevant contributing guide
- [x] `make check` passes (ruff + ty)
- [x] `make test` passes (pytest)
- [x] Smoke-tested affected configs (Charliecloud Kinetix image with `--dev`, CPU servers; sync and live at head)
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation

Commands run:
```
vla-eval serve -c configs/model_servers/rtc/rtc.yaml --arg delay=2 --arg horizon=2 --arg latency=wall ...
vla-eval run -c configs/benchmarks/kinetix/realtime.yaml --runtime charliecloud --dev --render cpu --shard-id i --num-shards 48
vla-eval run -c configs/benchmarks/kinetix/eval.yaml --runtime charliecloud --dev --render cpu --shard-id i --num-shards 40
```

body:
## P0 #1209 · QA Client A sintético, compactación reversible de bootstrap (v2)

**Source SHA de candidatura:** `388f647752ce00c4e7bd21f72245dd4248310a49`. Base Canary `c4d00aaf268ffa031bad2a0c2a39196fa8fa53eb`. Sin cambios Supabase PROD ni fusiones.

### Historial del fallo detectado y corrección
La primera migración QA `20261031213500` fue aplicada y probada con flag, pero la E2E real de Device #41257767683 falló: **Client A recibió cero sesiones en el bootstrap HTTP**. Causa identificada: la función externa `public.iberfit_bootstrap_v26()` filtraba las referencias `{id}` al exigir un `status` de publicación, aunque la función interna `..._rc29()` había verificado el canon. Canary Policy #41257767646 falló correctamente por dependencia Device. Se **apagó inmediatamente el flag** para restaurar el comportamiento original.

Segunda migración QA `20261101001000_p0_free_qa_compact_session_status_outer_parity_v2.sql` aplicada **con flag apagado y guard de hash**. El candidato devuelve `{id,status}` para sesiones publicadas; la función externa conserva sus controles de visibilidad y la proyección de seguridad sigue aplicándose. Las ejecuciones mantienen `{id}` dentro de la función interna (la función externa incorpora solo las propiedades vacías seguras). **No se alteró** `public.iberfit_bootstrap_v26()`, RLS, JWT, grants, WebAuthn ni datos de las tablas. Se reactivó flag QA solo tras verificar hash exacto de función `a8bf53fd05478bb2face12edc642dccc`; PROD mantiene original `a5c997a2c263357a99caacd90524291c`.

### Garantías
- Activación afecta **solo QA + rol Cliente + QA Client A con email sintético + flag historial previo y nuevo**; Coach, Admin, Cliente B y PROD mantienen rutas anteriores.
- Se exige equivalencia por entidad canónica, id, cliente, revisión y cuerpo JSON; sesiones deben ser visibles/publicadas; fallback proyección original si falta canon.
- Se conserva `m26Entities`, `results`, `feedback` y Progreso previo a carga bajo demanda. La prueba de dispositivo valida ahora el **HTTP final tras la función externa** y que cada referencia tiene entidad canónica correspondiente.
- Migraciones v1/v2 con rollbacks de hash exacto. En fallo apagar `supabase/qa-rollouts/20261031213500_p0_free_qa_legacy_compact_refs_v1.disable.sql` (un solo flag, sin pérdida de datos), luego revertir v2→v1→base si procede.
- El ahorro estimado de la primera simulación de la función interna **NO equivale al Egress real**; contrastar cuerpo HTTP post-proyección y Billing/Usage Free para declarar el cierre.

### Gates de esta versión
Fast Lane `41267561200` SUCCESS; resto de CI, Policy, Device, QA Real Write, Audit y WebAuthn deben terminar SUCCESS para el **HEAD exacto**. **NO MERGE** con un gate rojo, pendiente o no ejecutado. No repetir pruebas separadas si las workflows ya hacen la cobertura.

Issue #1209 permanece OPEN hasta verificar ahorro real y cuota Free de la organización.

author: terudoru
body:
#4 の上に積んだ PR です。Google の追加審査がいらない範囲（`drive.appdata` と、使い始めるときにだけ求める `drive.file`）で、スター以外の同期、同期先へのバックアップ、授業資料の Google ドライブ保存を追加します。#3 → #4 → この PR の順にマージしてください。

## 追加した機能
- **スター以外の同期**：お気に入り、設定、レポート下書き、通知済みの締切を、スターと同じ暗号化・同じ1回の同期で共有します。
  - 設定は端末に依存しないものだけです（機能のオン・オフ、通知、除外キーワード、カレンダー設定）。ログイン情報、二段階認証、保存先、保存方法、表示モード、スター機能のオン・オフは同期しません。
  - 下書きは学情のページを開いている間だけ読み書きします。
  - 設定画面の「同期する項目」で、項目ごとにオン・オフできます。
- **同期先への暗号化バックアップ**：端末ごとに最新の1件を置きます。自動は1日1回までで、手動のバックアップと復元もできます。端末固有の設定やファイルの保存先は含めません。
- **授業資料を Google ドライブに保存**：ダウンロードした資料を「More Better Gakujo/科目名/」に保存します。
  - 権限は `drive.file` で、アプリが作ったファイルしか触れません。
  - 名前と内容（MD5）が同じファイルは保存を省きます。
  - Android の `content://` のファイルは、少しずつ読みながら送ります。
- **無料枠の保証**：端末ごとに直近24時間の Drive API の利用量を数えます。
  - 自動の処理は1.5万ユニット、手動を含めた全体は2.5万ユニットを上限にし、1回1回の通信の前に確かめます。
  - 起動時の同期を0〜90秒にばらします。
  - これで、毎日上限まで使う端末でも約1.6万台まで、1日の無料枠（4億ユニット）に収まります。

## 安全性とデータの正確さ
- 取り込みは、端末内の内容が読み込んだときから変わっていない場合だけ書き込みます。下書きは全部書くか、何も書かないかのどちらかです。編集中のフォームの下書きは、取り込みを見送ります。
- 取り込みが見送られたら、時間を置いて再試行します（30秒から最大10分）。
- お気に入りの上限30件を全端末で共有し、押し出された分が削除として広がらないようにしました。
- バックアップからの復元は、スターと同じく「追加・上書き」です。「復元された」扱いにするのは、バックアップに実際に含まれるデータと項目だけです。復元後に消したものは、ちゃんと削除されます。取り出しから復元までは、アカウントに結び付けています。
- Google ドライブへの保存待ちの資料は、元の Google アカウントに結び付けています。

## 確認したこと
- Codex による独立したレビューを、機能全体で15巡、無料枠の仕組みで3巡行いました。最終巡は中以上の問題なしです。
- `flutter analyze lib test`：指摘なし
- `flutter test`：課題通知テスト1件を除いてすべて成功。この1件は日付が書き込まれたテストで、別ブランチ `fix/assignment-retention-test-date` で修正済みです。
- `flutter build windows --release`、`flutter build apk --debug`：成功

## 未確認のこと・既知の制約
- 実際の Google アカウントでの動作。OAuth クライアントの登録とテストユーザーの設定が必要です。
- macOS/iOS のビルド、Android 実機での `content://` の読み取り
- 端末の時計を24時間以上進めると、直近の利用分が数えられなくなります。クライアントIDは公開されるため、意図的な使い込みはもともと端末側では防げません。最後の守りは Google Cloud 側の設定（課金アカウントをつながない、割り当ての上限を設定する）で、設計書に記載しています。

body:
This change lets `diff`, `fmt` and `merge` read a template from stdin when the file name is `-`. Behavior does not change for commands without `-`.

Closes #71. Based on aws-cloudformation/rain#698 by @stilvoid, which answers aws-cloudformation/rain#694 by @dothomson. The commit credits @stilvoid as a co-author.

```
git show main:./template.yaml | cfnrain diff - template.yaml
```

## Decisions

None. The scope is the one in the issue: `diff`, `fmt` and `merge`. `tree`, `forecast` and `deploy` do not change.

## What the change does

- `cft/parse/parse.go`: a new function, `FileOrReader`, reads the given reader when the name is `-` and calls `parse.File` otherwise. `parse.File` does not change.
- `internal/cmd/stdin.go`: a new argument check, `StdinOnce`. A command can read stdin once, so a second `-` is an error.
- `diff`, `merge`: use `FileOrReader` and `StdinOnce`.
- `fmt`: `-` goes to the existing stdin code. `fmt -w -` stops with an error before it writes a file. With no file name and piped input, `fmt` reads stdin as before.
- The help text and the `diff`, `fmt` and `merge` pages describe `-`. To give a real file named `-`, use `./-`.

Changes from upstream aws-cloudformation/rain#698:

- Upstream changed `parse.File` to handle `-`. `tree`, `forecast` and module loading in `pkg` also call `parse.File`, so that change would add `-` to them too. This change adds a separate function.
- Upstream changed `deploy`, `forecast` and `tree`, and rewrote the branch in `fmt` for no arguments. This change leaves them out.
- The check for a second `-` is new.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| `diff`, `fmt` and `merge` accept `-` as a template file name and read stdin | Met: tests in each package, and a pipe into the built binary |
| Commands without `-` work as before | Met: the existing tests pass |
| The command pages in `docs/commands/` describe `-` | Met |

## Still to do

The audit found these bugs on `main`. This change does not cause them, and does not fix them:

1. `fmt` with no arguments and no piped input prints `CAKES`, then the help, then panics with a nil argument. The `CAKES` line is a leftover at `internal/cmd/fmt/fmt.go:152`.
2. `merge` panics with "assignment to entry in nil map" when one template is empty.
3. `diff` names the left file in the error for the right file.

## Verification

- The new tests fail before the change and pass after it.
- `go build ./cmd/cfnrain`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `staticcheck ./...` pass. `TestEveryCommandIsDocumented` passes.
- `git show HEAD:test/templates/success.template | cfnrain diff - test/templates/failure.template` prints the expected diff.
- `cfnrain diff - -` stops with `"-" (stdin) can be given only once`.
- Two Codex audit rounds approved the change. One finding, test cleanup, is fixed.
- Not run: the docs site build, and a check on Windows.

author: kallmek3nny
body:
## Summary

- `ios27-loader` now enters a Landlock domain with no rules before it opens the sealed launch payload. Depending on the ABI the kernel reports, the ruleset handles every filesystem right through `IOCTL_DEV` (ABI 5), TCP bind and connect (ABI 4), and the abstract UNIX socket and signal scopes (ABI 6). After enforcement the loader confirms that opening `/` fails with `EACCES`.
- `ENOSYS` or `EOPNOTSUPP` from the version query skips the domain, following the kernel's documented best-effort pattern. The mandatory seccomp filter still applies before guest entry. Any other Landlock failure is a loader setup error.
- `contained-process-supervisor` now execs the real `ios27-loader` build output from a separate launcher and injects seccomp answers. The cases cover enforcement, the skip for absent or disabled Landlock, `create_ruleset` and `restrict_self` failures, and a faked successful `restrict_self` that the probe catches.
- `docs/exec-guest-loader.md` documents the new step and its limits.

## Verification

- Local WSL2 x86_64 (Linux 6.18, Landlock ABI 7): the warnings-as-errors build succeeds and 18/18 CTest suites pass. The supervisor test reports the deny-all domain as enforced and probed.
- Native ARM64: pending CI on this PR.
- Not verified: Android kernels, Android app seccomp policy, or any Galaxy S25+ device.

## Scope

Trusted-fixture failure containment only. This is not a sandbox for untrusted Mach-O code, and it does not complete any capability gate.

author: lidge-jun
body:
Follow-up to #176 (error `disposition`), from its final review. #176 never reported `not_delivered`/`safe` when input could have been sent, but several paths that provably sent nothing reported `delivered_unverified`/`unsafe` or `unknown`/`unknown`, which pushes a model away from a harmless retry.

**Behavior after this change**
- `run_steps`: an action step whose call the registry refused before dispatch (app scope `outside_scope` / `foreground_not_allowed`, capture scope, consent, `session_ended`, `desktop_busy`, …) carries the typed `not_delivered` result of that call; the batch counts an action as delivered only when its call was not typed `not_delivered`. A batch whose every action was refused before dispatch reports `not_delivered`/`safe`; any dispatched action still makes it `delivered_unverified`/`unsafe`.
- `run_script`: the same per-call evidence; a call recorded as attempted but never completed (timeout, cancellation, missing history) keeps the conservative `delivery_uncertain`.
- Server and proxy rejections before any provider or daemon call (`permission_denied` from `authorize_tool_call`, `unknown_tool`) are stamped `not_delivered`/`safe` by that boundary itself; a tool's own JSON is still never trusted.
- Contradictory evidence (a `not_delivered` mark on a success or incomplete record) no longer keeps `safe`.
- Unchanged and documented: a step that times out before dispatch still reports `effect: "unverifiable"`, so its batch stays `delivered_unverified`/`unsafe` (the `effect` field's meaning is not changed here).

**Validation** (macOS, `rust/`): `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib` 1491 passed, 1 failed — the known pre-existing parallel flake `the_cached_identity_keeps_refusing_an_app_the_manifest_does_not_grant` (fixed separately); 17 integration suites ok; `cargo test -p cua-driver --test session_capture_scope_test` 2 passed; `cargo test -p cua-driver --bins proxy` 28 passed; clippy (core, contract, cua-driver) `-D warnings` ok; fmt ok. Failing first: `run_steps` and `run_script` scope refusals returned `delivered_unverified`/`unsafe`; server permission / unknown-tool and proxy permission rejections returned `unknown`/`unknown`; a contradictory not-delivered mark kept `safe`.

NOT RUN: Linux/Windows runtime (CI covers unit tests).

author: yuminn-k
body:
`Runner.Run` does not handle signals. A SIGTERM therefore kills the process, so exporters built on `bootstrap`, node_exporter among them, exit with status 143. systemd and Kubernetes count that as a failure on a normal stop (prometheus/node_exporter#2356).

With this change, `Run` catches SIGINT and SIGTERM, calls `Shutdown` on the HTTP server and returns nil, so `main` exits with 0. After the first signal the handler is removed, so a second signal still kills a shutdown that hangs. If the server fails before any signal arrives, `Run` returns the error as before.

This follows the direction in #152: the toolkit handles signals, and the server is shut down with `Shutdown` instead of calling `os.Exit(0)` from the handler (the approach Bogay and hhromic described there, as pushgateway does). The helper, `serveUntilSignal`, is unexported for now. If you'd rather export it for exporters that don't use `bootstrap`, I can move it into `web`.

SIGQUIT is not caught, so it still dumps goroutine stacks as Go does by default.

Fixes #152

@SuperQ @roidelapluie

**Tests**

- `TestRunReturnsNilOnSIGTERM` starts `runWithArgs` on a local port, waits for `/-/healthy`, sends SIGTERM to the test process, and expects `nil` within 5 seconds. It is skipped on Windows.
  - Before the fix, the test binary is killed: `signal: terminated`, `FAIL`.
  - After the fix, it passes.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` passes.
- `go vet ./...` and `GOOS=windows go vet ./bootstrap/` report no issues.
- `make common-lint` (golangci-lint) reports `0 issues`. I ran it with `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.0`, because the pinned golangci-lint binary panics on Go 1.27 even on an unchanged tree.

author: amitmohapatra
body:
## What and why

ADV-5 (backlog, *Adversarial suite*; `advres-01` in #98): `StallGuard` stopped the run after 3 steps in a row in which every call failed (`ERROR_STREAK`), even when each failure was different. A model correcting itself was cut off before its fourth call, which was correct: first a wrong type, then a missing argument, then a made-up tool name, then the right call.

Now the streak stops the run only when a failure in it repeats, meaning the same tool fails with the same error text. Failures that each differ mean the model read each error and changed its call. `max_steps` still bounds that case: LangChain's `ModelCallLimitMiddleware`, 12 by default.

## Challenge the change

1. **Right approach?** Alternatives:
   - Raise `ERROR_STREAK`. That only moves the cut.
   - Drop the streak. A dead tool that fails the same way whatever the arguments would then run to `max_steps`.
   - Chosen: the "same action, same error" signal of OpenHands' `StuckDetector`, which is the published stuck detector of an agent framework. Our repeated-call check (`MAX_REPEATS`) already covers the same call made again. This adds the same *failure* met again, even with different arguments.
   - LangChain has no native equivalent: `ToolCallLimitMiddleware` counts calls, not failures.
2. **Data structure / algorithm.** It is the same backward walk over this invocation's messages as before, plus one set of failure keys (`content_key(tool, error text)`). The cost is O(failing steps), and the walk stops at the first step that did not fail.
3. **Design pattern.** The change is in `_failing` alone; detection stays in one place. It is a separate hunk from #76's change (#76 turns the stop into a last answer), so the two compose. #76 keeps its `FAILING` message, and its tests still hold, because their failures repeat (`odd`, `down`).
4. **Accuracy evidence.** `test_react_parallel.py::test_different_failures_in_a_row_are_a_model_correcting_itself_not_a_stall` (wrong type, missing argument, made-up tool, right call): on main it is ERROR `stopped: every tool call failed in 3 consecutive steps`; now SUCCESS with the tool run once. The existing streak tests, where a failure repeats, still stop: `test_steps_in_which_every_call_failed_stop_the_run` (both files) and `test_a_failing_call_repeated_in_one_step_still_counts_toward_the_error_streak`. The full suite numbers are in the comment below.
5. **Latency, tokens, cost.** A run that recovers makes one more model call (its fourth) instead of failing. A run of differing failures can now use up to `max_steps`.
6. **What can be removed now?** #98's `KNOWN` entry for `advres-01/0` (ADV-5).

author: blackviperxiii-ui
body:
Before: the shell composer was typing only. Voice lived in the cabin, not in the desktop app's chat.

After: the composer has a hold-to-talk mic button (and Ctrl+G while the Chat tab shows). Holding records from the microphone; letting go sends the recording to xAI speech to text, and the words are added to the end of the draft. Nothing is sent until you press Send. The web remote shows no mic, and `transcribe` is not on its command allowlist.

How
- `src-tauri/src/voice.rs`: `transcribe(config_dir, wav)` refuses a recording over 10 MB or 60 s, or one that isn't a PCM WAV, before any request. It then runs the harness egress guard with the chat data class (Offline only refuses with the core note), and POSTs one multipart body (`stt_multipart`) to `stt_url()` through the shared HTTP facade with no redirects and a 60 s cap. The answer is read up to 1 MB and parsed with `parse_stt_text`. An empty transcript is an error. The bearer is the saved xAI key. With no key the note says to add one in Settings → Account; a 401 or 403 says to check it there.
- `GROKHUB_SHELL_STT_URL` points the call at a mock STT server for tests only. It counts only as a plain-http loopback URL (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1], no userinfo); any other value is ignored.
- The raw multipart body goes out with the core facade's `Request::send_bytes` (now on beta).
- `offline_guard.rs`: a GUARDED row for `src-tauri/src/voice.rs`.
- `capabilities.rs`: `voice` for desktops and phones, false elsewhere. The `transcribe` command checks it.
- Linux: the main window's WebKitGTK permission handler allows a microphone-only request (`is-for-audio-device` and not `is-for-video-device`) so `getUserMedia` works; camera and other requests keep the default.
- UI: `ui/src/wav.ts` downsamples to 16 kHz mono and writes a 16-bit PCM WAV; `ui/src/Mic.tsx` is the button and hotkey, with a 60 s auto-stop; notes (mic denied, no mic, the desktop's refusal) show in the chat's existing error line. Chat.tsx gets one line for the button.
- Also: `SlashMenu.test.tsx` and the new mic test needed the new `summonHotkey` and `notifications` settings fields to type-check after beta moved; the SlashMenu change is the same two lines as the open fix for that test, so they merge cleanly.

Run path exercised: the shell crate's tests start a loopback mock STT server and run `transcribe_at` against it; the mock gets the exact multipart body and bearer and answers with words, which come back. The over-cap, too-long, not-WAV and empty recordings are refused with no connection to the mock. Offline only returns the core note. In vitest the full Chat renders with a fake 48 kHz AudioContext: pressing and releasing the mic button sends a 16 kHz WAV with 3200 data bytes to `transcribe` and the draft reads "please open the build log", with no send; Ctrl+G does the same; a denied mic shows the permission note; the web app has no mic.

Local checks: `npm ci && npm run lint && npm test && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build` (35 files, 319 tests pass); shell fmt check, clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` (185 pass; beta's shell crate does not build right now because of the local_engine.rs Fetch::open change, so these ran with that fix applied locally and not committed); `cargo clippy -p grokhub-core --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p grokhub-core` (1614 lib tests and the integration tests pass; after the last beta merge, offline_guard was rerun and passes), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `scripts/ci-guards.sh` and the PII guard pass.

Skipped / not verified: no real microphone or real xAI call here (no display, audio device or key in this environment), so the WebKitGTK permission handler and the Windows WebView2 and macOS mic prompts are not checked in a running app. macOS NSMicrophoneUsageDescription is not added because the bundle config has no macOS section. Phones get the capability, but recording there is not tried.

author: rrpauls
body:
🚨 Severity: MEDIUM
💡 Vulnerability: Checking `path.exists()` before performing tree operations like `shutil.rmtree()` or `shutil.copytree()` left the controller vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS). If the target path was maliciously or accidentally created as a file rather than a directory, these operations would throw an unhandled `NotADirectoryError`, potentially crashing the process.
🎯 Impact: A failure during garbage collection or staging/promotion could block further automated workflows, disrupt evaluations, and lead to persistent controller crashes until operator intervention.
🔧 Fix: Replaced `path.exists()` checks with `path.is_dir()` for expected directory operations. Added fallback `elif path.is_file(): path.unlink()` handling where appropriate to safely remove unexpected files. 
✅ Verification: Ran `python3 -m unittest discover tests` and codebase validation scripts `python3 scripts/validate_*.py` ensuring all logic functions cleanly.

author: deelin221
body:
## Behavior

Home now acts as the main-agent console: its composer and new-session actions always target internal profile `default`, even after viewing another profile. The overview shows recent conversations and project folders across installed profiles, with profile badges and scoped links. All-profile reads do not write session state. The existing profile switcher remains available, and home no longer exposes the selected profile's writable sidebar.

Profiles now have a backend-persisted display-name field, including `default`. Empty names restore the existing localized fallback. Internal IDs, profile directories, configuration, session ownership, authentication, and permissions are unchanged. Aliases are per authenticated user (or instance owner), and badges retain the internal ID to distinguish equal display names.

## Scope

The existing roster and scoped session/project GET APIs provide the overview. The recent window remains 30 days and up to 24 sessions per profile; this is not a complete project archive. Project folders sort by loaded member activity and retain empty folders. Opening a conversation commits its owning profile before navigation. Existing scoped send, rename, and delete APIs remain in use. Failed sources discard cached cards and surface partial-load errors.

Display names are stored in the existing `<Workbench root>/.hermes-workbench/session-organization.sqlite3`, in the additive `profile_display_names` table keyed by `(owner, profile)`. The existing Workbench root resolver applies; no external database or localStorage setting is added. See `docs/profile-display-home.md` for root resolution, behavior, and rollback.

Rollback by reverting this feature commit and rebuilding through the normal release process. Older code ignores the additive table; leave it intact to preserve aliases. Do not delete the shared database, which also contains unrelated session metadata. No deployment, merge, data migration, or production changes were performed.

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:python`, and `pnpm build` passed.
- `pnpm privacy:check`, `pnpm release:verify`, `pnpm history:check`, `pnpm version:check`, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- The complete Playwright browser suite passed using the existing local fixture host and installed Brave Chromium. The focused profile-home test additionally passed project expansion, denied reads, and empty-roster behavior.
- Focused coverage includes backend recreation/persistence, owner isolation, authentication, alias reset, invalid profiles, default create/send with idempotent retry, same-ID project membership, cross-profile open/rename, send/delete profile boundaries, and read-only aggregation.
- Desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 were exercised and visually inspected. The focused flow reported no page or relevant console errors and no mobile horizontal overflow. Browser plugin was unavailable, so repository Playwright was used. Browser fixtures do not exercise a live production Hermes runtime.
- Two existing browser assertions now wait for their actual message fixture/count state, fixing observed render-timing races without changing the assertions.

Developed in an isolated worktree from `origin/main` at `df0737a`; other working trees were not modified.

Продуктовый выбор, исключение безопасности и недостаточные доказательства остаются отдельными исходами. Потраченный бюджет сохраняется при новом HEAD, задаче, восстановлении и settlement.

Публичные REVIEW/FIX команды связывают полный отчёт, PR/автора, epoch, четыре дерева процедур, task occurrence, reservation и одноразовый START. Исполнитель использует приватный проверенный checkout, одну удерживаемую границу процесса и один forward CAS с независимым readback; только подтверждённый результат публикует fix-done. Служебные author/progress/settlement операции сохраняют карантин при ошибке остановки и не запускают модель.

Парная часть A: https://github.com/ivanarama/onebase/pull/2452. Полные SHA согласованной пары и хеши отчётов фиксируются в комментариях ревью. Слияние разрешается только после полной приёмки пары, независимого ревью и всех обязательных проверок.

Проверки: целевые регрессии владения, транспорта, неизменяемой истории и восстановления; opt-in сквозной тест с настоящим Go checker и полными каноническими процедурами, приватным GraphQL peer и реальным локальным CAS. Три сценария — обычный проход, потерянный ответ push и изменение reader перед публикацией. Полный native pytest, пять обязательных CI и свежее независимое совместное ревью требуются для окончательного коммита; результаты старых HEAD их не заменяют.

Рабочие настройки и планировщик не включаются. Положительный native MERGE/TAIL относится к части B; staging, Dashboard и ограниченный пилот — к части C. Owned-process протокол не является OS-песочницей.

The VM emits `PROJECT_LOADED` on `vm.runtime` and never forwards it to `vm`. Four listeners registered on `vm` never ran:

author: qoeop
body:
## Summary

`replay explore`, `replay precheck`, `replay run` and `replay reproduce` opened one writer connection
before the trial and kept it through the containers. After the containers ended, often minutes or hours
later, the seal ran on that connection (`replay/entry.py` `execute` → `execution.seal_capture(..., conn)`),
and so did `ingest_run` and reproduce's checks. `db.write` retries only `CONCURRENT_WRITE`, and nothing
reconnects. A ledger restart while the containers ran therefore left the connection dead, and the seal
failed with `DOLT_SQL_ERROR` (MySQL 2006) even though the service was back. Unplanned restarts count too:
an OOM kill, a Docker Desktop restart. The trial then had a start receipt but no capture. For a
registered grid point, `retryable()` refuses a retry without a sealed capture
(`registration/register.py:353-357`), so the grid point could not be run again.

Change:

- The trial opens on a connection that is closed before the containers start.
- Each later ledger step opens its own connection: the seal (`seal_capture` without a connection already
  did this), a research or validation capture refused for size, the run's ingestion, and reproduce's
  checks.
- `execute` and `seal` no longer take a connection, and `_store_capture_refusal` is folded into its one
  caller.
- No refusal, audit check or stored field changes. An interrupted replay is still sealed as
  `interrupted` or `host_failure`, which is the case `retryable()` was written for.

## Validation

- New Dolt-backed test `test_a_ledger_restart_while_the_containers_run_still_seals_and_stores_the_run`:
  it stops and starts the test Dolt service during the native stage, then expects a passed run and its
  `trial-<id>-execution` bundle. It runs on its own registered grid point (`registration-grid-g`),
  because every other point is consumed by another test.
  - Positive control: with origin/main's `replay/entry.py` and `replay/reproduce.py` the same test fails
    with `DOLT_SQL_ERROR: ... (MySQL error 2006): MySQL server has gone away`.
- `RESEARCH_DOLT_BINARY=<dolt 2.4.2> uv run --frozen python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p 'test_*.py'`:
  730 tests OK, none skipped.
- `uv run --frozen ruff check .`: all checks passed. `uv run --frozen mypy`: no issues in 97 source files.

## Evidence and limitations

- Found while diagnosing the compose deployment's restarts. A read-only ledger query shows 0 of 513
  trials without their execution capture, so the case has not occurred yet. The 10-31 ledger OOM restart
  shows it can.
- Not covered: a connection that drops during `DOLT_COMMIT` itself. That still returns
  `write_status: unknown` with the operation id, as before.
- `deploy/README.md` ("Updating", from #1993): the ledger entry now says a restart interrupts only a replay
  opening or sealing its trial within the restart's seconds, instead of any replay running across it.

author: j2teamnnl
body:
## Summary

- New registry plugin `MemcachedDriverPlugin` over the text protocol, on SwiftNIO the way the Kafka plugin is. Parsing lives in a new PluginKit-free product, `TableProMemcachedCore`: the console parser, an incremental reply reader, the key listing parsers and the grid's browse spec.
- Connection form: host, port `11211`, username and password, SSL through NIOSSL, SSH tunnel and the other port forwards.
- How keys are found: the text protocol has no key listing, so the driver reads `stats settings` at connect. With `lru_crawler yes` (1.4.31 and later, the default) it lists keys with `lru_crawler metadump all` on a short-lived second connection, because a metadump cannot share a connection with other commands. Otherwise, or when the server refuses the metadump, it falls back to `stats items` plus `stats cachedump <slab> 0` per slab class. That list is a capped sample, and the table's comment says so. A listing stops at 1,000,000 keys and the extra connection is closed.
- One `keys` table with the item count from `stats`. Grid columns Key, Value, TTL and Flags. Values come from one multi-key `get` per 100 rows of the current page. TTL is the metadump or cachedump expiry minus the server's own `time`, empty for no expiry.
- Sorting is by key. Filters apply to Key only (`=`, `!=`, contains, starts with, ends with, IN, NOT IN, regex). A filter on another column is refused with a message, because filtering on Value would read every value.
- Edits: a changed Value or Flags runs `set` with the absolute time the item already expires at, so the save neither extends nor revives it; a TTL alone runs `touch`; a new row runs `set`; a deleted row runs `delete`. Key is immutable, and a key holding a quote is quoted in the statement. A TTL over 30 days is sent as the time it ends, since memcached reads a larger exptime as a Unix time. Truncate runs `flush_all`.
- The editor runs `get`, `gets`, `gat`, `gats`, `set`, `add`, `replace`, `append`, `prepend`, `cas`, `touch`, `delete`, `incr`, `decr`, `flush_all`, `stats`, `version` and `lru_crawler metadump`. Arguments follow the protocol, with the value as the last argument instead of a data block, quoted with `\n`, `\xHH` and similar escapes. Anything else is refused before it reaches the server.
- Query classifier: reads and the reading `stats` forms are safe, stores and `stats reset`, `stats detail on` or `stats sizes_enable` write, `delete` and `flush_all` are destructive.
- Server Dashboard: used memory, items, hit ratio, evictions, connections and uptime from `stats`.
- Registry entry, curated metadata, `DatabaseType.memcached` and the SF Symbol `memorychip` as icon (no brand mark in Simple Icons).

Defaults I picked, open to change:
- Auth uses the text protocol login of a server started with `-Y <auth file>` (1.5.15 and later). The driver sends the credentials only after the server refuses `version` with `CLIENT_ERROR unauthenticated`, so an open server never stores them as an item. SASL is left out: it needs the binary protocol, which memcached marks deprecated, and a SASL server refuses the text commands the key listing needs.
- One table for the whole server, since memcached has no namespaces.
- The listing cap is 1,000,000 keys.

Docs: TableProApp/docs#156

## Test plan

- `swift test --filter TableProMemcachedCoreTests`: the console parser and its quoting round trip (UTF-8 and raw bytes), the reply reader fed in pieces (a CRLF inside a value, the line limit, every error line), metadump and cachedump lines, slab classes, the browse spec's paging, sorting and every key comparison, and the write statements.
- Hosted: `QueryClassifierHardeningTests` (Memcached tiers), `MemcachedDashboardProviderTests`, and Memcached added to the factory, gate, listing, base query, parameter detection and type count suites. `DatabaseTypeTests` counts the new type.
- Live: `apple/scripts/probes/check-memcached.sh` runs the plugin's own sources against `memcached` 1.6.45 and 1.4.39 in Docker through an SSH tunnel. Every check passes on 1.6.45 (metadump), 1.4.39 (crawler off, cachedump fallback) and 1.6.45 with an auth file (no credentials and a wrong password fail with their own messages): paging with offsets, sort, every filter, TTLs, flags, escaped and quoted keys and values, `set`, `touch`, `delete`, insert, a value edit that keeps the expiry, `incr`, `add` on an existing key, `stats`, `stats reset`, `stats cachedump` and `lru_crawler metadump`. A silent endpoint fails with a timeout. A key touched just before a metadump is sometimes missing from that one walk; the server moves items between LRU segments during the crawl, so the docs say a listing is not a snapshot.
- `xcodebuild -scheme MemcachedDriverPlugin build` succeeds. The app target compiles; the hosted test bundle did not finish locally because the disk filled, so CI runs those suites.

Fixes #2483

author: gautam-achieveai
body:
Follow-up to #899. Its last review round asked for one more credential-masking fix. The fix was pushed after #899 was merged, so it never reached main.

## Problem
`judge close` masks credentials in a failed git step's error. After #899 it masked only the `access_token`, `token` and `sig` query values. A `--remote` URL carrying `key`, `signature`, `password`, `client_secret` or `X-Amz-Signature` still printed that value in a failed round discovery.

## Change
- `masked()` in `JudgeSandbox.py` now hides the value of any query parameter whose name holds `token`, `key`, `sig`, `secret`, `password` or `credential`.
  - This also covers names such as `X-Amz-Credential` and `api_key`, so the list no longer grows one name at a time.
  - Harmless parameters such as `ref` and `page` stay visible.
- README describes the rule.

## Tests
- `Close_prepare_fails_on_a_failed_round_discovery_without_printing_remote_credentials`: the remote now carries all seven names.
  - It asserts `?access_token=***&sig=***&key=***&signature=***&password=***&client_secret=***&X-Amz-Signature=***`.
  - It asserts no fake value reaches the error.
  - With the old name list, `key=FAKE-KEY-3333` leaks and the test fails.
  - The test runs only on the Linux leg: its failing transport is a `sh` script.
- `--filter ReviewdJudgeClose` on Windows: 117 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped (this test is one of the two).

author: ceoguy
body:
Closes the remaining agent-wallet security findings on `main`. The agent wallet stays **disabled by default** (`CHAINGPT_AGENT_WALLET_ENABLED`, #119); nothing here re-enables it.

**Changes (one commit each)**
- **Dashboard form save no longer drops limits.** The Form editor sends `mode=form`; the server merges only the form's own fields over the saved policy. Daily caps and the asset/Solana/Tron/ERC-4337 sections survive, and a form save cannot remove them. A save from a page whose policy changed meanwhile (e.g. kill switch engaged elsewhere) is refused. The raw JSON editor still replaces the whole policy.
- **Plan step operationIds are content-derived.** They come from the plan name + step, not the random `planId`, so deleting and re-saving a finished plan maps onto operations the signer has already recorded and refuses to sign again.
- **Admin token never enters the model context.** `serve_ui` writes the token only to its 0600 file (exclusive temp file + rename, never follows a symlink) and refuses to start if the file can't be written.
- **`.env` is credentials-only.** A working-directory `.env` can set API keys only. Keystore/policy/ledger/plan paths, the passphrase, `CHAINGPT_DISABLE_KEYCHAIN` and RPC URLs come from the real launch environment; ignored keys are warned on stderr.
- **Mainnet guard** asks for any `chaingpt_agent_wallet_*sign_and_send` (future chains included); Tron prompts show the TRX/TRC-20 amount, token and recipient.
- Docs (CHANGELOG, README, SECURITY.md, wallet-safety, agent-wallet skill) updated; `dist/` rebuilt.

**Compatibility:** RPC URLs and path overrides placed in a project `.env` are now ignored; set them in the MCP server launch environment.

**Validation (local; Actions disabled)**
- `scripts/test-all.sh --fast`: all 7 layers pass. MCP 725 tests (under load avg ~80, a real-solc compile test and one mock-server endpoint test timed out; both pass alone), mock 61, boot smoke 142 tools with a planted `.env`.
- New regression tests fail on `main` and pass here: form-save merge + stale-page refusal, token not in tool output + file mode + symlink + fail-closed start, delete/re-save operationId, `.env` filter, guard catch-all + Tron prompt. Independent review findings addressed in the last commit.
- Internal reproduction scripts re-run against this build with the wallet explicitly enabled: token transfer / unlimited approve / transferFrom / increaseAllowance refused under a loosened policy; Tron guard asks; concurrent sends limited to one; planted `.env` ignored; form save keeps caps; journaled plan re-runs refused.

**Known limit (unchanged, documented):** the signer runs as the same OS user as the agent. An agent with shell/file access can still read the token file, edit `policy.json`, or use a passphrase present in its environment. Closing that requires a separately isolated signer process; until then the wallet remains off by default.

author: ssebowadisan
body:
## What a person sees

**Before:** on a booted machine (image of `c4e6cee0`, 2026-11-01), pressing Enter on "files" in the alo Bar started Dolphin — the log said so — and nothing appeared. The window had opened *behind* alo's terminal, at the bottom of the pile, without the keyboard. Only Super+Tab showed it (`fifteenth-26b` versus `26e`).

**Now:** the first window of an application the person starts — from the Dock, the alo Bar, or a shortcut — comes in front of everything and takes the keyboard. A dialog opened by the application the person is using (a new window of the application holding the keyboard) does the same.

**What does not move:** a window nobody asked for, a window of an application in the background, an application the *agent* opened (only the person's own road changes what is in front, as #1044 decided), and a start that failed. If the person goes to another window before the new one arrives, it opens behind and does not pull them away.

This makes an existing promise true, because `docs/design/where-a-new-window-opens.md` rule 8 already says *a person-initiated opening activates the new window; background applications and alo must not steal focus*, and the owner's 2026-10-31 decision is *the window you go to comes in front*.

## How

- `Surfaces::commit` notes each window the moment it first gets a picture (`just_mapped`).
- `Server::start_what_was_asked_for` remembers the person's successful starts (not the agent's).
- Once a frame `crate::direct_desktop` calls `Server::what_the_person_opened_comes_in_front`, which brings in front the windows that match, through the same `the_person_goes_to_this_window` a Dock press uses.
- New file `crates/alo-shell/src/a_window_the_person_opened.rs`.

## Checks

**Run on every build (CI):**
- `crates/alo-shell/tests/a_window_the_person_opened` (six tests on real Wayland client connections): the started application comes in front with the keyboard and the applications move in front of alo's own windows; a second window of the same application does not; a window nobody asked for, a refused start, and a background application's dialog stay behind with no keyboard; a dialog of the focused application comes in front with the keyboard.
- `src/a_window_the_person_opened_tests.rs`: the agent's start is not waited for, a refused start is not, going elsewhere forgets, and the list has a bound.

**Run once, by hand:** the cheap local check (fmt, workspace clippy, workspace rustdoc, alo-shell tests). The results are in the task report.

**Not checked on a booted machine.** The match is by the identifier the application was started under, compared with the window's `app_id`. Dolphin's Flatpak window says `org.kde.dolphin`, which matches. An application whose window gives a different name from its menu entry will still open behind, as before.

body:
## Summary
The `/health` endpoint's Redis probe previously attempted to initialize a Redis client using `settings.redis_host` and `settings.redis_port`. Because `Settings` in `core/config.py` only defines `redis_url`, accessing these nonexistent attributes raised an `AttributeError`. The route's `except Exception` block caught the error and marked Redis as `unhealthy`, returning an HTTP 503 error even when Redis was running and reachable. This PR constructs the Redis client via `redis.Redis.from_url(settings.redis_url, decode_responses=True)` so that the health check reads the configured URL and accurately reports connectivity status.

## Issue
Closes #62

## Changes
- In `api/routes/health.py`: replaced `redis.Redis(host=settings.redis_host, port=settings.redis_port, db=0, decode_responses=True)` with `redis.Redis.from_url(settings.redis_url, decode_responses=True)`.
- In `pyproject.toml`: removed the `attr-defined` error suppression for `api.routes.health` and updated the inline comment to reflect that issue #62 is resolved (retaining `call-overload` and `index` for #61).
- In `tests/unit/test_health_redis.py`: added regression tests covering both the healthy path (client initialized with `settings.redis_url`, reporting healthy) and the error path (raising 503 when connection fails).

author: ronsse
body:
## What changed

Adds `trellis classify label-candidates`, a read-only scan that reports documents a person may want to label. It counts matches of four plain, deterministic rules in each document's text and reports **the document id, the rule that fired and a count**:

- `email_address`: an email-address shape
- `phone_number`: a US/Canada number with separators, e.g. `(212) 555-0123`
- `us_ssn_shape`: a 3-2-4 digit SSN/ITIN shape (shape only, not a validity check)
- `card_number_luhn`: a 13-19 digit run that passes the Luhn check

The rules live in one tuple, `LABEL_RULES` in `src/trellis/classify/label_proposer.py`, each with a match test and a near-miss test. `--limit` (default 5000) and `--page-size` bound the scan; `--format json` is supported, and the exit code does not depend on `--format`.

Properties, each covered by a test:

- **It never prints the matched value.** No excerpt, no text around a match, no matched string, in JSON, text, stderr or logs; a finding has exactly three fields, and the scan logs counts only. A sentinel-value test checks stdout, stderr and captured logs, and the same checks are run against deliberately defective subjects (a finding that quotes the value or the surrounding text, a leak on stderr, a leak in a log line) to show they can fail.
- **It writes nothing.** No label, tag, event or queue row. A test snapshots documents, event and trace counts, graph node and edge counts, the vector count and the data directory's file list before and after a run, in both formats, and fails against planted writes. The owner applies a label through the existing route, `trellis curate classify-sensitivity <doc_id> --sensitivity <level>`.
- **Already-labelled documents are skipped and counted** (any `data_classification` record, including a malformed one). Chunk rows are not read, since a chunk takes its parent's label. Documents with no text are counted separately.
- **The report says whether it stopped at the limit.** `stopped_at_limit` is true only if more documents followed the last one read; the status is then `partial` and the command still exits 0, as `classify backfill` does.
- **A miss proves nothing and this is not a PII guarantee.** Both output formats, the docs and the module docstring say so. The rules over-report (an asset named `icon@2x.png` reads as an email address; a 13-digit millisecond timestamp can pass the Luhn check) and miss shapes with no fixed form. Those over-reports and two known misses are pinned in tests so the docs stay true. Precision on a real store has not been measured.

It lives under `classify` because that group already holds the propose-for-a-human commands (`tag-candidates`, `domain-candidates`) and the document-scan conventions, while `curate` is where governed writes happen and this makes none. The group's other commands tag content, whereas the label this points at is the access label (`DataClassification`), so the command help and docs say a finding is a prompt to run `classify-sensitivity`, not a content tag.

Rich output follows `tests/unit/test_rich_id_markup_rule.py` (`build_console`, ids passed through `escape`); a test prints an id containing `[draft]` and `:book:` and finds it verbatim.

Fixtures use fake values only (`example.com`, 555-01xx numbers, published test card numbers).

## Left out on purpose

- No PII/PHI tag semantics. `regulatory_tags` is neither read nor written and no sensitivity floor is implied for a finding; that is a separate decision.
- No auto-apply, no queue, no event emission.
- No LLM and no new dependency.
- Nothing under `src/trellis/retrieve/` changed (checked with `git diff origin/main --stat -- src/trellis/retrieve`: empty).
- Rules for medical or other content with no fixed shape, and for names.

## Tests

- New: 62 library tests and 27 CLI tests, all passing.
- With the new tests, every `tests/unit/test_*_rule.py` (35 files), `tests/unit/mcp/test_exception_text_roster.py`, `tests/unit/classify/`, `tests/unit/cli/test_classify_*.py` and `tests/unit/test_claude_md_budget.py`: 1072 passed, run with the markers `make test` deselects. Ten further test files that read the agent guide or changelog: 402 passed.
- The full unit suite was not run locally for this PR.
- Planted defects, each reverted afterwards, each making the intended tests fail: a value leaked into a finding, to stderr, and into a log line; a label written back from inside the scan loop; truncation always reported; labelled documents not skipped; the exit code depending on `--format`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` on the changed files, and `mypy src/` over the whole tree (3.11): clean.
