author: wkentaro
body:
## Summary

AI Assist and AI text prompts now run OSAM in a spawned child process. Before, they ran on the UI thread, so a slow device froze the window (about 80 s per encode on Windows' software WebGPU renderer) and a native crash took the app down with unsaved Shapes.

```diff
 Canvas / MainWindow
-  AiAssistSession.request()          # runs OSAM on the UI thread
-  propose_shapes(...)
+  OsamWorker.submit(channel, job, InferenceRequest)
+    sender thread  --pipe-->  serve() in child process  (OSAM, image cache)
+    receiver thread <--pipe--
+    QTimer poll (20 ms) -> finished(job, annotations) | failed(job, message)
                           (held while any modal dialog is open)
+  _take_ai_job(job)                  # drop results that no longer apply
+  propose_shapes(annotations=...)
```

What a result applies to travels with its job:

```text
preview   dropped if the points moved since it was sent
finalize  dropped if the draft was cancelled or the image changed
text      dropped if the image changed; also held while a Shape is drawn or the
          pointer is held, then appended as one Undo step
```

- A newer preview replaces one that has not started.
- The canvas ignores input while an AI Shape is in flight, so the draft stays as sent.
- A crash or a 600 s hang fails the job and restarts the worker on the next request.
- The worker keeps the last image, so a repeated preview sends only its points. AI Assist and the text prompt share one image id, so they share the cached embedding.
- Deleting a model stops the worker so its files can be removed.

This is the first PR of a stack. Later PRs add CPU fallback when the GPU worker fails, an Auto/CPU device Setting, and a real-model artifact smoke test.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on `main`, `AiAssistSession.request()` calls `session.run()` on the UI thread, and no test covers a crashed or hung model.
  **After:** new worker tests run a scripted child process:

  ```text
  tests/unit/_automation/_osam_worker_test.py
    sends an image once per image id                      passed
    newer submit replaces a waiting one on its channel    passed
    model error keeps the worker                          passed
    crash  -> "AI worker exited with code 3", restarts    passed
    hang   -> "AI inference timed out after 1 s"          passed
    stall mid-response -> timed out, UI never blocks      passed (POSIX only; Windows pipes send whole messages)
    submit returns before a late worker reads 12 MB       passed
    holds results while a modal dialog is open            passed
    release fails the jobs it drops                       passed
  ```

- Interaction tests that fail with their fix disabled:
  - `test_text_result_waits_for_a_drag` (Undo restored a half-moved Shape)
  - `test_text_result_waits_for_a_held_vertex` (a resize was lost)
  - `test_text_result_keeps_the_selection_editable` (Edit Label did nothing)
  - `test_text_result_waits_for_the_draft`
  - `test_text_result_waits_for_the_label_dialog`
  - `test_ai_finalize_cancels_its_draft_when_the_pixmap_changes`
  - `test_ai_finalize_ignores_undo_last_point`
  - `test_ai_finalize_reports_drawing_and_unblocks_when_its_draft_drops`
  - `test_ai_finalize_*` and `test_ai_preview_drops_a_result_for_old_inputs`
- `pytest tests/e2e/annotation_test.py -m network`: 10 passed, through the real spawned worker with `efficientsam:10m`.
- `just test`: 1913 passed, 11 failed. The 11 failures (`settings_test` eliding, `label_dialog_placeholders_test[ja_JP]`, `_settings_dialog_test` Enter key) fail the same way on `main` in this environment.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting restores in-process inference. No file format or Setting changes.

**Blast Radius:** AI-features

Every AI Assist and AI text prompt path changes. Known limits:

- A cancelled AI Shape still runs to completion in the worker before the next job starts.
- Deleting a model during an in-flight AI Shape shows "AI inference failed: AI worker stopped".
- The UI shows no busy cursor while an AI Shape is pending.
- The first request on a fresh worker pays the spawn and model load cost again after a crash.

Codex review ran 3 rounds. All findings were fixed: GUI blocking on a pipe write, GUI blocking on a partial response, a text result dropping the draft, a text result landing under the label dialog, and Undo re-enabled mid-draw. PR review round 1 found that a brightness change during an AI Shape left a broken draft; the draft is now cancelled. A Windows VM review found a text result landing mid-drag split the drag's Undo step. That was the fourth case of one cause, so a text result now waits until the canvas is idle, which replaced the earlier per-case fixes. A second VM review found a result landing between press and first move lost a resize; the canvas now counts a held pointer as busy. PR review then found a result cleared the Label List selection but not the canvas's, so Edit Label did nothing; the Label List now resyncs from the canvas. A later review found an AI Shape finishing under a label edit reopened the label dialog; the worker now holds every result while a modal dialog is open, which replaced the text path's own dialog flag. The next review found the Undo Last Point action changed a pending AI Shape's draft; it is now ignored while the AI Shape is pending. The next found a Ctrl+click AI Shape left Undo enabled, and Undo then left every click blocked; the canvas now reports drawing when an AI Shape starts, and the pending state follows the draft, so dropping the draft unblocks input. No findings rejected or left open.

author: luigimonsoft
body:
## What
Port both upstream point-coordinate positional embeddings to MLX as part of #18.

## Why
The denoiser and decoders use distinct frequency schedules and output layouts for 3D positions. Their behavior must match the reference before integration.

## How
Generate each original frequency schedule from configuration, apply sine/cosine in the upstream order, reshape and zero-pad when required. For tested FP32/FP16 inputs, the denoiser version produces FP32 and the decoder version follows input dtype. For reduced-precision decoder inputs, scalar multiplication by π uses FP32 before restoring input dtype to match the tested PyTorch behavior. No learned weights or checkpoint loading are introduced.

## Diagram
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[3D coordinates] --> B[Variant-specific frequencies]
    B --> C[Angles]
    C --> D[Sine and cosine]
    D --> E[Reshape and optional zero padding]
```

## How to test
- `IDOL_REFERENCE_SOURCE=<pinned-upstream> IDOL_TEST_MLX_DEVICE=cpu <python> -m unittest discover -s tests -q`: 56 tests passed locally with MLX installed.
- `IDOL_REFERENCE_SOURCE=<pinned-upstream> IDOL_TEST_MLX_DEVICE=gpu <python> -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_layers_mlx.py' -q`: seven tests passed locally with MLX Metal versus PyTorch CPU.
- Synthetic spatial tests cover multiple samples/tokens, padding, extended V1 frequencies, fractional interior V2 frequencies, and FP32/FP16 inputs. V1 and FP32 V2 use atol 1e-5 and rtol 1e-4; FP16 V2 uses atol/rtol 3e-3. These cases do not establish full-model parity.

## Files changed
- `idol_mlx/layers.py`: two spatial embedding variants.
- `tests/test_layers_mlx.py`: upstream PyTorch parity tests.
- `docs/spatial-embeddings.md`, `es/spatial-embeddings.md`: semantics, tolerances and limitations.
- `README.md`, `es/README.md`: current status and documentation links.

## Objectives achieved
- [x] Port denoiser and decoder coordinate embeddings.
- [x] Compare synthetic shape, padding, dtype and numeric behavior on CPU and Metal locally.
- [x] Update English and Spanish documentation.
- [ ] Validate integration and untested shapes/dtypes in real models; issue #18 stays open.

## Español

### Qué y por qué
Este avance del issue #18 adapta a MLX los dos embeddings de coordenadas 3D usados por denoiser y decodificadores.

### Cómo
Cada variante usa sus frecuencias originales, concatena seno y coseno, reorganiza y rellena cuando corresponde. En las entradas FP32/FP16 probadas, la primera produce FP32 y la segunda conserva el tipo de entrada. En precisión reducida, la multiplicación por π se realiza en FP32 antes de restaurar el tipo. El diagrama anterior muestra el flujo.

### Cómo probar
La suite ejecutó 56 pruebas correctamente. Las siete pruebas de capas también pasaron con MLX Metal frente a PyTorch CPU, cubriendo relleno, frecuencias extendidas y fraccionarias, y entradas FP32/FP16.

### Archivos y objetivos
Los archivos se enumeran arriba e incluyen implementación, pruebas y documentación bilingüe. El issue permanece abierto para validar integración, otras formas y otros tipos en modelos reales.

author: rjwalters
body:
Part of #1699. This covers Curator steps 1–3. Step 4 is still open: measuring difficulty behaviour at low load on the testnet. It's a measurement, not a code change, and the fleet is pinned for x1.

## What changed (sim and docs only, no consensus code)

**Step 1: parity between the tail recompute and the node**
- New `MonetaryPolicy::block_reward_at(height, total_mined)`. It mirrors `botho::block::calculate_block_reward`: the halving reward in Phase 1, and in Phase 2 the tail reward **recomputed every block** from cumulative gross issuance.
- New `cumulative_issuance_at` / `issuance_at_checkpoints`. They are exact: closed form in Phase 1, then block by block in the tail. They use the node's height convention (genesis mints nothing).
- `emission_sweep::cumulative_supply_at` now delegates to these. It used to fix the tail reward once.
- `DifficultyController` now pays `block_reward_at` from gross issuance on every block. It used to fix the reward at transition, from supply net of burns. Its difficulty target is now block time in both phases, like the node's M5 controller. The old inflation-targeting Phase-2 kernel is kept as `#[allow(dead_code)]` and still has a test.
- `calculate_gini` now sums in u128. The default `emission-sweep` overflowed u64 at picocredit scale, because release builds run with overflow checks.

**Step 2: the "2% net" claim**
- The sweep has a new node-parity section. It computes realistic burn with the shared `consensus_fee_model` (#1728) and the 20% burn share.
- `expected_fee_burn_rate_bps` is a ratified consensus parameter, so I **restated the claim rather than recalibrating it**.

**Step 3: whitepaper parameters (checked against code)**
- Minimum block time: 5 s → 3 s (`ConsensusConfig::MIN_BLOCK_TIME_SECS`).
- Fee example: was "4 KB → 4,000 pico". Now a 1-in/2-out tx (990 bytes) has a consensus floor of 3,960 pico, and the default relay minimum of 1e8 pico is what wallets actually pay.
- "2% net" restated across §7, the appendices, the executive summary and the figures. The supply projection now uses node-exact values.
- PDFs rebuilt; the web copy is synced.
- README and `docs/{minting,concepts/tokenomics,concepts/monetary-policy}.md` restated to match.

**Drift guards** (`botho/src/ledger/emission_parity_tests.rs`)
- Sim issuance equals the node's `total_mined`, checked block by block over **20 policy-years** at every halving and year boundary (~126M calls, about 13 s in debug).
- `block_reward_at` equals `calculate_block_reward`, including supplies above u64.
- `mainnet_policy_mirror()` equals `mainnet_policy()`.
- `FEE_BURN_SHARE_PERMILLE` equals `1000 - canonical_config().pool_fraction_permille`.
- The difficulty target, min/max block time and `BLOCK_TIME_LEVELS` equal the node's.

## Results (`experiments/results/emission_sweep.md`, re-run)
- **Supply:** policy-year 6 is 626.48M BTH, year 10 is 692.36M, year 20 is **889.01M**. The old fixed-tail model gave 840.14M at year 20, an understatement of 5.82%. Tail growth is 2.532% per policy-year.
- **Tail reward:** 2.4219 BTH/block at onset, 3.5238 at year 20.
- **Burn:** for base fees to burn the assumed 0.5%/yr, the network would need **~4,844 tx/s** sustained at the relay minimum. At 5 tx/s, base-fee burn is 0.0005%/yr. Demurrage burn is at most 0.40%/yr (only if every coin were at max factor and settled every year). So **realized net tail is about 2.1–2.5%, near the top in practice**.
- **Calendar time:** time to tail is 3 years at ≥20 tx/s, 5 at 5 tx/s, 10 at 1–5 tx/s, 20 at 0.2–1 tx/s and 40 when idle. Gross emission per calendar year ranges from 0.31% to 4.17%.
- **Agent-based Gini/top-share:** essentially unchanged from the earlier run. The track still removes every fee from supply, where the node burns 20% and recycles 80%; the report states this.

**For a human decision, not changed here:** in practice the ratified tail (#351) is a ~2.5% net tail, not 2%. Two options: keep it and treat 2.5% as the real figure (the docs now say so), or change `tail_inflation_bps` / `expected_fee_burn_rate_bps`. The second is a consensus change.

## Remaining (#1699 step 4)
- Measure on the testnet whether difficulty eases to `MAX_DIFFICULTY` below ~5 tx/s. Use x1 evidence, or do it when the fleet is unpinned.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p bth-cluster-tax --release --tests`: 525 passed.
- `cargo test -p botho --lib -- emission_parity monetary:: block:: consensus_fee_model`: 53 passed.
- `cluster-tax-sim emission-sweep`: re-run with defaults; artifacts committed.

### Scope exception: CI

This PR also adds one step to `.github/workflows/workspace-build.yml`: `cargo test --locked -p botho --lib "ledger::emission_parity_tests::"`. Without it, the drift guards would only run when someone runs them locally. This is a deliberate exception to the "sim and docs only" scope. The tail-emission decision (keep the ratified parameters and restate ~2.5% as the headline figure, or recalibrate) is tracked in #1788.

author: jiahaoalbus
body:
Ordinary CP2/Term2 material could reach the strong-only ENROLLMENT_V1 startup verifier, which requires TPM AK/NV/PCR/counter facts. The previous SDK grammar described digest shapes without an ordinary Root-signed enrollment body. Add a separate strict ordinary body2 schema, unsigned codec, original envelope parser and full-original bindings. Preserve the original Root signing frame/roles and strong v1 validation.

The 19-field ordinary body binds the actual credential, administration domain, platform/service identity, original Scope7, storage/key/registration tuple and original enrollment chain/window. CP2 references the entire anchor enrollment envelope SHA and its administration domain; Term2 references the distinct issuer and same anchor envelopes. Credential, body and qualification hashes cannot substitute for these originals. Source generation and storage generation remain independent lossless values.

Validation uses only seven new functional groups and five new type counterexamples, followed by one actual normal archive consumer and byte checks against source. The previous 553 package members must remain; no old cryptographic or product matrix is rerun.

This unsigned DATA codec does not verify Root signatures, enroll a resource, authenticate Native Source or verify MAC. Auth must produce real approved ordinary enrollment originals and retained getters; Main must add a separate strict ordinary Root-verification material path. Initial Current3 persistent head/floor production, matching Native build/install and real Wallet/IDE business verification remain unfinished. No account/UNKNOWN is reset or replayed.

body:
## What
A new **Oscillator** node (Add Node > Animation & Effects). It's a wave that drives numeric properties of other nodes: moving platforms, bobbing pickups, flickering lights, pulsing effects.

- **Waves**: Sine, Triangle, Square (with Pulse Width), Saw, Reverse Saw, Random (a held value each cycle), Smooth Noise (glides between random values; Seed makes it repeatable) and Curve (drawn in the Inspector).
- **Rate**: in Hertz (cycles a second) or Seconds (the length of one cycle).
- **Mappings**: one oscillator can drive any number of properties. Each mapping has:
  - a target node (a path from the oscillator, such as `..` or `../Platform`);
  - a property: a number (`rotation`), one component (`position.x`, `color.a`) or a whole vector or colour (`scale`, `color`);
  - **Min** and **Max**;
  - **Relative** (the default: added to the value the property had at Start) or **Absolute**;
  - **Phase** (degrees) and **Value Offset**.
- **Control**:
  - **Start** remembers the targets' values.
  - **Stop** puts them back and rewinds the phase.
  - **Pause** holds the targets where they are, and **Resume** carries on from the same phase.
  - **Autostart** and **Loops**.
  - The `cycle` signal fires at the end of each cycle and `finished` after Loops cycles.
  - It runs on game time: the time scale, slow motion and hit-stop apply, and the game's pause through Pause Mode.
- **Lua**:
  - `oscillator_start`, `oscillator_stop`, `oscillator_pause`, `oscillator_resume`.
  - `oscillator_state()`, which returns the state and the cycles run.
  - `oscillator_add_mapping(target, property, min, max [, absolute])`; a property can also be `shader:<param>`.
  - `oscillator_clear_mappings()`.
- **Editor**:
  - A waveform graph with a playhead.
  - **Preview**, which runs the oscillator in the editor; Stop Preview puts the targets back. While a preview runs, saving and undo steps keep the real values, never the previewed ones.
  - The mappings list, with a node picker (drop from the tree) and a property picker that lists whole properties and their components.
  - The curve editor for Curve.
  - Renaming or moving a target node keeps its mapping pointed at it.

## Tests
- Engine test `test_oscillator_node`:
  - Relative and Absolute mappings, components and whole vectors, Phase and Value Offset;
  - Pause keeping the phase, Stop restoring;
  - Loops with `cycle` and `finished`, and no drift on a restart;
  - every wave;
  - property widths;
  - saving and reading back;
  - previewed values staying out of a save.
- Runner suite `tests/oscillator` (added to CI):
  - a golden picture: a swaying platform, spin + grow, a flicker and a square pulse;
  - a scripted scene: pause at 0.5 s, resume at 1 s with the phase kept, the `cycle` signal, Stop putting the box back at x = 300.
- Drive `oscillator`: adds an Oscillator under a Text node, adds a mapping and picks `position.x`, then checks that Preview moves the Text, Stop Preview puts it back, and the scene saves the mapping.
- Also passing: `task test`, `check_docs` (0 errors) and the drives `inspector_help`, `node_refs_rename` and `node_rename_scene_refs`.

## Already failing on main
The `welcome` drive fails on main as well (`node-icons` 68/70). Two pairs of node types share an icon: Empty Node and Touch Button, and Viewport and UI Container. The Oscillator has its own icon, so this branch shows 69/71.

author: jgus-bot
body:
## What

This repository has no GitHub Actions workflows at all, so nothing here builds on a pull request. The flake publishes a wrapped python application built on a `python3.withPackages` environment, which is fleet python, so it takes the fleet's python gate.

Two files, installed byte-for-byte from `jgus-org/flake-lib`'s `templates/workflows` at the head of the `v1` branch (`87fa38e`):

- `.github/workflows/build-and-check.yml` — runs `nix run github:jgus-org/flake-lib/v1#build-and-check` on every pull request.
- `.github/workflows/update-workflows.yml` — the sync tool that keeps the first file equal to the template.

## Why the gate and not just the check

`nix flake check` alone looks at the shape of `packages` without building them; a package that does not compile passes it. `build-and-check` builds every package the flake publishes for the runner's system and then runs the check, so the gate is the thing that would actually have caught a broken tree.

## The nixpkgs input on this branch

The first gate run failed on a pre-existing condition: the flake declares `nixos-unstable` with a comment saying fastmcp is not yet in 26.05, but on `nixos-unstable` fastmcp is absent and `fastmcp-slim` carries `meta.broken`, so the gate refuses to evaluate the tree at all. This branch moves the input to `release-26.05`, where `python3Packages.fastmcp` exists at 3.4.7 and the package builds (`comfyui-mcp-0.1.0`, `--help` starts). The comment names the reason the release branch is taken; it was the other way around on `main`.

## Out of scope

No updater is proposed, so no updater template is installed. The version here is a hand-written `"0.1.0"` over a carried source tree with no upstream pin to update.

author: tempestmk7
body:
## What changed

- **Zoom.** The Overlap board has a camera like Jigsaw's: the mouse wheel zooms about the pointer, two fingers pinch (a second finger still turns a piece that is in hand), the +/- control and the zoom label ("show everything") work, and a drag on the bare board or the right button moves it. It cannot zoom out past showing the whole board, and zooms in until a cell is about 200 device pixels wide (or twice the whole-board size, if that is more). The camera is saved with the puzzle and restored on resume.
- **Trays stay on the left.** The trays are now a panel in canvas pixels down the left side, drawn the same size whatever the zoom (about a third of the width at most, 60-100% of their old size on a narrow screen). Sizes with more trays than fit scroll: the wheel over the panel, a drag on its empty parts (so on a phone, drag beside the piece rather than on it), and a piece held near the top or bottom edge scrolls it by itself. A thin bar shows how far it is scrolled.
- **The trays no longer move to the top of a tall screen**; they are always at the left, as asked.
- **Held pieces.** Over the board a held piece is drawn at the zoomed size and snaps to the cell under it; over the panel it shrinks to the size it has in a tray and the tray lights up.
- **Graphics layer.** `VideoLayer.clipBefore(left)` draws what has been added so far only to the right of the panel (a scissor), and `FrontLayer.begin` takes the same clip for the ripples, so a zoomed board does not show over the trays. The 2D drawing (photos, no WebGL 2) covers it by drawing the panel over the board.
- Lines (cell borders, grid, board edge) stay about a pixel or two wide when zoomed in instead of growing with the zoom.

## How it was tested

`npm test` (815 tests, one new for the clip mark), `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` pass. In the browser pane (desktop 1000x640 and the 375x812 phone preset), with a photo and a generated 720p clip, Overlap at XXL (7 trays): wheel zoom to 448%, left-drag pan, wheel scroll of the panel, a wrong drop (red flash on the right cells, piece back on its stack), a correct drop found by trying every cell (the count went from 101 to 102), a held piece over the board and over the panel, auto-scroll with a piece held at the bottom edge, zoom restored after leaving and resuming, and the board clipped at the panel edge on both the graphics-card path and the 2D path.

## Not tested

- Real two-finger pinch and a real finger on a phone or tablet (the touch paths were only looked at through the phone-sized preset, and pointer events were sent by script).
- Frame rate while zoomed in with a big video, and a real GPU.
- The panel-scroll drag on touch needs the finger to start off the piece; that is a guess at what feels right and may need tuning.
- A puzzle saved before this change opens at the whole-board view (it has no saved camera).

author: bllshttng
body:
## Summary

A program that crashes inside a synchronized update froze its pane. vte holds the bytes after `CSI ?2026h` and asks its owner to expire the update after 150 ms, but nothing in `crates/fno/src` called `stop_sync`. The pane stayed frozen until an end-sync or 2 MB of output.

The core loop now sleeps until the earliest open sync deadline, applies the held bytes, and repaints the pane. The deadline is read from pane state on each loop pass, so every feed site is covered: live output, keeper replay and spawn replay.

## Changes

- `crates/fno/src/vt.rs`: `Pane::sync_deadline` and `Pane::expire_sync`.
- `crates/fno/src/server/pane_output.rs`: `next_sync_deadline` and `expire_sync_updates`. The second one broadcasts each expired pane, notifies pane watchers and re-syncs modes.
- `crates/fno/src/server/serve.rs`: one new `select!` arm. It is disabled while no pane has an open update, so an idle server gets no new wakeups.
- One leg only: `crates/fno-agents/src/screen.rs` also holds a vte `Processor`, but `poll_until_ready` in `daemon.rs` builds a fresh grid from a worker snapshot on each poll. It has no pane to freeze, so it stays as it is.

## Test Plan

Proved by hand on an isolated mux with the real binary, running `printf 'BEFORE-MARK\n\033[?2026hHELD-MARK\n'; sleep 20` in a pane and reading it 1, 2 and 3 s later:

- Before the fix: `HELD-MARK` was missing at all three reads.
- After the fix: `HELD-MARK` was present at all three reads.

The two new tests compile, but they did not run locally, because agent sessions run no tests on this machine. CI is their first run:

- `unterminated_sync_update_expires_without_further_output` drives the timer through the CLI.
- `expire_sync_applies_held_bytes_only_after_the_deadline` proves an update inside its window is not released early. The end-to-end test cannot see that.

## Test delta

| Language | Added | Removed | Net |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Python | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Rust | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| Shell | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **2** | **0** | **+2** |

Audited owners: crates/fno/src/vt.rs (no cut: I read the names of its 24 existing tests. They cover rendering, links, modes, OSC 133, blocks, scroll, selection, turns and search, and none touches synchronized updates. I did not read every test body, so this is an audit for overlap with this change, not a full prune.)

## Review

Reviewed at d9ba11d2b869ecda9695d8d462c9782e07fe421c: 1 rounds, 0 findings disposed.

Fixes x-918e

author: valleytechsolutions
body:
Add an opt-in `XIAO_ESP32_S3_TOUCH` target for the Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus with the 1.47-inch 172 × 320 JD9853A display. The target uses two physical buttons: BTN_A advances and wraps, and BTN_B selects or exits an activity.

The port preserves upstream startup without waiting for a serial client. USB CDC output is nonblocking during setup, then its normal bounded timeout is restored before the main loop so long CLI responses can drain normally. Disconnected native CDC writes return immediately. The unused SD slot is deselected before LCD initialization.

The display adapter reapplies its mirror correction after initialization and rotation. Menus page after ten visible rows; scan and graph exits work through BTN_B; BTN_A cycles analyzer channels/pages with wraparound; and brightness has physical-button controls. Debounce rejects contact bounce and short glitches without introducing hold-to-repeat behavior.

**Scope:** this is a display and button port. AXS5106L touch, SD, direct upload, and battery monitoring remain unsupported. GUI entries requiring unavailable text entry, storage, or GPS are omitted. CLI configuration and saved Wi-Fi management remain available. The release firmware matrix is unchanged.

### Validation

- Rebased onto current upstream `master` at `511bb3694d0c4dc064888e762bde44fcc9b7f48a`.
- 162 existing native tests and 9 XIAO native tests passed with GCC 16.2.0 / C++17.
- 86 Python checks passed, including compilation and execution of the actual graph input handler against wraparound, one-action-per-press, and exit-priority scenarios, plus startup/runtime CDC timeout ordering.
- Final firmware build passed with Arduino-ESP32 3.3.12, stock TFT_eSPI 2.5.34 plus the repository setup header, and NimBLE-Arduino 2.3.8. Sketch size is 1,514,097 / 3,342,336 bytes; static RAM is 79,852 / 327,680 bytes. Source hashes remained unchanged during compilation. The application image is 1,514,240 bytes, SHA-256 `05a70cfe28046a8843c196e500d8dd480a3c4255ff4676748e32966bcaa7b839`; esptool verifies its checksum, embedded hash, ESP32-S3 target, and 16 MB flash header.
- Upstream [Firmware Unit Tests](https://github.com/justcallmekoko/ESP32Marauder/actions/runs/41270092025) passed on final head `76fcb606`.
- Independent source review and `git diff --check` passed.

No board was available for this revised image. Battery/charger-only cold boot, USB detach/reconnect, real LCD colors/alignment, and Wi-Fi/BLE behavior still require hardware qualification; no hardware test is claimed by these software results. The [board guide](https://github.com/valleytechsolutions/ESP32Marauder/blob/hardware/xiao-s3-plus-147-reviewed/docs/xiao-147-display.md) records dependencies, controls, limitations, and the exact cold-boot procedure.

author: meepzilla
body:
Makes all built-in goal templates read the same way:

> By [date], the student will … with 80% accuracy across 3 consecutive sessions, as measured by SLP or teacher observation and data collection.

**Goal bank (903 templates; 688 goal texts and 105 names changed)**
The importer has a new `tidy_text` step. `--tidy` applies it to the bank already in the app, without the CSV. It changes:
- "STUDENT" and a bare "student will" to "the student".
- "HIS/HER", "HE/SHE", "HIM/HER" and "HIMSELF/HERSELF" to "their", "they", "them" and "themselves", with the verb agreeing ("they need", not "they needs").
- "[X]", "[Item]" and empty sounds "/ /" to "___" blanks, so they can be filled in Edit Goal.
- "using [preferred communication method]" and "using preferred communication method" to "using their preferred communication method".
- "i.g." to "e.g.", stray spaces before commas, and missing final periods.
- Every "as measured by" ending to the same wording, including 17 goals that ended "as measured by __________".
- Straight double quotes to curly ones.
- Labels such as "(Compensatory Goal)" at the start of a goal are removed.

**Original built-in templates (210)**
- They had no goal statement, so goals assigned from them were saved as "SMART goal for <name>". Each one now gets a statement written by `built-in-statements.ts`, using the template's target and a 3-session mastery.
- The criterion matches the goal's measure: accuracy, % of opportunities, story score, a rating out of 5, or the count already in the sentence for behavior goals.
- Fluency goals are stated as % fluent syllables. A handful of sentences that didn't fit the pattern are written out by hand.
- 14 Title Case names are now in sentence case, e.g. "Reduce Fronting of /k, g/" becomes "Reduce fronting of /k/ and /g/".
- Three articulation blend descriptions now say "in the initial position". The task analysis statements say "the student".

**Existing devices**
- Each device keeps its own copy of the templates, so a load step brings stored copies up to date. It replaces a statement or description only when it is still an earlier built-in wording, checked by hash: `goal-bank-text-updates.json` for the bank, and a short list for the others.
- Renamed templates are moved to the new name, so they aren't added twice.
- Goals assigned with the "SMART goal for …" placeholder get their template's statement.
- Templates the user edited keep their text. So do goals already assigned to students. Their names follow the renames, as earlier renames did.

**Also**
- Ratings ("a rating of at least 4 out of 5") and numbers of communication functions ("at least 4 different functions") now follow the goal's target.
- The goal pop-up no longer repeats a built-in template's description when it is just the goal in short form.
- README and Changelog are updated, and `__pycache__` is ignored.

**Checks**
- 102 tests pass. New tests cover:
  - every template's form;
  - the hash matching the importer's;
  - updating a stored bank template and a renamed built-in without adding a duplicate;
  - leaving edited text alone;
  - filling in placeholder goals.
- Typecheck, lint and the static build pass.
- Browser test: a device holding an old "Reduce Fronting of /k, g/" template and two placeholder goals. The template was renamed in place and given its statement. The profile showed "Ava will use regular plural -s in phrases or sentences with 70% accuracy across 4 consecutive sessions, …", following the goal's own target and mastery.

**Not changed**
- Long goal bank names are still cut off with "…". Shortening about 500 names well needs judgement for each one.
- The goal bank "purpose" text is unchanged.

author: 0x-auth
body:
Any step that turns one thing into another and is sometimes wrong (reading a page, summarising a chat, fitting a law, remembering) plugs in with `forward`, `mirror` and `compare`, plus an optional second `view`. The core never looks inside a field: it runs the round trip, places the trusted/review line once from a few known-right examples, and gives every output one `State`, the event z = t + i/t.

**What's added**
- `state.py`: z, z', dt, dx, the clock (u, turn), the four sides (you, retro, twin, retro twin) and the sector of the rebuilding rule S -> dx + 1/S. That rule is `Law(dx, 1, 1, 0)`; for real t its Delta is exactly dt^2, so the sectors are the stages of the seed (real t settles, t = ±i is the seam, |t| = 1 only turns).
- `mirror.py`: the `Field` contract, `CallableField` for any functions (OCR, an LLM, a parser), and `Mirror` (check, calibrate, state, route).
- `fields.py`: exact, memory, law and text fields, zero dependencies.
- `textcheck.py`: a Python port of the Memory Check tool, identical on its 96 test claims.
- CLI: `reality state <t>` and `reality check <source> <note>`.

**Tests**: 10 new, 27 in total, all passing locally. CI runs them on Python 3.9 and 3.x.

**One honest result** (in the README): on the darmiyan-fs OCR data, adding the second view as the turn caught 93% of wrong reads at 34% review, against 91% for the residual alone at the same budget. The difference is not significant.

Publishing to PyPI only happens on a release, so merging this does not publish 0.3.0.

author: bherbruck
body:
Follow-up to #2152. It removes most of the cost of building STEP bodies from their topology first.

## Rule

A topology build that is a closed solid and **needed no repair** is returned without running the stitched build. "Needed no repair" means:
- no face was left out;
- no face's seam fix or UV-trim pass failed;
- the seam fix and UV-trim pass left the edge and vertex counts as built.

Every other body runs exactly as in #2152: the stitched cross-check, the healed retry when both builds are closed but disagree, and the fallbacks.
- Bodies whose seam fix adds edges, for example `ap203/4pinplug.stp` body 6 (6 to 12 edges) and `ap214/io1-ug-214.stp` body 0 (23 to 40), count as repaired and keep the cross-check.
- So does a body with a failed seam split.

Only `crates/step-brep` (`lib.rs`, README) changes.

## Results (STEP Tools corpus, local only; 75 files, 1225 bodies)

- **Time:** 76.2 s by default against 48.4 s stitch-only, **1.57×**. #2152 measured 2.58× (152.7 s against 59.3 s).
- 0 worse, 18 gains, 107 changed. That's the same set as #2152 except one body, below.
- **`ap203/rear.stp` body 35 improves:**
  - default now 1645734.388;
  - C++ `--constructor` 1645734.510 (7e-8 relative);
  - #2152 gave 1645947.12 (1.3e-4);
  - stitching gives 1645976.55.
- The private 35-body test assembly is unchanged: 35 of 35 closed by default, against 33 stitch-only.

fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`) and the step crates' tests pass locally.

지금 효과음은 점프·사망·체크포인트·클리어 네 가지뿐입니다. 함정 30종이 발동해도 고유한 소리나 그림 반응이 없어, 당하는 순간의 "이걸 이렇게?" 반응이 약합니다.

author: matttelker
body:
### Problem

`_determine_kickoff_phase` labels any inferred kickoff at `t >= 300` as `OT`. But `t` is replay time, and the game clock stops for countdowns and after goals, so regulation runs well past 300 s of replay time. Regulation kickoffs read `OT`.

It also fails the other way. The parser reports `OT` only when the header has `bOverTime`, and no sample has that key, so the markers for a real overtime kickoff read `INITIAL`. One kickoff could hold both labels.

### Fix

Use the rules of the game. Every kickoff after the first follows a goal, except the one that starts overtime. That one comes at a level score, and it is the last kickoff because the next goal ends the match.

A new pass, `_mark_overtime_kickoff`, marks every event of the last ball reset when no goal came since the kickoff before it and the score is level. Parser markers that already say `OT` stay `OT`. Without goal data nothing proves overtime, so kickoffs stay `INITIAL`. `_determine_kickoff_phase` goes.

### Validation

Each replay's network data holds the real clock: the `GameEvent_Soccar` actor counts 300 to 0, then counts up during overtime. On all six tracked samples the new labels match it.

| Replay | Goes to OT (game clock) | `OT` events before | `OT` events after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0925` | No (forfeit) | none | none |
| `4985385d` | Yes, kickoff at 346.3 s | 351.3 | 346.3, 346.4, 351.3 |
| `6804bd43` | No (forfeit) | none | none |
| `70c0e78e` | No | 365.2 | none |
| `77253f53` | No | 323.7 | none |
| `testing_replay` | Yes, kickoff at 424.5 s | 343.0, 399.8, 429.6 | 424.5, 424.7, 429.6 |

Across the six replays this corrects 8 labels. Kickoff events are otherwise identical. The "before" column was measured with the timeline truncation fix applied. On `main` alone the `70c0e78e` kickoff at 365.2 s sits in the cut part of the replay, so it does not appear.

`TotalSecondsPlayed` is not a usable signal: it reads 302.85 on `70c0e78e`, whose clock shows no overtime, because the game runs on at 0:00 until the ball lands.

### Behavior changes to review

- `test_overtime_kickoff` asserted the bug (`t=350`, no goal data, expects `OT`), so it is replaced.
- `Header.overtime` and `match_length` no longer set the phase. No sample carries the flag.

### Known limits

- An equalizer at 0:00 leads to an overtime kickoff that follows a goal. Goals alone can't separate that from a regulation kickoff, so it stays `INITIAL`.
- `metadata.overtime` in the report still reads only the header, so it stays false on real overtime replays.
- Rust `infer_kickoff_phase` is unchanged. It needs the header flag, so it does not fire on these replays. If a header ever carries `bOverTime`, it still decides by replay time, and this pass only adds `OT`, so a parser marker that says `OT` is kept as it is.
- On `main` alone, a kickoff in the part of a replay that `_align_match_clock` cuts is not seen, so its phase can't be set. treygoff24/rlcoach#47 removes that cut.

### Tests

- 5 synthetic tests and 6 parametrized real-replay tests in `tests/test_events.py`. 8 of them fail without this change. The rest guard behavior that was already right.
- Local Windows run: same 16 failures and 3 collection errors before and after (existing `resource` import, symlink, temp-lock and TOML path issues), 647 to 657 passed. Also run with the timeline truncation fix underneath: same failures, 649 to 659 passed.
- ruff passes. black passes on the changed files.

body:
Row 1.3 asked for `ui` flake instances to be counted. This counts the second
`foresight-ui` one, observed on #405 an hour after the first was written up.

## Same three lines as #403

```
FAIL: the commitment appears in the pending list on screen
FAIL: and the commitment reached the conductor, question bound
HARNESS ERROR: locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded
  at main (scripts/live-verify/foresight-ui.mjs:409)
```

§7 failed, then §8 cascaded off it because it needs §7's pending commitment to
exist. Byte-for-byte the #403 failure.

## The diff could not have caused it

#405 changed three `scripts/*.mjs` endpoint callers and two documents. Nothing
under `scripts/live-verify/` or `.github/workflows/ui.yml` references any of the
three — the only mention anywhere is a comment in `index-lens.mjs`. There is no
code path from that change into the `ui` job. Same situation as #403, which was
a comment-only edit.

## It cleared on one re-run again

All seven checks green after the re-run, and every other job passed on its
**first** attempt — `partition-rejoin` included, which is worth noting given row
7.28. So `foresight-ui` is now twice observed and twice cleared by a single
re-run, where #339 failed its re-run identically. The split row 1.3 already
recorded gets sharper, not resolved: these harnesses genuinely differ in whether
a re-run clears them.

## The part that still resists the explanation

The §5 settle that closed `taxonomy-ui` was a timing fix — a re-render wiped a
form before validation ran. That cannot be what this is. Here §7's **chain-read**
check failed alongside the render check, so the write never reached the
conductor. A missing settle explains a paint that arrives too late; it does not
explain an absent write.

Counted, not explained. Nothing in this row claims a cause.

author: zhanfg
body:
## Context
Nohello v1.8.3.7 on KPatch-Next-EXP 0.13.14 is embedded in active boot but fails to register at pre-kernel-init (`rc=-2`, ENOENT). The same binary loads in original KPatch-Next. ELF analysis shows undefined `is_su_allow_uid` (five relocations). The symbol exists and is exported on KPatch-Next 0.13.5-2, but EXP removed it.

## Fix
Restore the legacy read-only `is_su_allow_uid(uid_t)` ABI export. Under EXP, only UID 0 may invoke the supercall; the compatibility predicate mirrors this policy and does not restore the old writable allowlist.

## Validation
- GitHub Actions build and symbol assertion successful: https://github.com/Zhanfg/KPatch-Next-EXP/actions/runs/41269885661
- Compiled `kpimg` uploaded as a CI artifact.
- Offline ELF symbol-name scan found all 44 unique Nohello external symbols in the new compiled image.

## Still needed
Actual boot repatch / rooted-device validation; do not claim Nohello is functional until tested. This PR does not itself alter any device boot partition.

author: johnjohn4
body:
Refs #269. This is the residual Notepad++-only failure that remains after #270: the daemon logs a normal paste, yet nothing lands.

## Why

The live evidence points at something specific to running *inside* the daemon. That process hosts the WH_KEYBOARD_LL hook and sends Ctrl+V shortly after the hook swallowed and replayed a Win/Alt key-up. The leading hypothesis is a stale modifier in Notepad++'s **thread** key state, which Scintilla reads with GetKeyState. Nobody has captured that state at a failure yet, so this PR makes every paste record it and also adds two cheap hardenings.

## 1. Self-diagnosing paste log (Windows)

Each regular paste and each Trigger Fire now logs one INFO line. It contains no dictated text and no clipboard contents:

```
Paste diag [paste]: target=0x15A0A18 fg_after=yes gui_flags=0x1[caretblinking] focus=Scintilla thread_keys(+250ms)=none async_keys=none since_mod_up_ms=412 replay_1s=yes settle_ms=0 sendinput=6/6
```

- `fg_after`: whether the target is still foreground right after SendInput. If not, it prints `no(0x...)`.
- `gui_flags` / `focus`: GetGUIThreadInfo for the target's GUI thread, with the flags decoded, and the class of its focus window.
- `thread_keys`: the target thread's key state for alt/lwin/rwin/ctrl/shift/v. `async_keys`: GetAsyncKeyState for the same keys.
- `since_mod_up_ms`: ms since the last physical modifier key-up. On a keyboard hotkey that is the combo release. If the hook replayed the key-up, the observed replay counts as the release. `replay_1s`: whether the hook swallowed and replayed a key-up in the last 1 s.
- `settle_ms`: the pre-injection wait from (b) below. `sendinput`: dispatched/requested for each SendInput call; a Trigger Fire shows two, e.g. `10/10,48/48`.
- Fields that couldn't be read print as `?`.

**AttachThreadInput safety.** The thread key state is read on a short-lived worker thread, 250 ms after the SendInput, never on the GUI thread at paste time. The worker attaches briefly and detaches in `finally`. There are two reasons:
- Windows documents that attaching resets the shared key state. Doing it while our Ctrl+V is still queued in the target could change the very paste we're diagnosing.
- An attach that involves a hung target can stall the caller. A worker can stall harmlessly; the Qt GUI thread must not.

If the state is stuck, a +250 ms read still shows it, because a stuck modifier stays stuck until the user types.

**Structure.**
- The snapshot dataclass and the pure formatter live in `paste/injection_diagnostics.py`, with unit tests.
- The gathering is `Win32KeystrokeSender.report_injection`, through a new optional `InjectionDiagnostics` protocol that only the Windows adapter implements.
- The pipeline calls it inside a guard that logs failures at DEBUG. The adapter guards it too, so it can never break a paste.
- The clipboard formats present just before Ctrl+V are logged at DEBUG, using GetUpdatedClipboardFormats, which doesn't need OpenClipboard.

## 2. Hardening

**(a) No-op sync key.** The Ctrl+V batch is now one SendInput of `[0xE8 down, 0xE8 up, Ctrl down, V down, V up, Ctrl up]`, all with the Dictatem tag. The target's thread dequeues a neutral, unassigned key before Ctrl, so its thread key state is up to date when Ctrl+V arrives.

**(b) Input settle (implemented).** The keyboard hook gets a passive `observe_key` observer that feeds an `InputTimeline`. `send_masked_release` records a replay as pending, and the hook clears it when it sees the tagged replayed key-up come back. Before the first injection of a paste or Trigger Fire, the adapter:
1. waits until the pending replay has been observed (polling every 5 ms, capped at 250 ms);
2. then waits until 50 ms have passed since the last modifier key-up.

The whole wait is bounded in both time and number of polls. In the common case it is zero, because transcription takes longer than 50 ms. The decision is pure (`paste/input_timeline.py`) and tested with a fake clock.

The #270 held-modifier wait already covers the async state. A swallowed key-up leaves async Alt/Win down until the replay passes the hook. What it doesn't cover is the time the *target thread* needs to dequeue that key-up, and the 50 ms settle covers that on the fast paths (a quick transcription, the "paste" voice action).

No other behaviour changes. macOS and the fakes are untouched. Only the Windows adapter implements the new protocol.

## Tests

- New: `test_input_timeline.py`, `test_injection_diagnostics.py`, `test_paste_injection_report.py`, and `test_win32_keystroke.py`. The last one is Windows-only, with SendInput and the attach patched out.
- `test_wh_keyboard_ll.py` gains tests for the observer.
- `uv run ruff check src tests`: clean. `uv run pyright`: 0 errors. `uv run pytest -q`: 1950 passed, 31 skipped.

## Manual QA

author: jmandel
body:
Every package the crawler stores, from any feed, can briefly be served as a missing or partial tarball. This PR makes sure an advertised `id#version` only ever has a complete file behind it.

## The problem

In `packages/package-crawler.js` the crawler:
1. commits the package to the database, after which the registry advertises it and redirects downloads (`bucketPath`) to `<id>-<version>.tgz` in the mirror, which nginx serves at `/web/` and the CDN fetches on a miss;
2. **then** writes the mirror file with `fs.writeFileSync` under its final name, which truncates and rewrites in place.

That gives two windows:
- **Every new package, any source:** between the commit and the end of the write, the package is listed but its file is missing (a 404, which the CDN caches briefly) or partly written. A partial file can look like a complete response and be cached by the CDN for up to a day. The window is short, but it opens on every publication, which is exactly when tools fetch the new version.
- **A direct copy replacing a Simplifier copy:** a file that has been served for a while is truncated and rewritten in place, so a download in progress, or one arriving during the rewrite, gets a short or mixed file.

## The change

The new tarball is written beside its target as `<file>.tmp-<pid>`, which never ends in `.tgz` and so is never served. It is then renamed onto the real name, and the step order depends on the case:
- **New package:** rename into place, then commit. The file is complete before anything can ask for it.
- **Replacement:** commit, then rename. The old file stays fully served until the replacement has committed, and then the name switches to the new file in one step.
- **If the commit fails:** the served file is untouched, the temp file is removed, and a new package's file is removed too, since it was never advertised.

On Linux, `rename` within one directory is atomic, and a reader that already has the old file open keeps reading it to the end. So readers see either the old file or the complete new one, never a mixture.

## Tests

New cases in `tests/packages/package-crawler-versions.test.js`:
- **New package:** the mirror holds the complete new file at the moment of commit. This one fails on current main.
- **Replacement:** at commit time the mirror still holds the old file, and afterwards it holds the new one.
- **Failed commit:** a replacement leaves the served file alone, and a new package leaves no file.
- **Earlier test, kept:** a reader that had the old file open still reads all of it.

All 176 tests in `tests/packages` pass.

body:
Refs #41

## Summary

Adds `plans/array-api-coverage.md`: a matrix that maps each Array API 2025.12 function and semantic rule onto ArrIR's proposed operations. The spec is pinned to <https://data-apis.org/array-api/2025.12/>, retrieved 2026-11-01, and the function lists come from its category pages.

Design only. The replacement IR implements none of this; every class describes proposed representation.

## Semantic decision

Each function gets exactly one class, with any condition that would change it given as a footnote. Results for the 135 main-namespace functions (the 6 inspection functions, constants, operators, attributes and extensions aren't counted):

| Direct | Compose | Compose after New | New | Blocked | Meta | Runtime | Deferred |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 79 | 9 | 2 | 11 | 8 | 6 | 0 | 20 |

The matrix follows the decisions recorded on #46 and #47 on 1 November:
- Axes are named or positional, and Array API arrays lower to positional shapes.
- `broadcast_to` and `broadcast_arrays` need no node only when the consumer's output shape already covers the target. Otherwise they wait on #46's broadcast-node question.
- `expand_dims` is positional only.
- Reductions declare `order` and a separate `result` dtype.
- Literals are `Constant { value, nan_is_missing }`.
- `var`/`std` are Blocked until their formula has a contract.

Eight functions are Blocked:
- `reshape`, on a traversal-order contract;
- `broadcast_to` and `broadcast_arrays`, on #46's question 7;
- `where`, on #32 including it in `Elementwise`;
- `std` and `var`, on a formula contract;
- `cumulative_sum` and `cumulative_prod`, on `Scan` and an offset size term.

Missing concepts, ranked by data-access use case:
1. `concat`
2. a `Reduce` specification issue
3. `expand_dims` (positional only)
4. a traversal-order contract
5. `Scan`

## Questions for review

These are also in the doc, each with a recommendation:
1. **`broadcast_to`.** Paired with #46's question 7. Recommendation: drop it only when the consumer's output shape covers the target, and reject every other case (including at the root) until #46 decides.
2. **`where`.** Recommendation: a ternary `Elementwise` variant (#32).
3. **`concat` first?** Recommendation: yes, assuming multi-file time series reach ArrIR as several `Open`s.
4. **Complex dtypes.** Recommendation: keep them deferred and rejected at lowering.

## Consistency check

Every row's citation was checked against plans/*.md on main, PRs #26, #45, #46 (`f033c7e`) and #47, and issues #2–#6 and #29–#42, including #34's 2026-11-01 scope update. Mismatches elsewhere:
- #46's `shapes.md` at `f033c7e` hasn't caught up with #34's scope update. It still right-aligns named operands, gives aligning named operands by name to #34, and keeps named outer broadcasting (`a(x) + b(y)`) open as question 10.
- #46's `SizeTerm` has no sum or offset form, which `concat` and `include_initial` need for symbolic extents.
- #6's scope body still says ArrIR stays linear and unary, and that adapters resolve labels first.
- #36's scope cites "PR #16 shape effects", but #15 now carries that code as `arrir::legacy`.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- A script checked that each of the 135 spec functions appears exactly once and that the counts match.

author: pbroom
body:
## Problem

With the hub/node split, `[dispatch.writable_roots]` lives on the node (laptop) config, but the hub's `_output_blocker` checked a node-bound request's declared outputs against the hub's own table and disk. A request that wrote outside its repo on the node could never launch. The error told the human to edit `[dispatch.writable_roots]`, and that edit could not help: the hub's table is empty by design, the node only read its table at start, and the hub checked paths on its own disk. Requests #898 and #899 (zark → Zen profile `sine-mods`) hit this.

## Changes

- **Node reports its roots.** `board node` sends `writable_roots` (runner key → project → `extra_roots`) in hello. It omits the field when empty, so older hubs still accept the hello. `nodes.hello` validates the field: offered runners only, plain absolute paths, no `/`, at most 10 roots per project.
- **Hub checks node-bound outputs against the node's roots.** `_node_output_blocker` allows the project path plus those roots. The match is by path, because the hub can't see the node's disk. The error names the node and the machine whose config to edit.
- **No restart for writable roots.**
  - The dispatcher's `refresh_config` now also reloads `writable_roots` (`RELOADED_TABLES`).
  - `Node.refresh_config` re-reads the settings files when their mtime changes, applies them on the next pass, and re-sends hello at once.
  - An edit that fails validation keeps the old config.
- README and DESIGN_NOTES are updated.

## Tests

- `tests/test_nodes.py`:
  - the node reports its roots, and the hub launches with an output inside them;
  - an output outside them fails preflight and names the node;
  - an edited config applies without a restart;
  - an invalid edit keeps the old config;
  - hello validation;
  - an older-hub-compatible hello.
- `tests/test_settings_page.py`: the dispatcher picks up an added writable root.
- Full suite: 2068 passed, 4 skipped.

## Deploy

Merge, then reinstall the runtime on both Macs (`scripts/install-launchagents.py --revision <merge sha>`) and restart the hub dispatcher and the laptop node.

author: adamousmer
body:
## Problem

Hub (BUS plane) connections had no failback. After a rolling node reboot, clients stayed on whichever remote hub they failed over to: nats-0 ended with 123 connections, nats-1 with 2, and 53% of hub connections crossed nodes. `PreferSameNode` only steers new dials.

## Change

**Go**
- `pkg/bus/failback.go`: one failback loop shared by the leaf (RPC) and hub (BUS) planes. A hub connection probes the node-local hub through `nats-local` and calls `ForceReconnect` only after `NATS_FAILBACK_SUCCESSES` consecutive probes see that hub answering under a different name than the one it is connected to.
- `busOptions` enables it when `NODE_NAME` and `NATS_HUB_URL` are both set.

**TypeScript (console dashboard + admin)**
- `web/kit/lib/server/nats.ts`: `enableHubFailback` runs the same loop on the `bus` connection. The probe dials `NATS_LOCAL_HUB_URL` (default `tls://nats-local.messaging:4222`) with the connection's own credentials and TLS. Leaf and hub now share `FailbackStreak`, so the leaf plane also gets the doubling backoff.
- `web/admin/src/lib/server/feed.ts`: the admin feed's hub connection uses it too.
- Enabled when `NODE_NAME` and `NATS_HUB_URL` are both set.

**Elixir (twitch-ingress)**
- `Ingress.NatsHubFailback`: the same loop for `:gnat_bus` and every `gnat_bus_pub_*` publisher shard. The probe dials `NATS_LOCAL_HUB_HOST` (default `nats-local.messaging.svc.cluster.local`) with the BUS auth and TLS. Enabled when `NODE_NAME` and `NATS_HUB_HOST` are both set. At most one connection moves per check.
- `Ingress.Nats.Publisher.failback/1`: a publisher shard moves without failing a publish. The shard:
  1. stops admitting, so `enqueue` spills to the next shard;
  2. flushes its queued entries;
  3. waits until every admitted entry is settled;
  4. then stops its connection so the supervisor redials.

  If it hasn't drained within one batch hold plus every ack attempt (12–16 s with defaults), it gives up and keeps its hub. With a single shard there is nowhere to spill, so the pool is left in place.

**Deploy**
- `deploy/messaging/nats.yaml`: new `nats-local` Service (`internalTrafficPolicy: Local`, client port only). The hub monitor port stays closed to `app`.
- `deploy/messaging/certificates.yaml`: `nats-local*` SANs on `nats-hub-tls`.

## Churn guarantees (all three runtimes)

- Already-local connections never probe and never reconnect.
- Local hub down or booting: probe fails, connection stays put. Never remote-to-remote.
- A failback that lands remote again doubles the required streak, capped at 16x.
- Random initial delay; probe result shared per process per interval.
- Each move is one reconnect: pull requests are re-issued, in-flight messages redeliver after AckWait. Publisher shards move only once nothing is in flight.

## Deploy order

1. Apply `certificates.yaml` first and wait until the hub has the reissued cert.
2. Then apply `nats.yaml` (Service only, no hub restart).
3. Then roll out the services onto an image with this change.

Until the cert is in place, probes fail TLS, which is safe: no failback happens.

## Not covered

- clusterops has no `NODE_NAME` and doesn't use `pkg/bus` for its claims connection, so it is unchanged.

## Tests

- Go: `go test ./pkg/bus/... ./deploy/... ./app/release/...` pass; failback tests pass 5x with `-race`.
- TS: `bun run test` in `web` (2200 pass, including the new `nats-hub-failback.test.ts`, which passed 5 out of 5 runs); `svelte-check` 0 errors for admin and dashboard.
- Elixir: `mix test` in twitch-ingress (315 tests, 0 failures; the full suite passed 3 out of 3 runs, and the failback and publisher tests passed 5 out of 5 runs). This includes publisher drain, drain timeout and one-move-per-check tests. `mix format --check-formatted` clean.

author: wenshao
body:
## What this PR does

Recognition of the Kimi K3 generation moves from a single-id rule to one generation-wide pattern shared by the curated context-window table and the models.dev catalog correction. Every id the generation is served under — `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k3.1-pro`, and Kimi Code's bare `k3.1-pro` / `k3.1-pro-highspeed` aliases, in either their dotted or dashed spelling — now resolves to the vendor-declared 1,000,000-token window instead of a family fallback or a rounded catalog value.

The generation's 256K variant is the one id that shares the prefix without sharing the window: `k3-256k` serves 262,144 tokens, so it is excluded from the 1M pattern and carries its own entry in both the table and the catalog corrections.

## Why it's needed

Kimi's K3.1 tiers ship the same 1M window as K3, but two separate gaps kept them from being sized that way. The curated table only matched ids beginning with the `kimi-k3` prefix, so Kimi Code's bare aliases fell through to the 256K Kimi family fallback (and, absent any table match, to the generic 200K default). Separately, the catalog is consulted before that table, and models.dev rounds the declared 1M up to the next binary size (1,048,576) while listing each K3.1 sub-version under both its dotted and dashed spellings; the previous one-id correction (`kimi-k3`) covered neither. A window larger than the model actually serves makes compaction fire too late, so an over-long request reaches the vendor and is rejected.

Matching the generation once, rather than enumerating ids, is what stops the next sub-version from slipping past: the two spellings models.dev publishes and any later tier are covered by the same rule, and the curated table and the catalog correction can no longer drift apart.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the core unit suites for the window table and the model catalog: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/models src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts`. Expect 10 files and 510 tests passing, including the K3 rows that assert 1,000,000 for each id shape, the 262,144 the generation's 256K variant keeps, and the unchanged 262,144 for `kimi-k2.7-code`.

The decisive check is the mutation witness: empty the generation-wide catalog-correction list and re-run the catalog suite. Four K3 rows must fail with `expected 1048576 to be 1000000`; restore the list and they pass again. That is what proves the new rows are pinned to the catalog correction and not merely to the name table. The 256K variant has its own three witnesses, each of which reddens the corresponding row and was reverted before this was pushed: dropping the `(?!-256k)` exclusion turns the catalog path red (the generation correction lifts a correct 262,144 to 1,000,000); deleting the table row turns the no-cache path red (the id falls to the generic 200,000 default); deleting the id-keyed correction turns the cached path red (an overstated 310,720 is left untouched).

Also worth confirming that the pattern does not over-reach: against both the bundled snapshot and a current models.dev cache, the shared pattern matches Kimi K3 ids only (one key in the bundled snapshot, five in the cache, none of them the 256K variant). The vendor's own read-only model list reports `k3-256k` at 262,144 and the three 1M tiers at 1,048,576 — this PR keeps the documented 1,000,000 for those, which is the same rounding decision the earlier K3 entry already made.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Resolved input window, measured against the same catalogs before and after the change:

| id | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `kimi-k3` | 1,000,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `kimi-k3.1-pro` | 1,048,576 | 1,000,000 |
| `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` | 1,048,576 | 1,000,000 |
| `k3.1-pro` | 200,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `k3.1-pro-highspeed` | 200,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `k3-256k` | 200,000 | 262,144 |
| `kimi-k2.7-code` | 262,144 | 262,144 |

The `200,000` cells are the generic default the bare aliases hit once the table missed them; the mutation witnesses above show exactly those values before the fix.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local checkout at `beaa46b172`, Node 22, `npx vitest` and `npx tsc --noEmit` run from `packages/core`. One read-only `GET /coding/v1/models` against Kimi Code confirmed the vendor's own context lengths; no completion request was made.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the catalog correction is pattern-based, so any id beginning with `kimi-k3` inherits the 1M window unless it is excluded or named ahead of the pattern — which is what `k3-256k` now does. A future smaller variant under a different suffix would need the same treatment; the exclusion is spelled next to the pattern rather than hidden in the table so the next one is hard to miss.
- Not validated / out of scope: no end-to-end request against the vendor at a context above 1M tokens; no change to output-token sizing for the bare aliases, which still take the generic output default rather than K3's 128K.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: ids the catalog had rounded to 1,048,576 now report 1,000,000. Compaction therefore triggers at the window the vendor documents rather than past it; no settings migration is required.

## Linked Issues

No tracking issue — the inconsistency surfaced while wiring Kimi Code's K3.1 aliases into a local provider configuration.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Kimi K3 世代的上下文窗口识别，从"单个 id"改为"整个世代共用一条模式"，由人工维护的窗口表与 models.dev 目录修正共同读取。该世代对外提供的所有 id —— `kimi-k3`、`kimi-k3.1-pro`，以及 Kimi Code 侧的裸别名 `k3.1-pro` / `k3.1-pro-highspeed`（点号与短横两种拼写）——现在都解析为厂商声明的 1,000,000 token 窗口，而不再落到家族兜底值或取整后的目录值。

该世代中唯一共享前缀却不共享窗口的是 256K 变体：`k3-256k` 只有 262,144 token，因此被排除在 1M 模式之外，并在窗口表与目录修正中各自单独列出。

## 为什么需要

Kimi 的 K3.1 档位与 K3 使用同样的 1M 窗口，但两处缺口让它没有按此计算。其一，人工窗口表只匹配以 `kimi-k3` 为前缀的 id，Kimi Code 的裸别名因此落到 Kimi 家族的 256K 兜底（若表完全未命中则落到通用 200K）。其二，目录先于该表被读取，而 models.dev 把声明的 1M 向上取整成下一个二进制尺寸（1,048,576），并把每个 K3.1 子版本按点号与短横两种拼写各列一条；原来的单 id 修正（`kimi-k3`）两处都没覆盖。窗口大于厂商实际可用值时，压缩触发得过晚，超长请求会一直发到厂商侧才被拒绝。

按世代匹配而非枚举 id，正是为了防止下一个子版本再次漏过：models.dev 发布的两种拼写与将来新增的档位都由同一条规则覆盖，人工窗口表与目录修正也不会再各自漂移。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 core 包内运行窗口表与模型目录的单测：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/models src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts`。预期 10 个文件、510 条用例通过，其中包括断言各 id 形态均为 1,000,000 的 K3 系列、世代的 256K 变体保持 262,144，以及保持 262,144 的 `kimi-k2.7-code`。

决定性检查是变异见证：清空按世代的目录修正列表后重跑目录套件，必须有 4 条 K3 用例以 `expected 1048576 to be 1000000` 失败；恢复后转绿。这一步证明新增用例钉住的是目录修正，而不只是名称表。256K 变体另有三个见证，均先转红再还原后才推送：去掉 `(?!-256k)` 排除后缓存路径转红（世代修正把正确的 262,144 抬成 1,000,000）；删除表内 256K 行后无缓存路径转红（落到通用 200,000 默认）；删除目录精确修正后缓存路径转红（偏大的 310,720 未被夹回）。

另需确认该模式没有误伤：在本仓库内置快照与当前 models.dev 缓存上，这条共享模式只命中 Kimi K3 的 id（内置快照 1 条，缓存 5 条，且都不含该 256K 变体）。厂商自己的只读模型清单给出 `k3-256k` 为 262,144、三个 1M 档位为 1,048,576；本 PR 对后者仍采用文档值 1,000,000，与先前 K3 条目的取整判定一致。

### 证据（改动前后）

同一批目录下解析出的输入窗口：

| id | 改动前 | 改动后 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `kimi-k3` | 1,000,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `kimi-k3.1-pro` | 1,048,576 | 1,000,000 |
| `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` | 1,048,576 | 1,000,000 |
| `k3.1-pro` | 200,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `k3.1-pro-highspeed` | 200,000 | 1,000,000 |
| `k3-256k` | 200,000 | 262,144 |
| `kimi-k2.7-code` | 262,144 | 262,144 |

这些 200,000 是裸别名在表中未命中后落到的通用默认值；上面的变异见证正是先跑出这些值再转红。

### 测试环境

在 `beaa46b172` 的本地检出、Node 22 上运行 `packages/core` 下的 `npx vitest` 与 `npx tsc --noEmit`。另对 Kimi Code 做过一次只读 `GET /coding/v1/models`，用于核对厂商自报的窗口；未发起任何补全请求。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：目录修正按模式匹配，任何以 `kimi-k3` 开头的 id 都会继承 1M 窗口，除非被显式排除或在其之前单独命名 —— `k3-256k` 现在正是如此。将来若在别的后缀下发布更小变体，需要同样处理；该排除写在模式旁边而不是藏在表里，正是为了让下一个不易漏掉。
- 未验证 / 范围外：没有针对厂商做超过 1M 上下文的端到端请求；裸别名的输出 token 尺寸未改动，仍取通用输出默认值而非 K3 的 128K。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：目录曾取整到 1,048,576 的 id 现在报告 1,000,000，压缩会在厂商文档的窗口处触发而不是越过它；无需迁移配置。

## 关联 issue

无跟踪 issue —— 该不一致是在把 Kimi Code 的 K3.1 别名接入本地模型配置时发现的。

</details>

author: clouatre
body:
## Summary

Eliminate redundant file reads, stats, and cache-key rebuilds in the analyze tool paths. Internal performance only; no observable behavior change: params, output schema, `structuredContent`, `_meta` fields, and text output stay byte-identical, and `_meta.content_hash` values are golden-identical for identical inputs.

## Related Issues

- Closes #1776
- Depends on #1782 (merge order only; branches are independent, this PR targets `main` and will be rebased if needed)

## Changes

- `crates/aptu-coder/src/tools/analyze_directory.rs`: the sorted `DirectoryCacheKey` is built once before the L1 check and serves both the L1 lookup and the disk key; the previous re-sort + re-hash disk-key path is removed.
- `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/cache.rs`: new `DirectoryCacheKey::disk_key()` hashes the existing key fields with a blake3 streaming hasher, normalizing mtime to seconds. The subsecond-to-seconds normalization is a deliberate one-time invalidation of existing disk entries (benign; documented in code).
- `crates/aptu-coder/src/tools/analyze_file.rs` + `crates/aptu-coder-core/src/analyze.rs`: the file is read once; the same bytes feed the disk-key hash and the analysis (`analyze_file_from_bytes`). Read-failure still maps to empty bytes and a distinct disk key, preserving today's semantics. Eligibility checks reuse `WalkEntry`-cached size/mtime instead of re-statting.
- `crates/aptu-coder/src/tools/analyze_symbol.rs` + `symbol_focused.rs`: `content_hash` is stored on the cached output at put time (hashed over the stored pre-cursor text) and reused on L1 hits — no full-output `String` clone and no `blake3::hash` on hits. Cursor-bearing responses hash the return-local text once, keeping `_meta.content_hash` golden-identical.
- New bench group `cache_paths` in `crates/aptu-coder-core/benches/analysis.rs`; new integration tests in `crates/aptu-coder/tests/analyze_cache_perf_tests.rs`.

## Test Plan

- `cargo test` (896 passing, 0 failed), including new tests: L1 directory hit performs no re-walk (cache_tier metric), symbol L1 hit serves golden `content_hash`, disk-key stability/staleness, bytes-parity for the single-read path
- Staleness: a file modified between calls still misses
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --check` clean

## Benchmarks

`cache_paths` criterion group, before (origin/main) vs after:

| Benchmark | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| directory_key_build | 113.0 µs | 112.6 µs |
| disk_key | 4.5 µs | 3.25 µs |
| file read+hash | 15.1 µs | 15.3 µs |
| symbol hash | 2.4 µs | 2.27 µs |
| overview (end-to-end) | 11.93 ms | 11.45 ms |
| file_details (end-to-end) | 784 µs | 762 µs |

Micro-benchmarks for the removed duplicate work are covered by the new tests (no re-walk on L1 hit, no second read on L2 miss, no clone+hash on symbol hits); end-to-end numbers are within noise on this machine, as expected for cold-path benches — the win is on warm L1-hit calls, which now skip the walk/sort/clone/hash work entirely.

## Verification Checklist

- [x] Tests pass: `cargo test`
- [x] Clippy clean: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
- [x] Formatted: `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `println!`, or `eprintln!` in library code
- [x] No hallucinated APIs (verified against Cargo.lock and crate docs; blake3 1.8.7 streaming hasher)
- [x] Commit GPG signed: `git commit -S`
- [x] DCO signed-off: `git commit --signoff`
- [x] No scope creep (changes match assigned issue)
- [x] No secrets, API keys, or credentials in diff
- [x] If the MCP tool surface changed (params, `structuredContent`, output schema, server instructions), `README.md` and `docs/` are updated to match, and the denylist in `.github/scripts/docs-output-contract-check.sh` was reviewed
- [x] New span attributes comply with the never-record policy in [OBSERVABILITY.md](../OBSERVABILITY.md) (no command strings, file content, or free-form user input)
- [x] I have reviewed every line in this PR and can explain it

`pkg install -y pkg` on the FreeBSD 15.1 image loops: `New version of pkg detected; it needs to be installed first` followed by `The most recent versions of packages are already installed`, so the job never reaches the prerequisites (run 41233057774 timed out at the 300 s bound).

Use the static binary to force-reinstall the matching `pkg` (`pkg-static install -fy pkg`), which breaks the self-upgrade loop, then install the prerequisites. `actionlint` clean.

author: ramazanberk20
body:
VPS diagnostics now show whether the VPS operating system gets automatic security updates, and whether an installed update still waits for a restart. The installer turns on automatic updates only on a VPS that lacks them.

## Why
Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 cloud images already ship `unattended-upgrades` enabled, but provider images vary, and the Owner had no way to tell from the app. A VPN server is usually set up once and then left alone, so silently missing security updates are a real risk.

## What changed
- **Two new VPS diagnostic checks.** Both are warning-only, because neither affects the tunnel. They live in `crates/server/src/diagnostics.rs`.
  - `os_security_updates` passes when all three hold: `/usr/bin/unattended-upgrade` exists, `apt-config` reports a non-zero `APT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade`, and `apt-daily-upgrade.timer` is enabled.
  - `os_reboot_required` warns when `/run/reboot-required` exists, or when a `/boot/vmlinuz-*` file's inode change time is after `btime` in `/proc/stat`. It uses ctime because dpkg keeps the package build time as the file's mtime.
  - Both are read locally on request; nothing is stored.
- **Client.** `crates/core/src/diagnostics/remote.rs` replaces the VPS text with fixed messages and turns any failure level into a warning. `diagnosticEvidence.ts` groups both checks as service state.
- **Installer.** When `unattended-upgrade` is missing, the installer installs `unattended-upgrades`, writes the standard `20auto-upgrades` file and enables the APT timers. An existing setup, even a deliberately disabled one, is left unchanged, and the VPS is never restarted automatically. This uses the existing "package installation is not rolled back" policy.
- **Docs.** `docs/current-diagnostics-2026-09-07.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `PRIVACY.md` now cover this. Where the installer adds the package, the VPS contacts its distribution mirrors daily, as stock cloud images already do.

## Verification
- `./scripts/test.sh` passes: 555 Rust tests, 245 vitest, 16 Python, privacy gate.
- New unit tests:
  - `apt-config` value parsing (`'1'`, `'7'`, `'0'`, empty, non-numeric);
  - restart detection (flag file, change time before and after boot, unreadable inputs);
  - the client turning `os_security_updates: fail` into a warning;
  - the installer script installing and enabling only when the package is missing.
- Two-VM Linux lab: all 29 checks pass. The first run warned on a real Debian VPS, so I kept the VMs alive and ran the probes as the `sirinvpn` user under the server unit's exact sandbox. `apt-config` returned `'1'` and `systemctl` worked, but `apt-daily-upgrade.timer` was disabled, because the lab itself disables the APT timers (`tests/vm/lab.py`) so they can't take the dpkg lock. The lab now checks both outcomes on the real VPS: a warning with the timer off, and a pass after `systemctl enable apt-daily-upgrade.timer` (the timer is not started and is disabled again afterwards). `os_reboot_required` passed.

## Not covered
- The install-when-missing path wasn't run end to end, because the lab image already has `unattended-upgrades`. Only the generated script text is tested.
- Older clients show the two new codes as a "server report format" compatibility warning, as they do for any new VPS check.

## Summary
