author: woahwhattheheck
body:
Spoiler updates currently compare only a prefix of the downloaded file and can replace the last usable database before the download is known to be complete. Overlapping requests and database reloads can also complete after Settings has changed, while closing Settings abandons a manual update.

This change keeps the update tied to its selected settings and destination, hashes the complete file, validates the full Cockatrice XML document structure and supported format, and uses an atomic file replacement. Invalid downloads or failed writes leave the prior file available.

Updater-owned database reloads run in sequence, with completion reported after the reload finishes. A manual Update retries the reload even when the downloaded bytes are unchanged. Disabling spoilers removes the file and refreshes the in-memory database, including when the file has already been removed.

Manual updates are owned by the application and continue after Settings closes. Superseded replies retire with their original request, the current update alone controls its button, and download, removal or reload errors appear in the existing Settings workflow.

author: colbymchenry
body:
Follow-up to #3187. A lambda or a method reference has no type of its own, so
the overload reader left it unread, and where overloads differ at that argument
the ranking's pick stood: Minestom's `.append(x, b -> …)` reached
`append(Argument, Execution)`, `item.withAmount(a -> a * 2)` reached
`withAmount(int)`, and `setDefaultValue(sender -> …)` the bare `T`.

The fix: javaArgumentType reads a lambda, with the count of its parameters, or
a method reference as a function value, and javaFunctionFit scores it against a
parameter. 1 for a JDK functional interface (java.util.function's, `Runnable`,
`Callable`, `Comparator`) whose method takes as many arguments as the lambda
has. 0 for what may be one: another interface, a library type, a type variable.
-1 for what can't take one: a primitive, `String`, `Object`, an array, a project
class or enum, and a JDK interface of another count. So `defaulted(s -> s)` is
the `Function` overload and `defaulted(() -> x)` the `Supplier` one. A string or
a number is no function for any JDK functional interface now, not only the ones
a lambda's parameter is read from. And a number may start at its point:
`spawnPos.sub(.5)` is `sub(double)`; `2d` is a double.

A project's own `@FunctionalInterface` isn't scored. I tried it: elasticsearch's
`parseList(parser, p -> …)` has a marked `CheckedBiFunction` in the index and its
`CheckedFunction` outside, and the marked one took 10 true calls to the wrong
overload. So two project interfaces tie, the ranking's pick stands, and Minestom's
`RegistryTaggedUnion(Registries::x, …)` stays open.

Validation:
- java-overload-arguments.test.ts: 5 of 27 cases fail on main, all pass.
- The 78 Java, JVM and resolution test files, 890 tests, pass. The change doesn't
  reach past Java: every new branch sits in the Java overload reader.
- A/B against main 15483713, calls moved: Minestom 27, spring-ai 137, kestra 45,
  elasticsearch 101. jsoup, rocksdb's java/ and okhttp unchanged, nothing added or
  lost anywhere. Controls serilog and flask identical.
- Read against source: all 27 on Minestom, and every group on spring-ai (14),
  kestra (5) and elasticsearch (37). True, except two classes that were false on
  main as well. spring-ai's 37 `SearchRequest.from(r).filterExpression("…")` sit on
  a wrong class before and after, and move between two of its overloads because
  a string is no `Supplier`. elasticsearch's 6 `stringListSetting(key, value -> …,
  Property.Dynamic)` move from `(String, Property...)` to `(String, List<String>,
  Property...)`, where `Validator` is right: `List` and `Validator` both may be
  functional, so the first of the count stands.
- The class #3187 left open, moved calls whose arguments don't settle the overload,
  recounted: jsoup 28 to 27, rocksdb 209 unchanged (no lambda among them), Minestom
  70 to 61, spring-ai 24 to 81. spring-ai rises because 57
  `FunctionToolCallback.builder("x", (City c) -> …)` calls now move to the right
  overload and stay open between `Function` and `Consumer`, each of one parameter.
  All calls left open, moved or not: jsoup 207 to 206, rocksdb 267 unchanged,
  Minestom 567 to 533, spring-ai 1,167 to 1,109.
- Read: all 61 left open on Minestom. 20 are on a wrong overload, all false on main
  too: 5 `RegistryTaggedUnion`, 4 `register(Key.key(…), …)`, 3 `allocateTrimmedPacket`
  with a `var` packet, 2 `Duration.of(…)`, 2 static-imported constants, 2
  `div(…get())`, 1 `setDefaultValue(Block.AIR)`, 1 on a wrong class.
- CPU, elasticsearch, median of 5 interleaved: 134.17 to 130.89 s, so no cost. Resolution only.

**Tests:** own file 27 passed; 78 Java, JVM and resolution files, 890 tests passed on this commit over main 4e96d759. No full suite: the change doesn't reach past Java.

author: excdinc-kassy
body:
Fixes #121

The settings preview painted once and then stretched downwards — a header at
the top, an enormous empty column below it, still growing. Nothing logged.

## Cause

The partial measured the framed document and wrote the result back as the
frame's own height, re-running from a `ResizeObserver` on its body:

```js
var height = Math.max(doc.documentElement.scrollHeight, doc.body.scrollHeight);
frame.style.height = height + 'px';
```

That cannot converge. The page inside is sized **in viewport units** —
`min-h-screen` on the body, the hero at `h-screen` — and inside an iframe the
viewport *is* the frame:

1. frame is *H* tall → hero is *H* tall
2. `scrollHeight` = *H* + header + content + footer (call the rest *R*)
3. frame becomes *H + R* → hero becomes *H + R*
4. `scrollHeight` = *H + R + R*
5. the observer fires, repeat

Each pass adds *R*. The measurement is an input to the thing it measures.

## Not a regression from the recent work

The loop has been in the code since the preview was rebuilt in #80. The frame
was **blank** until #118 let the browser render it, so there was never
anything to measure. This is the first time it could be seen.

## Fix

The frame now takes the height of the device the operator picked, and the page
scrolls inside it — the shape core's front page preview already uses
(`admin/front/index.blade.php` gives its iframe the preset's height and scales
it with a transform). With the height fixed, nothing about the content can
feed back into it, and `h-screen` inside the frame means one screen, as it
does on the real page.

The measuring block — `syncHeight`, the `load` hook, the `ResizeObserver`, the
`fonts.ready` hook — is deleted rather than guarded.

## Two things worth knowing

**The container's `aspectRatio` prop looked like the fix and is not.** It
takes one ratio for every device, so locking to the desktop 16:10 would render
the mobile preview as a **375×234 letterbox**. Tried and rejected.

**The device heights are written out in the theme.** They are the numbers the
container's own device buttons name in their tooltips — 375×667, 768×1024,
1440×900 — but it tracks only the widths (`DEVICE_WIDTHS`). They belong next
to the widths and the tooltips that already quote them; worth raising against
core, noted in the comment.

## Verified

The partial compiles; it no longer mentions `scrollHeight` or constructs a
`ResizeObserver`, and the iframe height is bound from `previewDevice`.

**Not verified: how it looks.** No browser in this session. The frame is now a
fixed box, so the runaway is gone by construction, but the result is worth one
glance before release.

## Test

`PreviewFrameHeightTest` encodes the narrow rule — do not derive the frame's
height from the frame's content — rather than the shape of this fix. The
defect had no symptom for as long as the frame was empty, which is exactly
when a test earns its place.

## Re-signing

One tracked file changes and one is added, so the theme needs re-signing
before its next release.

---

設定のプレビューは一度描画されたあと下に伸びていました。上にヘッダー、その下に
巨大な空の列があり、伸び続けます。ログには何も出ません。

## 原因

partial が枠の中の文書を計測し、その結果をフレーム自身の高さとして書き戻し、
body の `ResizeObserver` から再実行していました（コードは英語側）。

これは収束しません。中のページは**ビューポート単位**で大きさが決まっており
（body の `min-h-screen`、ヒーローの `h-screen`）、iframe の中ではビューポート
とは**フレームのこと**だからです。

1. フレームが *H* → ヒーローも *H*
2. `scrollHeight` = *H* ＋ ヘッダー・コンテンツ・フッター（残りを *R* とする）
3. フレームが *H + R* に → ヒーローも *H + R* に
4. `scrollHeight` = *H + R + R*
5. オブザーバが発火、繰り返し

1 周ごとに *R* 増えます。計測結果が計測対象への入力になっています。

## 最近の作業の回帰ではありません

ループはプレビューを作り直した #80 からコードにありました。#118 でブラウザが
描画するようになるまでフレームは**空**で、計測するものがありませんでした。今回
初めて見えたということです。

## 修正

フレームは運用者が選んだデバイスの高さを取り、ページはその中でスクロールします。
コアのフロントページのプレビューが既に取っている形です
（`admin/front/index.blade.php` は iframe にプリセットの高さを与え、transform で
縮小します）。高さが固定なら、中身がそこに跳ね返る経路はありません。そして
フレーム内の `h-screen` が、実ページと同じ「1 画面」を意味するようになります。

計測のブロック（`syncHeight`、`load` のフック、`ResizeObserver`、`fonts.ready`
のフック）はガードではなく削除しました。

## 知っておく価値のある 2 点

**コンテナの `aspectRatio` プロパティは一見この修正に見えますが違います。**
全デバイスに対して比率が 1 つなので、デスクトップの 16:10 に固定すると
モバイルのプレビューが **375×234 のレターボックス**になります。試して却下しました。

**デバイスの高さはテーマ側に書き出しています。** コンテナ自身のデバイスボタンが
ツールチップで名乗っている値（375×667、768×1024、1440×900）ですが、コンテナは
幅しか持っていません（`DEVICE_WIDTHS`）。本来は幅と、既にその値を書いている
ツールチップの隣にあるべきで、コアに提起する価値があります。コメントに残しました。

## 確認

partial はコンパイルでき、`scrollHeight` にも `ResizeObserver` の生成にも触れて
おらず、iframe の高さは `previewDevice` から束縛されています。

**未確認: 見た目。** このセッションではブラウザが使えませんでした。フレームは
固定の箱になったので暴走は構造的に消えていますが、リリース前に一度見る価値は
あります。

## テスト

`PreviewFrameHeightTest` は、この修正の形ではなく狭い規則 —「フレームの高さを
フレームの中身から導かない」— を固定します。この欠陥はフレームが空である限り
症状が出ませんでした。テストが価値を持つのはまさにそういう場合です。

## 再署名

追跡ファイル 1 個が変わり、1 個増えるので、次のリリースの前に再署名が必要です。

## Summary

Follow up on the review of merged #70 with two focused water-discovery fixes:

- Discover missing water entities after successful coordinator refreshes, so an initial API failure no longer requires an integration reload. Newly appearing water meters are discovered as well.

#70 has merged. This branch is rebased onto current `main` and contains one follow-up fix commit; the original #70 commit is no longer part of this PR's diff/history.

This remains a small foundation for #54's planned rework: the existing primary entity identities/behavior and water IDs `mijnted_<entry>_water_<type>_device_<number>` are preserved. The #54 author can build on the recovered discovery and primary-water support when rebasing the per-meter work.

body:
Arregla #133 y #134.

- **#133**: el paso que borra de `scripts/respaldo-anonimo.sh` ahora anula el nombre del cliente y las notas de los borradores de pedido. Se revisó todo el texto libre, y también se borra lo que pasaba intacto: motivos de pago devuelto, de baja y de apertura de caja, la nota del arqueo manual, el nombre de quien recibe la propina, la IP y el aparato de la asistencia, el antes y el después de la bitácora, la lectura del ticket de gastos, los correos del resumen del día, el contacto de las sucursales, el nombre del proveedor, las preferencias de pantalla y las credenciales de los operadores de la consola. `FUGAS` cuenta cada una de esas columnas.
- **#134**: `TestEveryColumnIsCoveredByTheAnonymousBackup` recorre el catálogo de la base migrada. Toda columna que no sea número, fecha, booleano o enum tiene que borrarse en el script (y contarse en `FUGAS`) o estar en `noPersonalData` con su porqué. La prueba también corre el paso y `FUGAS` contra el esquema actual. Reemplaza a la prueba de shell, así que el aviso pasa del pre-commit a la integración de CI.

Verificado en local con el respaldo del 2026-10-22, corriendo el script completo:

author: deehw
body:
**Outcome:** the drawing generator can now draw assembly sheets outside Fusion, in a new module (`tools/drawgen/assembly.py`) with its own read-back. Here is the sample of three, each with read-back PASS:
- **110101 BASE band assembly:** 8 table rows, 6 balloons, 10 interface sizes.
- **410101 CEILING panel C1:** 10 rows, 4 balloons, with the D-147 build-up section.
- **610101 AIR air column:** 9 rows, 9 balloons, with a section across the column.

They need a Reviewer's D-114 visual pass before they count.

**What a sheet has** (guideline 5.1, 5.2, 6; D-139, D-140, D-147):
- **Views:** first-angle views of the assembly's own parts, from the team STEP of the same revision: exact hidden-line projection, visible lines. A sub-assembly is one item. The views are only the ones needed to show every part and the three overall sizes, or the ones the entry names.
- **Sections:** where parts hide, each part's cut face is hatched its own way and thin ones are filled solid. A part the STEP puts under the assembly but the list doesn't is a reference outline in the phantom line, not hatched, with a note. AIR's cartridge 610301 is one: it ships on its own and slides in on site (D-61).
- **Balloons:** one per part number. The leader ends in an arrowhead on a free edge of that part (ISO 128-22), or in a dot on its face when every edge lies against another part (the column's fill).
- **Parts table:** the list's rows under the assembly, word for word (item, number, name, quantity, material, finish). Family 84 quantities are in metres. Rows the STEP doesn't model are marked * with no balloon (CEILING's hardware, BASE's held M10 nut and end cap).
- **Sizes:** the overall sizes, plus the interface ordinates and build-up sections an entry names. A build-up gets its layer faces and a balloon on each layer, D-147 (2) (CEILING's skin, bond gap and frame at 1:2).
- **Notes and title block:** the fixing order from the list's notes. The project title block says Autonomous as CREATED BY and as the PDF's author, with no maker line (D-140, D-147).

**Read-back** (every sheet, `assembly.check`):
- Every table row equals its list row.
- Every balloon:
  - names its table row;
  - names a part under the assembly in the STEP's tree (the repo's own STEP reader);
  - ends at an arrowhead or dot drawn where its 3D point projects through its view;
  - has that point in or on the part's solid, within 0.05 mm.
- Every part the STEP has carries a balloon.
- The interface ordinates measure again from the STEP.
- No text touches text or an outline, and no line runs through a text.
- What the mechanical check reads (UNITS: mm, MATERIAL:, FINISH:, TOLERANCE).

**Entries:** each team's file holds `ASSEMBLIES` (D-139): `teams/base.py` (110101), new `teams/ceiling.py` (410101) and new `teams/air.py` (610101). The keys are listed in assembly.py's docstring.

**Run it:** `<drawgen venv>/bin/python tools/drawgen/assembly.py generate 110101` (or `check PDF`).

**Not in this PR:**
- **The two hooks:** `specs.py` gathering `ASSEMBLIES` as kind "assembly", and `drawgen.py` handing it to this module, so `run.sh generate` draws assembly sheets too. They're asked of the Drawing Generator Engineer and wait for their OK.
- **The other 30 sheets:** they follow team by team, then the cassettes (510301, WALL's six) with the facts CEILING sends.
- **Weld notes and cut lists:** none of the three samples is a weldment on main. 410101's frame is still aluminium until CEILING's D-131 steel list lands.

**Checks, merged with main c35687c:**
- drawgen tests 21 of 21;
- assembly tests 10 of 10 (five are planted errors the read-back must catch: a changed table cell, a moved balloon, a wrong part, a part without a balloon, a line through a label);
- `tools/checks/tests` 144 passed;
- release checklist tests 87 passed;
- control pack OK, `build_master_bom.py --no-write` OK, `pack.py --check` OK, `run_all.py --check` OK;
- the mechanical checks lose the three C05 "no drawing" findings for 110101, 410101 and 610101, with no new finding;
- the sheets regenerate byte-identical on the merged tree.

**Most likely wrong here:**
- the view choice and balloon spread on assemblies much bigger than these three (the team-level sheets 110000, 410000, 610000);
- a section's plane, which is the entry's choice and needs the reviewer's eye.

author: hartiganhm
body:
Add a card from anywhere, PR 3 of 4: a **+ on every search result row** (direction C).

- **The +.** It sits after the bookmark: 44px on phone, 34px from `md`, with a `--border-strong` edge. A press opens Add cards through the shell host (#2576) with that card on the list, its printings open, no default and Save waiting (C4, C-D2). The press doesn't open card details. The + is off on `/card/…` and outside `CollectionEditScope` (E6).
- **O4, ⌘↵ kept.** ⌘↵ or Ctrl ↵ on the active row does the same add, from the field or a focused row. A held key adds once. The + is a pointer target, hidden from assistive tech and out of the tab order.
  - On a keyboard device (fine pointer or ≥768px), the row's name ends "add to your collection with Command Enter" and carries `aria-keyshortcuts`.
  - On a phone the name stays as shipped. Phone screen-reader users add through card details → Add to collection (#2575). That path was confirmed on the walk.
  - Recorded as READINESS E8.
- **O6, re-read.** Closing the sheet brings the search back with its query, scroll, focus and ring on the row. If the sheet saved, the search re-runs the query and re-reads the recent cards' ownership in place. That covers Add several too.
  - The saved row's count reads in `--success` while its ring shows (C6, C-D3; E9).
  - A dropped ask (a sheet already up, another modal) reopens the search instead of leaving it under the veil.
- **Desktop foot line.** It reads "↑ ↓ to move · ↵ to open · ⌘↵ to add". "esc to close" is dropped to fit 540px (E8).

**Copy** (`/copy-review`, E8): the + label is tightened so the row name doesn't repeat the card's name. The ⌘↵ / Ctrl ↵ and Command / Control Enter key names stay as drafted.

## Walk (feature-acceptance)

Neon scratch branch made from local-dev. It has been deleted.

| | 390 (touch emulation) | 1300 |
|---|---|---|
| **+ on a row with 0 owned** | Sheet with the card and printings. Pick a printing, then Save 1 copy and Done. The search returns with the query kept, focus and ring on the row, and ×1 in `--success`. | Same |
| **⌘↵** | — | Same flow from the arrowed row |
| **Earlier saved row** | Reads ×1 in normal color | Same |
| **Row name** | No keys clause | Command Enter clause and `Meta+Enter` |

The deck page behind updated its figures.

## Claude review

`cavecrew-reviewer` found 2 critical, 3 risks and 1 question.
- **Critical:** the first (the + return skips scroll and focus) was verified as not a bug. The return path sets `returned`, and both walks saw focus come back. The second, a test asserting the scroll on the wrong element, is fixed.
- **Risks:** all fixed. Held-key repeat is guarded. A dropped ask now reopens the search. Real `Rows` and `SearchRow` integration tests are added.
- **Question:** phone screen readers, answered above.

The pre-open pass caught a stale "just saved" marker after Add several. Fixed.

author: asuresh8
body:
## What the first full run showed

The first complete `pf_as_root` run on a macOS 27.0.1 host (root, after #599) printed this table. Four of 17 probes did not show what was expected; the security property held. `<own>` is the host's own address.

```text
ok   uid 4100  <own>:49959       listed                  got connected
ok   uid 4100  <own>:49960       own host, other port    got timed out   expected RefusedOrDropped
FAIL uid 4100  169.254.169.254:80 metadata address       got timed out   expected Refused
FAIL uid 4100  198.51.100.1:80   unlisted address        got timed out   expected Refused
ok   uid 4100  127.0.0.1:49961   loopback                got connected
(uid 4109: the same five rows, the same results)
ok   uid 4099 / 4110  <own>:49960  outside the range     got connected
ok   uid 4200  <own>:49959       control, listed         got connected
ok   uid 4200  <own>:49960       control, own host       got connected
ok   uid 4200  169.254.169.254:80 control, metadata      got timed out
ok   uid 4200  198.51.100.1:80   control, documentation  got failed: host unreachable
ok   uid 4100  <own>:49960       after remove            got connected
```

The anchor was empty afterwards. Two things follow.

1. `block return` gives no reset off the host either. #599 predicted that for lo0 only; the same checksum gate (`pf_test_rule` calls `pf_check_proto_cksum` before `pf_send_tcp`, xnu `bsd/net/pf.c`) applies to the physical interface, so a blocked TCP connect from a pool uid is dropped silently and times out on macOS. Only a host that answers itself would refuse.
2. The control uid cannot reach the metadata address (timed out) or the documentation address (host unreachable) either. For those two targets the client's outcome alone cannot tell "pf blocked it" from "there is no such host", so it proves nothing about pf.

## The change

A blocked probe is now proven by pf's own counters, not by the error.

- New `counters` module: parses `pfctl -a <anchor> -s rules -vv` (a `@N <rule>` line followed by `[ Evaluations: E Packets: P Bytes: B States: S ]`) into per-rule counters, sums the packets of the TCP block rules of one uid (pf expands `user { ... }` and `proto { ... }` lists into one rule per element), and takes the difference between two reads. Unit tests run it on a listing, every error shape, uid-list forms and the difference.
- `pf_as_root` reads the anchor's counters before and after each blocked probe. A blocked row passes only if the blocking rule's packet counter rose by at least 1 **and** the outcome is "refused" or "timed out". "connected" fails, and so does any other error (for example "host unreachable"): it would mean routing refused the connect and pf did not.
- If the counters cannot be read, the row is reported `UNPROVEN`, which fails the test.
- The own-address special case is gone. Every blocked probe has the same expectation.
- For each blocked target the table also records the control uid's outcome, and the counter rise. The own-address listener on an unlisted port stays in: the control connects there and the pool uid must not, so the counter has a case where the outcome is not in doubt.
- The README and the `render` docs drop the fail-fast claim for TCP: on macOS a blocked TCP connect is dropped silently and the job's connect times out. They cite the xnu reason. They do not claim anything about UDP; the source path for a UDP `block return` (`pf_send_icmp`, no checksum gate in that function) suggests an ICMP unreachable, but no run has shown it.

The rendered rules do not change.

## Not verified

I could not capture real `pfctl -vv` text. The listing in `tests/golden/pfctl_sr_vv.txt` is written after the documented format, not captured; the exact spacing, and whether `user = 4100` is printed with the `=`, are unconfirmed. The parser ignores spacing and accepts the user clause with or without `=` and with a brace list. If the real text differs, the next run reports the rows `UNPROVEN` with the parse error in the table, and the golden file is then replaced with the real text.

The real proof is the next `pf_as_root` run on a macOS 27 host.

## Squash commit

```text
js-mac-provision: prove a pf block by the rule's packet counter; TCP blocks time out on macOS

The first full pf_as_root run showed that `block return` sends no reset for a
pool uid's TCP connect off the host either: pf builds the reset only after
pf_check_proto_cksum accepts the packet, and an outbound SYN on an interface
with checksum assist does not have its checksum yet. The connect is blocked
and times out. The control uid could not reach the metadata or documentation
address either, so the client's error alone proved nothing about pf.

A new counters module parses `pfctl -a <anchor> -s rules -vv`. pf_as_root
reads the blocking rule's packet counter before and after each blocked probe
and passes the row only if the counter rose and the outcome is "refused" or
"timed out"; "connected" and other errors fail, and an unreadable counter is
"unproven". The table records the control uid's outcome and the counter rise.
The own-address special case is removed. The README and the render docs no
longer promise a fast refusal for TCP. The rendered rules are unchanged.
```

body:
Tool results now go through pure shapers (`src/tools/_shape.ts`) instead of returning Wave's raw payloads: a one-line paid invoice drops from 37 KB to 4.5 KB of JSON and no longer carries two ledger-account records per line tax or customers' saved card details, while every id the write tools need stays in place (`raw: true` on the two invoice reads returns the full record). Wave's endpoints, GraphQL documents, request-body keys and variable names are unchanged; the no-session live contract suite passes with no drift. Based on main at 3daf6a1 (after #6 and #7).

- Errors tell the model what Wave rejected: `WaveApiError` carries a body excerpt, GraphQL errors their code and path, and `didSucceed: false` payloads throw `WaveMutationError` instead of coming back as data.
- Defaults follow the workspace, not one user's conventions: invoice headings, footer, memo, payment terms and currency come from the business and its invoice settings; "today" is the local day, not UTC; `wave_update_invoice` is a partial update that reads first and keeps discounts, attachments, tags and approval state; estimates get the next free number and the business currency.
- New inputs: customer `search` (walks up to ten pages), estimate `status` filter replacing the three buckets, account `accountType` filter; `wave_send_invoice` is marked destructive and `wave_get_business` exposes the verified sender addresses it needs.
- Security and hygiene: the HTTP transport requires `WAVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` off loopback, rejects DNS-rebinding Host headers and oversized bodies; hidden prompts decode passwords as UTF-8; credentials.json is chmod 0600 on every write; dead exports, a duplicate CLI case and `.env.example` (nothing loaded it) are gone.

author: lrssn
body:
## Summary

Two additions to the C++ guide, found while recording Lmath's exceptions to it (Lrssn/Lmath#59 on Gitea):

- **Exceptions to the naming rules**: a library whose domain already has its own naming may use it for its whole public API, recorded in an ADR. Example: a graphics math library following GLSL and `<cmath>` (`dot`, `pi`, `Containment::inside`). Private members and helpers still follow the guide. This is a broader version of the Google guide's rule for names analogous to existing C or C++ entities.
- **Testing**: Catch2 is allowed next to GoogleTest, one framework per project. With Catch2, test names are sentences. The section explains when Catch2 fits (`STATIC_CHECK` for `constexpr` results, `TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE` for several types) and shows an example built on the guide's own `Gcd`.

- `npx markdownlint-cli2`: 0 issues.

author: atriumnook
body:
## Summary

Claude Code などの関連ツールが `.claude/settings.json` を書き戻すと、キーと配列の並びが変わる。実際の変更と並べ替えだけの変更が差分に混ざらないよう、git の clean filter `jsonsort` で、保存する前に並びを揃える。exec form の hook の `args` だけは並べ替えない。

```diff
 .gitattributes
+.claude/settings.json filter=jsonsort

 .config/git/dotfiles.gitconfig        # mise が全マシンの ~/.gitconfig から include させている
+[filter "jsonsort"]
+    clean = "jq -S 'def norm: ...オブジェクトはキー順、配列は sort。ただし args は触らない...; norm'"

 .claude/settings.json                 # git add --renormalize(値は変えず、並びだけ)
 .github/scripts/bootstrap-test.sh     # 新しいマシンで filter が効くことの check を2つ
```

[kawarimidoll さんの記事](https://zenn.dev/kawarimidoll/articles/d3f1a7542de71a)の [`jsonsort`](https://github.com/kawarimidoll/dotfiles/blob/8cf9601f143ace89048575c41569853b555fbda8/.config/git/config#L136-L138) と同じ方式で、違いは `args` を外したところだけ。

- hook の配列は並べ替えてよい。[hooks のドキュメント](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)に "When an event fires, its matching hooks run in parallel." とある
- exec form の `args` は "each `args` element is one argument exactly as written" で、順番が引数の並びそのもの。`["--write","--config","f"]` を sort すると `--config` の値が `--write` になる
- clean filter の出力はそのまま保存され、checkout で作業ツリーに出る(smudge が無い)。作業ツリーのファイルが mise で `~/.claude/settings.json` に merge される実際の設定なので、意味が変わる並べ替えは保存の段階でしてはいけない

git config では値の中の `;` がコメントになるため、`clean` の値全体を `"..."` で囲んでいる(囲まないと式が `; norm'` の手前で切れ、filter が失敗して素通しになった)。

## Evidence

- 試作用の clone で、キーと配列を並べ替えたうえで allow のルールを1つ足すと、素の diff は 145 行、`git diff` は `+ "Bash(ls:*)",` の1行だけ。並べ替えだけなら `git status` も空。`args` の並びを変えたときは差分に出る
- Claude Code に project の設定を書かせると、入力の並びに関係なくトップレベルのキーを同じ順に並べ直す(逆順にしたファイルでも同じ出力)。main の版は `model` が末尾にあるため、CLI が書くたびに `model` が `permissions` の後ろに移って差分になっていた
- renormalize の前後で、配列を sort して比べた値は一致する(並びだけの変更)
- 追加した CI の check を、偽の HOME でローカルに動かした:

| `filter.jsonsort.clean` | キーの並べ替えは差分にならない | hook の args は並べ替えずに保存する |
| :- | :- | :- |
| このPRの式 | PASS | PASS |
| 未定義 | FAIL | FAIL |
| 記事の式(`walk(... sort ...)`) | — | FAIL(`["--config","--write","f"]`) |

- `shellcheck` の指摘は main と同じ既存の2件(SC2016)のみ

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

revert で filter が外れる。保存済みの `settings.json` はキー順のまま残るが、値は同じ。

**Blast Radius:** 全マシンの git と `~/.dotfiles/.claude/settings.json`

- マージ後に clone・checkout すると、作業ツリーの `settings.json` はキー順・配列 sort 済みになり、その内容が `~/.claude/settings.json` に merge される。今の配列は空か要素1つなので、値は変わらない
- filter の定義が無いマシン、または jq が見つからないマシンでは、エラーは出ずに素通しになる(jq が無いと `error: external filter ... failed 127` と表示される)。そこで commit すると並べ替えていない内容が保存されるが、壊れはしない
- `dotfiles.gitconfig` は全 repo に読まれるが、`filter=jsonsort` を割り当てた path にしか効かない
- Windows の CI(`bootstrap-test.ps1`)には同じ check を足していない。filter の後に `eol=lf` が働くので CRLF にはならない想定だが、Windows の jq では試していない

body:
## Qué cambia

Tres mejoras del portapapeles de clips (1.1):

1. **Pegar insertando** (`edit.pasteInsert`, **Ctrl+Alt+V** en Rodaje, Ágil y Clásico; en Editar y en el menú del clip): `TimelineEdits.Paste` admite `PlacementMode.Insert` y abre un solo espacio del largo de lo copiado en las pistas donde cae, con los enlazados de lo que se corre (`TrackOps.InsertSpaceLinked`, como al mover insertando), en vez de tapar. Un paso del historial («Pegar insertando»). La tecla está libre en los tres estilos y en todos los catálogos (lo comprueba `NingunEstiloTieneDosAccionesConLaMismaTecla`).
2. **Pegar en otro proyecto:** `ClipClipboard` guarda ahora copias de los `MediaRef` de lo copiado. `ResolveMedia(Project)` dice qué medios están (mismo id y archivo), cuáles están con otro identificador (se renombran con `WithMediaRenamed`) y cuáles hay que importar. La sesión (`PasteAtPlayheadAsync`) importa los que falten por la ruta de su archivo con `ImportMediaAsync` (paso «Importar medio» aparte) y, si el archivo no existe, avisa «No se pudo pegar» con la ruta y no pega nada.
3. **Transiciones interiores:** copiar y duplicar llevan las transiciones cuyos dos clips están en la selección (`ClipClipboard.Transitions`), también con «ignorar grupos»; al pegar se clonan entre las copias con identificadores nuevos y `EnsureValid` las concilia con sus cortes.

Guía `docs/guia/atajos.md` regenerada con `RODAJE_ESCRIBIR_ATAJOS=1` y `ShortcutGuideTests` (la hoja imprimible de Ayuda sale del mismo catálogo en tiempo de ejecución; no hay archivo en el repo). `docs/guia/edicion.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` («Sin publicar») y `docs/pruebas-a-mano.md` al día. Incluye `git merge origin/main`.

## Por qué

Lo pedido para la 1.1: pegar sin pisar lo que sigue (como el pegar insertando de otros editores), que el portapapeles sobreviva de verdad al cambio de proyecto y que una selección con transiciones se copie entera.

## Cómo se probó

- `tests/Rodaje.Core.Tests/Editing/Organize/PasteInsertAndTransitionsTests.cs` (13 pruebas): insertar corre y parte lo que pasa por el cursor, abre un solo espacio con enlazados y no toca pistas ajenas, falla sin cambiar nada con una pista bloqueada; transiciones al copiar, duplicar, con ignorar grupos y las que no se llevan; `ResolveMedia`/`WithMediaRenamed`; el comando se deshace entero y rechaza `Strict`.
- `tests/Rodaje.App.Tests/Session/ClipboardSessionTests.cs` (4 pruebas): pegar insertando desde la sesión, importar por ruta en un proyecto nuevo (deshacer deja el medio), reutilizar el medio ya importado, y aviso sin cambios si el archivo no existe.
- En esta sesión (Linux, sin WinUI): `Rodaje.Core.Tests` completo en verde (3172) con `-warnaserror`; `Rodaje.App.Tests` compilado para `linux-x64` con 0 advertencias y las pruebas de atajos, sesión y portapapeles en verde. Las 83 pruebas de App que fallan en Linux fallan igual en `main` (API de Windows, rutas, módulos).
- Pendiente en Windows: `Probar.bat` y `Rodaje.bat` (AOT 0 advertencias, arranque); los pasos nuevos de `docs/pruebas-a-mano.md` «Portapapeles».

- [x] `Probar.bat` pasa en local (o `build\dotnet-local.cmd test`) — Core y las pruebas de App afectadas, en Linux; la solución entera la corre la CI de Windows.
- [ ] Si tocó `src\Rodaje.App`: `Rodaje.bat` compila y publica con Native AOT con 0 advertencias, y la app arranca correctamente.
- [x] Las pruebas nuevas no usan `Skip` salvo justificación por falta de hardware (con `[Trait("Categoria", "...")]`).

## Lista de comprobación

- [ ] **Firma DCO:** Todos los commits llevan `Signed-off-by: Nombre <correo>` (`git commit -s`), coincidente con la autoría.
- [x] **Licencia y procedencia:** El código es original o bajo licencia permisiva compatible (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD); sin código GPL externo ni activos comerciales.
- [x] **Convenciones de estilo:** Identificadores en inglés; comentarios, textos de interfaz, notas y commits en español.
- [x] **Zonas protegidas:** No modifica archivos protegidos (`build/`, `.github/`, `LICENSE`, `CLAUDE.md`, `TRADEMARK.md`, dependencias en `packages.lock.json` o `UpstreamAttribution.cs`) salvo autorización expresa en el issue.
- [x] **Documentación:** Si altera interfaz o comportamiento de usuario, se actualizó la guía en `docs/guia/` o `docs/arquitectura/`.
- [x] **Compatibilidad de proyecto:** Si altera el modelo `.rodaje`, se incrementó `schemaVersion` y se añadió migración con prueba hacia atrás. (No cambia el modelo.)

body:
## Problem

The Pull requests page is empty when a project is rooted at a non-Git folder containing repositories, even when its threads have linked PRs. Repository discovery drops the project because it has no repository identity.

## Change

Use saved thread PR links to discover repositories for projects without a resolved Git identity, limited to providers that already support public-host reads without a checkout. Reuse existing listing, filtering and pagination; prefer registered checkouts when deduplicating. Route details and stats by repository when a project has multiple linked repositories. Keep linked-repository routing in the selected project and require a host for ambiguous repository names.

## Scope and approval

This is a focused fix for an existing listing defect: PRs already linked to workspace threads disappear from the workspace PR page. No directory scanning, new providers or settings. The optional stats host field and web/mobile matching changes keep counts correct when one project links identical repository names on different hosts. Searched open issues and PRs first and found no matching report; #21530 and #26281 address separate cross-machine selection problems. Submitted under the focused obvious-bug exception, without prior maintainer approval.

## Verification

- The regression failed before the fix: selecting a non-Git project with links to two repositories returned `[]`.
- After the fix, focused tests verify open/merged listing, archived links, project scoping, duplicate links, checkout deduplication, excluded deleted/side-chat/dismissed links, repository-specific details and stats.
- `vp run check:changed` passed formatting, lint, both knip passes, GraphQL validation, affected typechecks and 111 tests across three files.
- Independent GPT-6.1 Sol review found no blocking issues. Existing listing cache can retain results for 30 seconds after manual link changes.
- Maria independently [verified the live server and web UI](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/28607#issuecomment-6557493679), including persistence after restart, details, counts, checkout deduplication and merged filtering. Native mobile and Electron were not exercised.
- Review follow-up: both routing defects reproduced in new regressions before the fix. `vp run check:changed HEAD` passed all stages with 113 tests across two files.
- Multi-host follow-up: identical project/repository/PR numbers on GitHub and Bitbucket now keep distinct counts through server batching, caches, persistence and web/mobile matching. Regressions failed before the fix. `vp run check:changed HEAD` passed 200 tests across seven files, 39 affected typechecks, formatting, lint, knip, GraphQL and React Compiler checks.
- Older-server hostless stats are used only when request refs identify one host unambiguously. The latest stats changes were tested with fixture providers; native clients and a live multi-host UI were not run.

Implemented and reviewed with GPT-6.1 Sol through the Codex harness in T3 Code.

author: vic-lsh
body:
## Problem

A desktop launch starts 16 `vibesys host <read>` processes at once, and the reads of screens nobody has opened (New run: the helper's features, harnesses, examples, the machine's compute settings and agent logins; Machines: one check per machine) are among them. A cheap read's latency is set by how many processes are runnable while it runs, so the Runs reads wait behind work for screens that are not shown. Replaying a launch without those reads finished the Runs reads about 31% sooner (#3597 item 1). Part of #3597.

## Solution

New run and the Machines screen start their host reads when first opened, and until then are idle. A click in the first second shows the screen's existing loading state (its `data-state` stays `loading` until the reads answer). No prefetch on hover or on a timer.

- `@vibesys/store` gains one `Open` action (`OPEN`, `Openable`): until the first `open` a store asks nothing, the first starts every read its state calls for, and later ones change nothing.
- The Machines reducer lists the machines at launch (the rail and Runs name them) and checks each one only after the first `open`; a listing that arrives after `open` checks as before.
- The New run machine starts in a new `idle` state: it follows the machine, the run to run again and the runs opened (the dashboard's draft card and Run again keep working) and starts its reads on `open`. The store opens a form it replaces once it has been opened, so a form respawned by the runs opened is not left idle.
- The shell wakes the stores through one table over the screen kinds (`screen-opening.ts`), for the window's first screen and for each selection, after what the screen was opened for (the machine New run starts on, the section Settings lands on) is in place. The table is typed over every screen kind, so a new screen must be added to it.
- `followCompute` (the Settings data New run follows) asks only once New run is open.
- The rail is on screen from the first frame and its Machines mark warns of a machine that cannot be reached, so the machines' checks are visible reads. The first version of this PR deferred them to the Machines screen and the e2e journey "Machines carries a warning dot while a machine cannot be reached" failed. They now start once Runs has read what it shows (`wakeRail`, called by the main window only), not beside its reads and not on a timer. A run window has no rail and never starts them.

Side effect, same cause: New run used to read the facts of This Mac and then of the machine of the run opened last (it respawned when the overview arrived). An idle form follows the runs for free, so it reads only the machine it ends on.

### Design

- Owner: the feature that owns each state (`features/machines`, `features/new-run`) owns its idle state; `apps/desktop-shell` owns which screen wakes which store, because only the shell knows the screens.
- Interface: `Open`, `OPEN`, `Openable` in `@vibesys/store`; `open` accepted by `MachinesAction` and `NewRunEvent`; `MachinesState.opened`; `openScreen` and `openRailWhenSettled` in the shell.
- Direction: the shell sends `open` to the stores; they never learn which screen did. No new package edge (`@vibesys/store` was already a dependency of all four packages).
- Drift: Machine settings already read only on demand; its launch reads came from the shell's `followCompute`, now gated. New run's `refresh` of a machine's Settings data still reads logins with compute (New run needs only compute); left as is, one more process on the first open of New run.

### Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  select[sidebar selection] --> table[screen-opening table]
  table -->|open| newrun[New run machine: idle to editing]
  table -->|open| machines[Machines store: checks]
  settled[Runs has read what it shows] -->|rail wake| machines
  newrun --> follow[followCompute: Settings data of its machine]
```

## Verification

### Correctness properties

- A launch starts the reads of Runs first (while they are held, nothing else starts), then only the rail's machine checks, and no read for New run, Settings or any other screen.
- For any sequence of screen visits, each non-Usage read is started once, and exactly the methods of the screens opened (plus the rail's) are started.
- Opening a screen again, or opening it before or after the machines are listed, starts nothing twice and loses nothing.
- An idle New run machine has no read in flight and no delay set, whatever events arrive; a form replaced after the screen was opened is read at once.

### Testing

- `shell-opening.property.dom.test.tsx` (new; shell over a recording bridge, both tests about 0.5 s together): at the merge base a launch starts 13 reads for screens nobody opened (both tests fail); at head both pass.
- Machines: the model test draws `open` and checks the idle and open invariants; two new reducer tests; one store test (checks only after open). New run: the model test draws `open` and holds the idle invariant; two new store tests. Each new test file section runs in under 0.1 s.
- `shell.test.ts`: one expectation changed: New run opened on a machine reads only that machine, not This Mac first.
- Existing tests that drive the stores now open them first (one helper per file).
- bun suites of libs/store, features/machines, features/new-run and apps/desktop-shell pass; `tsc -b`, `biome check`, `pnpm test:ts-architecture` pass; pre-push gate passes (51 s); CI is green at the head, including all five `clients-e2e` shards.
- Found by the deterministic tier first: the unopened-launch reads (shell over a recording bridge) and the respawned-idle-form case (New run store). Found by the e2e tier: the rail's warning dot depending on the checks (fixed above).

Real app, alternating merge base (`0bb9fdc45`) and head (`65de790f4`), fresh profile, This Mac with 96 runs, load average 6 to 14 from other agents, gateway killed before each cold launch, 24 launches, no read failed. Medians (range):

| | n | first visible-read answer | slowest read | Runs ready | processes started before Runs ready | process time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cold, merge base | 8 | 1.63 s (1.53 to 1.89) | 1.95 s | 3.08 s (3.03 to 4.77) | 16 | 17.0 s |
| cold, head | 8 | 1.33 s (1.30 to 1.37) | 1.50 s | 2.83 s (2.75 to 3.73) | 14 | 11.9 s |
| warm, merge base | 4 | 1.21 s (1.15 to 1.27) | 1.95 s | 2.79 s (2.72 to 2.88) | 16 | 17.3 s |
| warm, head | 4 | 1.00 s (0.97 to 1.04) | 1.45 s | 2.38 s (2.37 to 2.49) | 12 | 10.3 s |

Gap to the bound (estimates, same basis as #3592): first answer, bound about 0.8 s (0.5 s window load plus a 0.3 s process): cold gap 0.53 s (was 0.83 s), warm gap 0.20 s (was 0.41 s). Runs ready, bound about 1.4 s (0.5 s window load, 0.3 s first process, 0.6 s for the heaviest digest, the best seen here): cold gap 1.4 s (was 1.7 s), warm gap 1.0 s (was 1.4 s). Processes: the visible reads alone are 12 (inspect-candidate, the connection's describe-machine, 9 digests, one list-compute): warm gap 0 (was 4). The cold head count of 13 to 14 includes saved-run streams that finished before the probe stopped. Note that the first answer of K's table was the first answer of any read, which at the merge base is often a hidden-screen read; the table above counts the first read a visible screen needs. The remaining gap is the 9 digest reads and the import floor per process (#3597 items 2 and 3), not in this PR.

### Screens

Real Electron app at the head, window-only capture (`page.screenshot` of the app window, which sat off-screen; never a full-screen capture). Every screen was opened early (right after the window exists: New run, Machines, Settings; shown `loading` 60 ms after the click, then `ready`, 1.4 to 1.7 s) and late (after Runs settled), each switch both ways (Runs, New run, Machines, Settings, Usage, Machines, New run, Runs), light and dark. The late light sheet at the merge base and at the head show the same content on every screen; the early shots show each screen's existing loading sta

author: janusbifrons
body:
## A0: measure the structure network at base scale (plan soft-leaping-truffle v2)

Bases are going to be built from **real structures**: Capital, connectors, fields of Solars, banks of Batteries, rows of Cargo Bays, turrets and a powered Shield Pylon fence, all following the same building rules as players. A citadel is about 400 structures. This PR measures what that costs on the real code before any base content lands. It doesn't change gameplay.

### What's in it
- **Core: `buildStructureLattice(n, seed, fence)`.** A rule-valid N-structure base: a Capital, a connector spine and rows, 2–3 leaves per connector, and an optional closed pylon fence, with Solars added until the base is powered. `structureLattice.test.ts` checks every placement and link against the real `placementRejection` / `canConnect` and checks that everything connects to the Capital.
- **Server.**
  - `place(…, { skipAutoConnect })` plus `connectExplicit`, which re-checks `canConnect`, so a generated base supplies its intended graph. Greedy auto-connect would close gates.
  - The testMode room option `scaleGrid {n, seed, fence}` and the `structure-scale-test` room.
- **Measurement.** `tests/integration/sectorRoom/structureScale.measure.test.ts` uses a real room and the real msgpack encoder. `benchmarks/structures-scale.bench.ts` covers the pure Grid.
- **Budgets.** `src/shared-types/structureBudgets.ts`, with a consistency test. Ledger: `docs/architecture/structure-network-scale.md`.

### Findings (citadel ≈ 448 structures, 300 drones)

| | Today | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| `structures[]` slice | 35 KB/snapshot, **~689 KB/s per player** (a 46-structure outpost already adds 69 KB/s, more than the whole per-player baseline) | ≤ 512 B/snapshot (A2) |
| Turret tick | 5.1 ms median / 12.6 ms max per 10 Hz call | ≤ 1.0 ms (A1) |
| Route after a topology change | 0.94 ms per route | ≤ 0.5 ms for all (A1) |
| Binary full refresh | 15 KB/s | ≤ 2 KB/s (A2) |

The grid pulse, Grid rebuild and placement sweep are fine today.

### Verification
- typecheck: clean; lint: 0 errors.
- Unit: structure and budget tests pass. The full suite's 3 failures in that run (dbWorker, physics-worker boot, the latency proxy) were load timeouts and pass in isolation.
- Integration: structure suites (14 files) and the new measurement test pass.
- Server boots cleanly. In-game stills of the 448-structure base were captured on the real renderer.

The rating graph's dashed guide line and the grid holding the queue cards both
used the class `matchmaker-queue-grid`. Its rule sets `stroke-dasharray: 2 3`,
which is inherited, so through the container it reached every icon in every
queue card: the fact icons and the map pool button were drawn two units on,
three off. The icons set their own stroke colour and width, which is why only
the dash pattern leaked through.

- The guide line gets its own class, `matchmaker-queue-plot-grid`.
- #683 enlarged these icons to 16 px and removed their extra dimming on the
  assumption that thin strokes caused the dashes. The size stays; the
  stylesheet comment and #683's release note no longer claim it fixed them.
- A new test reads every stylesheet and component and fails when a rule that
  sets a dash pattern targets a class that an HTML element also carries.

## Changelog

- Give the matchmaker rating graph's guide line its own class so its dash pattern no longer reaches the queue cards.
- Correct the stylesheet comment and #683's release note about the queue fact icons.
- Add a test that keeps dash patterns off classes used on HTML elements.

## Testing

The new test fails on the card grid in `MatchmakingPanel.tsx` before the change
and passes after it; no other component carries a dashed class.

author: pirabellabs1-coder
body:
## Problème
Sur iPhone, dans la messagerie, une note vocale ne se lit pas : ni à l'écoute avant envoi, ni dans le fil.

## Cause
- `useVoiceRecorder` préférait `audio/webm;codecs=opus`. Chrome (Android, ordinateur) **et Safari récent**, qui sait désormais enregistrer en WebM, produisaient donc du WebM/Opus.
- **Safari sur iPhone ne lit pas le WebM dans un `<audio>`.** Les notes enregistrées sur iPhone ne se relisaient donc pas sur l'iPhone lui-même, et celles venues d'Android non plus.
- Constat en production (lecture seule) : les 7 notes vocales envoyées sont toutes en `audio/webm`. Le bucket accepte bien `audio/mp4`, et la CSP `media-src` est correcte.

## Correctif
- **Enregistrement** : ordre `audio/mp4;codecs=mp4a.40.2` → `audio/mp4` → `audio/aac` → WebM/Ogg. Le MP4/AAC se lit partout. Vérifié : Chrome 152 le produit et le relit.
- **Lecture** (`AudioPlayer`, nouveau `audioFallback.ts`) :
  - si le navigateur annonce ne pas lire le format (`canPlayType`) ou le refuse, le fichier est **décodé dans le navigateur** (Web Audio) puis **converti en WAV** 16 bits mono 22,05 kHz ;
  - la conversion démarre dès l'affichage, pour que l'appui sur « lecture » joue aussitôt (Safari refuse un `play()` après une attente) ;
  - si le décodage échoue aussi : « Format non lu par cet appareil », au lieu d'un bouton sans effet ;
  - vaut pour l'aperçu avant envoi (`Composer`) et pour le fil (`MessageBubble`).
- Côté serveur, rien à changer : le MP4 est déjà reconnu (copie dans le coffre, `lib/vault/from-source.ts`). Aucune migration.

## Vérifications
- Chrome (navigateur intégré), sans micro (tonalité enregistrée par MediaRecorder) : MP4/AAC lisible ; WebM décodé et converti en WAV lisible, durée juste.
- `npm run typecheck` ✅ · `npm run lint` ✅ (32) · `npm test` ✅ 429/429 (dont `tests/voice-playback.test.ts`).
- **Non testé sur iPhone** :
  - nouvelles notes en MP4 : lisibles nativement ;
  - les 7 anciennes notes WebM : la conversion dépend du décodage WebM/Opus de Safari, sinon le message « Format non lu » s'affiche. À vérifier après la mise en production.

author: g1oow
body:
## 背景/问题

`[21]` 部署成功后，脚本提示「下一步会把所有 Reality 节点的 SNI 改为 `<域名>`，并把其中一个迁移到 443 端口」，但实际只改 Reality 节点。其他 TLS 类节点（VLESS-WS/gRPC、Trojan-WS、AnyTLS、Hysteria2、TUIC）仍保留旧域名与旧证书，而伪装域名已经指向本机，这些节点在客户端侧直接连不上；提示文案与实际作用域也不一致。

## 改动要点

- 新增 `_camouflage_mutate_all_nodes` / `_camouflage_apply_all_nodes`，作为「同步所有节点」的统一入口：在同一笔事务内先执行 Reality 换 SNI 与 443 迁移，再同步 TLS 类节点的 `server_name`、`certificate_path`、`key_path` 到伪装域名与伪装站证书，并关闭客户端 `skip-cert-verify`（证书公网可信）；Hysteria2 跳跃子入站仍跟随主节点同步。任一步失败整笔回滚。
- 新增 `_camouflage_has_tls_nodes`，与 `[20]` 复用同一份 `_batch_sni_plan` 判定是否存在可复用的 TLS 类节点，两处口径不会漂移；没有 TLS 类节点时返回成功，避免纯 Reality 场景被误判成事务失败。
- 「选一个 Reality 节点迁移到 443」的步骤与 `_camouflage_pick_port443_tag` 逻辑保持不变。
- 部署提示与菜单第 2 项文案改为「所有节点」。
- `SCRIPT_VERSION` 111 → 112，README 第 5 行同步；README 当前行为描述与更新日志已补。

## 测试结果

按 AGENTS.md 固定流程实跑：

```
for f in singbox.sh advanced_relay.sh parser.sh xray_manager.sh \
         tests/test_node_naming.sh tests/test_batch_sni.sh tests/test_caddy_camouflage.sh; do
    bash -n "$f"
done
# 全部通过

bash tests/test_node_naming.sh        # 全部通过 (exit 0)
bash tests/test_batch_sni.sh          # 全部通过 (exit 0)
bash tests/test_caddy_camouflage.sh   # 全部通过 (exit 0)
```

`tests/test_caddy_camouflage.sh` 新增断言：

- Reality 与 TLS 类节点在同一事务内同时同步；
- Reality `server_name`/`handshake` 改为域名与本机回落，原 `listen_port` 不被改动；
- TLS 类节点证书/私钥换成伪装站证书，`skip-cert-verify` 关闭；
- 无证书路径的 TLS 节点同样只改 `server_name`；
- 纯 Reality 场景（无 TLS 类节点）同步仍成功；
- 部署提示与菜单第 2 项文案断言。

实现过程中查出并修复一个真实缺陷：`_camouflage_has_tls_nodes` 初期只 `read` 4 个变量，而计划行是 7 列，第 4 列会把余下各列一起吞掉，导致永远判定「没有 TLS 节点」、TLS 类节点不会被同步。已改为显式多接一个变量，并由上述用例断言住。

## 未覆盖项

- 未在真实服务器上跑完整 `[21]` 部署（需要公网域名、ACME 签发与真实端口占用），仅通过替身覆盖配置改写与事务外壳逻辑。
- 未验证 Hysteria2 跳跃子入站在混合场景下的端到端连通性（仅断言配置侧同步）。

## 脱敏

新增代码、测试数据与本文均只使用保留地址（`192.0.2.0/24`、`198.51.100.0/24`）与 `example.com`，无真实 IP、域名、凭据。

body:
<!-- cezar-stack:start -->
**Stack** ([native GitHub stack](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1880), bottom to top; each PR is based on the one above it in this list)

1. `main`
1. [#1880](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1880) Manager mode (draft)
1. [#1894](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1894) Report every task waiting on you (ready for review)
1. [#1881](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1881) Manager chat on a phone (draft)
1. [#1882](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1882) Phones open on Manager (draft)
1. [#1884](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1884) Manager approvals on every width (draft)
1. [#1899](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1899) macOS Manager notch (draft)
1. [#1879](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1879) Mobile apps spec (draft)
1. **[#1893](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1893) Relay and QR pairing spec** (ready for review) ← this PR
1. [#1895](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1895) Relay protocol (ready for review)
1. [#1900](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1900) Relay client and Connect a phone (draft)
1. [#1906](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1906) Built-in default relay (draft)
1. [#1883](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1883) Mobile app shell (draft)
1. [#1901](https://github.com/open-mercato/cezar/pull/1901) Android relay client (ready for review)
<!-- cezar-stack:end -->

Design spec for connecting the mobile app to cezar through an end-to-end encrypted relay with QR pairing. Stacked on #1879. One file, nothing built.

**The relay contract section is what `patzick/rome` builds against.** Any later change to it is a separate commit with a changelog line in the spec.

## Decisions

- **Cockpit loading:** a decrypting proxy inside the app on `127.0.0.1`, under #1883's plain webview. Bundling is rejected because it still needs a tunnel for every API call and adds an app-to-cezar version matrix. The spec lists what changes in #1883, file by file, and what survives.
- **Encryption:** `Noise_XXpsk3` to pair, `Noise_KK` per session, no 0-RTT, per-phone keys. A 6-digit match confirms the phone on desktop.
- **Authorization:** a relay request is a hosted request, even on a laptop. The main exposure was `localHandoff`, not the Host guard, because it gates the agent-config RCE closure and the shell default. One closure narrows it, and the guard changes by one line.
- **Sleep:** cezar sends only runtime-answered pings with no phone connected, and only the phone can open a stream. Public tests, a `patzick/rome` hibernation test and a production metric guard this.
- **Cost:** about $0.18 per cezar per month at 1 hour a day, or $4.05 if hibernation breaks.

## Not verified

- `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` were denied, so every Cloudflare price and limit and every Apple or Google API claim is marked `[M]`, from memory. Task R2 confirms pricing.
- The loopback proxy is untested on any device. R0 settles it, and R0 needs an iOS build that #1883 has not produced yet.
- Export compliance is a legal question and is flagged as QR7.

Eight open questions, each with a recommended answer, are at the end of the spec. Docs only, so no test gate was run.

body: ## Summary `DebugAgentPaneScriptTests.aPageThatDrawsNoFrameAnswersWithoutItsHookInSeconds` failed in the parallel runs of CmuxNextAppTests (width 4 and 6) and passes alone. It took 8.3 s, 7.6 s and 33.6 s against its 7 s bound (`DebugAgentPaneScriptTests.swift:34` at the logs' base). - **Cause (time as correctness, R5):** the test timed the call on its own wall clock (a 10 s poll, then `took < 7 s`). In a parallel run, other tests hold the main actor before WebKit delivers the answer. That time counted against the page. - **What the test checks:** a page with no debug hook answers "has no cmuxAcpmuxDebug.chatState" after the script's 5 s hook wait. The wait uses page timers, not animation frames. Thus the promise is about the page's time. - **Fix:** - The test now awaits the answer. A call that never answers (the old frame wait) is stopped by the suite's 1 min time limit. - The test times the script with the page's `performance.now()` and keeps the 7 s bound and the answer check. - This is a test-only change. `DebugAgentPane.script` is not changed. Owner: no OWNERS.md row covers `CmuxNextApp/Control/DebugAgentPane.swift` or this test. The agent pane web side is PL-webui (followups). The test harness is cmux-testing. ## Testing The command is `scripts/ci/package-test-lane.sh suite Packages/macOS/CmuxNext DebugAgentPaneScriptTests` on a fleet display worker (`CMUX_TEST_REQUIRE_GUI=1`, Xcode 26.6). Load method: the parallel run's main-actor load in the test itself. A test-only `MainActorStall` queues one CPU-busy main-actor turn of 8 s while the page answers. cmux-ci's step env allowlist does not take a new variable, so the stall is in the source for the red and green commits only. - **Red** at 678bf7477f4 (old wall-clock check + 8 s stall): job `b162529fdcc2` on cmux8s-Mac-mini. `(took → 8.061966042 seconds) < 7.0 seconds` failed at the same check as in the width-4 log. - **Green under the same load** at 80e7c9c6e4b (page clock + 8 s stall): job `0d84087e363d` on cmuxs-Mac-mini-3 passed (8.28 s). - **Green alone** at afd8a07453 (head, stall removed): job `0f8e16e22f66` on cmux8s-Mac-mini passed (6.07 s). `python3 scripts/cmux-next/prepush-gate.py`: no new violations. ### Observed / Not run - Observed: the three fleet jobs above. - Not run: a full CmuxNextAppTests run at width 4 with this head. ## Changelog none --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the hook-less agent pane debug test so parallel runs no longer fail: the test timed the call on its own wall clock, counting time other tests held the main actor. author: dodonov-dev
body:
## What and why

Follow-up to #231, found by running it over real MCP HTTP and in a browser.

**The hiring screen, for the demo**
- It jumped straight to the end. It now plays line by line in about 27 s (timed in Chromium), with Skip and Replay.
- Its CSS classes did not exist. It now uses the same screen and stage styles as the booking chat, and the form collapses so the chat gets the screen.
- Raw tool names as messages, and "speaks for the hotel", are replaced by readable lines from the Hive, Anouk's agent and the Hiring Hub.
- It said a CV was queued when nothing had been sent, and showed a "You approved" nobody gave. It now says it is a script.
- The Hiring Hub link appears only when `VITE_HIRING_HUB_URL` is set. It used to point at `localhost:3000` in every build, and at a `/positions/1` route that does not exist.

**The CV tools**
- `hr_read_cv` and `hr_submit_cv` handed over granted `shared` files that `GET /api/folders/file` refuses with a 404, and had no size limit, read budget or ledger row. They now follow the route's rules.
- `hr_grant_cv` with an empty path opened the candidate's whole folder. It is now refused.
- `hr_create_job` and `hr_submit_cv` spent the organisation's Hiring Hub key for any anonymous MCP caller. They now need that key in `X-Hiring-Hub-Key`, and refuse everyone while it is unset. **MCP callers of these two tools must send the new header.**

**Hiring Hub**
- Offline, every PDF candidate was named `--- Page 1 ---`. Fixed.
- Following the README, `docker compose` failed because `.env.example` lacked two required variables. Added.

**Still open, now in `LIMITS.md`**
- A candidate cannot hold their own link secret; only the operator can mint one.
- `hr_request_intro` feeds none of the CV tools.
- The hub relays CV bytes.
- The Hiring Hub frontend bundle carries `ADMIN_TOKEN`.

## Lane

HR workflows. Outside it: `GroupChat.tsx`, `TraceParts.tsx`, `styles.css`, `i18n/`, `SECURITY.md`, `documentation/`, `tools/mutate.py`, `Hiring Hub/`.

Over the 400-line guideline, and more than one topic: it was pushed in a hurry for the demo.

## How I checked it

- [x] After rebasing on latest `main`: ruff and format clean; `test_hr_cv`, `test_docs` and `test_mutation` pass (46); frontend format and `tsc` clean, 551 tests pass
- [ ] **The full backend suite after the rebase did not run before pushing, so CI is the check.** Before the rebase: 1076 passed, 1 skipped

body:
Bug: after reopening a canvas, a large imported frame stayed blank and Ctrl+scroll did nothing.

**Cause** (CPU profile from the new e2e): `StyleLibrary.found` → `syncStyle` → `commit` → effect → `found`… The library compared doc styles with the project copy via `JSON.stringify`; jsonb returns keys reordered, so the same style never matched and every frame was re-committed until Svelte's loop guard. One main-thread task of 190–208 s in 3/3 runs (dev build). Variables had the same comparison. Separately, the fit-to-content tween overwrote a zoom made while tiles arrived.

**Fix**: `sameValue` (key-order free) in `style-library.svelte.ts`, `variable-library.svelte.ts` and both sync paths in `GpuFlow.svelte`; `takeCamera()` cancels the tween on wheel, pinch, pointer down.

**Tests**: red first — `style-library.svelte.test.ts`, `variable-library.svelte.test.ts` (stored keys in another order → no push). e2e `tests/e2e/url-import-reopen.spec.ts` (test account, `E2E_REAL_STACK=1`; `REOPEN_SEED` reuses one real vercel.com import): after the fix longest task 272 ms–1.25 s, zoom < 100 ms, frame painted 0.7–2.4 s after its tile (one run of five missed the paint probe within 12 s).

author: samuel-williams-shopify
body:
## Purpose

Agents have each rebuilt ad-hoc round-trip harnesses (`/tmp/bm95/probe.rs`, `/tmp/r104/scratch/zz_fuzz.rs`, `/tmp/bm106/probe.rs`) with different corpora, so author and reviewer figures did not line up. This PR checks one in, `tests/roundtrip_fuzz.rs`, consolidating their corpora, with fixed seeds, an exact baseline and a CI check. A normalizer or serializer change (next: moving whitespace out of attention edges, and flattening emphasis in emphasis) can then be measured against main on the same inputs.

### Checks per input

Each input is parsed with `ParseOptions::normalize()` (the syntax `normalize_markdown` reads), or built as a tree by hand. It is then normalized, serialized with the default options, parsed and normalized again. It fails as:
- `normalized`: `is_normalized` is false after normalizing.
- `html`: the HTML of the two documents differs. The final line ending and a line ending after a hard break are ignored.
- `tree`: the HTML is the same, but `support::fixture::canonical` trees differ. I chose this over limiting the HTML leniency to tree inputs, because it was simpler. It catches a dropped line ending after a hard break, and structure the HTML flattens, such as links in image alt text.
- `unstable`: the second serialization differs.
- `error`: serializing a parsed document errors.

A panic is a hard failure. A hand-built tree the serializer rejects counts as rejected.

### Corpora

Each corpus has its own seed and uses an in-file xorshift generator. No new dependencies are added; `regex`, already a dev-dependency, is used only to bucket failures.
- `realistic`: a prose-like token mix: words, markers, escapes, references, links, code, block starts, tables and literal autolinks.
- `soup`: single characters from `*_~a. \n\`.
- `edge`: markers next to ` `, `
`, `	`, encoded letters and escaped markers, sometimes in a heading, cell, item or quote.
- `strike`: tilde runs among letters, attention, escapes, code and links.
- `tree-asterisk`, `tree-underscore`: the same hand-built paragraphs, headings and table cells of nested emphasis, strong, strikethrough, links, code and breaks, serialized with each marker. A hard break is never the last child, where it has no source, and never appears in a table cell, which GFM cannot write.

### Exact baseline

At the default 10,000 inputs per corpus, `tests/roundtrip_fuzz_baseline.txt` records `<corpus> <failures> <rejected> <digest>`. The digest is FNV-1a 64 over the sorted failing-input list.
- Any difference, up or down, fails the test. The message prints each count's change and how to bless.
- `FUZZ_BLESS=1` (exactly `1`) rewrites the baseline and prints what changed. It fails at a non-default size.
- Malformed or duplicate baseline lines are rejected with clear messages.

### Failure buckets

The report also buckets failures by known issue with simple rules; the buckets are approximate. The hard-break rule now runs after the more specific ones.

### Scaling test

The PR also adds `parsing_normalizing_and_serializing_is_linear`, an `assert_linear`-style check of parse, normalize and serialize together on six adversarial shapes:
- Each size takes the minimum of five alternating runs.
- 4x the input must take less than 12x the time.
- `round_trip_fuzz` takes the same `TIMING` mutex, so the two never run at the same time.

## Usage

```sh
cargo test --test roundtrip_fuzz -- --nocapture                      # CI size, with the report
FUZZ_INPUTS=1000000 cargo test --release --test roundtrip_fuzz round_trip_fuzz -- --nocapture
FUZZ_OUTPUT=/tmp/fuzz/branch cargo test ...                          # writes <corpus>.txt (sorted failing inputs) and <corpus>-details.txt
FUZZ_BLESS=1 cargo test --test roundtrip_fuzz round_trip_fuzz         # rewrite the baseline at the default size
```

To compare a branch with main:
1. Run both with the same `FUZZ_INPUTS` and different `FUZZ_OUTPUT` directories.
2. `LC_ALL=C comm -13 main/<corpus>.txt branch/<corpus>.txt` lists new failures, and `comm -23` lists fixed ones.

At 1M, each tree corpus writes about 220 MB of details and 140 MB of inputs. `context/roundtrip-fuzz.md` has the full recipe.

## Baseline figures

| Corpus | 10,000 (CI baseline: failures, rejected) | 1,000,000 (release, 14 s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| realistic | 254, 0 | 25,506 |
| soup | 8, 0 | 1,471 |
| edge | 1,109, 0 | 113,304 |
| strike | 745, 0 | 73,966 |
| tree-asterisk | 2,313, 0 | 230,983 |
| tree-underscore | 2,312, 0 | 230,957 |

- There are no panics, no `normalized` or `error` failures and no rejected trees.
- At 1M, realistic has 24 `tree` failures; at CI size it has 1. `unstable` is 21 for realistic and 3 for edge at 1M, and 1 at CI size.

Largest buckets at 1M:

| Bucket | Failures at 1M |
| --- | --- |
| #107 fence at document start reads as frontmatter | 73,907 strike, 7,195 edge, 4,209 realistic, 1,447 soup |
| #112 encoded line ending written raw | 86,235 edge, 62,095 per tree corpus |
| #108 lazy table | 11,731 realistic, 2,482 edge |
| #109 cell-edge whitespace | 3,882 realistic, 6,671 edge, 9,572 per tree corpus |
| Literal autolinks, by design | 5,376 realistic |
| #97 | 72 realistic |
| #101 | about 1,600 per tree corpus |

The harness also found three bug classes that have no issue yet:
- A line ending in table cell text: 10,644 edge, 89,588 per tree corpus.
- Adjacent code spans written as one, such as `` `~~``a~` ``: 67,544 per tree corpus.
- Links in image text lost while the HTML stays the same: part of the 24 `tree` failures.

Coverage is 16,985/16,985 regions with 21 exclusions, unchanged; test code is not measured.

author: cokavn11
body:
## What changes
- **Distill:** `POST /api/notes/:id/distill` drafts title, summary, why, next action and tags from a raw note. The note page fills the form with the draft; nothing is saved until the user clicks Save. The user's chosen `kind` is kept.
- **Connect:** notes are embedded with `@cf/baai/bge-m3` into a new `note_embeddings` table (D1 BLOB, cosine in the Worker). `suggest` gains a `semantic` source. `POST /api/notes/:id/connect` asks `@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast` for one reason per suggestion in a single call; the reason pre-fills the link prompt.
- **Backfill:** `POST /api/ai/backfill` plus an "Index notes with AI" button in Settings for existing and imported notes.
- **Safety:** AI output is only a draft or suggestion and never writes notes or links. Note text is treated as untrusted in the prompts. The `AI` binding is optional: without it the AI endpoints return 503 and the rest of the app works.
- `NotePage` is keyed by note id so drafts and reasons do not leak between notes.

## Requirements
- Migration `0002_embeddings.sql` (applied by `npm run deploy`).
- `wrangler.jsonc` gains the `ai` binding. Workers AI usage is billed to the Cloudflare account, and `npm run dev` now needs `wrangler login` because the binding is always remote.
- After deploying, click "Index notes with AI" once for existing notes.

## Validation
- `npm test` 16/16 and `npm run build` pass on a clean worktree of this branch.
- Live Workers AI against local D1: embedding on create, semantic suggest, connect reasons and distill in Vietnamese, prompt-injection text ignored.
- Backfill: wiped vectors, button reported 3 indexed, a second run reported 0. Deleting notes cascades to `note_embeddings`.
- UI checked: note page (vi, light) and Settings (en, dark). Not checked: note page in en/dark.

## Known limits
- The semantic threshold (0.5, top 5) is only tried on a handful of notes.
- Brute-force cosine in the Worker is unmeasured at scale (D1 returns each 4 KB vector as a 4096-entry array); move to Vectorize if `suggest` gets slow.
- AI tags can come back snake_case.

author: astrogilda
body:
Every corpus but the flagship moves from the repository root to `corpora/<id>/`, under its unchanged id, with no alias. The Go package that lived at `corpora/` becomes `corpusreaders/`, and `corpora/`, `packages/` and `interop/` carry a sentinel `go.mod` so the root module zip stops shipping corpus data: tracked files outside nested modules go from 14,025 files / 52,993,339 bytes at main to 1,870 files / 25,574,570 bytes here. `vectors/` stays at the root (pin P3), so a commit pinner's path does not move.

The digest list keeps its column `<id>/MANIFEST.json` (pin P5, an outside parser joins it into the wheel path), so the intake record's anchor now names the manifest the way the list does while `manifest.path` carries the record's path. W3C-I-022 ties the two: the listed name is the record's path or a trailing path of it cut at a directory boundary, so `ite/MANIFEST.json` cannot claim `corpora/suite/MANIFEST.json`. W3C-I-024 binds the line on the digest and the listed name as before and then reads the manifest at the record's path. Both checkers change the same way; `vectors-w3c-intake` gains two accept and three reject members that pin each clause, including the inside-a-component spoof and the record-path-instead-of-listed-name case; the signed list and every published record (the equality case) are unchanged. The ruling and its attacks are in the probity research record for the public-surface structure (amendment of 1 Nov).

The path rewrite had edited documents whose bytes other files pin (`spec/self-reported-record/v1.md`, `profiles/restoration-evidence.md`, the predicate specs behind `pages/predicate/v1/*`), which turned the Go corpus tests red; those files are back to main's bytes, because a spec names a corpus by its id and the registry maps the id to a directory. Pyright is pointed at `corpora/` by directory, the registry block in `pyproject.toml` and `corpora/README.md` are regenerated, and `release/` carries the regenerated digest list and 55 intake records, each admitted under the repository root.

author: llewellynvdm
body:
Deployment selection now shares Joomla/PHP/JCB requirements across the dashboard, editor and launcher. Required JCB deployments cannot select None; optional deployments can. The editor populates the complete setup, preserves maintained recipes, and supports named browser-saved custom copies, deletion, and full JSON import/export with basic and advanced inputs.

Custom extension and template URLs go directly to Joomla's existing `extension:install --url` command. An optional installer failure is reported while the site continues opening. Maintained packages retain their verified build path. Downloaded maintained images and successful custom builds are reusable from browser storage, with server manifest hashes invalidating outdated maintained images. Build and launch have separate progress stages, and users can view and delete stored images. Large image exports have a bounded execution allowance separate from ordinary requests; restored database tables have their optimizer statistics refreshed. Explicit snapshots have their own cache identity and are restored as selected, including fresh launches, while maintained URLs retain the server's current hash as authority.

Complete-site Download and dashboard Upload carry edited files, the database, runtime configuration, known administrator credentials and opening page. Upload creates an independent saved site, validates the payload hash when present, and accepts older hashless exports with a brief notice. Saved uploaded sites resume without resolving their original packages. Copies preserve subsequent edits inside Joomla and apply deliberate administrator changes only to the new copy. Unchanged packages, commands, language settings, menus and templates are not reapplied.

The dashboard replaces New site with Upload, countdown Stop is icon-only, Login details can submit the current Joomla login form, and mobile isolation fallback works independently of the optional image relay. Normal deployment messages no longer expose internal asset URLs. Documentation covers the complete site transfer and Joomla CLI installation paths.

Validation: all 454 local unit tests and syntax checks pass. Seven focused PHP/MariaDB checks cover export limits, restoration and database statistics. All 17 jobs in the strict [CI run](https://github.com/joomengine/playground/actions/runs/41312666205) pass for this commit, including native provisioning, demonstration images, version catalogs, Chromium/Firefox interactions and full runtime checks, Chromium/WebKit mobile startup, custom URL installation, image reuse, and portable site upload/copy tests. The export regression checks exact SQL values, files, dependent views, executing triggers, and a fresh download of the selected snapshot. Independent scenarios retain their diagnostic output; any failure still fails the overall gate.

The large Service Directory regression preserves 151,233 cities and 5,073 states. In CI, build/save took 165.3 seconds and a separate site opened its cities page from the cached image in 22.9 seconds, without repeating downloads, CLI installation or export.
