author: aneeshie
body:
## What changed

`bun run bench` measures the parts of Rook that decide how fast it feels, and saves the results with the machine's details so runs can be compared. `bun run bench:compare before.json after.json` marks each benchmark as faster, slower or noise. See `docs/benchmarks.md`.

| Suite | Measures |
|---|---|
| `layout` | Computing a 16-pane layout; split + close |
| `xterm` | xterm.js parse throughput (`@xterm/headless`, pinned to the app's 6.0.0) on four fixed 4 MB inputs: plain lines, colored logs, wide Unicode, nvim-style full-screen redraws |
| `pty` | Rust: `cat` of 32 MB through the PTY, and keystroke echo latency through a raw-mode `cat` |

**What makes it reproducible**

- Inputs are generated from a fixed seed, so every run parses identical bytes.
- The PTY benchmark starts zsh with an empty `ZDOTDIR`, so personal zsh config doesn't affect it.
- Comparisons use the fast end of the samples (p90 throughput, p10 latency). Background load can only slow a sample down, so that end is the stable one.
- 3 interleaved rounds per run with pooled samples, GC before each JS sample, and a release build for Rust.
- Every run records the CPU, OS, power source, load average, and the Bun, xterm and Rust versions. Runs warn on battery or under load, and comparisons flag mismatched environments.

`bench/terminal.sh` compares terminals end to end (including rendering), timing until the terminal answers a cursor-position request.

## Validation

- Two runs of the same code under heavy load (load average 4.7, then 7.7): 7 of 8 benchmarks were marked noise, most within ±3–9%. PTY `cat` throughput showed +31% against a ±29% threshold, a false positive under that load, which the docs mention.
- `bun run build`, `bun run test` (43 + 10) and `cargo check --all-targets` pass.

Current numbers on an M4: PTY output about 115–150 MB/s and keystroke echo about 10–12 µs, while xterm parses plain line output at about 40–47 MB/s. The parser, not the backend, is the bottleneck.

author: hamzakhanbuic
body:
## Title
fix(vertex_ai): map google.auth TransportError to APIConnectionError (#49419)

## Relevant Issue
Closes #49419

## Problem
When a network connection drop or socket timeout occurs while refreshing Google Auth credentials during a Vertex AI / Gemini API call (e.g. inside `_ensure_access_token_async`), `google.auth.exceptions.TransportError` is raised. Because `_map_vertex_exception` did not match `TransportError` (which carries no `status_code`), the exception fell through to the unmapped exception handler in `exception_mapping_utils.py`. This triggered `should_report_bug()` and appended the automated bug report URL notice, falsely signaling an internal LiteLLM defect rather than normalizing it as a connection error.

## Solution
1. Explicitly map `TransportError` (from `google.auth.exceptions`) in `_map_vertex_exception` to `litellm.APIConnectionError`.
2. Map `RefreshError`, `GoogleAuthError`, and `DefaultCredentialsError` to `litellm.AuthenticationError`.
3. Add unit tests in `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py` verifying that:
   - `google.auth.exceptions.TransportError` maps to `litellm.APIConnectionError` without attaching bug report URLs.
   - `google.auth.exceptions.RefreshError` maps to `litellm.AuthenticationError` (status code 401).

## Tests
- Added unit tests:
  - `test_vertex_auth_transport_error_maps_to_api_connection_error`
  - `test_vertex_auth_refresh_error_maps_to_authentication_error`
- Verified locally with pytest:
  `15 passed in test_exception_mapping_utils.py`

author: sahandking86-lgtm
body:
## What this adds

A complete desktop-style app that takes a **downloaded video** (drag & drop or file
dialog) and gives back **the same video with Kurdish (Sorani) subtitles burned in**.

Flow exactly as requested:

1. drop / choose a video
2. choose one of **five accuracy levels** — very low, low, medium, high, perfect
3. watch the progress (audio extraction → speech recognition → translation → styling → burn-in)
4. get the video back with Kurdish subtitles inside the picture

## Highlights

- **Local & private**: speech recognition (faster-whisper) and rendering happen on the
  user's machine; only the translation step may go online. No accounts, no uploads.
- **Five real accuracy tiers**, each a full recipe: Whisper model (`tiny` → `large-v3`),
  VAD profile, beam size, word timings, sentence grouping, a proof-reading pass and the
  subtitle formatting rules (chars/line, lines per cue, reading speed, cue padding).
  Bigger models are tried first and fall back automatically (low RAM never hard-fails).
- **Free translation with no practical limits**: keyless Google Translate endpoint,
  Lingva mirror fallback, optional free Gemini key (best Sorani, safety filters off,
  keeps slang/profanity/explicit content), local Ollama, NLLB offline, LibreTranslate.
  Automatic fallback between engines and repair of any dropped line.
- **Real Sorani typography**: Arabic look-alike letters folded to `ک ی ه`, bidi marks
  stripped, balanced two-line wrapping, ≤42 chars/line, 16–19 chars/s reading speed,
  cues split when too fast, never overlapping. Bundled Noto fonts are loaded via
  `fontsdir` + a private fontconfig, so shaping is correct on Windows and Linux.
- **Result screen**: play the video, click a line to jump to it, double-click to fix
  the Kurdish, change size/position/bilingual mode and re-render, download MP4 or .srt,
  reveal the output folder.
- **Windows + Linux**: `start-windows.bat` / `start-linux.sh` create a venv, install
  everything once and open the browser (bundled static ffmpeg via `imageio-ffmpeg`).
- **47 offline tests** (`pytest`, no network, no models) and a `--demo` mode so the UI
  can be exercised without downloading anything.

## Try it

```bash
./start-linux.sh          # or start-windows.bat
# without models / offline UI check:
python -m app --demo
```

Screens/console API is documented in `README.md` (`/api/jobs/upload`, `/api/jobs/{id}` …).

author: xzb177
body:
## 背景

2026-11-01 限额试点（`run_manual_aggregation(import_series_limit=10)`，源 id=4 乐观服）18:16 启动，4 个电影库 2 分钟走完，随后在国产剧库（61,000 条）磨了 85+ 分钟未走完、托管剧落库 0；进程 State=R、上下文切换约 3,400 次/秒——没卡死，是逐条往返的活太重。试点已停，本 PR 为加速版。

## 剖析证据（先剖析后动手，探针为内存 SQLite 夹具）

- **配对不是瓶颈**：`pair_aggregates` 用整页 IN 批量查，一窗 5000 条仅 102 SQL / 0.84s，已批量。
- **写映射逐对往返**：`record_mapping` 每对 1 次 SELECT + 1 次 flush，3100 对 = 6200 SQL / 4.95s。
- **进库逐集往返**：一窗 1900 集补集 = **13,601 SQL / 35.3s**（约 7 SQL/集：定位 2 + guid 查 1–2 + 保季 1 + 写映射 2）。
- **头号杀手是标题回落**：无 SeriesId 且剧不在本窗配对结论时，`_resolve_series_row` 每集做 2 次全表 `.all()` 扫描（本源托管剧 + 全部本地活剧），800 剧规模实测 **44ms/集**，随本地剧总数线性涨——生产规模足以解释 85+ 分钟。
- **拉取不是主因**：串行分页 500/页约 0.3s/页（旧全轮 157k 条约 16 分钟），但可并发拿掉尾巴。
- **限额早停**：进库模块零 HTTP——剧树数据随库分页清单同行到达，不存在逐剧抓取；预算拒绝的剧整树跳过、其集按 SeriesId 在定位前确定性跳过（旧行为，本 PR 加回归测试钉住）。

## 改动（结果语义逐字不变：result_json 计数口径、幂等 upsert、lifecycle 守卫、增量水位逻辑一律未动）

1. `upstream_item_mappings.record_mappings_batch`：存在性一条 IN 查（键集取输入∪既有值，Python 端三元组精确对齐）+ 攒批一次 flush；非法条目先纯校验隔离并返回下标集——run 侧逐个计数/告警同旧逐条版，import 侧整窗抛 ValueError 中止同旧口径。开关关时全 None 不校验（同单条版）。
2. `upstream_import`：`_GuidRowCache` 按 guid 整窗预取（含软删行；软删未合并复活、merged 跟随 ≤8 跳，与 `_usable_row_by_guid` 逐字同序）；`_SeriesLocator` 把配对行、SeriesId 映射、托管/本地标题索引各预取一次（定位步骤顺序与 `_resolve_series_row` 逐字同序）；季行 (剧,季) 窗内缓存（新行落库即登记）；电影/剧树两函数的映射改攒批末尾一次写。同探针复测：**13,601 SQL / 35.3s → 4,306 SQL / 5.2s，统计逐字一致**（剩余主要是 2000 行 INSERT 本身）。
3. 拉取有界并发：`_PrefetchingPageFetcher` 只改请求时序——预取页集合与串行请求集合逐页相等（只提交 start < TotalRecordCount 的页）、页长与上游总量对不上时丢预取同步重锚（取数总量校验不变）、页错误存到消费该页时才抛（错误点不变）；增量路径带 sort_by 恒不套用、维持串行。
4. 新 SystemConfig 键 `upstream_aggregate_fetch_concurrency`，默认 4、钳 [1,16]——四齐：config_schema 注册（纯 SystemConfig 键，不进 env.example）＋管理端 GET/PUT 端点（`/admin/upstream-sources/upstream-fetch-concurrency-config`）＋admin.ts 方法＋UpstreamSources.vue「聚合拉取」字段行＋越界 400。
5. 测试：`test_upstream_aggregate_persist` 两例的冲突注入点随实现从 `record_mapping` 迁到 `record_mappings_batch`，断言逐字未动（冲突仍在 flush 处抛、单库隔离/旧口径穿透语义不变）。

## 测试

- 新增 `tests/test_upstream_aggregate_accel.py`（先红后绿，旧代码 11 failed / 1 passed）：批量映射等价与校验隔离、进库 SELECT 预算（旧代码实测 2700 → 预算 150）、拉取并发钳制、预取页序/错误点/重锚对齐串行、限额拒绝集跳过回归。
- 本地（3.12 定向）：上游+applecms+config 家族 797 passed。
- **全量（InstaBox 沙盒机，Python 3.11.17，CI 原样命令与 env）**：`python -m pytest tests/ -q --durations=30` → **8610 passed, 29 skipped, 0 failed**（1048s）。

## 已知偏差

- 进库非法条目（缺 provider_item_id）：旧逐条版在抛错前已 flush 的行留在会话待提交，批量版隔离后一行不写；两者该窗最终都 rollback（单库隔离口径），落库结果一致，仅会话中间态不同。
- 极端负数集号（`Season EpisodeNumber < 0`，Emby 正常数据不会出现）：批量版可能比旧版少写个别映射行，下轮聚合按幂等补齐；正常数据（集号 ≥ 0 或 NULL）等价已由测试钉住。

author: arimendelow
body:
A centred dialog whose content changed moved as a whole: the viewport centres it at every height,[^centre] so a dialog whose steps tick by, such as an app's first-run welcome, jumped up by half of each step and shifted the page's layout.

Once open, a centred dialog now keeps the top edge it opened at and grows downward, as a macOS sheet does: [as its content grows](registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx "verify:testExists(registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx::Dialog's top edge while its content changes > opens centred, then keeps its top edge where it opened as its content grows)") and [as it shrinks](registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx "verify:testExists(registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx::Dialog's top edge while its content changes > keeps its top edge where it opened as its content shrinks)"). It [moves up only as far as it must](registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx "verify:testExists(registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx::Dialog's top edge while its content changes > moves up only as far as it must when it grows past the screen's bottom margin)") to stay inside the screen's margin. A window of a new height [centres it again](registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx "verify:testExists(registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx::Dialog's top edge while its content changes > centres itself again for a window of a new size)"), and [a change of width alone does not](registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx "verify:testExists(registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog.test.tsx::Dialog's top edge while its content changes > keeps its top edge when only the window's width changes, as when a page's scroll bar comes or goes)"), so a page's scroll bar coming or going leaves it where it is.

The popup keeps its own margins: the hold is a relative offset from where the viewport centres it, and a popup taller than the room, such as Lightbox's full screen, stays where the viewport puts it.[^offset] Nothing animates, so reduced motion needs nothing of its own. The hold is in `DialogPopup`'s own popup, which Command's palette and ConfirmDialog render too.[^popup]

## Visual proof

![A dialog at open, two steps, its top on the dashed line](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/blob/86704a73eb422421bb1c174b1292f1c0b1ac5f88/dialog-held-top/dialog-after-1.png?raw=true)

Notice: the dashed red line marks the dialog's top edge as it opened with its first steps.

![Before: the same dialog with six steps, moved up above the line](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/blob/86704a73eb422421bb1c174b1292f1c0b1ac5f88/dialog-held-top/dialog-before-2.png?raw=true)
![After: the same dialog with six steps, its top still on the line](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/blob/86704a73eb422421bb1c174b1292f1c0b1ac5f88/dialog-held-top/dialog-after-2.png?raw=true)

Notice: once its later steps arrive, the dialog before had moved up above the dashed line; after, its top stays on the line and it has grown downward.

Page: https://ui.ouro.bot/docs/dialog/

[^centre]: registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog-parts.tsx verify:fileLine(registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog-parts.tsx, /fixed inset-0 z-1000 box-border flex items-center justify-center/)
[^offset]: test:registry/ouro/components/ouro/lightbox/lightbox.mosaic.test.tsx::Lightbox full screen > covers the whole screen with no frame, from the thumbnails or controlled verify:testExists(registry/ouro/components/ouro/lightbox/lightbox.mosaic.test.tsx::Lightbox full screen > covers the whole screen with no frame, from the thumbnails or controlled)
[^popup]: registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog-parts.tsx verify:fileLine(registry/ouro/components/ouro/dialog/dialog-parts.tsx, /const holdRef = useMergedRef\(ref, useHeldTop\(\)\);/)

author: hugogresse
body:
Closes #1476

With the project setting **Hide votes until the user vote** (`hideVotesUntilUserVote`) on, the results of a talk appeared as soon as the attendee cast any single vote, which biased the next choices. Following the maintainer's chosen behaviour ("a single vote should not display the results, but a refresh on the page after a vote yes"), not the end-of-talk timer discussed in the thread.

## Behaviour
- Whether to show the results is decided **once per talk page load**: they show only if the attendee had already voted on this talk when it loaded.
- Votes cast during the visit keep counts and other attendees' comments hidden.
- The next load of the talk (refresh, or back to the list and in again) shows them.
- Unchanged: outside the vote window or with `?displayVotes=true` results show; with the setting off nothing changes.
- "Voted" means an active or moderated-hidden vote on the talk. A user who removed all their votes counts as not voted (previously any vote document, deleted ones included, counted).

## Changes
- `voteResultsVisibility.ts`: pure `snapshotVotedOnTalkAtLoad` (taken once per talk, waits for the user votes to settle so an early render never marks "not voted") and `shouldShowVoteResults`, unit tested.
- `Talk.tsx` keeps the snapshot in component state, keyed by talk id; `getVoteResultSelectorSelector` takes it instead of the live user votes. The selector now uses `isVoteWindowOpen` directly, primitive input selectors and a shared empty result, so it stays memoized.
- Vote slice: `userVotesSettled` flag, set when the user votes load or fail to load.
- `isVoteAllowed` refuses a vote until the user votes have settled (same "try again in a moment" message as before sign-in). A vote cast in that gap would have landed in the "voted at load" snapshot, and it also missed the existing vote to update. A load error still allows voting, as before.
- Admin help text (en, fr) and the API schema description describe the new behaviour.
- Cypress: new case in `talk.spec.js` turns the setting on for the test project via the Firestore emulator REST API, votes (boolean + comment), asserts results stay hidden, reloads, asserts they show, and turns the setting back off.

## Screenshots
Local emulators, `testprojectid` with the setting on, fresh anonymous user.

| After voting (same visit) | After a page refresh |
| --- | --- |
| ![After voting: comment saved and vote selected, no counts and no comments list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17ed8ade-587f-49db-9fa3-391298095585) | ![After a refresh: vote count and the comments list are shown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/807a0f28-6118-4e55-89d7-ae727c603fb2) |

Before this PR, the counts and comments list appeared right after the first vote, as in the right-hand image.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` (Biome), `npm run lint:i18n`, functions `tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `vitest run src/feedback`: 36 tests, incl. new visibility, reducer and `isVoteAllowed` cases
- [x] Cypress `cypress/e2e/feedback/talk.spec.js` on the emulators: 5/5 passing
- [x] By hand on the emulators: vote and comment, results stay hidden; refresh, results show
- [x] `/code-review max`: 7 findings fixed, 1 kept as intended (deleted votes don't count), 5 pre-existing or low-impact left out (votes not reset on auth user change, live results listener running while hidden, route vs store talk id for one unpainted render, E2E writing to the shared fixture project, `?displayVotes=false` showing results)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: giomf
body:
## Description

**Summary of Changes:**

Draft for discussing the design proposed in #2236: sync project state over the network by listening to `Doc` signals instead of a per-action Tardis code in every UI method.

This PR covers Functions only, but the same approach could be extended to every `Doc` element (fixtures, groups, palettes, ...), since they all emit change signals and serialize themselves with `saveXML()`/`loadXML()`.

- **engine:** new `DocSync`. It listens to `Doc`'s Function signals and emits each changed Function as its `saveXML()`, batched over 100 ms. Received snapshots are copied over the existing Function with `copyFrom()` while the universes are held. Remote changes are not echoed back.
- **qmlui:** new `SyncFunction`/`SyncFunctionDelete` network codes. Tardis still forwards the actions DocSync doesn't cover and records everything for undo.

This fixes Function changes that never reached the peer, e.g. cloned Functions, a Sequence's bound Scene, RGB Matrix "save to sequence", chaser speed modes.

**Known limitations:**
- Changes to existing Shows still use per-action sync (`Show::copyFrom()` duplicates tracks instead of replacing them).
- Two peers creating a Function at the same time can pick the same ID.
- The server still doesn't forward a client's change to the other clients.

**Related Issues:**

#2236

**Results:**

body:
## What changes for visitors

- **Every card arrives sealed.** A recipient first sees an envelope addressed to her ("Gửi Mẹ yêu") with a wax seal in her flowers' colour. Opening it lifts the flap, raises the letter, and starts her bouquet growing. Escape opens it too, and with reduced motion it opens at once.
- **Chat previews show her name.** Links are now `/for/Lan` (English) or `/gui/Lan` (Vietnamese). Messenger, Zalo and others show "Lan, a bloom for you 💐" with a share image drawn for that name. The message and sender stay in the `#fragment`, which never reaches a server. Card pages are `noindex`, and analytics records them only as `/for/[name]` and `/gui/[name]`.
- **Replies and previews.** A card ends with "Send a bloom back to {sender}". Preview shows the sender the sealed envelope exactly as it will arrive.
- **Story.** The timeline adds 1995 (Beijing Platform) and follows UN wording.
- **Fixes carried over from the old page:** in-page links no longer wipe a card from the `#fragment`, and the EN/VI buttons now meet WCAG 2.5.3 (label in name).
- **Old links still work.** Fragment-only links shared before this change (`/#to=…&lang=vi`) still open.

## Under the hood

- Next.js 16.4 App Router on Node 26.13, Yarn 4 via Corepack, the same pinned toolchain as open-kiln.
- The CSS bouquet, sky canvas and stylesheet are ported as they were. The bouquet and page sections are server components. Client state uses `useSyncExternalStore`, so hydration never mismatches the language picked before first paint.
- Share images are generated with `next/og` from a captured background and local font subsets. The function traces only `src/features/og/assets/`.
- Security headers: a content security policy, `nosniff`, `DENY` framing, a strict referrer policy and a permissions policy. An `X-Build` header lets the production watch confirm which commit is live.

## Checks

- **IWD quality:** immutable install, high/critical audit, formatting, zero-warning ESLint, route types, TypeScript, 18 unit tests, 14 lint-rule tests, production build.
- **IWD browser:** 33 Playwright scenarios at 375, 768 and 1440 px, including axe WCAG 2.2 AA audits.
- **IWD production** (runs after merge): read-only `@smoke` checks against the live domain after each production deploy and every 6 hours. It opens a "Production check failed" issue on failure.

All of these pass locally on Node 26.13.0.

## Settings changed outside the repo (already applied)

- **GitHub:**
  - ruleset *Protect main with verified changes*: PR required, IWD quality and IWD browser required on an up-to-date branch, linear history, no force pushes or deletion
  - squash-only merges with merged branches deleted
  - SHA-pinned Actions required
  - Dependabot alerts and security updates, and CodeQL default setup, turned on
- **Vercel:**
  - Node 26.x and Fluid compute
  - Web Analytics turned on
  - protected source maps
  - Vercel Authentication on everything except the production domain
  - deployment checks: IWD quality and IWD browser block the production alias

## After merging

- [ ] Set the dashboard framework preset to Next.js: `vercel project update internation-women-day --framework nextjs --scope=perceval-wilhelms-projects`
- [ ] Optionally enable Speed Insights yourself; the CLI flags it as possibly adding charges: `vercel project speed-insights enable internation-women-day --scope=perceval-wilhelms-projects`
- [ ] Confirm the first **IWD production** run passes

Settings record: `docs/deployment.md`. Contributor guide: `AGENTS.md`.

author: hndrr
body:
Adds standalone audio monitoring and range selection, plus small capture controls for the existing Recorder and Live nodes.

- **Audio Meter** displays independent left/right dBFS meters and silence status while capture runs, and passes `AUDIO` through unchanged.
- **Audio Range Select** previews the full input waveform, synchronizes drag selection with start/end seconds, and outputs only the selected samples. Load Waveform executes only through this node; it creates no audio files.
- **Recorder** supports pause/resume within the same sharing session, excluding paused time from the recording.
- **Live** saves an immutable snapshot of the latest N seconds as Original, WAV or M4A while capture continues, including repeated saves and saves after stopping.

Existing node IDs, outputs and runtime dependencies are preserved. README screenshots and example workflows are updated; the package check now requires the new nodes, frontend files and all four screenshots.

## Validation

- Python: **110 passed** (`python -m pytest -q`).
- Frontend/worklet: **80 passed** (`node --test tests/*.mjs`).
- Release/package tooling: **40 passed** (`python -m unittest discover -s .github/tests -q`).
- Browser checks with generated stereo audio covered independent meter cleanup, silence detection, pause/resume, saving while paused, and Live saves in all three formats without interrupting capture.
- A 0.94–3.06 second selection produced a 2.12 second downstream audio preview. Saved files were decoded to verify codec, sample rate, channels and duration.
- Review regressions cover array-form partial execution, 26 shared Python/JavaScript sample-boundary cases, concurrent Recorder/Live saves, malformed requests, expired snapshots and unchanged idle meter rendering.

The browser sharing picker and OS system-audio permissions were not exercised. Screenshots use generated demo audio; the periodic waveform reflects that source.

## Screenshots

**Recorder pause/resume**

author: yuezk
body:
## Summary

Browser authentication can stop with ‘URL handler registration did not take effect’ when a desktop-specific user MIME override still selects an older callback handler. The generic xdg-mime setter writes mimeapps.list, which has lower priority than files such as niri-mimeapps.list.

## Main Changes

- Move Linux, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD callback registration into an XDG module.
- After setting the generic default, update the first active user desktop override containing a globalprotectcallback default, following XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP order.
- Replace only the callback default, preserving unrelated settings, comments, line endings, file permissions, and symlinks. Keep the final effective-handler verification.
- Add regression coverage for registration, multiple desktops, absent overrides, and file preservation.

## API / Usage

For XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=Niri:GNOME, registration updates the callback entry in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/niri-mimeapps.list if present; otherwise it checks gnome-mimeapps.list. Files without a callback default remain unchanged. The selected entry becomes:

```ini
[Default Applications]
x-scheme-handler/globalprotectcallback=gpgui.desktop;
```

No CLI flags change.

## Related PRs

- Related to the browser callback report in [NixOS/nixpkgs#573002](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/573002#issuecomment-6537777675).

## Verification

- cargo check -p auth --features browser-auth — passed on macOS.
- cargo test -p auth --features browser-auth callback:: — 16 passed.
- cargo fmt -p auth -- --check and git diff --check — passed.
- Reproduced the old-handler result with upstream xdg-mime 1.2.1 and isolated configuration; the same registration path selects gpgui.desktop after the change.
- Linux cross-compilation was blocked by the missing x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc compiler. Native Linux, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD desktop testing remains outstanding.

Grid's component docs, which ship in the package and feed `astryx component Grid`, said `align` and `justify` default to `'stretch'`. Grid's record (FR5) and the code say unset leaves the browser default: `Grid.tsx` applies no `align-items` or `justify-items` style when a prop is unset. Someone reading the docs could expect an image or other naturally sized item to stretch, when the browser's `normal` keeps its natural size. The docs now say what happens.

- `Grid.tsx`: `align != null && alignStyles[align]` and `justify != null && justifyStyles[justify]`, so no style applies when unset.

author: uthree
body:
Stacked on #83 for its `[workspace]` fix; retarget to `main` once that merges. This is the one change in the series that alters shipped audio.

## The measurement

A `pop-band` preset composed and rendered on a Mac, measured with `ffmpeg astats` rather than reasoned about:

| Stem | DC offset | Peak |
|------|-----------|------|
| `lead` (`auris.physical.violin`) | **+0.005740** | -12.20 dBFS |
| `strings` (`auris.physical.violin`) | +0.001486 | -21.95 dBFS |
| `Drums` | -0.001511 | -0.30 dBFS |
| guitar, lead_alt (`electric_guitar`), keys, piano (`piano`), pluck (`mallet`), bass, sub_bass, riser | ≤ 1.3e-4 | — |
| **master** | **L +0.005786 / R +0.004077** | -0.3006 dBFS |

The only two stems carrying any are the two the composer gave the bowed model. On `lead` the offset is 2.3 % of that stem's own peak.

## Why it was there

A bow pushes the string one way for as long as it is drawn, so its friction force has a mean — a pluck and a strike average to nothing, which is why only this model shows it. A bridge does not transmit that mean to the air, and nothing in the chain was removing it: `body.rs:40` fits its highpass for `Model::Piano` only, and `body.rs:188` asserts the consequence outright — "The piano's soundboard does not radiate DC at all; the others pass it unchanged." That decision was never tested against an excitation that *has* a mean.

The cost is headroom. The limiter judges absolute peak, so an offset comes off the ceiling before any music reaches it.

## Where the blocker goes, and the placement the suite rejected

Two placements were tried:

1. **In `Body`** — where it belongs physically, and wrong. The body runs on the summed stereo bus *after* each voice's envelope (`physical.rs:913` applies `raw * envelope` per voice; the body comes later). A 5 Hz blocker there rings for about a second after the last note, with no envelope left to gate it, and `violin_legato_keeps_the_existing_wave_and_counts_overlapping_keys` caught it on `peak(&released[4000..]) < 1e-6`. A track that never quite reaches silence breaks tail measurement and the `--no-tail` export, so this was a real defect and not a stale assertion.
2. **On `StringModel::next`'s return** — before the envelope, so the envelope gates the settling. The returned value is the bridge read and is *not* part of the loop (the loop writes from `neck` and `filtered`), so the friction junction's own dynamics are untouched.

Placement 2 is what this PR does. Worth recording because the first one looks more correct than it is.

## `DcBlocker`, in `auris-dsp`

New primitive, where the instrument crates' primitives belong. Two choices worth stating:

* **One-pole, not a `Biquad` highpass.** At 5 Hz against a 192 kHz rate the normalised frequency is 2.6e-5, and a direct-form biquad spends most of its `f32` mantissa on the difference between coefficients that are all but equal. This form has one coefficient and stays well conditioned wherever the corner is.
* **`Default` written out, not derived.** A derived retention of zero is `y[n] = x[n] - x[n-1]` — a differentiator. An unprepared value belongs to a voice that has not sounded yet and must pass audio through untouched; there is a test for exactly that.

Five hertz because it is below every fundamental the bow plays: a bowed cello's open C is 65 Hz and a double bass's open E is 41 Hz, which this costs 0.07 dB. Tested against the closed form `f / hypot(f, corner)` at 44.1, 48, 96 and 192 kHz.

## The measurement half

`ExportInspection` gains `dc_offset` — the worst channel's mean, sign kept. None of `lufs`, `peak_db` or `true_peak_db` can see an offset, so a master could pass all three and still carry one, and `verify_render` could not report what it cannot measure. The struct is `Serialize`, so it reaches the agent-facing report too. The worst channel rather than the mix's mean, because a mono source panned off centre offsets one side more and it is that side which runs out of room first.

## Verification

Re-rendering the same project with the same seed:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Left DC | +0.005786 | **-0.001228** |
| Right DC | +0.004077 | **-0.001297** |
| Peak | -0.3006 dBFS | -0.3006 dBFS |
| Flat factor | 0.000000 | 0.000000 |

`cargo test -p auris-synth`: **219 passed, 0 failed** — including the legato test that rejected the first placement. `cargo test -p auris-session export_inspection`: 2 passed. `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p auris-dsp -p auris-synth -p auris-session --all-targets --locked`: clean.

## What is left

The drum stem's own **-0.001511**, which used to partly cancel the violin's and is now what remains in the master. At 0.15 % of that stem's peak it is a tenth of what this was, and a different source — worth its own look rather than widening this change.

**Draft: the shimmer gate fails.** Two views fail: PCL east 600 m (main 0.12 → branch 0.15, the limit is +0.02) and PCL east 250 m (-0.05 → -0.03). The 120 m east and north-east 250 m views pass. The demo stage has not run. The next step is a frame-difference map at 600 m east.

What changed in the PCL build (only tile t_0_1; the other 6 buildings in the tile are proved identical):
- **Plaza furniture.** 11 umbrellas and 12 picnic tables. Their places come from the two solved cameras: table feet are ray-cast onto the plaza; the two umbrellas nearest the stair top are triangulated from both photos, and those rays meet within 0.13-0.18 m.
- **Two lamp posts and the flowering shrub** in the north stair planter.
- **Concrete colour.** Live drew the concrete brighter and pinker than both photos, while the pavers matched within 2/255. It is now the photos' neutral grey. The window recess panels are the same concrete, as the photos show.
- **Fades** for the umbrella poles, the table frames and the flowers (photo_materials.json).

What we know about the failure: a change to the umbrella and shrub colours alone left the gate numbers exactly the same. The likely cause is the concrete or panel colour change on the window grid, but that is not proven yet.

Journal: 2026-11-01, mac/v2-pcl-r3. PCL round 3 adds the plaza's umbrellas, picnic tables, lamps and the yellow-flowering shrub, and corrects the concrete to the photos' neutral grey. The scores against the owner's photos are about 7.5 for the stair view (live about 7.5) and about 7.5 for the entrance view (live about 7). The east 250 m and 600 m shimmer views are over the limit, so this stays a draft until the cause is found.

author: vogella
body: FormHeading.onPaint rendered every paint of a heading with a separator or background image into a new Image the size of the client area and copied it onto the paint GC. On GTK the heading repaints whenever one of its children redraws, so this allocation also happens without the heading itself changing. The heading now draws straight onto the paint GC and restores the GC colors afterwards, and it is created with SWT.DOUBLE_BUFFERED so painting stays flicker-free on Windows (GTK and Cocoa already double buffer). This follows the same change made for title bar sections in Section.onPaint.

author: aethai
body:
Built on #269 (it uses `ListedRoleOf`), so merge that one first; this diff shrinks to one commit then.

From the review of point 10:

- **Local panel could ban nobody.** With an empty GM list every account is Admin, so the rank rule answered 403 to every ban. The rule now compares the role by the lists.
- **Unban had no rank rule.** A Moderator could lift a ban an Admin placed. Same rule as a ban now, and a ban stands against anyone below the one who placed it.
- **Logout and 2FA reset stay open between Admins, on purpose.** They already need Admin, are audited, and the reset is how an Admin who lost a phone gets back in. Written down in `panel.md`.
- **IPv6.** 30 of 30 logins from one /64 passed through a trusted proxy. Login and gift code budgets now count the /64, like the sign-up limit.
- **Refused Host.** A proxy that keeps the player's Host with neither option set saw 404s with nothing logged. One warning per ten minutes names `PublicUrl` and `TrustedProxies`.

Filtered tests: `PanelAdmin`, `Panel`, `PanelSignUp`, `LoginLimit`, `GiftCode`, `OpsEndpoints`, 93 passed. New: `AnUnbanFollowsTheSameRanks`, `AnOpenLocalPanelCanBanAndUnban`, `AnIpv6NetworkSharesOneBudget`. The warning has no unit test; checked on a real server: 5 requests with a foreign Host gave 404 and one log line, and the machine's own Host still answered 200.

author: koradon
body:
## Intent

The captain reported (2026-11-01) that the daily log did not record commits, and explained that captains-log groups the logs when the first day of a new month starts. Diagnosis by firstmate (read `~/git/vault/General/Captains Log/Daily Log Publication Stops On A Half-Finished Rename Reorganization.md` and verify it yourself in the code): at the month boundary `LogManager._organize_old_log_files` moves the previous months day files into `<project>/<year>/<month>/` with a plain filesystem rename (`_move_log_file_to_year_month`, `src/logs/log_manager.py`), and the staging code in `src/git/git_operations.py` (`add_all`, driven by `git status --porcelain`) then adds paths; for a staged rename `R old -> new` it adds the old path "for deletion". Once any run has left the log repository with staged renames or partly staged moves, the old path no longer exists in the index or the worktree, so `git add <old> ...` fails with "pathspec ... did not match any files", the whole batch aborts, and every later hook run repeats it: entries are saved locally to the day file and queued as JSON under `~/.captains-log/pending/` but never committed or pushed. Observed on 2026-11-01: 30 consecutive failures from 08:37 UTC, 39 pending entries, repository state in `~/git/vault/daily-log` with 6 staged renames, 19 unstaged deletions, 2 untracked paths. The ask: fix this so that a month-boundary grouping, or any half-finished move state, can never block publication again, and the queued entries publish on the next successful run. The resulting PR is merged by the captain; repairing the captains current log repository is NOT part of this task (firstmate handles that separately).

## What Changed

- Rewrote `GitOperations.add_all()` to read `git status --porcelain -z`, stage rename destinations and deletions without passing missing rename sources to `git add`, and keep staging other markdown paths when one path fails.
- Month-boundary log organization uses `git mv` for tracked files in git-backed log repositories when moving day files into year/month subdirectories.
- Added integration regressions for half-finished grouping and pending backlog publication, and updated the publication reliability spec to describe the new staging behavior.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change directly fixes the reported pathspec failure mode, adds prevention via git mv during month grouping, and is covered by real-git integration tests including half-finished rename recovery and pending clearance on publish.

## Testing

Ran four focused pytest cases for staging, commit-and-push, partial-failure tolerance, and pending replay after half-finished grouping; then drove the real CLI via a disposable sandbox script that reproduced staged renames plus a pending JSON queue, November publication with October files at project root, and confirmed legacy `git add` on missing rename sources fails while `GitOperations.add_all` succeeds. Scenarios A–C have live transcript evidence; scenarios D–E were exercised only through pytest in the rejected run and are marked untested for live validation.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 3 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Commit hook run (`update_log`) while the log git repo has half-finished month moves (staged renames) and queued pending JSON — publishes new commit entry and backlog to remote, clears pending, leaves… | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M6BV0RANWA6HHGSMZRQAHCZM/live-driver-transcript.txt (sections A) |
| First-day-of-month commit when a prior-month daily file still sits in the project root — organizes into year/month and publishes without leaving a dirty log repository | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M6BV0RANWA6HHGSMZRQAHCZM/live-driver-transcript.txt (sections B) |
| Adversarial half-finished rename state — direct `git add` on missing old path still fails (legacy failure mode) but product staging via `GitOperations.add_all` completes without pathspec abort | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M6BV0RANWA6HHGSMZRQAHCZM/live-driver-transcript.txt (sections C) |
| One bad markdown staging path does not prevent other log markdown paths from being staged | ⏸️ untested | no | Prior payload did not establish a live result: only pytest reference tests/test_month_grouping_staging.py::test_one_bad_add_path_does_not_abort_other_staging was cited with live=false while result was… |
| `GitOperations.commit_and_push` finishes half-finished renames and unstaged deletions then pushes | ⏸️ untested | no | Prior payload did not establish a live result: only pytest reference tests/test_month_grouping_staging.py::test_commit_and_push_finishes_staged_renames_and_unstaged_deletions was cited with live=false… |

author: rami195
body:
Sin issue asociado: son arreglos de una ronda de QA local del 2026-11-01.

## What it does

- **Agregar al plan → plan nuevo (CU27):** desde Explorar o el detalle de una actividad, el creador abría directamente en el paso 2 (Recorrido, la búsqueda del catálogo). Ahora abre en el paso 1 (Plan), con la actividad ya en el recorrido que se ve debajo del formulario.
- **Mis planes (CU29):** toda la tarjeta abre el plan, no solo el título. Editar, eliminar y publicar siguen funcionando: el link del título se estira sobre la tarjeta y los controles quedan por encima, así que sigue siendo un solo link por tarjeta.
- **Ver plan (CU29):** en mobile, Editar / Eliminar / Guardar / Compartir / WhatsApp se cortaban como venían y quedaba un botón suelto abajo. Ahora van en una grilla de 3 columnas, con el ícono arriba del texto.
- **Favoritos:** en mobile, las pestañas Planes y Actividades quedaban en los extremos de la pantalla; ahora van juntas, como en desktop.
- **Panel de admin (CU4):** no había forma de cerrar sesión ("Salir del panel" solo vuelve a la app). Ahora el sidebar y el menú mobile tienen "Cerrar sesión", con la misma confirmación que el menú de usuario.
- **Navbar:** saqué "Crear plan" de la barra superior mobile. Crear un plan sigue disponible desde Mis planes (menú de cuenta) y Comunidad, además de Planificar en la barra inferior.

Las sugerencias del creador que repetían siempre las mismas actividades se arreglan en el back: SmartPlan-UTN/SmartPlan-back#158. Este PR no depende de ese.

## How to test it

```bash
git switch fix/qa-feedback-2026-11-01
node --version    # 24.x, see .nvmrc
pnpm install
pnpm lint
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

Con el back corriendo y la ventana a menos de 900 px:
1. Explorar → una actividad → "Agregar al plan" → crear plan nuevo: abre en el paso 1 (Plan) y la actividad aparece en el recorrido.
2. Mis planes: tocar cualquier parte de una tarjeta abre el plan; el lápiz, la papelera y "Publicar" hacen lo suyo sin abrirlo.
3. Abrir un plan propio y bajar hasta las acciones: quedan en una grilla pareja.
4. Favoritos: Planes y Actividades van juntas a la izquierda.
5. Con un admin, en /admin, "Cerrar sesión" (sidebar, o menú ☰ en mobile) pide confirmación y lleva a /login.
6. La barra superior ya no muestra "Crear plan".

## What's out of scope

- Los cambios de estilo no tienen QA visual en navegador todavía: conviene mirarlos en mobile con los pasos de arriba.
- Encontrado en la misma prueba y sin tocar acá: Planificar falla con `NO_VALID_COMBINATIONS` cuando la ubicación del dispositivo cae lejos del catálogo, en vez de ampliar el radio.

---

## Definition of Done

Full criteria in [`skills/02-git-flow/DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md`](https://github.com/SmartPlan-UTN/SmartPlan-front/blob/develop/skills/02-git-flow/DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md).

- [x] The branch starts from `develop` and the PR targets `develop`
- [x] `pnpm lint` with no errors (5 existing warnings in files not touched here)
- [ ] `pnpm test` green: 1.387/1.388 in the full run. The failing test (`CreatePlanForm.assistant-races` › "does not ask again for a route it already answered", 3 s timing) passes 3/3 in isolation; CI decides.
- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] The issue's acceptance criteria are met (no issue; the QA points above)
- [x] No hardcoded credentials, tokens, or URLs
- [x] Styles use design system tokens, no hand-written hex values
- [x] Loading, error, and empty states are covered (no new API consumption)
- [x] [`TRACKING.md`](https://github.com/SmartPlan-UTN/SmartPlan-front/blob/develop/TRACKING.md) updated: status, branch, and PR
- [x] Documented where relevant (`README.md` or `skills/`)

O painel passa a salvar somente o usuário do Showdown. Ao ligar ou reconectar, abre Edge/Chrome em um perfil dedicado para autenticação; o bot recebe uma autorização temporária vinculada à conta e à conexão. Falhas encerram a tentativa sem retornar ao login por senha.

A integração instala o auxiliar Windows e a caixa de mensagens temporária do serviço, migra configurações do painel ao ligar/reiniciar e mantém o modo de senha explícito para instalações Linux sem interface gráfica. A documentação explica o fluxo e seus limites: a classificação de bot emitida pelo Showdown é preservada; não há garantia de evitar ou remover essa marca.

Validação local: 135 testes Python do backend, 3 testes de autenticação no patch Ai-vgc, transporte CDP/cliente JavaScript simulados no PowerShell 5.1, 3.548 verificações do painel, sintaxe dos scripts e aplicação/reversão do patch no commit fixado. Nenhuma conta real foi autenticada.

body:
## 目标

实现真实仓库读取的持久缓存适配层，保留现有无缓存 `RepositorySession` 行为。任务：`repository-cache`。

## 行为

- 新增显式 `CachedRepositorySession`，注入现有 session、同一 `CacheStore` clone 和匹配账户的 `CacheScope`。
- 缓存 repository metadata、branches、ref/固定 commit、tree、README discovery 和 blob bytes；离线 content 继续走原有准备/大小/二进制语义。
- 返回 Network/Snapshot、fetched/verified 时间与完整性；OfflineOnly 未读内容明确 NotCached，不冒充空值或最新 main。
- 版本化 DTO 校验仓库与 Git 对象关系；账户/partition 隔离；写入前 ticket 和仓库级权限 proof；旧响应与取消不发布。
- 精确表示的 304 复用匹配 validator 的原 bytes；validator 丢失/不匹配自动无条件重取；no-store 使旧值失效。
- 所有 CacheStore 操作在 blocking worker；401、取消、上下文失效及模糊 403/404 不用缓存伪装成功。

## 验证

全部通过共享 `node scripts/verify.mjs -- cargo ...`：

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check --locked --all-targets`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --locked`（959 项）
- `cargo build --locked`
- 9 项 repository-cache 真实服务组合测试：临时账户/CacheStore + 合成 PAT + mock transport，在线→关闭/重建→离线 repository/tree/README/source、A→B、跨账户、304/no-store/损坏/取消/旧响应/gate/Partial/空/二进制。

## 边界与文档

正式 Shell 组装、账户 lifecycle 事件和离线 UI 由后续唯一接线任务交付；本 PR 不做 GUI 或真实 PAT/实网验收。行为与验证边界见 `docs/repository-cache.md` 和本任务开发日志。

author: nlimper
body:
## Summary

Booting with no panel connected (or a panel that does not respond) took about 10 minutes: every BUSY wait in the boot-screen path ran into its timeout. This adds a short presence check before the boot screen.

`bootPanelResponds()` pulses the panel reset and waits up to 2 s for BUSY to report idle (HIGH on UC81xx, LOW on SSD16xx). After a hardware reset every controller does that within milliseconds, which is also what the GoodDisplay sample code waits for. If BUSY stays busy, `initDisplay()` logs a warning, cuts the rail with `pwrmgm(false)` and skips the boot screen.

- Boot without a panel: ~10 min → ~4 s.
- `pwrmgm(false)` instead of `epdSessionForceOff()`: ForceOff sends sleep commands and waits on BUSY, which is exactly what hangs here (same pattern as the FastEPD init-failed tail).
- Dual chip-select (`BBEP_SPLIT_BUFFER`) panels, and configs without a BUSY or RESET pin, are not probed (untested), so their behaviour is unchanged.
- No change to image uploads after boot.

## Testing

On a Seeed EN04 (nRF52840), with this change on top of a branch that also adds new panels (not part of this PR):
- No panel connected: boot completes in ~4 s, log shows `Panel not responding (BUSY stays busy after reset) - skipping boot screen`, BLE works and a config can be written.
- Panels connected: boot screen as before for the GDEY0266F52H (57), GDEM0122T61 (13, SSD1681) and GDEY029F51H (30).

Builds against the current bb_epaper pin: `nrf52840custom`, `esp32-s3-N16R8`, `esp32-c3-N4`, `esp32-wrover-e-N4R8`.

## C53 — P0 real Stripe TEST acceptance execution blocker (REVIEW ONLY; NO-GO)
**Base:** Q73 #305 exact independently green `168a3e5100ce9177ef173798a8ed02d5e2306b8b` ([CI 41308232306](https://github.com/faisalwrokksa-hub/THEEPMOTEST/actions/runs/41308232306), 4/4 SUCCESS). **Source head:** `c8a1c73903e820c238baa6127e72806daad7657e`. Four isolated files, no C48–C52 rework.

**Executable P0 defect:** `StripeBillingService.prepareRecurringCheckout()` exists but is intentionally not exposed by the customer billing controller, so the required first-customer TEST subscription checkout cannot be initiated by an authenticated operator. C52 is an offline receipt validator, not a provider executor.

**Minimal fix:** Separate `StripeTestOperatorController` at `POST /api/v1/subscription/billing/stripe/operator/recurring-checkout`, registered with existing session TenantMiddleware. Requires `pmoa_admin`, HTTPS `req.secure`, empty request body (no caller tenant/price/amount), independently provisioned operator secret in constant-time comparison, `DEPLOYMENT_ENV=staging`, explicit `STRIPE_TEST_OPERATOR_ENABLED=true` and `STRIPE_RECURRING_CHECKOUT_ENABLED=true`, TEST-only Stripe key/webhook secret and exact HTTPS `staging.theepmo.com` webhook URL. Existing service independently validates server-owned Price, tenant locks, replay protection and pending-only session; no entitlement grant or live mode. No customer frontend route, payment, secrets or deployment.

**Synthetic local focused tests:** C53 policy/controller source tests 3/3 PASS under Node 22 `--experimental-strip-types`; no real Stripe call. **CI for this exact SHA:** pending independent Actions verification; do not call green before 4/4. The existing C29/C30 tests intentionally continue to prohibit customer exposure in `billing.controller.ts`.

**External prerequisites (NOT authorized/provisioned):** isolated approved HTTPS staging, restricted TEST key and webhook secret, operator credential in secret store, approved recurring TEST Price, two disposable tenant sessions, reviewer. Do not invoke the operator route or perform test checkout without separate authorization. Seven provider scenarios 0/7, commercial 0/9, `candidateSha:null`, `decision:NO-GO`.

**EPMO5:** Integrate only after exact-head 4/4 CI, inspect concurrent F62 (red verify), confirm no changed-path overlap and rerun combined exact-SHA CI. Never merge protected main, deploy, modify DNS, or charge live money.

VibeGlobe grants no right to map data. The application chooses its sources, holds their keys and keeps to their terms, whether development-only, non-commercial or paid plans.

- **Docs:** the sources guide ("Provider profiles") and the README's licensing section now say this.
- **Playground:** the Europe preset reads two variables from a never-committed `apps/playground/.env.local`:

  - `VITE_ONLINE_IMAGERY_CREDIT`: the credit the provider asks for.
- **What the preset does with them:** it adds that imagery worldwide from level 12 to 19, above the free sources. The imagery is asked from the network only and its credit is required. Below level 12, the free sources and the offline package show as before.

This replaces #109. The earlier branch had first pushed the entry as F681, and main took F681 meanwhile, so the feature-list guard of the push run failed on that renumbering. The changes are the same, in one commit on current main.

author: prdb-net
body:
The core of the plugin:

- **Candidates** – movies without a prdb id in libraries where the prdb metadata provider is switched on (the same rule Jellyfin applies before calling a metadata provider, via `IBaseItemManager.IsMetadataFetcherEnabled`), so a library prdb is not enabled for never reaches prdb.
- **Identification** – file name without folder, size and OSHash, 200 files per `POST /videos/identify` with `includeVideoDetails`. Files are hashed batch by batch.
- **Match policy** – by confidence: Exact ← hash switch, Strong ← exact file name switch, Probable ← heuristics switch. Ambiguous, Partial, None and unknown values never apply.
- **Applying** – sets the `Prdb` provider id, saves the item and queues a full refresh that replaces metadata and images (locked fields stay). The video document from the identify answer is cached for that refresh.
- **Remembering** – answers that apply nothing are stored per file path with name, size, modification time and the switches; the file is asked about again when any of those change or after seven days. A known hash is reused instead of reading the file again.
- **Triggers** – scheduled task *prdb → Identify library* (daily, rechecks stale answers) and a post-scan task after every library scan (new files only). One run at a time. A prdb failure stops the run; the next run picks the files up.

## Validation

- `dotnet test`: 113 tests pass, including every combination of confidence and switches, remembering/rechecking (changed file, changed switches, stale answers, restart), batching and failure handling.

author: capazme
body:
L3 of spec #391 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-document-hyperlinks-design.md` §11). It covers: the link set (§4); the address client for `POST /fetch_norm_links` (#395, L1); «Prepara i link» as state; and the paste builder (§5.2). This is web logic only, with no screen: L5 draws it. Decisions applied: G-398 (all ten §12 questions answered as recommended) and G-395 (the link is dated today). **Stacked on #399** (PR 2 of #376), because the links come from its rows. The base is develop so that CI runs, which means the diff also shows #399's commits until #399 is merged. This PR's own work is commit `1250350a`. Merge #399 first. ## What changes - **`documentLinks.ts`** (pure): - **Which rows get a link** (§4.1–§4.4): - a row read from its own words, or chosen by the user for that row, is linked once its address is `ok`; - an inherited row, or one completed in bulk, gets a link only once confirmed (Q8); - a row left out («Senza link») or still to complete never gets one; - a range or «e ss.» links to its first article (Q7). - **Addresses**: any address that fails `sourceAddress` (#385) is dropped, even if the server sent it. - **`linkSpan`**: the link covers the citation from the article head to the act. It leaves out «l'»/«dell'» and the punctuation after the act, and never crosses a line break. - **`documentLinks`**: produces `{start, end, href}`, the shape L4's writer takes. A list gets one link per number. - **`buildLinkedPaste`**: - HTML: one `

` per line, every character escaped (the address too), only `` and no other markup; - plain text: the address in brackets after each linked citation; - a link with a bad address, across a line break or overlapping another is left out, and the text stays whole. - **`copyLinkedPaste`**: writes HTML and plain text in one `clipboard.write`, with the items as promises so a late answer does not lose the click. If that write is refused, it writes the plain text alone. Where the clipboard cannot be written at all, it throws, so L5 can say so. - **`prepareLinks`**: «Prepara i link», «Riprova» (`retry`) and the user's choices. It asks only for the distinct norms not yet answered; «Riprova» also asks again for the ones the source left silent. Each call costs quota points. - **An empty annex is kept as `''`** (the act's own text, chosen by the user for an `ambiguous_part`), distinct from no annex, as the route reads it. - **`documentLinkServer.ts`**: - chunks of at most 200 norms, 30 distinct acts and 48 KB, sent one after another, with 25 s for each; - acts are counted on the type as written, so the browser never counts fewer acts than the server's `normalize_act_type` and no chunk is refused; - no `pin_day` is sent: the server dates the link to today in Rome (G-395); - only the norms' readings `{act_type, act_number, date, article, annex}` are sent, and no norm is logged; - a failed chunk stops the reading; its norms and those after it are left for «Riprova». ## What leaves the browser (§8) When the user asks for links, the norms to link go out as readings: each distinct norm once, including those of confirmed inherited rows. Never the text, a passage, the place of a citation, or how a row was found. With «Riconosci solo nel browser» (PR 3 of #376), L5 must not call this at all; that switch belongs to the screen. ## Measures `documentLinksCorpus.test.ts` replays the route's answers, recorded from a running API on the spec's corpus (`__tests__/corpus/links.json`, `record_links.py`). The test fails on any link whose act or article differs from the corpus's mark, checked in the address too: the Normattiva URN with its number, year and `~artN`, or EUR-Lex's year and number. - **94 links written, 0 wrong.** As the rows come, 7 inherited rows wait for a confirmation. - No link: 14 rows to complete, and **4 articles of the Costituzione answered `date_incomplete`**. - **That is an L1 defect, not this PR's.** In strict mode the route treats an act with no date as incomplete, and the Costituzione has neither date nor number. So «art. 24 Cost.» never gets a link. The fix belongs in the Python API: treat the Costituzione as the codes are treated, with its fixed URN. ## Tests - New: `documentLinks.test.ts` (20), `documentLinkServer.test.ts` (8), `documentLinksCorpus.test.ts` (3). All green, run file by file. - `tsc -b`: green. `eslint` on the folder: green. - **Not yet run:** the full suite, a browser pass (there is no screen in L3) and the Word/Pages paste check (L5). CI runs the full suite. On this Mac the suite is not reliable under tonight's load, while #399's CI is all green. - **Independent review** (code-reviewer): no blocker found. I fixed its medium finding (an empty annex must stay `''`). I also applied its low ones: tighter address checks in the corpus test, `normKey` imported rather than copied, «Riprova» separated from re-asking after a confirmation, and the clipboard's last fallback. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: bborbe
body:
## What this does

Turns a deploy of one nuke-dev component into a CQRS command instead of a hand-run `make apply`.

`POST /api/1.0/command/nuke-apply-v1/apply` with `{"path": "<component>"}` publishes to
`develop-nuke-apply-v1-request`. The service resolves the component and runs exactly that
component's own target — `make -C <repo>/<path> BRANCH=dev apply` — then publishes one result
per command.

## Design notes

- **The recipe is never rewritten.** Whatever a component's `apply` target does is what runs, so
  the service stays in step with the Makefiles rather than duplicating them.
- **Two refusals, both publishing a Failure result naming the reason:** a component whose `apply`
  recipe invokes `docker`, and one with no `apply` target. The docker check reads the resolved
  recipe rather than a hard-coded list, so a newly added docker component is caught without a code
  change.
- **`cdb.ErrCommandObjectSkipped` is deliberately not used** for those refusals. It suppresses the
  result entirely, which would leave the operator with no record that the command was refused.
- **Only `BRANCH=dev` is accepted.** The applier refuses any other branch, so a mis-set environment
  fails loudly instead of deploying somewhere unexpected.

## Image

Moved from `scratch` to `alpine`: the service shells out to `make`, which shells out to `git`,
`bash`, `kubectl` and `teamvault-cli`. An image that cannot run a component's own apply target
would fail at the first deploy rather than at startup. `kubectl` is pinned to `v1.36.4`, the
nuke-dev server version; `teamvault-cli` to `v5.10.1`.

No teamvault config file is shipped: when one exists its `url`/`user`/`pass` overwrite the
environment unconditionally, which would silently defeat the per-stage credentials. The three
`TEAMVAULT_*` env vars are the flag defaults, so the Makefiles stay untouched.

## Verification

`make test` green (8 packages). `go vet` clean. `make format` applied. `make lint` currently fails
machine-wide on a Go 1.27.3 export-data version mismatch — it reproduces on the untouched
`go-skeleton` template, so CI is the lint gate for this change.

## Open before this can deploy

- The `nuke-apply-git` deploy-key Secret and the `nuke-apply-teamvault` Secret do not exist in
  nuke-dev yet.
- Every component Makefile sets `KUBECONFIG := $(HOME)/.kube/nuke-$(STAGE)` and calls bare
  `kubectl`. In-cluster that path is absent and kubectl falls through to the pod's service account
  only after a warning. Worth confirming on the first real apply rather than assuming.

## Note on the tag

`v0.7.0` was already cut on this branch before the PR existed, so the release commit `1703ddf` is
part of this PR. The repo is now merge-commits-only, so the tag stays reachable from `master`
once this merges.

author: gfrmin
body:
Phase 3 (PR 6) of the latency programme. Small, and independent of everything else.

**Why:** since 2026-02, Cloudflare serves an expired object instantly (`UPDATING`) and revalidates in the background, but only if the origin sends `stale-while-revalidate`. That's the single change that helps every page at once: today a "latest" page expires from the edge every 4 h, and the next visitor waits for a full origin render. You've approved up to a 24 h stale window.

**The catch:** Cloudflare's docs disagree on where it reads the directive. The revalidation page says "in the Cache-Control header". The CDN-Cache-Control page says Cache-Control "does not affect caching decisions" once `CDN-Cache-Control` is present, and that's how every data page here is sent.

**What:** `/_probe/swr/<variant>` has no DB and no template, and returns a timestamp body. It's robots-disallowed and untouched by `_set_cache_headers`. It offers four header variants, each with a 30 s edge TTL and a 10 min SWR window:

| variant | header carrying SWR |
|---|---|
| `cc` | `Cache-Control` (the documented case) |
| `cdn` | `CDN-Cache-Control` (the target) |
| `cfcdn` | `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control` (fallback) |
| `mixed` | SWR in `Cache-Control`, TTL in `CDN-Cache-Control` (expected to fail) |

**After deploy:** run the curl protocol in `deploy/README.md` ("Edge stale-while-revalidate"). Whichever variant answers `UPDATING` with the old body decides the header the follow-up PR sets on the data pages.

**Tests:** `tests/test_app_hardening.py` item 6 checks that each variant's headers come out exactly as declared, unknown variants 404, and robots disallows the path.

body:
## Why
"7 days" of estimated API cost can span two limit periods, so it doesn't show what a period actually used. Some plans also have one long window, such as a monthly one.

## What changed
- **This cycle / Last cycle tabs** in the cost breakdown, separate from the day tabs. Costs are cut at the exact reset time of the profile's longest limit: weekly for Claude, the longest reported window for Codex.
- **Cost tile** now shows the last-picked day period next to the current cycle, as a two-column stat.
- **Window labels:** 28–31 day Codex windows read "Monthly" and other whole-day windows read e.g. "14-day window", instead of "720-hour window".
- Adds a `get_profile_api_cost_between` command. Cycles come from the usage the card already fetched, so there are no extra network calls.

## Limits
- Providers report only the next reset, so a cycle's start is the reset minus the window length. "Last cycle" can include some earlier use after an early reset or an idle gap.
- The cycle tabs and tile figure are hidden when usage has no reset time. A picked cycle isn't remembered across restarts; the day period is.

## Testing
- Vitest, cargo test, clippy, biome, typecheck and fallow audit pass.
- Tile checked in a browser preview with mock data, dark theme only.
- Not run in the real app. The free-plan monthly window is tested only with made-up data, as no real response was available.

author: coopbri
body:
## Description

Follow-up to the Tauri blank-screen fix. The build-time `disable` flag (keyed on `TAURI_ENV_PLATFORM`) did not reliably take effect during Tauri's `beforeBuildCommand`, so the service worker was still bundled and registered in the desktop app, blanking the WebKitGTK webview. Worse, a service worker registered by an earlier build persists in the app's storage and keeps breaking it even after the SW is removed from the bundle.

Fix: a runtime guard in `main.tsx` detects Tauri (`__TAURI_INTERNALS__`) and (a) never registers the service worker there, and (b) unregisters any previously registered worker, so the desktop app self-heals. The web PWA is unchanged.

## Testing

Web build + 124 tests pass; the bundle carries the `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` guard. Desktop app rebuilt; app storage (with the stale SW) cleared.

author: rifryx
body:
Продолжение #82 (был смержен без последнего коммита — этот PR его возвращает).

## Проблема
Диагностика из #82 показала точную причину «коммент не генерится»: DeepSeek отдаёт **401 Unauthorized** — ключ, выбранный в кампании, пустой/битый. При этом `has_llm=true` (есть рабочий ключ Gemini), поэтому dev-заглушка не подставляется, а кампания настроена на `deepseek` → 401, и коммент не создаётся.

## Фикс — фолбэк провайдера
Если LLM-провайдер из кампании падает (любая ошибка генерации, в т.ч. 401), а ключ **другого** провайдера задан — генерим им. Частый кейс: в кампании `deepseek`, а рабочий ключ у `gemini` (или наоборот) → теперь комментинг всё равно работает на том ключе, что валиден.

Если ключа второго провайдера нет — ошибка пробрасывается и видна в таймлайне (как и прежде, ничего не прячем). В тестах с инъекцией `ctx['llm_provider']` фолбэк отключён.

## Тесты
- `test_generate_falls_back_to_other_provider` — primary падает + ключ второго есть → используем второй.
- `test_generate_no_fallback_when_other_key_absent` — без второго ключа ошибка пробрасывается.

Прогон: **914 passed** (на ветке #82), `tsc` не затрагивался.

body:
Follow-up to #11 (which you merged before this measurement landed) and to the `compat.json` note that said "真实 0.8.1 运行时未实测". This PR is that measurement, on a real **dsh-mobile 0.8.1** gateway.

## Measured (isolated `DSH_HOME`, headless Chromium, dedicated page, 390×844 coarse, same counting rules as `check-pack`)

| state | slot (n / min / <44) | market root (n / min / <44) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **no packs** | 141 / **44** / **0** | 138 / **44** / **0** |
| `core-panel` only | 141 / 44 / 0 | 138 / 44 / 0 |
| `dshmarket-mobile` only | 141 / 44 / 0 | 138 / 44 / 0 |
| both | 141 / 44 / 0 | 138 / 44 / 0 |
| no packs + document-level `data-dsh-adapt="off"` | 141 / **12.1** / **141** | 138 / **12.1** / **138** |

0.8.0 baseline for the same page: 141/12.1/141 and 138/12.1/138 with no packs; 141/44/0 with the packs.

## The precision this PR is careful about

The host floor in `lib/mobile-layout.js` (0.8.1, four rules: 505–506 scroll/width clamp, 507 the 44px floor, 508 `touch-action`) covers `button` / `[role="button"]` / `select` / `input` and sets `min-width`/`min-height`. **It does not cover `textarea`.** The measured market panel has no `textarea`, so "no-op" is claimed for **that panel** only — both packs still carry `textarea` rules that this round did not exercise, and they remain the floor source for 0.8.0 and earlier. The doc, README table, `compat.json` summary and the two pack READMEs all state that boundary.

Also corrected: the host floor covers width as well (`min-width:44px`), so `core-panel`'s width rule is redundant too on 0.8.1; and a document-level `data-dsh-adapt="off"` turns the host floor off as well, because the host CSS excludes `[data-dsh-adapt="off"] *` (documented, measured).

## Files

- `docs/0.8.1-宿主下限验证.md` (new) — method, numbers, mechanism (with the textarea caveat), impact, boundaries, evidence paths.
- `README.md` — release-line table now 0.8.0 vs **0.8.1 (#319)** with measured numbers; the "after #319" verification row updated.
- `compat.json` — `hostBaseline` 0.8.1 summary/evidence corrected with the measurement (host covers min-width too; document-level opt-out disables the floor).
- `catalog.json` — `core-panel`: closes the "含 #319 的发布版未实测" missing item, adds the measured evidence, updates `verifiedWith`; `dshmarket-mobile`: adds the measured 0.8.1 line and caveat.
- `packs/core-panel/README.md`, `packs/dshmarket-mobile/README.md` — when the packs still matter, and the textarea boundary.

## Verified locally

`node tools/check-pack.mjs` → 121 passed / 0 failed / 8 skipped; `node --test` → 19/19; `node tools/cli.mjs compat` renders the new host baseline; `node tools/cli.mjs list` reports catalog/disk consistency.

## Not done

- 0.8.1 on a **physical device** (the phone disconnected; the real-device round in #11 used a 0.8.0 gateway).
- Only the "插件 → 插件市场" panel state; panels containing `textarea` were not exercised.

author: tstotzer
body:
When an existing IFC element has no geometry in the old model and gains a Body representation in the new model, `IfcDiff.diff()` queues both versions for geometry comparison. The old iterator initializes to false, but `summarise_shapes()` still calls `get()`, raising `RuntimeError: No elements processed` and aborting the diff.

Return an empty shape summary when the iterator cannot initialize, following its existing iteration convention. The normal comparison then reports `geometry_changed` for the existing element. Two regression tests cover the full geometry-added comparison and direct summarization of an element without geometry.

Validation (Windows, Python 3.12.10, IfcOpenShell 0.9.0.post1, DeepDiff 9.1.0):
- Both new tests fail on the base revision with `RuntimeError: No elements processed`.
- Complete IfcDiff package suite: `python -m pytest -p no:pytest-blender test.py -q` — 8 passed.
- Ruff 0.17.1 format/check, changed-file whitespace checks using the Linux LF convention, and `git diff --check` pass.
- The package wheel builds successfully. An independent Codex review found no issues and exercised additional synthetic empty/mixed geometry cases.

Native IfcOpenShell/Blender builds and the full monorepo CI were not run locally. A false iterator initialization cannot distinguish absent geometry from failed conversion; this uses the existing iterator convention and does not validate model geometry. Geometry removal that bypasses the current representation-selection logic remains outside this change.

AI disclosure: This entire contribution (fix, tests, commit message and PR description) was generated and tested by Codex under the account owner's standing authorization. No per-change human review has occurred.

author: fallrising
body:
Add an explicit Pi crash acceptance mode to the unified dispatcher. It holds the first request on loopback with no owner API key or upstream connection, waits for the real worker to be working, then signals only its observed native CLI PID after checking process identity. The native exited state, absence of completion/artifact, bounded no-restart observation and complete descendant cleanup must all pass. The result viewer keeps these tasks failed even when the fault test passes.

The pinned upstream PTY reports exit code 0 after SIGKILL. Acceptance therefore uses the injected signal and native state evidence rather than treating that code as task success. Crash target handoff is atomic, and explicit prompt-free startup now requires idle with no prompt or relay requests.

T-0015; AC-07/08/09/11 subsets. Native evidence preserves two crash runs and one explicitly requested fresh-session startup. Final crash/startup tracked 40/38 processes, all exited before slot release; duplicate dispatch was blocked, no automatic restart observed, and the new session differs from the crashed session. This is not same-session resume or task retry.

Validation: 106 Python + 35 Node tests; publication/index/diff checks; browser checks across 43 runs and four providers, including crash and startup-only classification, filters and refresh with no external requests or browser errors. Zero remote model calls; Strata never started. Evidence: `labs/agent-office-lab/docs/evidence/pi-crash-2026-11-01.json`.

Full MVP remains incomplete. Other provider crashes, same-session recovery, host restart and bounded explicit task retries remain pending.

author: corneeldh
body:
## What and why

In de end-to-end-proef van #118 weigerde de werkplek de eerste echte launch. De tick-regel zei alleen `launch of run 1 not accepted`, en het issue toonde een 🤖 Gestart terwijl er geen agent draaide. De reden stond alleen in `runs.reason`.

Nu noemt de tick-regel de reden, en een geweigerde launch krijgt op het issue een 🤖 Teruggegeven *start mislukt: <reden>* onder de Gestart. De volgorde van een start uit plan 114 (Gestart vóór de launch) blijft: de agent vindt zo zijn eigen Gestart, en een mislukte post na de launch kan geen agent zonder Gestart achterlaten. Het besluit staat in het plan, sectie *Besluit: een vervolg-comment, en wel een Teruggegeven*.

## Changes

- `internal/workplace/lifecycle.go`: `Launch` geeft bij `NotAccepted` ook de reden terug waarmee hij de run sloot (`(Outcome, string, error)`).
- `internal/dispatch/apply.go`:
  - de regels `launch of run <id> not accepted: <reden>` en `… uncertain: <fout>` staan op één regel (`oneLine`);
  - na een `NotAccepted` post `returnStartFailed` een Teruggegeven met `reason_start_failed` en de sessie van de run. Decide (`issueCtx.startFailed`) ziet die na de tweede weigering staan en post niets dubbel. Mislukt de post, dan logt apply één regel; dat is geen actiefout;
  - een usage-hervatting krijgt de Teruggegeven pas na haar tweede weigering. Haar tweede poging post geen kop, dus een eerdere Teruggegeven bleef anders de laatste kop terwijl de agent draait. Dit kwam uit de review van de hele branch.
- `internal/dispatch/testdata/decide/dedup-one-start-failed-returned.json`: een golden die vastpint dat een Teruggegeven na poging 1 de tweede poging niet tegenhoudt.
- Tests in `apply_test.go`, `lifecycle_test.go` en `internal/cli/run_test.go`.
- `docs/tick.md` en `docs/workplace.md`: wat de gebruiker ziet bij een geweigerde of onzekere launch.
- `changelog.d/issue-195-launch-reden.md`.

## Related issues

Closes #195

### Evidence #195

| AC | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1. De tick-regel noemt de reden bij `not accepted` en `uncertain` (getest) | `grep -F -e 'func TestApplyNotAcceptedLogsReason' -e 'func TestApplyUncertainLogsReason' internal/dispatch/apply_test.go` | `func TestApplyUncertainLogsReason` |
| 2. Het issue toont na een geweigerde launch dat er geen agent draait, met de reden (getest) | `grep -F 'reason: start failed: ' internal/cli/run_test.go` | `reason: start failed: ` |
| 3. `docs/tick.md` beschrijft wat de gebruiker in beide gevallen ziet | `grep -F 'Een geweigerde of onzekere launch.' docs/tick.md` | `**Een geweigerde of onzekere launch.**` |

## Before / After

- **Voor:** `lighthouse: o/r#7: launch of run 1 not accepted`. Op het issue alleen een 🤖 Gestart.
- **Na:** `lighthouse: o/r#7: launch of run 1 not accepted: kenn-forge answered 409: …; …: workplace: spawn not accepted`. Onder de Gestart staat een 🤖 Teruggegeven *start mislukt: <reden>*. De volgende tick start een tweede poging met een nieuwe Gestart of Hervat. Tot dan toont de UI het issue als teruggegeven; dat nemen we bewust voor lief.
- Een onzekere launch noemt haar fout op de tick-regel en post niets op het issue, want er kan een agent draaien.

## Verification

- Per taak: `go test -race ./internal/dispatch ./internal/workplace ./internal/cli` groen. Na de fix uit de review ook `go test -race ./...` groen (31 pakketten ok).
- Mutatiechecks: zonder de reden in de logregel wordt `TestApplyNotAcceptedLogsReason` rood, met `%v` in plaats van `oneLine` `TestApplyUncertainLogsReason`, en zonder sessie in de Teruggegeven `TestApplyNotAcceptedPostsReturned`.
- De commit-test-gate was groen op elke commit.
- suite: CI
- Review van de hele branch door een verse reviewer: 0 Critical, 1 Important (gefixt, zie Changes), 4 Minor. Die vier zijn uitgesteld:
  - Faalt `SetWorkplace`, dan geeft `Launch` een samengevoegde fout terug. Apply post daar dus geen Teruggegeven, terwijl de nieuwe zin in `docs/workplace.md` dat suggereert.
  - `oneLine` vervangt alleen `\n`, geen `\r`.
  - Bij een `KindResume` mist het vangnet van decide een mislukte tweede post als de eerste post wel lukte.
  - Er zijn twee `oneLine`-helpers (in `cli` en in `dispatch`).

author: kja031199
body:
Finding 4. The site holds personal data, loads a third-party SDK, and set exactly one header: `Cache-Control`.

**This ships the CSP in report-only mode.** A policy written without being able to load the deployed site is a guess, and the failure mode of a wrong guess is being locked out of your own app. The browser evaluates it and logs violations while blocking nothing; the enforcing header is a follow-up once the real flows have been exercised. The other headers can't break anything that works today and are enforced now.

## Enforced now

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` |
| `Permissions-Policy` | `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=()` |
| `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` | `same-origin-allow-popups` |

**That last one is the trap.** The stricter `same-origin` severs `window.opener` and **breaks `signInWithPopup`** — the single most likely way a headers change takes this app down, and a failure that appears only on the deployed site. There's an assertion against that exact value with the reason written into it.

`Permissions-Policy` grants nothing because the app uses nothing: receipts arrive through a file input, and GPS station detection was dropped in the port. If either changes, the test is the reminder that the header must change too.

## Two things the investigation turned up

**OCR fetches from a third-party CDN at runtime.** `createWorker('eng')` takes no paths, so tesseract.js pulls its worker script, wasm core and English language data from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` at scan time. The domain appears **nowhere in this repository's source** — it's a default inside the library, and it's exactly the kind of entry a hand-written `connect-src` misses. jsdelivr learns that somebody started a scan; not the image, not the result. It also means scanning fails wherever that CDN is blocked — as it is in this authoring container, which is why OCR accuracy was originally measured in Node against the npm package. Now in the README.

**The built page has no inline script at all** — one `<script src>` and nothing else. So `script-src 'self'` works with no nonce or hash machinery, which is the version of CSP actually worth having. Nothing *enforced* that, though: Vite merely happens to emit it that way, and a plugin or a hand edit could add one. That would break in production, once the policy is enforced, and nowhere else. So a test now holds it.

## Testing

`npm test` — **747 passed**, up from 737. New `src/ui/csp.test.ts` reads `dist/` and `firebase.json`, so it sits in the same family as `manifest.test.ts` and relies on the same build-before-test ordering.

**Mutation-tested, because a config test that cannot fail is decoration:**

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `COOP: same-origin` | fails *"does not isolate the opener"* |
| Drop `cdn.jsdelivr.net` from `connect-src` | fails *"names every origin the app contacts"* |
| Plant an inline `<script>` in the built page | fails *"has no inline script"* |
| Restored | 10 pass |

One failure each, the right one each time.
