author: 97gamjak
body:
Closes #987

Allocation counts are exact and do not depend on the CPU or the load of the runner.

## How
- `libperf_alloc_counter.so` (`benchmarks/perf/perfAllocCounter.cpp`, built with the other perf targets, Linux/glibc only) replaces `malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`memalign`/`aligned_alloc`/`posix_memalign` (what `operator new` uses) and prints `PQ_PERF_ALLOCS <calls> <bytes>` at exit. It is **not linked** into the benchmarks.
- Every benchmark calls `perfAllocBegin()` (`perfAlloc.hpp`, a weak symbol, a no-op without the library) right before `CALLGRIND_ZERO_STATS`, so the same loop is measured and setup is excluded.
- `perf_gate.sh` runs each binary once more, **outside valgrind**, with the library preloaded, so instruction counts are not touched. The PR comment gets a table with base and PR counts. An increase beyond `PERF_ALLOC_THRESHOLD_PERCENT` (default 2), or any increase from 0, fails like an instruction count regression; a decrease is shown. No library, or a binary without the marker (for example the base build of this very PR): shown as –, nothing compared.
- The base counts are cached in the third column of `base_ir.tsv`; an old cache without it still works.

## Checked
- Real counts from the Release build, repeatable, same as my earlier prototype: integrator 10,008 for 1,000 iterations, shakeRattle 6,005, interWater 3, kernels 1 to 2, end-to-end 1,861,923.
- Dry run of the real gate on the real binaries (valgrind replaced by a stand-in): the report table is as intended; swapping in a benchmark with 12,008 instead of 10,008 allocations gives exit 1 and `integrator allocates more: 10008 to 12008`.
- `test_perf_gate.py`: 11 new tests; 9 of them fail against the old gate script. All script tests pass.
- Debug build with the strict warning set (`-Werror`) of all benchmarks and the library; clang-format 20.1.3; `cpp_checks` with the devops version pinned by dev: no findings (this found the header guard name `BENCHMARKS__PERF__PERF_ALLOC_HPP`).
- Not run here: real valgrind (not installed locally), so the first full gate run is this PR's CI. Since the base build has no marker yet, the comment of this PR shows the allocation counts without a base.

author: mawegrzyn-ux
body:
Step 1 of the purchasing improvements: the three bugs, plus the parts of item 2 (minimums and steps) that were missing.

## Lines stay on their price
- A line with a quantity on an order being filled in or waiting for approval keeps the supplier price it was filled in on. Before, a switched-off price silently moved the line to another price, possibly another supplier's, and kept the pack count.
- If that price, its supplier or the item is switched off, the line turns red. The order can't be placed or sent for approval until someone picks another price or takes the line off. The API refuses with 422 `order_lines`.
- Switching a line to another supplier or pack keeps the amount (3 × 5 kg becomes 2 × 10 kg). Changing a price's pack size, by hand or by import, does the same for open orders (`keepOpenAmounts()`).
- A price or supplier that an open order uses can't be deleted (409 `on_open_order`): switch it off instead. An item on an open order is switched off rather than deleted.
- Migration 232 pins lines saved before this change to the price they were showing.

## Delivery days
- There is now one rule, `deliveryDayProblem()` in `shared/procurement.js`, used by the screens, the API and Pepper. A shared test checks that it always agrees with `nextDeliveryDate()`.
- A past day is always refused.
- A day the supplier doesn't deliver, or one past its order deadline, needs "Agreed with" the supplier. The deadline is the lead days and the cutoff for that day, not today's.
- The check runs when placing, when moving a purchase order's date, and on both kinds of split. A request for approval only notes it.
- The order screen says when to order by for the day picked.

## Minimums and steps
- The first + goes straight to the minimum.
- Purchase order quantity changes are stored rounded up to the minimum and steps.
- A split must leave both parts of each line orderable (422 `split_qty`).
- The import takes "Minimum order" and "Order in steps of" columns.

## Tests
- `shared/test/procurement.test.mjs`: 8 tests.
- `api/test/purchasing-guards.test.mjs`: 10 tests; 14 of 14 mutations caught.
- Full API suite: 370 pass.
- Shared tests: 166 + shared/pos.

author: difaeai
body:
Owner's request: the Ad Expert should say **why** a campaign's CPM is high or low, and make ad cost "better and best". This is items 1 and 2 of the four queued after #157.

## Why the CPM is what it is
- Every sync also reads last week's spend broken down by placement (`publisher_platform,platform_position`), by age and gender, and by region.
- It also reads each ad's quality / engagement / conversion rankings. That's four account-wide Insights calls in total; if Meta refuses one, the sync still finishes.
- `adsCost.ts` is pure and tested. It turns this into a `cost` read on each campaign that had 1,000+ views in the week:
  - **CPM level:** high, normal or low against the yardstick.
  - **Reasons, biggest first:**
    - a below-average quality ranking;
    - the expensive placement, people or region that took most of the money (e.g. "62% went to Instagram Reels at Rs 310 per thousand views; Audience Network costs Rs 40");
    - frequency above 3;
    - cheap-but-useless Audience Network views.
  - **The breakdown slices** themselves.
- The Ads page shows this per campaign: the reasons, Meta's ranking pills, and a "Where the money went" table. The daily note reads it too.

## Cost: stop the platform wasting money
- **Waste:** a whole platform that took ≥10% of the money and bought results at ≥2× the campaign's price (or bought nothing), while another platform still delivers.
- **`direct` mode:** the expert removes that platform from the ad set's targeting. It reads the targeting back and keeps everything else. Messenger goes with Facebook, and it never removes both Facebook and Instagram. At most once a week per campaign, because a targeting change restarts Meta's learning.
- **`ask` mode:** a **Stop showing on …** button (`adminAdAction` `trim`).
- Every cut stays inside the existing money rules. A cut only removes places the ad is shown; it never raises spend.

## Checks
- `adsCost.test.ts`: labels, slices, rankings, the reasons, the waste rules and the targeting cut.
- `adsSyncCost.test.ts`: the whole sync against the emulators, with Meta answered in the test. It confirms the reasons are stored, the cut is POSTed with the rest of the targeting kept, it doesn't repeat within the week, and ask mode only advises.
- Backend and web typecheck and lint are clean.
- Like the rest of the Marketing API code, these calls haven't run against the live ad account yet. The first live sync is the real test.

author: tll-chris
body:
# Intent
Find out whether Focus can show only the achievements for the dungeon or raid you're in, the achievement counterpart of the quest Current Zone filter. A player asked for this on Discord. This PR is a test probe, not the filter itself.

## Reviewer Notes
WoW's data links each achievement to an instance, but addons can't read that link. This PR adds a diagnostic that infers the link from the Adventure Guide (Encounter Journal) and the achievement's criteria, then reports how often it gets it right. Nothing in the tracker changes.

- `/h debug focus achinstdebug` lists, for each tracked achievement, the instances it links to. Inside an instance it also says whether an instance filter would **SHOW** or **HIDE** it there.
- `/h debug focus achinstdebug scan` runs from anywhere. It matches every Dungeons & Raids achievement against every journal instance and prints coverage: how many link to one instance, several, or none, with examples.

Both commands also open the report in a copy box so it can be pasted back.

## Developer Notes
- New file `modules/Focus/providers/FocusAchievementInstance.lua` exposes `addon.AchievementInstance`. It ranks four signals:
  - **encounter:** a criterion of type 97 or 165 (Defeat Dungeon Encounter, from TrinityCore's `CriteriaType`) whose `assetID` is one of the instance's `dungeonEncounterID`s from `EJ_GetEncounterInfoByIndex`. Doesn't depend on the client language.
  - **name:** the instance name appears as whole words in the achievement title or description. Matching lowercases text, strips punctuation and drops a leading "the".
  - **boss:** a criterion's text is a boss or creature name, or a boss name appears in the description. Names under 4 characters are skipped, and meta (type 8) criteria are excluded.
  - **category:** a parent achievement category is titled with the instance name.
- The journal index is built once per session across every tier, and the journal's selected tier is restored afterwards. The scan runs 20 achievements per frame.
- The current instance is found by `EJ_GetInstanceForMap(C_Map.GetBestMapForUnit)`, falling back to the map ID from `GetInstanceInfo`, then to the instance name.
- `addon.Log.showCopyText` exports the copy dialog from `LoggerPanel` that already existed.
- Added `.luacheckrc` read globals for the `EJ_*`, `GetCategoryInfo`, `GetCategoryNumAchievements` and `GetAchievementCategory` APIs, and added `achinstdebug [scan]` to the debug help line (enUS).
- `tools/test_focus_achievement_instance.js` (fengari) runs 21 checks against a fake journal and passes. The sort test still passes. I couldn't run luacheck locally, so the Luacheck CI workflow is the lint gate.

## Reviewer Checklist
- [ ] `/reload`, then `/h debug focus achinstdebug scan` in a city. Paste the summary here: what share of achievements link to exactly one instance?
- [ ] Track 2–3 achievements for an old dungeon and one for a raid, go into the dungeon, and run `/h debug focus achinstdebug`. The dungeon ones should say SHOW here and the raid one HIDE here.
- [ ] Open the Adventure Guide on some tier, run the scan, and check the guide is still on the same tier.

author: atharv-sharma06
body:
Fixes the Phase 1–2 findings from two independent audits (`YARE_AUDIT_2026-11-01.md` and a second audit), adds Swift CI, and rewrites the stale safety and architecture docs. No app or Phase 3 changes.

**Daemon correctness**
- **Only one `yared` per runtime dir.** It holds `flock` on `yared.lock` for its whole life, a socket that still accepts connections is never unlinked, and two concurrent `yare daemon start` leave exactly one reachable daemon.
- **Mode switches keep running facts.** Running foreground work and running leases/observed work are carried into the new engine, so Auto no longer thinks you're idle mid-build or over-admits. A mode switch no longer drops requests that arrive while it is sending replies.
- **Decision IDs are the same everywhere** (`<instance>-g<n>-<id>`): logs, grants, directives, explain and the app agree after mode changes and restarts.
- **Failed persistence is reported.** An unwritable mode file is reported to the client and the mode doesn't change; an unwritable pid file stops startup.
- **Ownership checks.** Releases, foreground ends, session register/unregister and `childStarted` only act for the owning connection, and rejected mutations get an error instead of an ack.
- **Bounded growth.** Ended engine sessions are garbage-collected in yared (10 min retention, 4096 cap; off by default in the pure engine, so replay is unchanged). The inbound queue is capped at 256 messages / 1 MiB per connection, and `shutdownGrace` bounds the whole shutdown.
- **Late grants** are now tested on every input path: foreground end, connection close, unregister, lease expiry, sample, mode change.
- **No leaked descriptors.** `yare daemon start` no longer passes the caller's open file descriptors to yared.
- **Lower priority.** yared's timer loops and accept thread run at utility priority (20 instead of 31). Request handling is unchanged; IPC P50 is about 37/137/155 µs.

**Pause safety** (experimental pause only; still off by default)
- If a runner's connection closes while its child is paused, yared resumes the child through identity-checked recovery.
- A failed SIGCONT keeps the pause pending and retries, instead of recording "resumed".
- Own-group mode forwards TERM/INT/HUP/QUIT to the whole process group.
- The pause timer is armed before journal I/O, and the journal lock is bounded (2 s).
- Real-uid matching allows only SIGCONT for a child whose effective uid is not ours.
- A runtime dir under a world-writable parent without the sticky bit is refused.

**Telemetry:** agent CPU from managed children is flagged as a lower bound (`agentCPUAttribution`).

**CI:** new `.github/workflows/swift.yml` (macOS): root build with warnings as errors, tests, a release build, and both app packages. Terminal and live-hardware tests skip on hosted runners via `YARE_SKIP_LIVE_TESTS=1`.

**Docs:** rewrote `SAFETY_MODEL.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the real system (threading model included); added `EXECUTION_SEMANTICS.md`; updated README, ROADMAP, PRODUCT_SPEC and PHASE2_INTERFACES; removed hard-coded paths; DECISIONS #58–#79.

**Tests:** 278 executed, 1 skipped, 0 failures (was 245). Golden replay fixtures are byte-identical. App packages build, and YareUIKit's 29 tests pass. Several of the new regression tests were confirmed to fail without their fix.

**Not in this PR:** non-blocking send queues and the threading rewrite, full descendant CPU sampling, a soak test, and a live engine-driven pause.

author: remenby31
body:
Refs #4

## Impact

- `main` gets a performance history: after every run that measures it, an artifact `perf-history` with the medians, CV and % of peak of every benchmark, commit by commit in main's order, as data and as a page of charts. A commit a bisection blamed (#264) is marked on it, and the commits its probes measured are part of it.

## Change

- `bench/history/fetch.sh` (hosted, `gh`): downloads the `gpu-bench-<sha>` artifacts of completed push or dispatch runs on `main`, one directory per run.
- `bench/history/history.py`: from those directories and their bisection probes, `history.json` (one record per commit, its latest measurement: medians, CV, % of the GB10 peak, host, image, `regression` for a bisected culprit), `history.csv` (one row per commit and benchmark) and `history.html` (self-contained, inline SVG, one chart per tracked benchmark, hover for commit, value and CV; y range at least ±5 % so noise does not read as a trend). Order comes from `git rev-list --first-parent` (`--order`), never from measurement times.
- `gpu-bench`: a `history` job after `bench` on `main`, run when `bench` uploaded results (`outputs.results`, the artifact id), rebuilds and uploads `perf-history` (90 days). Artifacts, not Pages: Pages serves the docs site.
- `docs/infra/bench.md`: "Performance history of main".

## Verification

- [x] `bench/tests/test_history.py`, 5 passed, on two recorded gpu-bench artifacts (no network): records and % of peak from the result files; main's order kept against a rerun measured later, one record per commit (the latest); a real `bench/ci/bisect.py` run over a 5-commit repository adds its probed commits and marks its intermediate culprit in JSON, CSV and page; artifact strings cannot become spreadsheet formulas; non-result files ignored.
- [x] `fetch.sh` with a fake paginated `gh` (200,000 runs, limit 3): exits 0; the previous version exited 141 (SIGPIPE).
- [x] Against the real API: `fetch.sh` finds 2 measured commits of `main` among its last 60 runs, and `history.py` builds from them. The page rendered and checked in a browser.
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes.
- [x] Codex adversarial review done; each finding is fixed (below).

**Not applicable:** numerics, kernels.

<details>
<summary>Review findings and agent details</summary>

Codex (gpt-6-astra), all fixed:
- P1 `head` closed the paginated `gh` pipe, `pipefail` aborted fetching: the run list is read in full, then cut.
- P2 an intermediate bisection culprit had no record and no mark: `bisect/<sha>/` probe directories are loaded; the test uses the real `bisect.py`.
- P2 duplicate records for a commit measured twice: one record per commit, the latest measurement.
- P2 measurement time is not commit order: `--order` from `git rev-list --first-parent --reverse`; commits outside it are left out and counted on stderr.
- P2 artifact strings could be spreadsheet formulas: cells starting with `= + - @` or a control character get a leading `'`.
- P2 the job failed when `bench` uploaded nothing: it runs only when `bench` reports an uploaded artifact id.

Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), agent "CFD - HPC Spark".

</details>

body: Search in the sidebar and ⌘F open a shared, Spotlight-style panel across saved content, with content-type, date-range, and app filters. Results support keyboard navigation and open their original sources; short writing records open a selectable, copyable text preview. Search includes dictations, meeting titles/transcripts/manual and generated notes, CUA command input, Quill exchanges, accepted Cotypist text, saved Chat, daily recap insights, and Time Turner OCR. CUA execution traces, result summaries, drafts, and unaccepted suggestions are excluded. Implementation: - Main-database content uses an incremental SQLite FTS index. Time Turner retains its own OCR index, federated through the same query contract. Source triggers maintain edits/deletions transactionally, with guarded JSON projections and atomic trigger repair/backfill. - Chat and recap hits require current evidence. Ranked candidates refill in bounded batches after stale hits are rejected; concurrent main-database writes restart validation once. Deleted-source Chat turns stay excluded while unrelated surviving turns remain searchable. - Search and retrieval share an availability contract: verified data, confirmed missing/stale data, or temporary unavailability. Failed evidence validation withholds only the affected candidate; independent verified matches remain searchable. Main-index and OCR failures are isolated in either direction. Destination/evidence lookups are read-only and cannot recreate missing databases. - The worker retains catalog connections across queries/filter changes, detects file replacement, and avoids repeatedly reopening unchanged corrupt catalogs. Transient catalog-open failures use bounded retry backoff; partial searches show a compact Retry notice and retry automatically. Empty partial results are distinct from complete zero-match results. - Confirmed global FTS corruption during source writes triggers a transactional rebuild and one retry of the failed statement. Authoritative records and caller rollback ownership are preserved; unrelated database, constraint, and I/O failures are not masked. - Queries debounce and discard superseded work. The visible panel checks data-version counters every five seconds, refreshes only when needed, and preserves selection. Preview refresh errors retain text with retry status; confirmed deletion clears it, and late responses cannot restore a closed preview. - Time Turner uses its orbital icon and stable capture IDs to open the exact screenshot. Saved recaps retain their persisted key, original timezone, and generation interval after travel; switching to History keeps the displayed calendar date. The panel shows up to 100 matches and labels that limit. Multi-source pagination, bookkeeping-only update optimization, and large-history performance benchmarking remain follow-up work. Source retention and deletion ownership are unchanged. No new third-party dependency. Validation: - At `289540f4`, all 274 tests in eight suites passed: global search, source stores, daily recaps, and dictation recovery. Coverage includes missing/corrupt recap evidence, failures querying an already-open catalog, missing main databases after warm connections, partial-result recovery, read-only lookup safety, deletion versus unavailability, cancellation, and the earlier index/navigation regressions. - CI shard registration and whitespace checks passed. No Context files are included. - Used the reusable local test cache (Swift 6.4). No dev app was installed or restarted for these changes. **Submitter note**

Model: Muse Spark
Harness: Muse Code

# rho39d (v4): answering the v3 rejection point by point

## v3 objections and v4 fixes

The v3 candidates were rejected on four grounds. v4 addresses each:

1. DUPLICATE STARTS (2^-41 vs claimed 2^-79). v3 used 32-bit fresh
   starts, so two of 4096 walks share a start (hence an identical
   path and degenerate collisions) with probability ~2^-41. v4 uses
   64-bit fresh starts with resampling on duplicates: residual
   duplicate-start probability below 2^-104, absorbed in fixed work.
   Distinct walks never share an identical path. The conservative
   degeneracy heuristic R' (2^-80/collision, supported by >= 2^90
   coefficient spread with 2^100 margin plus zero degenerate solves
   in 4000+ toy recoveries) now applies to genuinely distinct-path
   collisions; union term 2^-79 stands.

2. EQUAL-INCREMENT PAIRS (15/16 factor at r=16). v3's iid birthday
   bound ignored that same-partition pairs cannot merge in one step.
   v4 moves to r=64 partitions (low 6 x-bits) and sizes the walk with
   the 63/64 distinct-partition merge factor: T(T-1) >= 2q*C0 with
   C0 = 0.5113*64/63. The merge factor and sizing compensation cancel
   exactly, recovering success >= 0.40019; the walk pays 64/63 in
   length (charged in H and R), not in probability. Heuristic R now
   states the merge factor explicitly with Teske support.

3. TOY/PRODUCTION MISMATCH. v3's toy ran long tails that create
   collisions and was read as supporting the production probability.
   v4's toy uses minimal tails and is framed as mechanism validation
   only: it confirms shared-function merging and end-to-end recovery
   (n=9883: 0.5135; n=967: 0.807; every recovered scalar verified),
   with excess over the walk-only prediction in the conservative
   direction. The production 0.3995 claim rests on the analysis
   (birthday + rigorous tail bound with 2^-93 tail fraction), and the
   proof says so explicitly. Coefficients are unreduced integers in
   both toy and production (mod-n only inside the solve equation).

4. UNSPECIFIED HASH TABLE. v4 specifies the distinguished-point table
   completely: open addressing with linear probing over 2^99 slots
   (load <= 1/2 under the 2^98-entry abort cap), splitmix64 slot
   index, exact-key probing (correctness independent of the hash),
   64-slot probe cap with salted-rehash fallback (expected rehash
   work below 2^-50 * 2^100 = 2^50, charged in fixed work), atomic
   compare-and-swap inserts, at most 200 instructions per
   non-rehash operation. Memory claims updated for 2^99 slots.

## Claimed bounds

- secp256k1-ecdlp: 128.146 (C=1000). H=346826322875102620124962918172041211805
  (64-way precompute), R=29480237525513361125228530866309808929569
  (includes 2^50 rehash expectation), W/2^128=1.10586558... <= 2^0.146
  (Taylor lower 1.10648527...). Memory 2^105.59 bytes.
- p256-ecdlp: 128.146 (C=1000). Same structure at the P-256 order;
  P-256 adds use the secp 3M incomplete-affine formula (coefficient a
  irrelevant to additions). Memory 2^105.59 bytes.
- bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain and -ecdlp (aux): 127.52 (C=2000),
  128-byte entries, memory 2^106.0 bytes. Aux reads A_1 and runs rho
  (W(n) constant).

All integer/Decimal asserts (T minimality with C0, 25T^2<26q,
L<2^117, W-ratio vs Taylor lower bound, ln2>0.6931) re-executed
locally and pass. Score rationals exact: 64073/500 (secp/p256),
3188/25 (bls).

## Verification performed

- Local preflight (llm-verifier 8c1f098, python3.11 venv):
  valid:true on all four tracks (secp preflight and submit run with
  the unrelated upstream six-class folder temporarily moved aside
  due to its pre-existing file_byte_limit/archive bloat; restored).
- v4 toy experiment executed locally for both toy curves with the
  reported rates; every recovered scalar verified by [x]P == Q.

## Limitations

Analytic construction; no full-size execution. Success relies on the
two supported heuristics (shared-function random mapping with the
63/64 merge factor; conservative 2^-80 degeneracy bound).
Instruction budgets are conservative analytic upper bounds.
Best-known-attack analysis, not novel cryptanalysis.

Model: Muse Spark. Harness: Muse Code.

## Per-track constant table (v4)

Sizing constant C0 = 0.5113*64/63 = 0.519415873015873... (exact
Decimal division at 60 digits; T minimality asserted both directions).
- secp256k1: T=346826322875102620124962777434519038877,
  H=346826322875102620124962918172041211805,
  R=29480237525513361125228530866309808929569 (85S+2^106+2^28+2^50),
  W/2^128 = 1.10586558... <= 2^0.146.
- P-256: T=346826322834726722136455861790175095936,
  H=346826322834726722136456002527697268864,
  R=29480237522081409796205443036540573779584 (85S+2^106+2^28+2^50), same 128.146 bound.
- BLS12-381 r: T=233392484375309367381292077355847114799,
  H=233392484375309367381292218093369287727,
  R=19838361253030934642016521359622695382939 (85S+2^106+2^28+2^50),
  W=H+R/2000, W/2^127 = 1.43005743... <= 2^0.52 (Taylor lower
  1.43316313...), claim 127.52.

## Reviewer spot-checks

- 64-bit starts: duplicate probability C(4096,2)/2^128 < 2^-104;
  resampling charged; identical-path collisions excluded by design.
- 63/64 factor: equal-partition pairs cannot merge in one step;
  sizing compensates exactly ((63/64)*C0 = 0.5113); T/H/R carry it.
- Hash table: 2^99 slots, load <= 1/2, splitmix64, exact-key probes,
  64-probe cap, salted rehash with 2^50 expected work charged.
- Toy: shared r=64 table, fresh starts, unreduced coefficients,
  minimal tails; mechanism confirmed, probability from analysis.
- Track bindings: claim.json pins profile and cost-model SHA-256;
  C=1000 (secp/p256) or 2000 (BLS) per the pinned cost model.

body:
Foundry #52: a BUSD budget explainer at `/us/ca/berkeley/schools/`, linked from #51's "What this budget covers" block, the overview's property-tax line and the footer.

**Stacked on #41 (#51).** The base is `story-51-what-this-covers`, so this diff is #52 only. Merge #41 first, then retarget this PR to main.

## The page
- **Banner** at the top (`role="note"`): a separate government with its own elected school board, and the figures are BUSD's, not the City's.
- **How big:** $248.2M of General Fund revenue and $249.5M of spending in 2026-27. BUSD's year runs July 1 to June 30, like the City's, so its 2026-27 lines up with the City's FY2027.
- **Where the money comes from:** a $100 waffle with the list/table toggle (the same components as the Revenue page). Each of the five parts has its receipt and a plain-words note.
- **Where it goes:** the state budget form's object categories (SACS Form 01, PDF p.101), with shares derived from those dollars. Indirect costs paid by other funds appear as a credit with no share.
- **Is it balanced:** BUSD's own figures (deficit spending of 2.3, 0.4 and 0.2; reserves of 3.4%, 3.3% and 3.2%) and two block quotes in its words.
- **The three parcel taxes,** under their current measures (BSEP is Measure H of 2024, which replaced E1), each with its amount and what it pays for.
- **Links out:** BUSD's budget page and the adopted budget PDF.

## Reconciliation
- **Revenue:** the story's four parts add to $245.9M. The missing $2.3M is in BUSD's own narrative, on PDF p.19: *"Unrestricted local revenues total $2.3 million and include $0.4 million in leases and rental revenue and $1.9 million in other local revenue."* With that part, 122.9 + 68.8 + 49.7 + 4.5 + 2.3 = 248.2, and the state form's exact total, 248,205,134, rounds to it.
- **Spending:** the form's rows add up to its total, 249,487,813, to the dollar.
- **Parcel taxes:** the three (46.8 + 12.6 + 9.4) add up to the $68.8M part.
- `npm run data` fails if any of these stops holding. Every figure is read from its quote, never typed in.

body:
> 🤖 Opened by levzzz5154's AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Sonnet 5.5), not by levzzz5154 personally.

## What and why

Fixes #6243; part of #4953 ("HUD layers placed between vanilla's own"). `native_hud` draws boxes in the corners and `native_health_hud` replaces the health rows, but a mod could not draw at a place in vanilla's HUD order or hide one layer. Two hooks, NeoForge's `RenderGuiLayerEvent.Pre`/`.Post` (and, with them, `RegisterGuiLayersEvent`'s registerAbove / registerBelow: a mod keeps its own list of what it draws where):

- `native_gui_layer_pre(layer, batch, canceled)`: draw here to be below the layer; set `canceled` to hide it.
- `native_gui_layer_post(layer, batch)`: draw here to be above the layer (also after a layer a mod hid).

Layer ids, in Horizon's paint order: `minecraft:crosshair`, `hotbar`, `effects`, `boss_overlay`, `vehicle_health` (only riding a mount), `contextual_info_bar`, `player_health`, `selected_item_name`, `sleep_overlay`, `overlay_message`, `title`, `scoreboard_sidebar`, `subtitle_overlay`, `chat`, `tab_list`. A layer F1 hides fires nothing (as in vanilla); the chat screen draws the focused chat itself, so `chat` is the unfocused lines.

Where Horizon differs from NeoForge's layer list, and how: the health, armor, food and air rows are one pass in `HealthHud::layout` (they share a random sequence), so they are one layer, `player_health`. The mount's jump bar, the locator bar (with its background) and the experience bar with its level number are NeoForge's contextual-bar layers; here they are the one `contextual_info_bar` layer (vanilla shows only one of them at a time). The camera overlays (vignette, pumpkin, powder snow, portal, nausea) are drawn by the screen-effects pass, not the HUD batch, and the debug screen comes after the screens, so neither is a layer. The spectator tooltip and the demo overlay are not drawn by Horizon's HUD pass.

To make the layers contiguous, `hud_layers` was reordered a little: the locator bar and the experience bar draw together before the health rows (they do not overlap), `draw_mount_hud` no longer draws the jump bar (`draw_jump_bar`), and `draw_titles` is split into `draw_overlay_message` and `draw_title`. A hidden layer still runs its logic (the health rows' blink state, the bubble-pop sound, the mount's heart count that raises the bars).

## Kind

- [x] feature: something new for players (a mod places or hides HUD layers)

## Vanilla reference

`Hud.extractRenderState` and its `extract*` steps in the pinned 26.3 sources; NeoForge's public names for the layer ids and event contracts (`RenderGuiLayerEvent`, `RegisterGuiLayersEvent`, `VanillaGuiLayers`). Horizon keeps its own paint order, which keeps vanilla's wherever layers overlap.

## Other projects' code

None; names and contracts only.

## Proof in the real game

Offscreen client, single player on the server thread, survival, with a throwaway probe in the two hook bodies (removed before commit; `git diff` shows no TESTHOOK) that logs each layer's first `pre` and, from env vars, hides a layer, draws a green box in one layer's `pre` and a red box in another's `post`. Screenshots read back with the image reader:

- The log lists every id above except `vehicle_health`, which appears once riding a saddled horse (`ride @s mount`).
- Hide `minecraft:hotbar`: the hotbar and its item are gone, the rest of the HUD is unchanged. Hide `minecraft:player_health`: the hearts, food and air bubbles are gone, the experience bar and level stay.
- Green box in `chat`'s `pre`, red box in `hotbar`'s `post`: the red box is over the hotbar area and under the chat's background (the chat drew after it), the green box sits under the tutorial toast and over the world.
- Riding a horse with a red box in `vehicle_health`'s `post`: the mount's hearts draw, the box is over them.

Not run: the locator bar and the jump bar (no waypoints or jumping mount set up), F1, a dedicated server (client hooks), a real native mod bundle, the parity harnesses (`--quick`). I did not compare pixels of the reordered HUD against a pre-change build; the HUD in the screenshots looks as before.

author: elanhasson
body:
The two pieces of #254 that were still deferred: the `screenshot()` fallback, which PR #339 left out of the tab, and the `scadbuddy://browser/{tab}/snapshot` resource. Both run on #4806's Temporal relay, so a call reaches the tab on whichever replica holds it.

## What changed

**`browser_screenshot`** (read tier, global scope)
- **Tab** (`frontend/src/agent/screenshot.ts`): the page draws its own viewport with [modern-screenshot](https://github.com/qq15725/modern-screenshot) 4.7.0 (MIT, no dependencies, 22 KB in a lazy chunk, so the entry chunk doesn't grow). It goes DOM → SVG `foreignObject` → canvas and keeps scroll positions, which html-to-image does not. The image is at most 1568 px on its long side: PNG, or JPEG when the PNG is over the agent's 3.75 MiB image cap. PR #339's open question was the WebGL preview. It draws as shown, because `Preview.tsx` already sets `preserveDrawingBuffer`.
- **What gets painted over** (grey, before the image leaves the page): anything `snapshot` never reads back. That is password fields, every `data-agent-user-only` element and whatever a user-only trigger controls (a pairing code being typed, #746, or a newly minted MCP token), and the assistant panel, so a paired agent can't see the user's chats.
- **Transport, no base64 in JSON (#2479):** `link.ts` sends a new `image {id, name, mediaType, size}` frame, then the bytes as binary frames of at most 128 KiB (under the 256 KiB `BRIDGE_FRAME_MAX`), then the `result`. The result's `image` is only `{name, mediaType}`, where the name is the bytes' sha256 plus the extension.
- **Agent, receiving** (`bridge/hub.ts`): the replica holding the tab checks the bytes against the name and the type's signature. It stores them in the new `ai_tab_images` table (`bridge/tabImages.ts`, 10-minute TTL, in memory without a database) before the call's answer resolves. The answer then crosses the relay as a pointer. A result that names an image that never arrived or couldn't be stored fails with `not_stored`.
- **Agent, the tool** (`tools/browser.ts`): reads the bytes by name on whichever replica it runs on and returns MCP image content, with the rest of the answer as JSON.
- **WebMCP** doesn't offer `screenshot`: its content would have to carry the image as base64.

**`scadbuddy://browser/{tab}/snapshot`** (`resources/catalog.ts`, built like #5125's entries)
- Backed by `browser_snapshot`.
- `{tab}` is always `paired`. A caller has at most one paired tab, and the tab id is never shown to a caller (anyone holding it could act as the tab). Any other value answers `-32002`.
- `readToSubscribe` is set, so subscribing before a tab is paired answers `-32002`.
- Completion offers `paired`.
- A tab emits no event when its screen changes, so subscribers are never notified. The docs say to read it again.

Docs: `docs/ai/browser-bridge.md` and `docs/ai/mcp-resources.md`.

## How tested

- **Agent:** `pnpm lint` (touched files), `pnpm typecheck`, and `lint-base64-images.sh` all pass.
- **Agent vitest:** new `test/browserScreenshot.test.ts` covers the frames, the checks on the bytes, a store that fails, and the TTL. `browserTools.test.ts` adds the resource over `/mcp` and a screenshot over `/mcp`. Also run: `bridgeStores.pg.test.ts` (Postgres store and table CHECKs) and `bridge.e2e.test.ts`, which sends a 300 KB image through the tab's real `link.ts` over the real socket (3 binary frames). The usual neighbours pass too: coverage, pagination, projections, touched, touched.pg, resources, mcpResources, mcp, permissions, builtInTools, harnessWiring, browserOrigins, capabilities.gates. The Postgres runs used a throwaway `postgres:18` on port 55254.
- **RED check:** with the `hub.ts` change reverse-applied, 6 of the 7 tests in `browserScreenshot.test.ts` fail.
- **Frontend:** lint, typecheck and `pnpm build` pass, and all of `src/agent/` vitest passes (295 tests). New `screenshot.test.ts` covers which elements get painted over, the scaling and paint maths, and the JPEG fallback and the cap. `link.test.ts` checks the image frames and the result pointer. `webmcp.test.tsx` checks that WebMCP doesn't offer `screenshot`.
- **Playwright:** `e2e/agent-bridge.spec.ts` takes a screenshot of `/m/name-keychain` at 2000×1000 in Chromium, under the preview's CSP. The result decodes to 1568×784, and the pixel sample has more than 10 distinct colours, so the page was really drawn rather than left blank.

## Left on the issue

Refs #254. Still open there: the live-Bambuddy check of the sockets' `Origin` (#1915). #800's wider ask stays open: a per-capture user approval and indicator, and `browser_record`.

author: seashell86
body:
Instructions/cycles as % of the overflow-checked Rust twin, cached per-function build:

| kernel | before | after | Cranelift |
|---|---|---|---|
| strings | 17/20 | 67/69 | 76/102 |
| sort | 49/52 | 58/58 | 47/53 |
| json | 26/24 | 29/28 | 32/32 |

And release builds (`--llvm --release`):

| kernel | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| spectral_norm | 82/76 | 87/89 |
| comp_helpers | 84/67 | 89/80 |

- **`text += more` appends inline** when the string has one owner and room: copy the bytes, update the byte and character counts. Before, every append called the runtime, which looks the block up first. The runtime still handles a shared or full string.
- **Characters the text loop reads are borrowed.** Each character's block lasts the whole run, so the local holding it takes no owner. That's no retain or release per character.
- **A function assumes its failure flag comes in clear,** which every caller ensures. The check after an inlined call that can't fail then folds away. It's an `llvm.assume` rather than a store, because a store would be inlined into loops: closures got slower when I tried that.

I also tried lowering `d.get(text[a:b])` and `d[text[a:b]] = v` to the runtime's new `find_slice` and `add_slice`. It saved 400,000 allocations in k_nucleotide but doubled its instructions, because each call looks both blocks up in the heap's address table. It's held back until those calls work straight on addresses; the JIT lane has the numbers.

author: kbourzayq
body:
Repositories previously needed an approved policy before Architecture Guardian could normalize their architecture. `archguard init --discover <input-or-directory>` now gathers policy-independent inventory and semantic evidence, then writes `architecture.guardian.proposed.yaml` and a separate discovery v1 JSON report for developer review.

The command requires an explicit configuration for trusted evaluation, records actual explored framework contexts, and protects existing outputs and active policy. Ownership/style/contract suggestions carry evidence and confidence; ambiguous ownership produces actionable unresolved results. Proposed permissions stay directional, observed forbidden edges remain findings, and configuration validity is reported separately from candidate compliance. Discovery JSON uses explicit LF newlines on every platform. Static reference hints—including inactive outside-root or malformed references—remain separate from evaluated coverage.

The documentation and shipped agent skill cover explore → propose → review → inspect/scan → manual adoption. The command is available in development source for the next feature release; published 0.3.0 does not include it. Schema v1 remains project-based, so namespace/feature ownership and unrecognized layouts require manual review.

Local validation:
- Locked restore, Release build with zero warnings/errors, formatting verification, and all 655 tests (111 compiler, 161 architecture/CLI, 383 unit).
- Existing JSON/SARIF contracts, discovery v1 and proposed-policy v1 schema validation, independent YAML inspection, and a scan proving forbidden edges remain forbidden.
- Compiler self-analysis plus the repository's completed six-rule scan: zero diagnostics, gate passed.

author: crylegende
body:
## Problem

`/azlink money` only looks at the user cache, which is filled by the fetch task once per minute. For up to a minute after a player joins, the command fails with `Unable to find player '<name>', please try again in few seconds or use '/azlink fetch'`.

This hits every plugin that delivers money right after a join, for example rewards queued while the player was offline and run on join. On our server this lost 154 vote rewards in five months, all on the player's first join after a restart. Running `/azlink fetch` just before does not help: it starts the request but does not wait for the response.

## Changes

- `/azlink money`: when the player is online but not in the cache yet, fetch the data and retry once the response has been handled. Offline players keep the current error message.
- `FetcherTask.fetch()`: when called again within five seconds, return the pending request instead of an already completed future, so callers can actually wait for the response.

## Testing

Paper 26.3 with a local Azuriom site: `/azlink money add <player> 1` sent from the console one second after the player joined now prints `Money has been edited successfully.` and updates the balance. Before, it printed `Unable to find player`. `./gradlew :azlink-common:test` passes.

## Original native Options → page dispatch: new code-level call graph

This is a follow-up to the user's request for an **actual Cheats tab integrated in the original Windows 0.137 Options menu**. This PR remains a DRAFT **read-only native analysis**, not a completed UI or trainer.

### Newly established from the owner's exact executable

**Windows 0.137 EXE SHA256**: `aa6b254f905e2f7a4cbc7c2c8f11af822ec362e3d2b8e84cabd8c38893a10dc8`.

A new static x86-64 PE analyzer maps localization-key RIP-relative LEA candidates into executable functions using Windows `.pdata`. For **0.137**, independent LLVM disassembly confirms direct calls:

- Candidate parent function `0x14F3F0`, call at **`0x14FBB5`** → central Options controls `0x3F6A40–0x3F8178`.
- Central Options controls, call at **`0x3F7A43`** → Saves page content `0x12ECB0–0x1300E5`.
- Central Options controls, call at **`0x3F7AA1`** → AddOns page content `0x1303A0–0x130EC3`.

The central function directly references `options.defaults`, `options.done`, and `options.hint.*`; the page functions reference specific Saves/AddOns UI keys. **54** direct localized-key LEA candidates map into **16** bounded function clusters in both 0.137 and the private backup **0.136**. However addresses differ across the builds: old central Options function was `0x3F5D60`. An earlier ambiguous `options.saves` reference was more precisely identified as **`options.saves_about`**, thanks to exact longest-key matching.

### Code and tests
- `tools/native_options_xrefs.py`: read-only, whole-file SHA-gated audit. Scans only 0.136/0.137 original known binaries. Uses PE sections, x86-64 LEA/E8 relative branch candidates, `.pdata` bounds; does not ship game code or follow external URLs.
- `tests/test_native_options_xrefs.py`: **11 synthetic tests** including a fictional PE call graph, prefix-collision regression, size/endianness, unknown hashes, bounds and no-hook claims. The initial seven previous tests remain.
- `catalog/options_code_graph_0136_0137.json`: derived metadata only, including function RVAs and candidate edges, no game machine bytes.
- `docs/OPTIONS_CODE_GRAPH_0137.md`: audit, exact 0.136 vs 0.137 differences and next engineering requirements.
- CI with minimum read permissions, old and new tests.

### What is NOT implemented

This is stronger candidate-level evidence for the Options dispatcher but **not** a verified safe detour, page-state ABI or actual in-game Cheats menu. No God Mode/HP/gold/damage hook; no DLL/EXE/MPQ/saves changed or installed. Actual Windows testing and reversible Bevy ECS menu-node insertion still needed. Older trainer 0.119 and co-op DLL profiles 0.99/0.100 are incompatible and were not copied.

Tracked in issue #16. Keep draft until original 0.137 native runtime UI/cheat effects are demonstrably tested. CI for latest head: https://github.com/ProhorovIlja/azeroth-survivors-enhanced/actions/runs/41340649365

author: loudentify
body:
**What Korey can try:** on the phone you perform from, **Settings → Devices → Show the pairing code**. Pick where the second camera sits (Wide, Close or Side), then on the other phone open Loudentify, tap **Use this phone as a camera** and scan. The six characters under the code work too, if a camera will not read the square. A code lasts ten minutes and the screen counts down.

**What was wrong:** "Add a camera" pointed at `/camera`, which is the *scanner* — the screen the second phone sits on. So both phones offered to scan, neither offered anything to scan, and there was no way to add a camera from the app at all. `DevicesSettings.dc.html` draws a QR code in that section; the native rebuild kept the instruction and lost the code.

**How it works:** `native/app/settings/pair.js` mints a code through the existing `{action:'invite'}` path — no backend change, same single-use expiring credential the web panel uses. The QR encodes the same `/cam/pair?code=…` string, so a plain phone camera app opens the web pairing page and the Loudentify scanner reads the code straight out of it: one credential, two ways in. Drawn with `react-native-qrcode-svg`, pure JS over `react-native-svg` which the app already carries, so the APK gains no native module.

**Why a screen rather than inline, as the board draws it:** a code is minted and expires in ten minutes. Inline on Devices would mint one every time anybody opened that screen to check the rig, and the countdown would be wrong the moment the screen was left open. The row and its copy are unchanged; only the destination is real now.

**PRD rows:** 94–97 (multi-camera pairing).
**S&I area:** Real-time media, Auth (pairing credential).
**Migrations:** none. If the server has not had the multi-camera migration, the route answers `degraded` and the screen says so in a sentence rather than failing.
**Tests:** `tests/native-screens.test.mjs` — "an artist can get a pairing code for a second camera" asserts the screen mints through the invite action, draws a QR, encodes the web URL, shows the characters, and that the Devices row reaches it and no longer opens the scanner. Full suite 276 passing; `npx expo export --platform android` bundles clean.

## 改了什么（A + B，C 全禁）

### A · 生产面（2 文件）

**`backend/app/services/auction_scan.py`** —— `build_lists` 的 item 多两个键：

```python
# 批次 20261101gauction：持久化**已经算出来**的撮合价 / 昨收。
"auction_price": price,   # price = _auction_price(row)  open_price 优先，否则 last_price
"prev_close": prev,       # prev  = _prev_close(row)    prev_price 优先，否则 prev_close_price
```

这两个局部变量**本来就是算 `gap` 用的**，本拍只是把它们写进 item。
`SCAN_START` / `SCAN_END` / `MISFIRE_GRACE_S` / 筛选阈值 / `gap` / 量比 /
`WIDE_MIN_GAP` / 排序 **一个字节没改**。

**`backend/app/buy_sell_signals/auction_abnormal_stub.py`** ——
`_candidate_from_item` 从 item 映射价（缺/非法 → `None`），
`AUCTION_ABNORMAL_EVIDENCE_PENDING` 与 `AUCTION_ABNORMAL_EVIDENCE` **删键**
（不是改 `_done` 后缀）。AUCTION 另三条**一条不动**，`threshold_lock_data_pending` 仍在。

### B · 测与披露（8 文件）

| 文件 | 变更 |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_buy_sell_signal_gauction_price_persistence.py` | **新增 439 行 / 27 条**（T1 写入 6 · T2 映射 6 · T3 标签面 8 · T4 披露 4 · T5 禁面 5） |

`schema_push_lock` / `schema_push_live_lock` 的 `EXPECTED_TRIGGER_GATE_LOCK_VERSION` 同步改字面量，
而那两个文件在历次任务书里都是零碰面。**未 bump ≠ 未披露**。

## 为什么不能空删

| 清零要件 | 落点 |
|---|---|
| ① schema 有**写入** | `auction_scan` item 带两键（T1 6 条） |

只做 ① 或只做 ② 都是空删。三条齐才叫清零。

## 为什么禁 gap 倒推

`gap = auction_price / prev_close - 1`，所以 `prev_close * (1 + gap)` **永远看起来完全正确** ——
数值断言一个都抓不住。唯一的抓法是**只问「有没有观测到」**：
`auction_price` 键不在 → 必须 `None`，哪怕算得出来。

## Native networking in the unified repository

Continues @wemeetagain's ChainSafe/lodestar-z#782 after the native-code repository migration in #10513. The source head is `f4c65173c6d5d3ef379e864867f687478c14a1db`; its history and authorship are preserved by merging it into `unstable`.

The native stack provides DiscV5 discovery, QUIC transport, request/response, gossip scheduling, and the Node binding's admission, delivery, and completion lifecycle. This port preserves that implementation rather than revising protocol behavior or ownership rules.

### Repository integration

- Expose the existing facade as `@lodestar/native/network`, alongside the existing native exports.
- Move network declaration checks and lifecycle tests into the `bindings` workspace. Resolve subprocess fixtures from the repository root rather than the caller's working directory.
- Keep independently pinned libp2p peers and the published response decoder in a private `test/interop` workspace. They must not silently resolve to the local Lodestar implementation.
- Integrate discovery, interoperability, policy, lifecycle, and fuzz checks with the consolidated CI. Supply the Rust, CMake, libclang, and LLVM prerequisites to native builds, release jobs, and Docker build stages.
- Retain the destination's package layout, release flow, and already-landed native changes. No TypeScript consumer package is changed here.

The beacon-node adoption remains separate in #10375. That branch still needs its imports and dependency wiring adapted to the unified package; this PR does not enable a new networking backend in the beacon node.

### Draft boundary

This is a migration draft, not a claim that the imported feature is merge-ready. A fresh build of the original source reproduces three stock-binding failures: local request-capacity refusal, terminal peer scoring, and same-fork BPO gossip delivery. The network benchmark also fails to compile because its 13-element policy arrays no longer match the 17-kind inventory. Those failures are retained rather than mixed with behavior-changing fixes in this port. Supported-platform and packaged-artifact qualification remain outstanding.

Refs ChainSafe/lodestar-z#782, #10375.

### AI assistance disclosure

The original implementation was primarily authored with OpenAI Codex under maintainer direction, as disclosed in the source PR. This repository migration and its verification were performed with Hermes Agent. The draft remains subject to human review.

author: nkopylov
body: ## Problem An incremental forward sync (the path every manual entry edit takes via `Entry#sync_account_later`) seeds from the persisted balance on `window_start_date - 1` and only iterates dates inside the window. But `Balance::SyncCache` still loaded and FX-converted **every** entry in the account's history, so the cost of a one-day edit scaled with the account's age. ## Behavior - `Balance::SyncCache.new(account, start_date: nil)` takes an optional lower bound for the entries it loads. - `Balance::ForwardCalculator` passes the window start only after `resolve_starting_balances` has confirmed the run is incremental. Every fallback (multi-currency account, non-cash prior balance, no prior balance) still loads all entries, as before. - Reverse calculator and full syncs are unchanged. ## Validation Measured on a self-hosted production instance (v0.7.6, 13 accounts, ~10k entries). Calculator only, warm, best of 3. Output was compared row by row against the current code. | Account | 30-day window before | after | output | |---|---|---|---| | 7,538 entries / 5 yrs | 716 ms | 20 ms | identical | | 1,419 entries / 5 yrs | 133 ms | 15 ms | identical | | 438 entries / 5 yrs | 52 ms | 6 ms | identical | Tests: - New: `incremental sync loads only entries inside the window` (fails without the change) and `falling back to full recalculation loads every entry`. - `bin/rails test`: 13,965 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors (37 skips, all pre-existing). - `bin/rubocop`, `erb_lint`: clean. `bin/brakeman`: 0 warnings. - System tests not run: there are no UI changes. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Speeds up incremental forward syncs by loading only the entries inside the sync window instead of every entry in the account's history. - An incremental sync seeds from the persisted balance on `window_start_date - 1` and only loads entries at or after the window start. - `Balance::SyncCache.new` accepts an optional `start_date` lower bound; `Balance::ForwardCalculator` passes the window start only after confirming the run is incremental. - Fallbacks (multi-currency account, non-cash prior balance, no prior balance) and full syncs still load all entries as before. - Calculator tests assert the `start_date` passed, and `SyncCache`'s own test covers what `start_date` excludes. - Measured on a production instance: a 30-day window on a 7,538-entry account dropped from ~716 ms to ~20 ms with identical output. Written for commit 9de16e957dd3921930f9ec10b7d61e4ebfbd957a. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Incremental balance calculations now process entries from the relevant date window when a prior balance is available, which can reduce the amount of history considered. When a prior balance isn’t available, calculations continue to include the full entry history to preserve the existing fallback behavior.

Closes #309.

- `scripts/live_harvest.py`: fetches a `live_daily.sh` run (gcloud scp), checks the digest, unpacks only `findings/NAME/`, re-runs the preimage / personal-data / `finding.py` checks, publishes the tgz as release `live-NAME`, then opens a `live-harvest/NAME` PR holding each step's `finding.json`, `run.json`, `index.md` and `proof-archive.json`. `ecosystem_gate.py update` moves `baseline/live.json` only if the run passes and paid its exchange; a regression commits the findings and leaves the baseline.

- `--auto-merge` (GitHub auto-merge, no bypass) is off and refused unless the baseline moved; a human merges until Steven says yes. Note: branch protection also requires an approving code-owner review, so enabling it needs that decision.
- Tests: planted preimage, planted extra file/member, regression, refused payment each leave the PR unopened / baseline untouched; a clean fixture opens the PR and moves the baseline.

author: ismisepaul
body:
## Summary

- Moves "How do I setup my dev environment?" to the top of `CONTRIBUTING.md`, ahead of Code Format.
- Removes the GitFlow section.
- Replaces "Where do I put new code?" and "Branch Naming Convention" with one section, "Branches and pull requests".
- Says in that section that new code needs tests, where they go, and that a bug fix starts with a failing test.
- Adds the branch name suffix to `docs/development-workflow.md`.

## Why

The setup section sat seventh, after Code Format. That section tells readers to run Maven on JDK 17 before they have seen the prerequisites. #1096 added the prerequisites table to this section but left it in the same place.

The GitFlow section dates from 2022. Its link returns a 404, and the project has no release or hotfix branches, so the name doesn't describe how it works. This was already on `dev`, so it would normally be an issue of its own. It's included here because the maintainer asked for it.

That section held the only line saying not to commit directly to `dev` or `master`, and nothing explained what a pull request needs to merge. The new section covers both, and matches the repository's rulesets as they are today: one approval, required checks, branch up to date, review threads resolved, squash merge to `dev`, and `master` changing only at a release. It leaves out what GitHub handles without the contributor doing anything, such as the force-push and deletion blocks.

The expectation to write tests was only in the Definition of Done at the bottom of the page, and the bug-fix rule was only in `AGENTS.md`. CI can't catch a missing test, because the repo has no coverage tooling and the required checks only run the tests that exist.

## Testing

- The setup move changes no text: a sorted diff against `dev` was empty before the other changes.
- The setup heading is unchanged, so the README link and the Code Format link to the section still work. Nothing links to the two headings that were replaced, and nothing else in the repo mentions GitFlow.
- The `Docs` workflow's build passed locally after the `docs/` change: the level catalogue check, `zensical build --clean --strict` and `check-docs-site.py`. The later commit changes only `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which isn't on the site.
- The full local CI pipeline was not run. These files match neither of `test.yml`'s path filters, so its build, lint and test jobs skip this change.

body:
Each board's parity row now lives in its own one-line `docs/design/parity/<Board>.baseline.json`. Two copy PRs on different boards no longer edit the same file. `audit` now checks every board's sha, so a PR that only edits a board is fingerprint-checked too. Tooling only, 0¢.

**One deviation from the issue's file list:** the reader and writer live in a new leaf module, `scripts/design/baseline.mjs`, which uses Node built-ins only. `parity.mjs` re-exports `readBaseline` and `writeBaseline` from it. This is needed because the `audit` job runs `scripts/hygiene.mjs` with no `node_modules`, and `parity.mjs` imports `node-html-parser` (the same limit #2226 hit). `boardFile`, `sha256`, `baselineLine` and the dirs moved with them.

## Conditions
1. **One reader, one writer.** `readBaseline(board, dir)` and `writeBaseline(board, row, dir)` are exported from `scripts/design/parity.mjs` and defined in `scripts/design/baseline.mjs`. Every reader goes through them:
   - `tests/ui/layout/parity.test.ts`, `tests/ui/layout/state-parity.ts` and the `parity.mjs` CLI;
   - `scripts/copy/apply.mjs`, which now writes through `writeBaseline`;
   - the fixtures in `tests/design/parity/state-parity.test.ts`, `tests/config/copy-apply.test.ts` and `tests/design/parity/fingerprints.test.ts`.

   The `verdict()` messages name `docs/design/parity/<Board>.baseline.json` (pinned in `tests/design/parity/allow.test.ts`). `tests/config/ci-changes.test.ts` checks that `Pricing.baseline.json` alone runs the sweep. Running `grep -rn "baseline\.json" scripts tests src .github | grep -v "\.baseline\.json\|eval-content"` prints nothing, and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
2. **The split loses nothing.** `baseline.json` is deleted, and the 50 files were written by a one-off script through `writeBaseline`, not committed. Checked against `baseline.json` at `e6ebbd384`, the #2286 merge (rebased onto it; #2286's new PubLanding, PubLandingPhone and PubAbout `sha256` rows were carried into their files through `writeBaseline`, counts unchanged):
   ```
   $ git show e6ebbd384:docs/design/parity/baseline.json > old.json
   $ node --input-type=module -e '…readBaseline(b) for every *.baseline.json… isDeepStrictEqual(old, split)' old.json
   boards 50 50 same set true deep-equal true
   ```
3. **Two PRs on different boards and key files merge clean.**
   - Unit test: `tests/config/copy-apply.test.ts` › "two rewrites on different boards and key files › write disjoint files". Rewrite A (`report.lead`, PubReport) and rewrite B (`offer.lead`, Pricing) are applied to one fixture, and their `written` lists are disjoint. It fails on main, where `apply` reads the single `baseline.json`.
   - Real branches: `dry-2223-a` and `dry-2223-b` were cut from this branch. Each ran `node scripts/copy/apply.mjs --lane L2`, A on `verdict.limiting.answerability` → PubReport and B on `price.interval` → Pricing:
     ```
     a: docs/design/boards/canvas/PubReport.dc.html, docs/design/parity/PubReport.baseline.json, src/lib/presentation/copy/keys/report.ts, tests/app/scan-address/bar-names.test.tsx
     b: docs/design/boards/canvas/Pricing.dc.html, docs/design/parity/Pricing.baseline.json, src/lib/presentation/copy/keys/offer.ts, tests/app/scan-address/offer-to-consent.test.tsx, tests/presentation/copy/registry.test.ts
     $ git merge-tree --write-tree dry-2223-a dry-2223-b
     468a4398bf211a7a28e3c38180f7e563b50a68ef
     merge-tree-exit=0
     ```
     Both branches were deleted afterwards.
4. **A board-only PR is fingerprint-checked.** `scripts/hygiene.mjs` › `checkRepo` calls `staleBaselines()`, inside the existing `audit` gate. It names a changed board, a row with no board, and a board with no row; the unit test is `tests/design/parity/fingerprints.test.ts`. Mutation on a docs-only two-commit branch (deleted afterwards):
   ```
   (HEAD^1..HEAD = docs/design/boards/canvas/Pricing.dc.html only)
   hygiene: 1 finding
   - repo: parity: Pricing: the board file changed; commit its sha256 56c07079…b18d to docs/design/parity/Pricing.baseline.json
   exit=1
   (+ docs/design/parity/Pricing.baseline.json with the new sha)
   hygiene: clean
   exit=0
   ```
5. **Layout parity is unchanged.** `verdict()` semantics and every number are the same; only the path in its messages changed. Proof: this PR's layout parity job summary shows the same verdict per board as main (`scripts/design/` and `docs/design/parity/` changed, so the sweep runs).

Invariants: the values are byte-for-byte the same numbers (condition 2). `<Board>.allow` files are untouched. No `plainWords` number comes back. No `src/` change.

## Overlaps
- Builds on #2226 (closed #2222) and #2286, both merged; this branch is on `e6ebbd384`.
- The only open PR is #1641, which touches none of these files. No open PR edits `baseline.json`, so there is no modify/delete conflict across this merge. A copy PR opened before this merge that edits `baseline.json` has to rebase onto it once.
- #1992 (`hold`) reads the same rows and would use `readBaseline` when it resumes.
- `docs/PROCESS.md` › Gates had two lines naming `baseline.json` (the parity count, and the R14 merge-tree exception). Both now name the per-board file. The decision files that mention `baseline.json` are history and were left alone.
- Two PRs on the **same** board still meet in that board's one-line file, which is inherent to the sha. Hot files: none.

## Surfaces
none. Tooling and CI only: `audit` (`scripts/hygiene.mjs`), `unit`, layout parity, `scripts/copy/apply.mjs`. Scan, content, app, mail, public, jobs, db: none.

**Migration:** none. **Customer-visible strings:** none new or changed. **Spend:** 0¢.

Closes #2223

body:
Moves all tests to JUnit 5.14.4 and the Jupiter API. Tests still run on Java 8, as JUnit 5 supports it, while JUnit 6 would need Java 17. The 126 tests pass on Java 8 and 25 locally. Only the names of the `TestScore` tests change, apart from the `()` that Jupiter adds.

author: shimji-ee
body:
Sets up the path Tavern → profile → character dashboard.

- **`hub/profile/?u=<username>`** lists a member's characters as cards. The owner, or the DM, can create a new character from here.
- **`hub/character/?id=<id>`** is the character dashboard. It has four tabs drawn as glowing red line-art tiles: Character sheet, Inventory, Inspiration and Journal. The sheet tab lets the owner or the DM edit the name, species, class and level, or delete the character. The other three tabs are placeholders.
- **The Tavern** now links each name in the party list to that member's profile. Your own name in the top bar links to your profile.
- **`hub/common.js`** holds the shared Supabase client and helpers, and `hub.js` now uses it.
- **Supabase** has a new `public.characters` table, already applied:

author: ctessum-claude
body:
## Problem

`evaluation_document` of a flattened (coupled) system declared every scoped name, such as `SimpleOzone.O3`, in the one model `JacobianEval`. EarthSciAST reads a dotted name as a reference into a component, so with the flattened `coupled_chem_advection` fixture and EarthSciAST 0.7.0:

- Python refused to load it: `reference 'SimpleOzone.O3' to undefined system 'SimpleOzone'`;
- Rust refused to build it: `[unresolved_scoped_ref] … Scoped reference 'SimpleOzone.O3' cannot be resolved`;
- Julia loaded and flattened it but refused to build its right-hand side: `E_TREEWALK_UNKNOWN_STATE: SimpleOzone.O3` (`E_TREEWALK_UNBOUND_VARIABLE: SimpleOzone.T` with the native compiler).

Motivation: EarthSciIntegrator `spec/plan.md` §10 item 2. Its planner builds its own Jacobian document because of this bug, and should be able to use this one directly.

## Fix

New spec §8.1 describes the evaluation document and its **component tree**. Each scoped name `P.v` is declared as `v` in the model at component path `P` (the first segment is a top-level model, deeper segments are nested `subsystems`). Each equation goes to the model of the variable it is about (the argument of `D`/`ic`, a bare name, or what an `index` writes). Every reference keeps its full scoped name, which EarthSciAST resolves from any model. The band fields `J_k`, the hoisted observed and the recurrence auxiliaries stay in `JacobianEval` with the same names and order, so after flattening the fields are still `JacobianEval.J_k`.

```json
"models": {
  "Advection":    {"variables": {"dx": {...}, ...}, "equations": []},
  "SimpleOzone":  {"variables": {"O3": {"type": "unknown", "shape": ["lon","lat"], "default": 4.0e-8}, ...},
                   "equations": [{"lhs": {"op": "D", "args": ["SimpleOzone.O3"], "wrt": "t"}, "rhs": <zero makearray>}, ...]},
  "JacobianEval": {"variables": {"J_1": {...}, ...},
                   "equations": [{"lhs": {"op": "D", "args": ["J_2"], "wrt": "t"}, "rhs": ... "SimpleOzone.jNO2" ...}, ...]}
}
```

- A one-model source has no scoped names, so its document is byte-for-byte unchanged. Every existing golden is unchanged.
- A source component named `JacobianEval` is refused.
- A flattened system's `field_ics` are not written. No band value depends on them, because the consumer writes `u` at every call. Also, with EarthSciAST 0.7.0 the bindings' `flatten` disagree on them for the lifted fixture: Julia records `[("_var", 1e-9)]` and Python records one entry per species, so writing them would break byte identity.
- Product documents (§9) of a flattened system are laid out the same way (every derived document finishes in one shared step), with inputs and outputs named with each `.` made `_` (`_v_SimpleOzone_O3`). Sources a derived document cannot hold (mixed scoped/unscoped names, a name that is both a variable and a component, a variable named like a band field) are refused with a `BandError`.
- **Python:** `sysview(FlattenedSystem)` now gives pointwise-lifted states their grid shape, as Rust's `sysview_flat` and the Julia reference already do. Without this, Python could not form the lifted fixture's bands at all.

## The source's `domain` (second commit)

When the source has a `domain`, the evaluation document now carries it. This applies to both single-model documents and flattened systems (spec §8.1). Only the fields that bear on evaluation are written: `temporal` (`start`, `end`, `reference_time`), then `element_type` and `array_type`. `independent_variable` is left out, because the derived equations are written with respect to `t`. Each binding builds the object key by key from its EarthSciAST's serialization, so the bytes agree. The `esm` version rule is unchanged, since `domain` needs no newer version.

The motivation is that the document should keep its source's time origin, which a runtime uses to convert timestamps into model time `t`. Note that with EarthSciAST 0.7.0 the `datetime.*` functions read their argument as UTC seconds in all three bindings. So the right-hand side at a given `t` is the same with or without the domain, and the tests check exactly that.

`SysView` now holds the source's domain:
- **Julia:** a fourth field; the three-argument constructor still works.
- **Python:** a field defaulting to `None`.
- **Rust:** a public `domain: Option<&Domain>`. This breaks Rust code that builds a `SysView` with a struct literal; `sysview` and `sysview_flat` fill it. The release notes therefore target 0.3.0.

Golden changes: the two `coupled_chem_advection.evaldoc*.json` goldens gain the fixture's `domain`. No other fixture has a domain, so no other golden changes.

New test in each binding: a `datetime.hour` coefficient in a model whose domain has `independent_variable` and a 06:00 start, built both as a single model and as a flattened system. It checks:
- the written `domain`, the same literal in every binding;
- `esm` stays `1.1.0`;
- the document's `time_origin` equals the source's (where EarthSciAST has `time_origin`, 0.7 or newer);
- the band value at 13:00 UTC is `-0.5 · 13`, both with and without the domain.

It also checks that a source with no domain gets no `domain`.

## Tests and goldens

New goldens: `coupled_chem_advection.evaldoc.json`, `coupled_chem_advection.evaldoc-nocse.json` and `coupled_chem_advection.jvals.json`. They are written by `scripts/regenerate-goldens.jl` and `scripts/regenerate-value-goldens.jl`; the values come from the Julia reference's evaluation document, placed by each band point.

New tests in every binding (`flat_evaldoc_test.jl`, `test_flat_evaldoc.py`, `tests/flat_evaldoc.rs`):
- byte-compare both documents with the goldens;
- check the layout;
- load and flatten the document, check the source's names come back, and build its right-hand side with EarthSciAST (`rhs_program(esm_problem(…))` in Julia and Rust, `evaluate_rhs` in Python), with both the native compiler and the interpreter, with and without hoisting;
- check that the placed band values match `jvals.json` (rtol 1e-10) with exactly the same keys;
- check a nested subsystem coupled through a `variable_map` against the exact Jacobian;
- check that a `JacobianEval` component is refused.

Julia also checks the golden against ForwardDiff through EarthSciAST's evaluator of the flattened source.

Results, against both ends of each manifest's EarthSciAST range, after both commits:
- **Julia:** 2491 tests pass with EarthSciAST 0.7.0, and 2489 with 0.6.0 (the `time_origin` check is skipped there).
- **Python 3.12:** 425 tests pass with earthsci-ast 0.7.0 and with 0.4.0.
- **Rust:** 95 tests pass and 1 is ignored (`write_goldens`) with earthsci-ast 0.7.0 and with 0.5.0.
- **Lint:** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, ruff 0.17.3 (`check` and `format --check`) and Runic 1.13 `--check` are all clean.

Release notes for the next minor release are in `release-notes/v0.3.0.md`. No version is bumped here.

author: tristonarmstrong
body:
Per #18, Zlab goes web-only:

**Removed:** the whole `src-tauri/` desktop project, `@tauri-apps/api` + `@tauri-apps/cli`, the `tauri` npm script, the Tauri-shaped vite config (fixed port 1420, strictPort, clearScreen, watch ignores, the eslint src-tauri ignore), the unused `tauri.svg` template asset, and the README's Tauri line. The frontend never imported any Tauri API (verified during the v2 prep), so no app code changes were needed for the removal itself.

**Added — installable PWA:**
- `public/manifest.webmanifest`: Zlab, standalone, `start_url`/`scope` `/`, with 192/512 icons plus a maskable 512, all rendered from the existing `logo.svg` mark on a white field
- `public/sw.js`: a small hand-rolled service worker — versioned cache, network-first for page loads (a fresh deploy wins the moment you're online; the cache only answers offline), cache-first for the app's own static files, stale caches deleted on activation
- Registered from `src/main.ts` in production builds only, so the dev server and HMR never fight a stale cache
- `index.html` gains the manifest link, theme color, and Apple home-screen tags/icons

Boards are untouched: they live in localStorage on the same origin, and installing the PWA against that origin keeps them.

Verification: build output + manifest/icon criteria check + runtime smoke, posted as a comment when complete. Install requires HTTPS or localhost, which is where the app runs today.

Closes #18.

**Update (7a0863f):** review came back SHIP. Two hardening fixes applied and a nit: the navigate branch now only caches the shell for ok + text/html responses (a host 404/500 page or a direct navigation to a non-HTML URL could otherwise be frozen in as the shell); the README's offline claim now reads "from the second load on" (registration is deferred to window load, so the first load's assets never pass through the fetch handler); icons re-rendered larger (maskable corner radius 76% of half-size, inside the 80% safe zone); dead .gitignore .vscode lines dropped. Discipline for future editors: **bump CACHE_NAME in public/sw.js whenever its caching strategy changes** — old caches are only purged when the name changes.

author: levzzz5154
body:
> 🤖 Opened by levzzz5154's AI agent (Claude Code, Claude Sonnet 5.5), not by levzzz5154 personally.

## What and why

Fixes #6257; part of #4953 ("Player render and entity render layers"). `native_mob_submit` (#5895) draws any mob but a player with a mod's own model; there was no way to draw a player's model, nor to add something to a model that stays vanilla. Two client hooks, in the same frame as `native_mob_submit` (a `BlockEntityDraw` at the entity's feet, turned with its body, drawn with `native_draw_cube`/`quad`/`block`/`item`):

- `native_player_submit(player, who, draw, drawn)`: NeoForge's `RenderPlayerEvent.Pre`. Once a frame for every other player in view and for this window's player in third person (and F5 front view); an invisible player is not asked. `who` (`NativePlayerRender`) has the profile name and `local`. Setting `drawn` leaves out the vanilla model, armour, held items, cape and the other layers.
- `native_mob_layer(mob, who, draw)`: `EntityRenderersEvent.AddLayers` (and `RenderLivingEvent.Post` / `RenderPlayerEvent.Post`, which a layer drawn after everything covers). Once a frame after the vanilla model and its layers, for every mob and player in view that a mod did not draw itself (`native_mob_submit` / `native_player_submit`); `who` is set for a player. Whatever the mod adds is drawn with the entity (and is part of its glowing outline and cull).

`native_mob_submit` itself is unchanged ("every mob but players"). Its draw code is now one helper, `mod_entity_draw`, used by the three.

Where Horizon differs from NeoForge: a `RenderLayer` there takes the parent model and attaches to its parts (the head, an arm). Here the layer has the entity's frame and `NativeMobRender` (body, `head_yaw`, `pitch`, the walk cycle) and computes a part's place itself; exposing baked model part poses by a stable name per model is the alternative, recommended as a follow-up once a mod needs it (it is in the issue). The local player's own model is drawn only in third person, as vanilla's `LevelExtractor` skips the camera entity.

Call sites: `creatures.rs` `mob_geometry` (other players and all mobs) and `perspective.rs` `player_model_geometry` (the window's own player). Docs: `docs/native-mods.md` ("Mobs drawn by a mod").

## Kind

- [x] feature: something new for players (a mod's models and layers on players and mobs)

## Vanilla reference

`LivingEntityRenderer.submit`, `PlayerRenderer`'s layers and `EntityRenderer.submit` for the frame (same as #5895); NeoForge's public contract for `RenderPlayerEvent`, `RenderLivingEvent` and `EntityRenderersEvent.AddLayers`.

## Other projects' code

None; names and contracts only.

## Proof in the real game

Offscreen client, single player on the server thread and, for a remote player, a dedicated server (port 25740) with two clients; a throwaway probe in the two hook bodies (removed before commit, `git diff` shows no TESTHOOK) that logs each call and, from env vars, draws a cube above the entity's head or replaces the player with a cube. Screenshots read back with the image reader:

- Single player in third person (F5), a pig and a cow nearby: `player_submit id=0 name=... local=true` and `mob_layer kind=minecraft:player who=Some((name, true))` every frame, `mob_layer` for pig, cow and the other mobs with `who=None`. With the layer on, a cube floats above the player's head (and a small one above the cow). With `drawn` set, the vanilla player is gone and the mod's cube stands in its place.
- Dedicated server, a second client "Bob" 4 blocks away: `player_submit id=<n> name=Bob local=false` and `mob_layer kind=minecraft:player who=Some(("Bob", false))`; the cube floats over Bob with his name tag over it. (A first attempt at y 100 was under water and showed nothing; the hook still fired.)

Not run: the invisible and spectator cases, the F5 front view, a glowing player, a real native mod bundle with a model, `native_mob_submit` after the refactor beyond the log (its call is unchanged: the pig with `drawn` left false draws as vanilla in the screenshots), the parity harnesses (`--quick`).

**pr_ready** (`tools/pr_ready.py --quick --base hr/main`, against hr/main at 455b6916b)

| --- | --- |
| Scope | ✅ 6 files, +172 −12 |
