author: jlengelbrecht
body:
## Summary

Let tuppr run Kubernetes upgrades the same way it runs Talos upgrades: Renovate bumps the version, the PR is merged by hand, and tuppr rolls it out.

The new `KubernetesUpgrade` sits at the running version (v1.34.1), so merging this starts nothing. It records Completed until a later PR changes the version.

## Changes

- `kubernetesupgrade.yaml`: cluster-wide plan with the same health checks as the Talos plan (external Ceph HEALTH_OK, every node Ready). tuppr waits for a running TalosUpgrade to finish before it starts.
- `scripts/check-talos-versions.sh`: the KubernetesUpgrade version is a third Kubernetes copy and must match `talos/topf.yaml`.
- Renovate: the kubelet custom manager and the `kubernetes-cluster-version` group now include the KubernetesUpgrade. Both version groups set `separateMultipleMinor`, so a jump such as 1.34 to 1.37 arrives as one PR per minor version. Kubernetes does not support skipping a minor, and tuppr does not enforce the path.
- `.github/renovate.json5`: kubelet tracking is disabled everywhere except the files listed in its override rule; the KubernetesUpgrade is added there, otherwise Renovate would bump only two of the three copies.
- Renovate automerge: the manual-merge rule for the Kubernetes version now covers the KubernetesUpgrade too. Without it, the default patch and minor automerge rules would match that file.
- `talosupgrade.yaml`: the header no longer says that no node is enrolled; all of them are.
- `talos/README.md`: point Kubernetes upgrades at the KubernetesUpgrade instead of `talosctl upgrade-k8s`.

## Testing

- `scripts/check-talos-versions.sh` passes (Talos: 5 copies, Kubernetes: 3 copies), and fails when the KubernetesUpgrade version alone is changed to v1.35.0.
- `renovate-config-validator --strict`: no errors. Its config-migration warning concerns the Flux Local rule and shows up on main as well.
- The Renovate kubelet regex matches `v1.34.1` in the new file.
- `kubectl kustomize` builds both plans, and the KubernetesUpgrade passes a server-side dry run.

author: var1377
body: Reconstructing historical archives currently calls `sync_all` for every newly installed source member before Cargo uses the working tree. These sources are reconstructible from checksum-verified archives and have no crash-durability contract. Install the complete files with the existing atomic no-clobber operation and leave final documentation publication at its original durability boundary. For N new members, explicit source-file durability barriers go from N to zero. Required work remains destination validation, one temporary output and source input per new member, byte transfer, and atomic no-clobber installation; no new allocation, copy, provider request, task or wait is introduced. Import/publication still scales with actual bytes and members. Existing checksum snapshots, source-replacement checks, immutable-file comparison and independent post-Cargo verification remain. No OS-wide syscall measurement or crash-recovery qualification is inferred from the source-level barrier count. Linux x86_64: `cargo test --locked -p sdk-generation --lib historical::tests::archive_codec::staged_archive_matches_retained_decoder_and_immutable_publication -- --exact`, 1/1 passed, 0.01 s (compile 20.08 s). This existing control checks plain/compressed archive parity against the independent retained decoder, repeat installation and refusal to overwrite mutated output. Local `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` passed for the changed Rust file. --- ## Summary by cubic Removes the explicit `sync_all()` durability barrier from archive source reconstruction so installing complete members into the Cargo working tree no longer waits on per-member fsync. These sources are reconstructible from checksum-verified archives and have no crash-durability contract; final documentation publication still owns its separate durability boundary, and atomic no-clobber installation with checksum and post-install verification remain unchanged. Written for commit 509a10ed601f3b432e0a3aeef6448633fa827337. Summary will update on new commits.

author: jorenham
body:

body:
## Summary

The drift check (`scripts/drift.py`, on `feat/drift-check`) found the deployed scanner image built from `b85206d`, with `lambda/iac-scanner/local_main.py` changed on main since. The change is a comment from `9f6af66`. This PR pins the image rebuilt from `b22fc47`, which is already published and deployed, and records the eval run on it.

- **Pins:** `SCANNER_IMAGE` (`cli/src/cascadesec/scan.py`), `cli/Dockerfile`'s default and the docker hook's entry in `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` now name:
  - scanner `ghcr.io/konradkelly/cascadesec-scanner@sha256:a60b6aaae929ed7799ca9869b427763bd64efa0aee1013bc2a09f1198ad50c8b`
  - hook `ghcr.io/konradkelly/cascadesec-hook@sha256:73af04c3c2e15684460dc1e8058a1bdd2787429dc61b9e6a3844e66202e91289`
- **Eval and coverage:** the README, the eval README and completion.md §3 now name the 2026-11-01 run. They also carry mapping coverage remeasured on 90 cases. The published coverage figures dated from 2026-09-12.

## What was checked before anything was pushed

- **Build:** from a clean worktree at `b22fc47`. 13 of the image's 16 layers are the deployed image's own, checkov's unpinned dependencies included, because the build cache held them.
- **Files:** of the three layers that differ, only `local_main.py`'s content does, and it matches main's copy. The corpus files are byte-identical.
- **Scans:** both images ran over `corpus/eval/cases` in local mode. They gave the same 517 findings, equal in every field, with no parse errors, over the same 92 files.

## Deployed, 2026-11-01

- **Published:** `build-image.sh --ghcr` pushed ECR `latest` and `b22fc47` at `sha256:a60b6aaa…`, the image compared above. GHCR serves the same manifest byte for byte. The hook is built on it.
- **Applied:** `deploy.py --apply-saved` applied a plan of 0 creates, 2 updates, 0 replaces, 0 destroys:
  - `aws_lambda_function.iac_scanner`: its `image_uri` changed from `@sha256:6b0d0417…` to `@sha256:a60b6aaa…`;
  - `aws_iam_role_policy.pipeline`: known only after apply, because its document reads that function's ARN, which does not change.
- **Lambda:** runs `sha256:a60b6aaa…`, update status `Successful`.

## Eval on the deployed scanner

| | 2026-11-01, `b22fc47` | 2026-09-23, `3b74055` |
|---|---|---|
| Detection recall | 178/180, 98.9% | 178/180, 98.9% |
| By source | Trivy 63/63, KICS 22/22, checkov 93/95 | the same |
| Misses | `CKV_AWS_60`, `CKV_SECRET_6` | the same |
| Clean controls | nothing raised | nothing raised |
| Findings, all on their file's target_type | 517 | 517 |
| Coverage, labelled pairs | 131/133, 98.5% | 44/61, 72% (2026-09-12, 40 cases) |
| Coverage, distinct rules | 174/242, 71.9% | 48/123, 39% (2026-09-12) |

## After merge

`scripts/drift.py` should then report the scanner clean. Until this merges, it reports that the CLI's pin on `origin/main` differs from the Lambda's image.

## Test plan

- [x] `cli/tests/test_hook.py` and `cli/tests/test_scan.py` hold the three pins equal: 37 passed
- [x] corpus tests: 219 passed
- [x] no file outside these names the old digests
- [x] CI: all 17 jobs passed ([run 41339043223](https://github.com/konradkelly/CascadeSec/actions/runs/41339043223))

author: marcus100
body:
Slice 5 of the GMS homepage v2. **Stacked on #1009 → #1007 → #1005**: merge those first.

**API** (`/api/v1/eregister/public/month-summary`, additive, non-breaking)
- `heavy_rain_days` (24 h total ≥ 10 mm, Climpact R10mm) computed in the same SQL as rain days.
- `longest_dry_spell_days` + start/end dates and `current_dry_spell_days` (Climpact CDD, under 1 mm). A day with no 24 h total breaks a run: the register cannot say it was dry.
- `mean_wind_kt` (calm counts as 0), `prevailing_wind_direction` (most frequent 8-point direction of non-calm readings), `max_gust_kt` + `max_gust_at`, decoded with the same `wind`/`gust` functions as the latest-observation card.
- `openapi.json` and `@barrelsgd/api-client` regenerated; `check:drift` passes.

**GMS**
- Four cards: **Rainfall** (total, heavy rain days), **Temperature** (hottest, coolest), **Wind** (average with direction, strongest gust), **Dry spells** (longest with dates, current). Wind follows the Metric/Imperial switch. Unreported figures say so, never 0.
- Before the 5th the section shows the previous month in full ("October at MBIA"), then "November so far at MBIA" (`dataMonth`).

**Not included:** the 1991–2020 "normal" comparison line. No normals exist in the system; GMS must supply them.

**Verification:** `pnpm verify:changed`: format+lint, api lint+types, api tests, type-check, api client drift, guardrails, docs all pass. The `test` gate failed once on an unrelated Bookings test (`settings-submit.test.tsx`, waiting for an alert) during a 29-minute run; it passes on its own (6/6) and this PR does not touch Bookings. New tests: dry spells, wind month, heavy rain days and dry-spell dates in the SQL integration test, four-card mapping, previous-month rule.

Refs #1002

author: the78mole
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"the78mole"} -->
_Requested by **Maulwurf** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01RpDHUcqFTY7EUP7WfNSeza?thread=cmsg_01RpDHUcqFTY7EUP7WfNSezaVvL911miQaZvypWH4upSdX)_

## Was ändert sich?

Fuzzing für die offenen Teile von SYSR-SEC-009 in diesem Repository: GHCR-Artefakte fremder Instanzen und ENTSO-E-Antworten. Folgt auf #231 (gribkit ausgelagert).

**wx-exchange (neues Modul `safe.py`, SWR-WXX-060, SWA-WXX-SAFE)**
- `read_tar`: nur relative, eindeutige Pfade ohne `..` und Steuerzeichen, Obergrenzen für Einträge und entpackte Größe (auch gzip), alle Lesefehler als `ArtifactError` (ein `ValueError`). Genutzt von `artifact.files_from_tar`/`unpack`, `idx.unpack`, `gefs.unpack`.
- **Fund:** `files_from_tar` übernahm bisher jeden Namen ungeprüft und ohne Größengrenze.
- Manifeste und Deskriptoren (`MonthArtifact`, `GefsMonth`, `IdxLayer`): Typprüfung, Digest nur `sha256:<64 hex>` (landet sonst ungeprüft in der Registry-URL), Läufe ohne Zeitzone werden UTC. **Fund:** Ein unvollständiger Deskriptor brach den Import mit `KeyError` ab. Jetzt überspringen GFS- und GEFS-Import das Manifest mit Warnung; beim Bronze-Aufräumen bleibt Bronze dann liegen.
- `parse_tag` ist jetzt genau die Umkehrung von `tag`. **Fund:** `9999-12-00z` führte in `month_bounds` zu `OverflowError`, `2026-1-00z` wurde akzeptiert.

**energy-ingest, ENTSO-E (SWR-ENI-033, Teilweise)**
- **Funde:** `PT0M` → `ZeroDivisionError`; XML mit unbekannter Kodierung → `LookupError`; Period über Jahrtausende in Minuten → Milliarden Schleifendurchläufe; `nan`/`1e400` wurden als Werte übernommen; ungültige Zeitpunkte und Zahlen → `ValueError`/`ParseError`.
- Jetzt `FormatError`, höchstens `MAX_POINTS` (100 000) je Period, nur endliche Werte; eine Period mit Ende vor Beginn ist ein Formatfehler.

**Tests und Fuzzer**
- Hypothesis-Tests `services/wx_exchange/tests/test_robustheit_artefakte.py` und `services/energy_ingest/tests/test_robustheit_entsoe.py` (jede CI).
- `fuzz/predictiondb_fuzz.py` mit den Zielen `tar`, `manifest` (strukturierte Manifeste aus den Fuzz-Bytes) und `entsoe`, Startkorpus unter `fuzz/korpus/`; `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml` wöchentlich und bei Änderungen an den Parsern. Damit erkennt OpenSSF Scorecard wieder Fuzzing.
- `hypothesis` (dev) und Gruppe `fuzz` (atheris) wieder im Root-`pyproject.toml`.
- SYSR-SEC-009 nachgezogen; offen bleiben die übrigen Energiequellen (Netztransparenz, Eurostat, SMARD …), MaStR-XML und die pdb-predict-Pakete.

## Wie wurde es geprüft?

- `uv run pytest`: 362 passed, 40 skipped
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: alles grün (inkl. `reqs-abdeckung`, StrictDoc, mypy)
- Fuzzer lokal je 40–60 s nach den Fixes ohne Fund: `tar` 369 000, `manifest` 1,8 Mio., `entsoe` 490 000 Läufe

## Beitragsbedingungen

- [x] Ich habe die [Beitragsbedingungen](https://github.com/the78mole/PredictionDB/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) gelesen und akzeptiere sie. Alle Commits tragen eine `Signed-off-by`-Zeile (`git commit -s`).

author: bridestowebelstonecc
body:
Two additions for beta 4, from today's testing.

## A practice match from the start
"How is today's match being scored?" (the app's home screen; `[3]` at the console) has a third answer, **A practice match**. Match day starts as usual (OBS, the overlay) and the launcher starts the control panel's existing practice match (2 overs a side) once the server's up, so a new club can check its whole set-up with no scorer in one press. The panel's Practice match card still shows and stops it.

The practice was paced at 2.5s a ball, so the next ball came while a boundary's or wicket's replay was still on screen. `practiceGap()` now gives 15s a ball, plus the replay's own time (from `replay_duration`; the side-on replay and walk-out when camera 2 does them) and time for the end of an over. Measured: 2 overs ≈ 14 min, 5 ≈ 28, 10 ≈ 51 (the panel says 15/30/50).

## A QR code for the scorer's phone
Match day started for manual scoring pops up the scoring page's QR code once: in the control panel (the window's own, or on this laptop) and on the clubhouse screen when it started match day "By hand". **Scoring link** (panel top bar) and **Get ready → Scoring link** (screen) bring it back. `/remote/info` and `/remote/qr.png` take `page=scoring`; `/remote/info` also returns `manual_today`. The clubhouse link's `proxyGET` gains those two reads (addresses only, the same the panel shows anyone on the network) — not `viewGET`, so score-only screens can't.

Also: the beta 4 release notes and changelog.

## Test plan
- [x] gofmt, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` pass
- [x] `TestPracticeLeavesTimeForReplays`, `TestPracticeChoiceReachesMatchDay`, `TestScoringQRLinksToTheScoringPage`
- [ ] Fresh build here: start a practice match from the home screen and watch the replays in OBS
- [ ] Manual scoring from the Pi: the QR code shows on the Pi and in the panel, and a phone opens /scoring

author: gruberchris
body:
Adds six aggregation stages and pipeline-style updates (ADR-263, ADR-265).

- **Stages:** `$sortByCount`, `$replaceWith`, the `$unset` stage, `$sample` (a uniform random sample in random order), `$redact` with `$$DESCEND`, `$$PRUNE` and `$$KEEP`, and `$unionWith` (both forms, with a sub-pipeline; `read` on both collections; refused when it reads the `$merge`/`$out` target). The expression engine gains the named `$cond: {if, then, else}` form.
- **Pipeline-style updates:** an aggregation pipeline as the update document in update, findAndModify and upsert. `_id` is judged on the final result: a removed `_id` is put back, and a changed one is refused.
- **A missing collection** read by `$lookup`, `$graphLookup` or `$unionWith` reads as empty on a node with no peers, and answers 404 with a retry hint on a node with peers.
- **Breaking:** an expression that names a missing field leaves the field out of `$addFields`/`$set`/`$project` results, and removes an existing field, instead of storing null.
- `$mod` accepts Decimal128.
- Docs: `aggregation.md`, `query-language.md`, `http-api.md`, `deviations.md`, the decisions log and the CHANGELOG.

body:
## Qué cambia

Proceso genérico y repetible para atender a cada cliente (tenant), del brief al cierre con respaldo.

- **`scripts/tenant/export.mjs <slug>`**: respaldo local de un evento. Exporta la fila de `events`, sus tablas hijas y el brief (`data.json`), descarga los archivos de los tres buckets bajo `{event_id}/` y escribe `manifest.json` con conteos y sha256. Nunca exporta `guest_credentials.pin_hash`; redacta `guests.token` y `events.activation_code`; excluye `identify_attempts`. Opción `--sin-archivos` para solo la base.
- **`scripts/marcos/`**: el pipeline de marcos de IA (quitar fondo negro, preparar WebP y SQL, subir a Storage) como scripts genéricos que reciben la carpeta del cliente.
- **`docs/operaciones/ciclo-de-vida-tenant.md`**: runbook en seis pasos (brief, evento, marcos, pruebas en teléfonos, día de la fiesta, cierre y respaldo) y reglas de privacidad. Enlazado desde `docs/README.md` y `CLAUDE.md`.
- El material de cada cliente vive en un repositorio privado aparte; `respaldos/` queda ignorado.

## Verificación

- `npm run typecheck`: pasa.
- `npm test`: 122 archivos, 1580 tests en verde.
- `npm run test:db`: 15 archivos, 374 tests en verde (incluye `tenant-export.test.ts`, 7 tests: aislamiento entre eventos, sin `pin_hash`, redacción, slug desconocido y manifiesto).

author: well-prado
body:
Closes #1721.

The unpaired screen and Home both showed Oby with the app's one `WebPage`. When `PhoneRoot` swaps one screen for the other (pairing done, or the Mac revoked this iPhone), both are on screen for a moment, and WebKit stops the app: a `WebPage` shows in one `WebView` at a time.

Now each screen has a page of its own, held by the app in a `StageCharacter` and made the first time that screen shows it. Two reasons:
- A view's `@State` default is built again on every redraw.
- A page loaded while no `WebView` shows it never draws. Made up front, Home's page stayed blank after a fresh, unpaired launch was paired.

Each page is paused off its own screen: Home's also while the unpaired screen shows.

**Checked:** in the iOS Simulator, paired through a local Obysphere to a dev obid, by pasted invitation.
- Before the fix, the app quit on pairing and on a revoke from obid (two crash reports, `_WebKit_SwiftUI` in `makeViewProvider`).
- After it, three paths work with no crash, Oby on screen each time:
  - a fresh unpaired launch, paired, goes to Home;
  - a revoke goes back to "Your Mac removed this iPhone…";
  - a launch already paired opens on Home.

There's no unit test: the crash is WebKit's, and only shows on screen.

author: gascity-infra-agent[bot]
body:
## Problem

`[[orders.overrides]]` entries are applied in order, and an entry that has no `name` or matches no order stopped every entry listed after it from applying. The orchestrator's order scan and the API's order views tolerate the override error, so they kept running with only the overrides that came *before* the bad one.

Minimal repro (`city.toml`):

```toml
[[orders.overrides]]
name = "retired-order"   # no longer exists (renamed, retired, typo, disabled by its own file, or removed by [orders] skip)
enabled = false

[[orders.overrides]]
name = "nightly-report"  # exists
enabled = false
```

Expected: `nightly-report` is disabled. Actual: the orchestrator logs the error for `retired-order` and keeps dispatching `nightly-report`. Disabling an order through the API (which appends an override) likewise has no effect once any earlier override is stale.

## Root cause

`internal/orders/override.go` — `ApplyOverrides` returned at the first bad entry (`return fmt.Errorf("orders.overrides[%d]: name is required", i)` at line 54 and `return notFoundError(i, ov, aa)` at line 68 on main), leaving the remaining overrides unapplied while callers treated the partially applied set as final.

## Fix

`ApplyOverrides` now applies every override that matches and returns one `errors.Join` error with an entry per bad override, in config order. `gc order` commands still exit 1 on a bad override and now name every bad entry at once. The `OverrideErrorHandler` doc comment, the orders tutorial, and the CHANGELOG describe the new behavior.

## Tests

- `internal/orders`: `TestApplyOverridesAppliesEveryMatchAfterBadOverride`
- `internal/orderdiscovery`: `TestScanAllOverrideHandlerKeepsOverridesAfterUnmatchedOne`
- `cmd/gc`: `TestControllerStateOrdersHonorsOverridesAfterUnmatchedOne`, `TestControllerStateDisableOrderAfterUnmatchedOverride`, `TestOrderScanContractDispatcherHonorsOverridesAfterUnmatchedOne`, `TestOrderScanContractLoadAllOrdersReportsEveryUnmatchedOverride`

Verified on top of current `main` with `bazel test --config=ci //internal/orders:orders_test //internal/orderdiscovery:orderdiscovery_test //cmd/gc:gc_test //cmd/gc:gc_split_strict_test` — all pass.

## Risk

Low. Valid override sets behave exactly as before. The only behavior change is for configs that contain a bad override: overrides after it now take effect (previously they were silently dropped), and the error message lists every bad entry instead of only the first. Exit codes for `gc order` commands are unchanged.

Refs: ga-hfly3b.20

author: emaspa
body:
Picking a profile in the EQ editor's list now loads it. The Load button is gone.

## What changes

- A pick in the Profile list does what Load did: the band count check with the same message, the bands shown at once with the EQ on, and one `loadEqProfile`. The list's tooltip says so (`EqProfileListTip`, in every language). `EqProfileLoad` and `EqProfileLoadTip` are removed from every language file.
- The list shows the profile the microphone's EQ holds now. A band edit here or from another client, Paste, Reset or the EQ switched off puts it back on "Choose a profile". A load from the deck, a script or another editor chooses the profile it loaded, and so does opening the editor on an EQ that holds one. When several profiles have the same bands, the one picked stays chosen, or else the first in list order. Compare keeps the switch on, so it keeps the choice. Because the list clears after an edit, picking the same profile again loads it again.
- `EqProfilesViewModel` tells a pick from its own choices. The list binds to `Selected`, whose setter loads. The choices the row makes as the list or the EQ changes (refresh, a rename followed, the profile just saved, the held profile) go through a quiet assignment and send nothing.
- The "EQ holds these bands" rule moves from `MicSetupPreset.Holds` into `MicEq.Holds`, which the presets and the profiles share.
- Save starts from the chosen saved profile's name, or else from the saved profile last picked or saved in this editor, so pick, adjust and save offers to replace that profile, behind the existing confirmation. A built-in pick offers no name.
- The manual's Profile row and EQ profiles section describe the new behaviour.

## Decisions

- An EQ that is off holds no profile, so saving with the EQ off leaves the list on its placeholder. Before, the profile just saved was chosen.
- A pick refused for its band count stays shown with the reason until the EQ or the list next changes, as before. It does not clear at once.
- A pick by keyboard on the closed list, or by the wheel over a focused one, is a pick too and loads.

## Tests

- `dotnet build src/OpenXLR.slnx -c Release --no-restore -warnaserror`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `EqProfileTests` reworked around a pick that loads. New cases: a quiet refresh sends nothing; a pick loads exactly once and the same choice again sends nothing; editing a band clears the choice; a load from elsewhere chooses the held profile; picking again after an edit loads again; Save after pick and tweak offers that name; Compare keeps the choice, the switch off clears it.
- `EqProfileTests`, `EqProfileStoreTests`, `EqEditorModelTests`, `MicSetupModelTests`, `LocalizationTests`, `LocalizationRenderingTests`: pass.
- `OPENXLR_TEST_EQ=1 xvfb-run ... EqEditorWindowTests`: passes. It drives the real ComboBox: one command for each pick, none for a refresh, a save, a rename or the state that comes back, a re-pick after a band edit loads again, and the Save dialog offers the picked name. The row with one button fewer still fits at 640, 1040 and 2400 in both sizings and at 640 in every language.

## Hardware

Not tried on the desk. Only Xvfb and unit tests ran.

```

* Place the first keyframe at the initial localization pose; re-initialize from the state estimator after a bad first ICP
* Post-relocalization: start ICP from the re-localized pose; relocalize_from_gnss() resets the state estimator first (#193 <https://github.com/MOLAorg/mola_lidar_odometry/issues/193>)
```

author: xxjsonderuloxx
body:
## Problem

Steam gets the internal library plus a single "second library". Users on Discord keep asking for more:
- an SD library for big games *and* an internal folder outside the Linux runtime (so a runtime repair or reinstall doesn't take the games with it)
- a GameNative / other-launcher folder alongside the SD card
- a USB drive or a `Documents/Steam` folder alongside the card

The only way around this today is the hidden Games-folder path: a Games folder becomes a library only if it already holds installed games, and only while the second library is set to automatic.

## What this PR does

- **Added libraries.** Settings → Library → *More Steam libraries* lists up to 4 folders on top of internal storage and the card library. You can **add** a folder (empty is fine), **rename** it (the name shown in Steam's install dialog and storage manager) and **remove** it. Removing only unregisters the library; its games stay on disk.
- Each library gets a fixed mount, `/mnt/droiddeck-lib/<id>`, so renaming never changes the path Steam has registered. Ids are never reused.
- Libraries are set up the same way as the card library, using `SecondaryLibrary.binds`: prefixes, shader cache, Proton, the runtimes and FEX stay in private storage, and the native `/mnt/media_rw` route is used when it checks out. Each library is skipped for the session if it is not attached, overlaps the card library, or would overflow the PRoot fast path's 256-bind budget.
- When the x86-64 client is present, it gets each library's `x86-64` subfolder, the same way it gets the card's.
- Host side: `Library.steamLibraries` (game list, prefixes, storage report), `AddedGames` guest/host path mapping and `steamLibraryMounts` (downloads page) all include the added libraries. A Games folder that is also an added library is not registered twice.
- Guest side: `droiddeck-steam-library` forgets removed `/mnt/droiddeck-lib/*` entries. Desktop bookmarks, the compat restart check and redist seeding also cover them.

Not in this PR (planned follow-ups): marking a library as the default install location, an uninstall-safe default location for new SD libraries, and moving a whole library folder (which needs re-keying its private prefixes).

## Testing

- New `SteamLibrariesTest` (add/rename/remove, stable ids, overlap and cap refusals, listing, path mapping, Games-folder de-duplication, bad JSON)
- New `droiddeck-steam-library` test: an added library is registered while listed and forgotten once removed, and its files are kept

Seven groups were written with slashes and matched nothing, so their members arrived as separate PRs: clj-otel-api and clj-otel-sdk as #216 and #217, malli as #212, ring-jetty9-adapter as #194, next.jdbc on a branch of its own.

Follow-up to #3. The page still reloaded after the memory fix. Home page images now total ~30 MB, so memory alone no longer explains it.

## What I found
- Sitting idle on the hero (iPhone 13 emulation), the page used ~300% CPU across renderer and GPU. Safari reloads pages that use "significant energy" (Mac), and iOS kills busy background tabs, which shows up as a reload when you come back.
- The ambient Web Audio synth (about 24 oscillators plus a convolution reverb) kept running while the tab was hidden.
- Attribution: pausing the portrait glow's `orbit` animation alone saved ~90% CPU. It animates `--ang` on a conic gradient under a large image mask, inside a double drop-shadow, so the layer repaints on every frame. 44 CSS animations were running, most of them in off-screen sections. A rAF loop set 3 style properties every frame forever.

## Changes
- Suspend the AudioContext on `visibilitychange` (hidden) and resume it when visible, if sound is on.
- Pause CSS animations in off-screen sections (IntersectionObserver plus `.zz-off`): 44 → 14 running at the hero.
- Portrait glow: rotate a pre-drawn conic with `rotate` instead of animating `--ang`. Looks the same, with no repaint.
- Hero outline loop only writes styles when the values change.
- Hidden full-screen backdrop blurs (`.scrim`, `.warp`) get `visibility: hidden` and keep their fade.
- `overscroll-behavior-y: none` on html/body to stop accidental pull-to-refresh.

Hero idle CPU: renderer 220% → 98%, renderer+GPU ~300% → ~190% (headless software rendering, so absolute numbers are inflated; the ratio is what matters). Smoke test: contact modal, project open/close, no page errors.

Same change is in the Toheeb Ledger artifact (v129).

author: huitzidomingo
body:
Tareas: BLOG-004, BLOG-005, BLOG-028 (nueva) y BLOG-003 (parcial: targets `db-*`).

## Qué cambia

- **`docker-compose.yml`:** `mongo:8.0` standalone, publicado solo en `127.0.0.1:27017`, con volumen con nombre y healthcheck.
- **`.env.example`:** `MONGO_URI`, `MONGO_DB_NAME` y credenciales de root con valores de ejemplo.
- **Makefile:** `db-up`, `db-down`, `db-logs` y `db-reset`. `db-down` conserva el volumen; `db-reset` lo borra tras pedir confirmación.
- **Config:** `MONGO_URI` y `MONGO_DB_NAME` son obligatorias.
- **`internal/repository/mongodb`:** conexión con Ping de 5 s al arrancar; si falla, la API no arranca.
- **`GET /ready`:** Ping con timeout de 2 s; responde 200 o 503.
- **Shutdown:** `Disconnect` corre después de `server.Shutdown`, dentro de los mismos 8 s.
- **CLAUDE.md:** comandos `db-*` y regla de transacciones.
- **Roadmap:** añade `BLOG-028` y marca `BLOG-002`, `006` y `007`, mergeadas en #5.

## Decisiones

- **Paquete `mongodb`:** evita chocar con el paquete `mongo` del driver.
- **`make api-run` carga `.env`:** la API solo lee variables del proceso, así que sin esto dejaría de arrancar con `make`. Si falta `.env`, falla con un mensaje claro.
- **`/ready` no devuelve el error:** va a los logs. El cliente solo recibe `{"status":"unavailable"}`, para no exponer detalles de la infraestructura.
- **`BLOG-028`:** ninguna tarea cubría la conexión ni `/ready`; `BLOG-009` sigue siendo los repositorios.

## Dependencias

- **`go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2` v2.9.2:** driver decidido en ADR-006. Ya era dependencia indirecta de Gin en v2.5.0; pasa a directa.

## Modo aprendizaje Go

**¿Por qué `Pinger` se define en `handler` y no en el paquete de Mongo?** En Go las interfaces se satisfacen de forma implícita: un tipo las implementa con solo tener los métodos, sin declararlo. Por eso quien consume la dependencia puede definir exactamente lo que necesita. `handler` solo necesita `Ping(ctx) error`, así que esa es toda la interfaz. Eso tiene tres ventajas: `handler` no importa nada de Mongo, la dependencia apunta hacia adentro como pide ADR-002, y en los tests basta un fake de un método. Si la interfaz viviera en el paquete de Mongo, `handler` tendría que importarlo solo para conocerla. `mongodb.Client` envuelve al driver porque su `Ping` real pide además un `readpref`.

**Liveness (`/health`) vs. readiness (`/ready`).** Liveness pregunta "¿el proceso está vivo?"; si falla, reiniciarlo puede arreglarlo. Readiness pregunta "¿puede atender tráfico ahora?"; si falla, se deja de enviarle peticiones, pero no se reinicia. Si Mongo cae, `/health` sigue en 200 porque reiniciar la API no arregla Mongo, y `/ready` da 503. Por eso `/ready` no debe usarse como sonda de liveness: una caída de la base de datos reiniciaría todas las instancias sin motivo.

**¿Por qué el bind a `127.0.0.1`?** `27017:27017` publica el puerto en `0.0.0.0`, es decir, en todas las interfaces, y cualquiera en tu red (por ejemplo, un Wi-Fi público) podría intentar conectarse a una base con contraseña de desarrollo. Con `127.0.0.1:27017:27017`, solo se llega desde tu máquina. Además, Docker gestiona sus propias reglas de red, así que un firewall local no siempre protege un puerto publicado.

## Verificación

Pasan `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go build`, `go test -race`, golangci-lint v2.15.0 y `govulncheck` (0 vulnerabilidades alcanzables).

Prueba manual con Mongo real en Docker:

| Caso | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `make db-up` | Healthy en 20 s; escucha solo en `127.0.0.1:27017` |
| API con Mongo arriba | `/health` 200, `/ready` 200 |
| Mongo parado | `/ready` 503 en 2,0 s, `/health` 200 |
| Mongo de vuelta | `/ready` vuelve a 200 sin reiniciar la API |
| SIGTERM | Shutdown limpio, código 0 |
| Arrancar con Mongo caído | Código 1 tras 5 s |
| Contraseña incorrecta, URI inválida o variable ausente | Código 1; la contraseña no aparece en la salida |
| `make db-down` | Conserva el volumen |
| `make db-reset` | Cancela sin la confirmación; borra el volumen con ella |
| `make api-run` | Falla con mensaje claro sin `.env`; arranca con `.env` |

body:
## Összefoglaló
A Flyway-migrációk védelme eddig csak szabály volt, most egy PreToolUse hook technikailag is érvényesíti az Edit, Write és MultiEdit eszközökre. A hookok `|| exit 2` biztosítékot kaptak, hogy hibás futásnál se engedjék át a műveletet, és bővült a `.env` fájlok deny listája.

## Változások
- Új `.claude/hooks/protect-migrations.js`, amely tiltja:
  - a `main` vagy `origin/main` ágon már meglévő migráció szerkesztését;
  - a helyben vagy a main ágon foglalt verziószámot;
  - a main legnagyobb verziójánál kisebb számot;
  - az almappába kerülő fájlt és a `V<szám>__Leiras.sql` formától eltérő nevet.
- Minden hibaág 2-es kóddal áll le (fail closed), az útvonalat a hook ellenőrzés előtt normalizálja.
- Új `.claude/hooks/protect-migrations.test.js` (19 eset).
- `.claude/settings.json`: a hook bekötése, valamint a `.env.*.local`, `.env.production` és `.env.local` a deny listán minden mappában.
- `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md`: `|| exit 2` a `readonly-bash.js` hookhoz.
- `.claude/rules/backend.md`: a hook leírása és a megkerülés tiltása.

## Code review
- Végső ítélet: **MEHET** (három kör: JAVÍTANDÓ, JAVÍTANDÓ, MEHET). A második kört követő, utolsó engedélyezett újrafuttatás adta.
- Javítva: verzióütközés lemaradt ágnál, a main alatti szám, nem normalizált útvonal és almappa, `.sql` kiterjesztés, kis- és nagybetű-érzékeny név új fájlnál, futásidőben számolt tesztszámok.
- Javítatlan apróságok:
  - A teszt a szabad számot az `origin/main` nélkül számolja, ezért fetch után hamisan bukhat, ha az `origin/main` előrébb jár.
  - A hook fejléce nem említi, hogy a Bash-ből végzett módosítást nem védi.

## Tesztelés
- `node .claude/hooks/protect-migrations.test.js`: 19 eset, mind sikeres.
- `node .claude/hooks/readonly-bash.test.js`: 84 eset, mind sikeres.
- `mvn test` és `npm run build` nem futott, mert backend- és frontendkód nem változott.
- Kézi próba a korábbi változaton, az éles hookkal: a `V1__Initial_Schema.sql` szerkesztését és a `V8__Hook_Teszt.sql` létrehozását is letiltotta.
- A lemaradt ág esetére (a szám csak a main ágon foglalt) nincs automata teszt, ezt csak a reviewer ellenőrizte kódolvasással.

## Kockázatok / figyelendő
- A hook csak az Edit, Write és MultiEdit eszközökre fut, a Bash-ből végzett módosítást nem fogja meg. Ez ellen a `backend.md` szabálya és az engedélykérés véd.
- Az `|| exit 2` és a fail-closed működés miatt a hook hibája vagy a hiányzó `node` a projektben minden Edit és Write műveletet tilt. A fejlesztés közben ez egyszer meg is történt, a hookot kézzel kellett helyreállítani.
- A hook nem futtat `git fetch`-et, így elavult ref mellett nem látja a GitHubon már mergelt migrációt, és CI sincs, ami ezt megfogná.
- Későbbre:
  - `.env.production` felvétele a `.gitignore`-ba, mert most commitolható lenne.
  - A deny lista felsorolásos: a `.env.staging`, `.env.prod`, `.env.development` és `.env.test` olvasható marad.
  - A `backend.md` nem említi a `node` előfeltételt, a `git fetch`-et és a hook összes tiltását.

author: cashew-nut
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"cashew-nut"} -->
_Requested by **Luke** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018hkSdio51UveZAMk7tRYWs?thread=cmsg_018hkSdio51UveZAMk7tRYWsEAdyCqHsN7cTCdpajt2Pun)_

## What this does

The Paladin treatment (PR #44) for the Ashen Foundries Brute: Luke's Meshy Brute (6.24M triangles, one closed surface) is cut into 10 closed solids that plug together with keyed D-pegs and magnet pockets, then assembled joint to joint in Blender. The scripts run with `MODEL=brute` (settings and the reasons behind them in `assets/blender/parts/composite/brute.py`). The Paladin is still the default and runs unchanged. No Meshy credits were spent, and everything ran in the cloud container.

## Changes from the Meshy model, and why

- **Print scale 1.5x.** Following Luke's answer, the Brute is cut at 2.1x the bulwark kit (the web already grows bulwark parts by 1.4), which puts it about 75 mm to the helm top. Pegs are up to 8 mm across. Magnet pockets take stock 5×2, 3×2 or 2×1 mm discs. Game GLBs are scaled back to kit size, with origins on the `foundries/bulwark` joints.
- **Symmetric limbs.** Each sided part is cut from the walker's left and mirrored, so one pauldron and one leg fit either side. Labels use |x|, so the torso and pelvis are carved where the mirrored parts will sit. Any overlap left over is trimmed off the centre parts. The torso, helm and stacks keep Meshy's asymmetric detail. The "07" plate crosses the centre line, so mirroring half the torso would have broken it.
- **Gun forearms.** The Brute has no hands. Each gun is a whole forearm on an elbow socket. The 3 mm upper-arm stub under the pauldron is too small to print, so it is now part of the pauldron. That replaces three thin joints with one.
- **One shared socket.** Meshy's gatling (raised on the right arm) is mirrored, turned onto the cannon's barrel axis (10°), moved onto its breech, trimmed where it would hit the pauldron, and given the cannon's exact peg plus a collar. Either gun fits either elbow (`swap.png`).
- **Pegs tried both ways.** `joints.py` can now put the peg on either part and keeps the one that holds better. This moved the hip from a 3 mm peg with a 2×1 magnet to a 4.6 mm peg with a 3×2.

| Joint | Peg | Magnet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| torso → pelvis | 8 mm, on pelvis | 5×2 |
| back → torso | 8 mm | 5×2 |
| pauldron → torso | 5.2 mm | 3×2 |
| thigh → pelvis | 4.6 mm, on pelvis | 3×2 |
| shin → thigh | 6 mm, 1.8 long | 2×1 |
| foot → shin | 3 mm, 1.5 long | 2×1 |
| helm → torso | 2.6 mm | 2×1 |
| cannon / gatling → pauldron (elbow) | 3 mm, 3.5 long | 2×1 |

## Verified

- All 10 print STLs are closed and in one piece (manifold3d), with sizes and volumes in `report.json`.
- Assembled with the right side mirrored and the gatling on the right arm, no two parts overlap (boolean check, 0 mm³ after trimming).
- Renders of the parts sheet, assembled, exploded, gun swap and pose come from the assembled `.blend`, so the joint hierarchy works.
- Paladin defaults are unchanged (import check of layout, split and joints without `MODEL`). The Paladin pipeline was not re-run.

## Not verified / known limits

- Not test-printed. Luke has no printer yet. Thin antennae and overhangs have not been checked for printability.
- The elbow is the weakest load joint (3 mm peg, 2×1 magnet, carrying a 1.1 cm³ gun). A designed elbow boss would be the next structural step.
- The gatling has a flat gunmetal face down its back where it touched the hip armour in Meshy's pose. It shows when the arm is raised.
- Game integration is not done. The game still loads the open-shell Brute parts. Publishing needs a decision: the Brute now has no `arm`/`hand` parts, and its guns are whole forearms.
- Outputs are not in the repo: `/mnt/project-files/models/brute-composite/` (blend, glb, stl, report.json) and `/mnt/project-files/renders/brute-composite/`.

_Requested by **Mark Phillips** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011xxRP8VFN19WGhaksXcs4W?thread=cmsg_011xxRP8VFN19WGhaksXcs4WBiyZ5HmNan44kgopYyZfkd)_

## Summary

Third PR for Medicaid reimbursement methods. It is independent of #1718 and #1723 and is based on main.

It adds the state payment formulas that turn an APR-DRG and severity (`139-3`) into an allowed amount, in `FeeScheduleEngine/Medicaid`:

- **`TexasMedicaidDrgPricer`**, following 1 TAC §355.8052(i):
  - payment is the final SDA × relative weight;
  - a transferring hospital is paid a per diem × the lesser of MLOS and allowed days, capped at 30 days for patients 21 or older;
  - for clients under 21, both the day outlier and the cost outlier are computed and the higher one is paid. Urban and rural hospitals get 90% of it and children's hospitals get 100%.
- **`MediCalDrgPricer`**, following State Plan 4.19-A:
  - the base price is wage-adjusted by labor share, except for transitional base prices;
  - policy adjustors depend on care category, SOI and NICU designation, plus age adjustors;
  - acute transfers use the Medicare formula (per diem × (days + 1), capped), with status 65 added;
  - the cost outlier is tiered and uses the CCR;
  - an optional low-side outlier is available;
  - payment is capped at charges.

Both are pure functions with every state number supplied as data. When an input is missing they return the stay unpriced with a reason, never $0. Each result includes its arithmetic step by step, for examiners and appeals.

Not yet wired into `PricingStage`. The next PR adds importers for the state weight tables and hospital files, and wires these in.

## Type

Feature (pure engine code, no behavior change)

## Validation

`dotnet test tests/CloudHealthOffice.FeeScheduleEngine.Tests --filter DrgPricerTests`: 27 passed. Each case was worked by hand from the rule. One of them is the DHCS design document's own example (194-1: 0.4968 × $7,200 = $3,577).

## Evidence And Limitations

The open points to verify are listed in `docs/integration/MEDICAID-DRG-PRICING.md`:

- **Texas transfer statuses.** The rule doesn't enumerate them, so the code defaults to Medicare's acute list.
- **Texas downgraded-DRG outlier.** The rule for downgraded DRGs is not implemented yet.
- **Medi-Cal marginal cost percentage.** It is required as configuration, with no hard-coded 60%.
- **Medi-Cal interim claims, administrative days and rehab per diems.** These are separate methods and out of scope.

MCO contracts may also pay something other than the FFS formula.

## Security And Privacy

None. The code does no I/O and handles no PHI.

## Docs

`docs/integration/MEDICAID-DRG-PRICING.md` covers the formulas, inputs, SFY 2026-27 Medi-Cal values and sources.

body:
A disk swap on .101 or .103 would have left the new disk with no default route, the same way .102 failed its image pulls on 2026-11-01. Their route came from `META` key `0x0a` on disk, so their machine configs looked complete.

This PR only records the change. **The live changes are already applied, by hand and outside GitOps, so merging changes nothing in the cluster.**

## Applied to .101 and .103

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| default route | `dhcp4` operator from `META` | `0.0.0.0/0` via `10.0.0.1`, `configuration` layer |
| nameservers | `1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8` from DHCP | `10.0.0.1, 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8` |
| `install.image` | `ghcr.io/siderolabs/installer:v1.11.3` | `metal-installer` schematic `c9078f94…`, v1.13.12 |
| `install.disk` | `by-label/TALOS_INSTALL` | `diskSelector.busPath` for the SATA port |

Applied with a streamed `talosctl apply-config --mode=auto`, .103 then .101. Neither node rebooted, etcd stayed on three voters at term 1799, and all upstreams report healthy. `regen-served-configs.sh 1.13.12` then rebuilt the served files, which carry the route. Matchbox is still stopped.

## What to look at

**The router is a new DNS upstream on these two nodes.** The handoff assumed `META`'s list was already in effect, but it sits at the `platform` layer and DHCP overrode it. Adding `10.0.0.1` was a deliberate choice to match .102, and it reverses the reason `dns.yaml` was withdrawn in August. All 23 HTTPRoute hostnames answer the same from all three resolvers today; that stops being true if the router's records drift from Cloudflare's. So this PR also corrects `known-issues.md`, `commands.md`, `upgrades.md` and the `dns.yaml` header. `dns.yaml` itself stays withdrawn.

## Not proven

- The `busPath` selector only runs at install time, and nothing has installed from it. The path matches `get disks` on all three nodes.
- Whether the host-DNS proxy spreads queries across upstreams or prefers the first was not tested.

## Left alone

- .102's live config is unchanged: `install.image` names v1.11.6 and its selector is `model: 'PNY*'`. The runbook says to change the selector before replacing that disk.
- `META` `0x0a` stays on .101 and .103. The config layer overrides it.

`/okf:validate docs/okf`: conformant, no new warnings. `--strict` still exits 1 on the existing cross-link warnings.

author: zeroliu
body:
Relates to Brevilabs/obsidian-copilot-private#813
Relates to Brevilabs/obsidian-copilot-private#819

## Why

Copilot Navigator ships as a preview for Supporters. Before this PR anyone with Agent Mode can open it, so it reaches people it is not offered to, and those without access get no explanation of what it is or how to get it.

Preview access comes from the signed entitlement token, which Copilot verifies after Obsidian starts. Until that check finishes, a Supporter whose Navigator was open must not see a "no access" notice flash or the chat tabs flicker back.

## What

| Situation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| License with preview access | Navigator opens | Unchanged |
| Copilot Plus license without preview, or no license | Navigator opens | The icon and the **Open Copilot Navigator** command open a dialog |
| Dialog | None | "Copilot Navigator is a preview for Supporters", a short description and GIF, **See plans** (pricing with `utm_medium=navigator_dialog`), and **Already a Supporter? Enter your license key**, which closes the dialog and opens Copilot settings on the license field. The GIF is capped at 40% of the window height, so both buttons show without scrolling in a short window (1024x689) |
| Navigator panel without preview access | Navigator list | "Your preview access ended" / "Copilot Navigator is a preview for Supporters. Your chats are still under Recent chats in Agent Chat.", **See plans** (`navigator_blocked_view`), **Close** (closes the panel), and the license-key action. The chat tabs stay visible beside it |
| Preview becomes active after the dialog or that panel was shown this session | n/a | Navigator opens once |
| Obsidian starts with the Navigator open, before the stored token is verified | Navigator list | Navigator list and hidden tabs stay; the notice appears only if verification finds no preview |

- The command stays listed for everyone, so a search for "Navigator" or a bound hotkey always reaches the Navigator or the dialog.
- The dialog GIF is hosted on `images.brevilabs.com`.

## Non goal

- A trial, new analytics, or new UTM mediums.
- Changing what Supporters see inside the Navigator.
- Navigator cards in the tab overflow menu or on the Agent Chat home page.
- A preview marker on the tab-strip icon or the command; every upsell surface already names Supporters.
- Changing which plans carry the preview entitlement.

## Screenshot

Free user: the command is listed in the palette.

![free-command-palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e234097c-ad17-460f-8cc5-826e7c2d7528)

Free user: running the command opens the preview dialog. In a 1024x689 window the whole dialog fits, buttons included, without scrolling.

![free-dialog-from-command](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be261a0a-d44d-4a34-8a36-b494c32d280d)

Free user: the Navigator icon opens the same dialog, with the license-key action and **See plans**.

![free-dialog-from-icon](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04731363-cb0d-4057-8435-8112f5437266)

A Navigator panel without preview access, beside the chat tabs.

![free-blocked-notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43551d09-0b53-46c9-a287-49da5f472025)

After applying a license key with preview access from the dialog, the Navigator opens (behind the license welcome dialog).

![supporter-license-applied-navigator-opens](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52d067ec-66fe-4117-aa2e-4a6b4c664eed)

The Navigator after restarting the vault window with it open.

![supporter-navigator-after-restart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1859f2e7-780c-4d5b-8ab9-4730dd6d69d7)

## Risk

**High**

| Criterion | Status | Reason |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| No behavior change, or a cosmetic/copy/docs/config change visible where it renders, or deterministic tests cover the changed behavior | ✅ | Tests drive the real verify and apply-license paths for preview, Plus-without-preview, free and still-verifying users: the gate, the dialog, the panel, the tab strip, open-once after activation, and startup without a notice flash or tab flicker |
| A defect would fail CI or be obvious on first use | ❌ | jsdom cannot show the dialog closing before Copilot settings opens, or the dialog's height in a short window; both were checked only in a real vault |
| A revert fully restores prior state, including persisted data | ✅ | Nothing new is persisted; the "prompt shown" state lives only for the session |
| No auth, permissions, secrets, or input-handling surface changes | ❌ | The Navigator gains an entitlement gate on the signed preview feature, and the preview check gains an "unknown" state: a stored token that has not been verified this session counts as allowed until verification runs |
| No public API, plugin API, message, or on-disk contract changes | ✅ | Command id and name are unchanged; no settings field added |
| No core-path concurrency, async-lifecycle, or state-machine changes | ❌ | The gate now depends on the order of startup token verification and the Navigator's first render, and on license activation signalling preview before settings are saved |
| No hot-path behavior lacks deterministic coverage | ✅ | Every new branch has unit tests |
| No new dependency | ✅ | Dependency manifests are unchanged |
| Human-only behavior stays in one feature area and surfaces quickly | ✅ | Limited to the Navigator dialog, panel and tab strip |

Review: inspect `isPreviewEnabled`, `subscribeToPreviewAccess` and `useIsPreviewEnabled` in `src/plusUtils.ts`, `openNavigatorWhenPreviewActivates` and `openSessionsSidebar` in `src/agentMode/navigator/openSessionsSidebar.ts`, `PreviewSessionsSidebar` in `src/agentMode/navigator/ui/SessionsSidebarView.tsx`, and `useSessionsSidebarOpen` in `src/agentMode/navigator/hooks/useSessionsSidebarOpen.ts` line by line, then run Verification steps 2-6.

## Verification

1. In a vault without a license key, enable Agent Mode and open Agent Chat.
2. Make the Obsidian window short (about 1024x690). Open the command palette, type "Navigator", and run **Open Copilot Navigator**. A dialog titled "Copilot Navigator is a preview for Supporters" opens with **Already a Supporter? Enter your license key** and **See plans** visible without scrolling. Close it and select the Navigator icon at the left end of the tabs; the same dialog opens.
3. Select **Already a Supporter? Enter your license key**. The dialog closes and Copilot settings opens with the license key field. Paste a key with preview access and select **Apply**. Copilot Navigator opens in the left sidebar and the chat tabs hide.
4. With the Navigator open, restart Obsidian. The Navigator comes back with your chats; "Your preview access ended" never appears and the chat tabs stay hidden.
5. Replace the key with a Copilot Plus key that has no preview access, or remove it. The command and the icon open the dialog.
6. Still without preview access, open a Navigator panel (for example from a workspace saved while you had access). It reads "Your preview access ended"; **See plans** opens pricing, **Close** removes the panel, and the chat tabs stay visible beside it.

author: siy
body:
Closes #2553

## What changes
Since #2545 a node dedupes its DHT replication report against what it filed, not against the store. The leader drops the report of a member it holds `Dead` (`liveReports`); a live process that rejoins went on believing it had filed, so the open change stayed `APPLYING` for ever.

In `DhtReplicationSettlement`, a node now treats its report as filed only while its own store holds it:
- a core reads its KV; a worker reads its replica store (`ReplicaFilter` includes report keys), and only while the replica is ready (`isPassiveClientReady`), so a half-installed snapshot never reads as "dropped";
- it re-files only while a change is open (with none open an absent report costs nothing: a change opened later is filed anyway because its version exceeds what the node filed);
- re-files are damped: no sooner than 1 s after the last filing, then 2, 4, ... up to 60 s; the interval resets only when the report is SEEN present once the interval has passed (`now >= due`): a sighting inside the interval, such as the node's own fresh re-file glimpsed before the leader's drop, does not reset it, so a member held `Dead` that keeps committing stays at about two commits a minute. A not-ready replica is no sighting, and the re-file decision is atomic (concurrent `report()` calls cannot file twice). **1 s and 60 s are guesses**, not measurements: 1 s is far above the 100 ms retry tick, 60 s bounds a node the leader keeps dropping to two commits a minute;
- re-files are counted (`refileCount()`), so a trickle is observable;
- the stale "a worker never sees report keys" javadoc is corrected.

Wiring: one new `Inputs` component (`replicaReady`), passed from `DhtAssembly` as `clusterNode::isPassiveClientReady`. That is the only line outside `DhtReplicationSettlement.java` in `src/main`.

## Evidence
Red first (cloudbb-d1, behaviour neutralised so the new API compiles): `DhtReplicationReportLifecycleTest` 4 of the new tests red (rejoin re-file, worker with a ready replica, churn bound, backoff reset), the two controls (not-ready worker, no open change) green. Ember `workerReportDropped_sameLiveProcessRejoins_refilesAndChangeSettles` red at "the worker files it again" after both instrument checks passed.

Green at `0e497fe775`: `DhtReplicationReportLifecycleTest` 12; `DhtReplication*Test` + `AetherNodeDhtReplicationTest` + Ember `EmberWorkerDhtReplicationTest` (2); full `aether/node` suite 4522 `<testcase>` (= `tests=`), 0 failures, 11 skipped. jbct: `aether/node` 242 files, `aether/ember` 6 files, passed.

Ember test: the worker's own store holds its report key before the drop and loses it after (so the replica feed carries report keys and removes), then it re-files and the change settles. A second worker, silenced before the change, holds the change open. The drop is injected as the exact commit the leader makes (a `Remove` of the key) instead of waiting for a `Dead` verdict, which would also let the change settle without the worker.

Mutation (bb-mutate, pushed SHA, 33-testcase control): 18 mutants on the changed lines (one pattern was first rejected as invalid and re-run), 17 RED, 1 survivor (below). The churn test pins the exact gaps (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60, 60 s), so the damping, the doubling, the cap and the arming each go red. The Ember pair: `() -> false` for the readiness wiring RED, `() -> true` the survivor.

## Verifier round (v2556, FIX -> revised patch applied)
B1 (the reset on any sighting let a Dead-held member churn at about 1 re-file a second), N1 (a not-ready replica counted as a sighting) and N2 (a check-then-act re-file decision) are fixed by the verifier's revised patch (sha256 `0d0da1f8d73500e1...`), applied as-is, with its pins (the glimpse pin and a 4-contender spin-barrier pin for N2). The readiness-wiring pin is `DhtSettlementReadinessWiringTest` (mine, kept: `() -> true`, `() -> false` and a wrong-flag variant all go red). I first applied the earlier patch version and swapped the tests; a follow-up commit restores the tree: it now equals `3c006a1499` + the revised patch + the rc5 merge (checked by diffing against a fresh apply and merge: 0 lines).

## Author pre-check (internal/author-precheck.md), head `13f8413c77`
1. **Mutation at a pushed SHA:** my 20 mutants were all RED at `3c006a1499`; the verifier re-ran the changed lines on the patched tree (see its report). Survivors: none known.
2. **No hangs:** the lifecycle tests are synchronous (the spin-barrier pin has its own deadline); the Ember test carries `@Timeout`.
3. **Wiring pinned:** `DhtSettlementReadinessWiringTest` reddens `() -> true`, `() -> false` and a wrong-flag variant for the readiness input.
4. **Claims tested:** the churn bound is the exact gap assertions (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60, 60 s) plus the B1 glimpse pin; "no re-file with no open change" is `absentReport_noOpenChange_doesNotRefile`; the replica feed carrying report keys and removes is the Ember instrument checks.
5. **CI bookkeeping:** no new Ember or consensus test class (no shard weight); changelog fragment `0-2553-dht-report-refile.md`; `tools/test_ember_shard.py` and `test_consensus_shard.py` OK; pre-push gate PASS (jbct `aether/node` 244 files, `aether/ember` 6).
6. **Flakes:** none seen. On the merged head (cloudbb-d1): full `aether/node` suite 4563 `<testcase>`, 0 failures, 11 skipped; lifecycle 16, `DhtReplication*` + `AetherNodeDhtReplicationTest` + wiring test, 58 in the targeted run (before the rc5 merge); `EmberWorkerDhtReplicationTest` 2, 0 failures.
7. **rc5 merge:** `origin/release-1.0.0-rc5` (`19aa282f20`) merged once into `fbdc36d8ec` (base + patch); merge commit `fd7fb7680d`, then the follow-up commit `13f8413c77` (test file swap only); no conflicts, no hand-resolved files.

## Residual
The Ember test injects the drop (a `Remove` of the report key) and does not reach `liveReports` -> `dropReport`; each link has its own unit test (the leader's drop, the replica carrying the remove, the re-file). A `Dead` verdict would also let the change settle without the worker, so it cannot be the trigger in an end-to-end test.

body:
## Summary

Owner requests (2026-11-01), client-only in `v2/card-game`; no rules, pack or bundle change.

**1. The brown status box is gone.** `#notice` (the translucent pill fixed over the stage, `shared.css`) carried:
- progress lines for a pending play ("Vale is travelling…", "is waiting…") for local queued plays and shared sent/playing plays, plus a 2.5 s "Played: X.";
- every failure: shared refusals ("Not played: X. reason"), unconfirmed sends and lost connections, unsaved-world and storage-blocked warnings, "updated in another tab", stale-play refusals, nudges, and shared-controls errors.

The element, its CSS (`.notice`, `#notice`), `showQueuedPlay`, the `sharedPlayText` progress/played lines, the played timer and `playProgressLine` are removed. A pending play already reads on its own button ("Travelling…", `data-sent`), so the progress lines go without a replacement. Failures are the only signal for refused or unconfirmed plays and unsaved worlds, so they now read as plain words on the action bar's status line (`#play-status`) inside the existing action panel above the hand, the spot the README reserved for it (#1725). Nothing sits over the stage.

**2. Long names under the card to their left.** #1813 reserved the next card's overlap on a name's right. A chosen or open (raised) card has a higher z-index, so it covers the *left* of the card after it. With a place's stack open, the first road shows "oad to Theban / Courtyard". The card after a raised or chosen card now moves out from under it: the raised card gets `margin-right: var(--fan-overlap)` when a visible card follows it. That keeps the name's full width, where reserving left padding would squeeze it to a few characters on phones.

`smoke-card-hand-frame` now hit-tests both ends of every line of every name with `elementFromPoint`, so it catches covers from either side. It runs again with "Road to Theban Courtyard" on every card. Without the CSS fix it fails at 390 px (`lamp name under vale`).

## Tests

author: donseba
body:
htmx 2 stays the default. `app.SetVersion(htmx.Version4)` makes handlers read and write the headers the way htmx 4 does. Every change is an addition, so this can be a minor release (v1.14.0).

## htmx 4 mode

- `RenderPartial()` is also false for `HX-Request-Type: full`, which htmx 4 sends for body swaps, `hx-select` and history restoration.
- `TargetID()` and `SourceID()` decode the `tagName#id` of `HX-Target` and `HX-Source`. With htmx 2 they return `HX-Target` and `HX-Trigger`.
- `Prompt()` decodes the URI-encoded answer of the `hx-prompt` extension.
- `ReSwapWithObject` writes the htmx 4 swap syntax: `show:top showTarget:"#list"`, `focusScroll`, and durations htmx 4 parses.
- `TriggerAfterSwap*` and `TriggerAfterSettle*` set nothing: htmx 4 removed both headers, and it triggers the events of `HX-Trigger` after the swap and settle.
- `StopPolling()` still sends 286, which htmx 4 swaps like a 200; the README shows how to stop polling with htmx 4.

## Additions for both versions

- `HxRequestHeader.HxRequestType` and `HxRequestHeader.HxSource`, `Swap.StringFor(version)`, and the htmx 4 swap styles `SwapInnerMorph`, `SwapOuterMorph`, `SwapOuterSync` and `SwapTextContent`.
- SSE: data of several lines is sent as one `data:` field per line, so it arrives whole. A message of one line is written as before.
- The linter warnings are fixed: golangci-lint reports 0 issues.

## Docs and examples

- The README has an htmx 4 section.
- The examples that load htmx use htmx 4.0.0 with `SetVersion(htmx.Version4)`. The SSE examples use `hx-sse:connect`.
- A `go.work` in `examples` builds the examples against the go-htmx code in the repository, so they need no `replace`. A copy made with `gonew` does not take it along; the example READMEs run `go get github.com/donseba/go-htmx@latest` for the newest release.

## Tests

- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...` and golangci-lint pass.
- Checked in a browser against htmx 4.0.0: the five examples, that 286 no longer stops polling while replacing the polling element does, and that `TargetID`, `SourceID` and `Prompt` decode what htmx 4 sends.

author: hackatoan
body:
🚨 Severity: LOW
💡 Vulnerability: The Content-Security-Policy in `firebase.json` allow-lists several third-party origins for script/frame/img/connect that nothing under `public/` actually loads from: `pagead2.googlesyndication.com` (AdSense — this site's cookie-notice.js runs in `data-mode="essential"`, ads are off), `static.cloudflareinsights.com` + `cloudflareinsights.com` (Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon, never embedded), `cdn.jsdelivr.net` (no script references it), `api.qrserver.com` (the QR code is a pre-generated static file at `/assets/qr-site.png`, not fetched live), and `player.twitch.tv` (Twitch only appears as a plain outbound `<a>` link, never an embedded iframe).
🎯 Impact: Trusting origins the site never actually uses is unnecessary attack surface — if any of those unrelated third-party domains/services were ever compromised or repurposed, the CSP would still let them execute script / render frames / receive connections in this site's origin for no functional benefit. Mirrors the earlier `alexgama11.github.io` CSP cleanup (#162).
🔧 Fix: Removed the 5 unused origins from the relevant CSP directives in `firebase.json`. Kept `cdnjs.cloudflare.com` (confirmed in use — `html2pdf.bundle.min.js` dynamically references it for a `pdfobject` fallback), `www.youtube.com` / `s.ytimg.com` (YouTube iframe embeds on the songs/index pages), and `www.buymeacoffee.com` (support link).
✅ Verification:
- `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('firebase.json'))"` — still valid JSON
- `npm test` — 18/18 passing
- `npx eslint "public/**/*.js" "*.js" "scripts/*.js"` — same 5 pre-existing errors as on `Main`, unrelated to this change
- Repo-wide `grep` across all HTML/JS confirms none of the 5 removed domains are referenced anywhere under `public/`

author: yashvvvv
body:
## Problem
`RateLimitingFilter` stopped limiting new clients once it tracked 10,000 addresses, until entries aged out two minutes later. In a local load test the map filled in about 6 seconds; after that, one address sent 1,000 requests to `/api/v1/published-events` and none were refused.

## Fix
The map is now least-recently-used, capped at the same 10,000. A full map evicts the longest-idle client, which only hands that client a fresh quota. A client that keeps sending is never the eldest entry, so flooding new addresses can't reset its quota. One lock guards the map, which also removes a race where two threads could reset the same expired window.

## Verification
| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `aFullMapStillLimitsANewClient` | fails (61st request 200) | passes (429) |
| `floodingNewAddressesCannotResetAnActiveClient` | passes | passes |
| Full backend suite | | 184 tests, 0 failures |
| Live replay: 21k addresses, then a new one sends 1,000 | 1,000 through | 60 through, 940 refused |
| 100 concurrent clients on the event list | ~2,200 req/s, p95 75 ms | ~2,400 req/s, p95 70 ms |

## Not covered
The limiter keys on `CF-Connecting-IP`. That's only trustworthy if the origin accepts traffic from Cloudflare alone; otherwise one machine can still present thousands of addresses.

body:
> **Depends on #508.** This branch is built on it, so its first commit (`00e55dce`) is #508's. Please merge #508 first; the changes in this PR are the four commits after it.

## Summary
With #508 Shield Charge became usable, but its charge was broken: it moved at walk speed, never ended (the player kept running in place and no other skill worked until a manual move), and hit once around the starting cell. Traced with Frida on the 3.29.3b client; documented in 11-skills.md §10k.

- **The charge ends** (`fix:`). On arrival the client's charge action starts an end-of-charge attack that swings the shield, and only that attack's completion starts the end phase. It read `off_hand_total_base_weapon_attack_duration_ms` 0, since off-hand attack stats were only sent for off-hand weapons. A shield skill with a shield in the off hand now carries the gem's own GrantedEffectsPerLevel `AttackTime` (Shield Charge 500 ms; `SkillCatalog.AttackTimeMs`, `RequiresShield`).
- **Charge speed** (`feat:`). The client moves a charge at the player's own `movement_velocity_+%` (`0x141e7c0b0`, the player's Stats, not the skill's); the game adds the gem's +90% through the invisible buff `shield_charge_movement_speed_while_charging`. Network stats run no calculators, so while a charge runs the server adds the bonus to the pools' movement speed and sends it, walks its own estimate to the target at that speed instead of the generic movement skill's teleport, and removes the bonus when the walk arrives (`ShieldCharge.cs`).
- **Hits along the path and at the end** (`feat:`). The client hits within 8 cells about every 100 ms along the way and within 16 cells on arrival. The server lands the same hits on its walk (each monster at most one path hit per charge); the generic hit, which fell back to the starting cell, skips Shield Charge. `AreaSkillHit` gains an optional radius and an "only once" set.
- Four read-only Frida traces in `scripts/re/frida/` (action state, stats read inside one function, which stat set answers a read, a moving attack's hits); docs, status, address index and a roadmap item for the remaining damage work.

## Testing
- Live with the 3.29.3b client: the charge stops and plays its end effect; `movement_velocity_+%` goes 22 → 112 → 22 and the charge runs about twice as fast; path and arrival hits land (a monster hit on the way was hit again on arrival).
- Base `main` `dfcdc8f3`, head `bb1b6302`: the solution builds with 0 warnings; Core 436, Data 45 and Gateway 55 tests pass (new: `ShieldChargeCatalogTests`).

## Not in this PR
- The charge's damage is still the ordinary weapon hit: the gem's shield damage and `shield_charge_damage_+%_maximum` by distance are a roadmap item.
- Footstep triggers (Abberath's Fury) should now fire during a charge, since it walks; not checked live.

AlarMe 1.6.3 could stall after child IPC EOF during normal Decky shutdown. Managed installs now deliver the existing child-only EOF adapter atomically, record `alarme-ipc-eof`, and refuse installation if that adapter is missing. The native probe disconnects a real child peer and requires the unload callback, zero child exit status and no forced kill.

This repair stays above #496, which owns the separate paused-timer restart fix. Current publication `a65f439a9cb4e99e40fad747faa97f8babae118c` normally integrates main `1c2e48c89f031ae70136106c1de3ba556a4c6c74`; its tested implementation is `4b936a59dd8681c5c7cdfc2cda7e582f77befcce`. Merge into #496 only after exact-head qualification, then qualify that combined parent before main.

Exact cached store **124 / AlarMe 1.6.3** ZIP: `17d4166a9e98979df5fdb07c7eae42317acd54a453d3b82757508f971193c0fe`. No fresh live-store claim. Compatibility stays **partial**; existing copies require Update/reinstall.

## Verification

- Source audit retains all **40 main native cases**, adds AlarMe as case 41, and preserves all **116 pins/flags/policies/ratings** and the other **115 catalog rows**. Installer/APPLY, checker, e2e and store-test ASTs outside AlarMe match main. Download All and LocalSend EOF repairs and negative controls are preserved. The shared IPC adapter, strict primary gate, AlarMe probe and original ZIP retain their bytes. Generated docs and diff checks pass.

- Published Decky **3.3.0 native AMD64**: **39 managed / 38 original RPCs**, all 77 responses independently match. Exact backend reconstruction, private silent events and original paused/elapsed-deadline failures are checked. Two strict parent-only managed stops take **0.225s / 0.215s**, including real child peer EOF before the first stop; no forced kill, shutdown error or surviving exact descendant. All **43 source fingerprints** bind the combined implementation. Known JSON diagnostics remain; cleanup claims are scoped.

## Was drin ist

Drei Texte der feministischen Wissenschaftstheorie, zusammen ausgewertet nach dem Muster von `extern/` (je `quelle.md` ohne Volltext, weil urheberrechtlich geschützt, und `auswertung.md`):

- **Longino (1993), Subjects, Power, and Knowledge:** Objektivität als Leistung der Gemeinschaft, vier Kriterien, Pluralismus der Modelle. Gegenstellen GS 4-13 (Kritik, Abschnitt 5), GS 3-09 (Habermas), GS 4-94 (Popper), GS 3-01 (Gene).
- **Intemann (2010), 25 Years of Feminist Empiricism and Standpoint Theory:** Werte in der Wissenschaft, das »bias paradox«, Vielfalt der Werte gegen Vielfalt der Lagen. Gegenstellen GS 4-13 (Betroffenheit), GS 2-05 (Armutsbericht), GS 4-15 (Gerechtigkeit), GS 2-01 (Pharma und Aids).
- **Wylie (2012), Standpoint Matters:** Erkenntnisvorteil der Unterdrückten, Entdeckung neuer Tatsachen, Archäologie. Gegenstellen GS 3-25 (falsches Bewusstsein, Marx-Lesart), GS 4-19 (Frau im Kapitalismus).

Kernbefunde: Der GSP löst das Paradox der Parteilichkeit besser (das Interesse ist Anlass und Maßstab, nicht Prämisse; verdorben wird das Urteil vom Willen zur Anpassung). Er hat aber keine Theorie der Entdeckung, keinen Mechanismus, durch den die Konkurrenz im Fach den Inhalt der Naturwissenschaften bestimmt, und eine negative Standpunktthese (Sorgestandpunkt), die er nicht ausführt. Vorschlag: neuer Angriffspunkt 32 „Welches Interesse verdirbt das Urteil?“ (in der Intemann-Auswertung, Abschnitt 4).

author: yarden-zamir
body:
Follow-up to the CodeRabbit review of [#452](https://github.com/Yarden-zamir/t3code/pull/452) "feat(fork): one worktree lifecycle model with branch cleanup".

## Finding 1: race between branch cleanup and worktree work (partly valid)

- **Not valid as written.** Cleanup cannot delete a new commit. A commit needs the branch in a worktree, and `git branch -D` refuses a branch that a worktree uses. The checkout lease that commits take is keyed per checkout, not per repository. It would not order cleanup against commits in other worktrees.
- **Valid part.** A worktree creation with a new branch runs `git branch` and then `git worktree add`. Between these steps, a cleanup with an old thread row for the same branch name sees a spare branch and deletes it. The creation then fails. This happens, for example, when "Recreate on a new branch" or a new thread reuses the branch name of a deleted thread.
- **Change.** A new repository lease, keyed by the real path of the Git common folder (`withRepositoryLease` in `workspaceLease.ts`):
  - Worktree creation holds it shared from the branch creation to the end of `git worktree add`. The lease is in `GitVcsDriverCore.createWorktree`, so `GitManager` paths that skip `GitWorkflowService` are covered too.
  - Cleanup holds it exclusive for the inspection, the tip check and `git branch -D`. Each branch group now inspects again under the lease, so the sweep no longer caches an old inspection. The folder leases, the checked-out guard and all eligibility rules stay.
  - Parallel worktree creations still run together. Only cleanup waits.
- **Cost.** The common folder read moves before the creation, and the cache invalidation reuses it. Creation still spawns one `--git-common-dir`.

## Finding 2: settings search (valid)

"Artifact eviction inactivity days" found nothing. The row now has the terms "eviction" and "inactivity". Title and route stay. No search test covers this row, so I added none.

## Tests

- New in `ForkWorktreeBranches.test.ts`: at `git worktree add`, a cleanup that asks for the lease first must wait, and a second creation must share it. This test fails when the creation lease is removed.
- `GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts` "invalidates cached metadata after interrupted worktree creation" now interrupts at the end of `git worktree add`. The common folder read that it held now runs before the creation.
- `check:changed`: format, lint, knip and typecheck pass. One test fails here and also fails on `main` on this Mac: "keeps generated worktree folders short" (`/var` against `/private/var`).

## Not tested

- No end-to-end test runs the real sweep against a real creation. A test can only prove that the sweep waits by waiting on a timer, and the test rules do not allow timers.
- Git commands from a terminal or an agent shell take no lease. `git branch -D` still refuses a branch that a worktree uses, and the tip check stays.

author: nranderson
body:
## Problem

Downstream consumers of `lodge104-keys` (specifically `lodge104-memberdata`
in [members.lodgemaster.lambda.lodge104.net](https://github.com/Lodge104/members.lodgemaster.lambda.lodge104.net))
were hitting an infinite redirect loop to
`id.oa-scouting.org/connect/authorize` (`MaxRetryError: too many
redirects`) even after forwarding *every* cookie this function writes to
`lodge104-keys`.

## Root cause

`collectCookies()` only queries `page.cookies()` for the hosts in
`COOKIE_URLS`:

```js
const COOKIE_URLS = [
  "https://lodgemaster-client.oa-scouting.org/",
  "https://portal.oa-scouting.org/",
];
```

`login()` does briefly land on `id.oa-scouting.org` as part of the OIDC
redirect chain, and that host sets its own session cookie there -- but
since `id.oa-scouting.org` was never in `COOKIE_URLS`, that cookie was
never captured or written to `lodge104-keys`. Without it, consumers that
replay the stored cookies against `lodgemaster-client.oa-scouting.org`
have an auth cookie jar the app considers incomplete, so any request that
triggers a silent OIDC re-check bounces to the identity server and loops.

## Fix

Add `https://id.oa-scouting.org/` to `COOKIE_URLS` so its session cookie
is captured and written alongside the `lodgemaster-client`/`portal`
cookies, same as before.

## Verification

- `node --check src/index.js` passes.
- Confirmed via `DescribeTable`/`Scan` against the live `lodge104-keys`
  table that no `id.oa-scouting.org`-scoped cookie currently exists there,
  consistent with this being the missing piece.
- Could not fully verify end-to-end locally (requires live LodgeMaster
  credentials + Puppeteer/Chromium); recommend validating with
  `send_test_automation`-style manual invoke after merge, then re-testing
  `lodge104-memberdata`.

author: jeremysball
body:
The suite failed on any machine with the global git hooks installed, and it had nothing to do with the code under test.

`tests/unit/lib/git-blame.test.js` builds throwaway repos under the temp directory and commits into them. Every one of those is a primary checkout by definition, so the global `pre-commit` gate refused the commit with "make the change in a linked worktree instead". The test passed only where no global hooks existed.

The fixture now points `core.hooksPath` at an empty directory inside its own temp repo. That keeps real `git commit` calls rather than opting out with `--no-verify`, and it leaves the machine's hooks untouched for real work.

The SSE route test had a smaller version of the same environment leak. It returned a rejected promise from a process-wide module mock, so whenever a sibling test file mocked `lib/cache` too, the promise was never awaited and surfaced as an unhandled rejection. Throwing from inside the call keeps the same assertion without the orphan promise.

Verification: `bun test tests/unit` gives 728 pass, 0 fail. `bun run check` exits 0 with warnings only, matching the existing baseline.
