body:
Lets TeamAICoder be the default app for Markdown, so double-clicking a `.md` file opens it rendered in the app.

**What changes**
- **File associations:** `Info.plist` declares a Markdown document type (`net.daringfireball.markdown`; `.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`) with the Editor role, so the app appears under Finder's **Open With**.
- **`open-file` handling:** the file opens in a Build tab, switching sections if needed and reusing an existing tab. Paths that arrive before the window is ready are queued until `init()` finishes, so cold starts work.
- **`make install`** builds and copies the app to `/Applications` (unsigned unless `CSC_NAME` is set). The old `install` target (`npm install`) is renamed `deps`.
- **`make default-markdown`** sets the app as the default via `NSWorkspace.setDefaultApplication`. The older `LSSetDefaultRoleHandlerForContentType` returns success but is ignored on current macOS.
- **Packaged builds** no longer open DevTools or try electron-reload (`app.isPackaged`).

**Tested**
- 3 new UI tests (`tests/ui/open-file.test.js`). Full suite: 52 UI and 50 unit tests passing.
- By hand on the installed app: `make install`, then `make default-markdown` (default confirmed as `/Applications/TeamAICoder.app`), then `open file.md`. The app log shows the `open-file` and the tab opening, both while running and from a cold start.

Docs: building-and-installing covers `make install` and the default-app step, and the README command table is updated.

author: dnesdan
body:
## Problem
The source-owned program runtime could perform live lookups, but the existing mission APIs could not borrow the mission's own program, actor world and scene arena together. Callers needed a real composition path that preserves callback mutations and the original game-first named-program lookup order.

## Changes
- Add an invocation context borrowing the actual ModelArena and caller-owned current Scene reference slot, with separate required effect and diagnostic services.
- Execute the existing CProgram in MissionContentOwner against that same owner's ActorWorld. No second program, copied register bank, actor registry or scene owner is created.
- Resolve the actual Scene lazily when an instruction reaches it; reject foreign arenas, stale references and a sector presented as a Scene.
- Let diagnostics mutate the live program fields, owner, actor world, arena and current Scene selection. Later lookup reads observe those mutations.
- Add a required game-global runner, then re-read the mission's current reverse-priority named-program collection. Existing named selection is factored without changing its ordering.
- Reuse the same live actor/frame projection helpers in old and new lookup paths.

## Validation
Exact reviewed/tested source: `32937ca736b39381e56ab68d7bb26358539ddd60`.
Published head: `6e12702009e18b754addb185362e8ff6d66e151a`.
Exact complete tree: `7b53308458edee1ff4c44c3ce761b9a498820824`; fresh fetch and empty source diff verified the GitHub transport.

- All nine focused actual-loader/world integration tests passed.
- `scripts/test.sh` completed: 2,000 ordinary Rust tests and 106 Python tests, formatting, workspace checks, strict Clippy and progress checks. The final receipt explicitly verifies all four Python suite summaries and a final completion sentinel.
- `cargo test --locked --workspace --all-features`: 2,003 passed; 25 existing GPU cases ignored.
- `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Two sequential independent final-diff source reviews approved the exact final revision. The final lexical test-scope correction changes no production behavior or assertion.

Fixtures load actual synthetic AE20/AE50 sources into genuine Scene/ModelArena/ActorWorld owners and cover lookup-bank effects, callback redirection, lazy validation, error prefixes, caught unwind and required game-global behavior.

## Scope and remaining integration
This is a callable MissionContentOwner execution binding. It adds no command, full scheduler, GameInit flag or original-function coverage credit. The external MissionLoadSession API still exposes its retained loader/arena immutably; exposing this binding through that session and connecting application startup/ticking are follow-ups.

FRM_SETON, recording effects, derived Entity VM behavior and missing runtime effects remain explicit dependencies. No production success-only backend is supplied. This PR has no fresh GPU, original-game or playable-mission claim.

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution -->
_Requested by **Farah** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01LRDerNr6Ce3dWtx8TecS6w?thread=cmsg_01LRDerNr6Ce3dWtx8TecS6wMAvgQR9KAd4PX71M1hZLHA)_

## What this adds

Phase 4 of 6: profiles, payroll with PDF salary slips, goals, policies and tasks, all saved to the database.

- **Payroll:** HR previews the month from each employee's salary structure, runs it to create draft slips, checks the figures (and can recalculate), then publishes. Employees are notified and see only their own published slips.
  - Each slip downloads as a **branded PDF** generated on the server. Only the owner, or HR, can download it.
  - The tax and provident fund rule is the demo's simplified flat rule, and is labelled as not tax advice.
- **My Profile:** employees edit their phone, address and emergency contact, and upload or remove a photo. The photo must be a JPG, PNG or WebP up to 500 KB, and is checked by its file bytes, not its name. Employment details stay HR-only.
- **Goals and reviews:** managers (for their department and direct reports) and HR assign monthly or annual goals and write 1–5 reviews. Employees update their progress and get notified.
- **Policies:** HR uploads a PDF policy or a new version. The file must be a real PDF up to 5 MB, and a new version needs a new version number. All staff are notified. Staff can open or download policies, and signed-out visitors cannot.
  - Files are stored in the database, so no extra file storage is needed to deploy.
  - The seed creates short sample PDFs.
- **Tasks:** HR assigns tasks with a deadline and priority. Employees update progress with a note or mark them complete, and HR is notified.
- **Forms keep what you typed** when the server rejects a value. React 19 otherwise clears the form after every submit; this now applies to all 12 forms.
- The seed adds goals and reviews across teams and contact details for everyone. The README status line is corrected.

Tickets, the helpdesk, announcements, notifications and reports come in Phases 5 and 6.

## Database

One migration: `Policy` gets file fields (`fileData`, `fileName`, `fileSize`, `summary`, `updatedBy`) and drops the unused `fileUrl`, and `Task` gets `note` and `updatedAt`. Run `npm run db:migrate`, then `npm run db:seed` for fresh demo data.

- Phase 2 (31) and Phase 3 (41) suites still pass.

body:
`SaveManager.Init` previously registered `MC_POST_EFFECT_INIT` and `MC_POST_ENTITY_REMOVE` for every mod, even when they weren't needed. This PR registers them only when entity save data requires them and skips unnecessary checks in entity callbacks

1. **Register callbacks only when needed**
   - `MC_POST_ENTITY_REMOVE` is registered when non-global default data is configured, entity data is found in a loaded save, or entity save data is retrieved
   - `MC_POST_EFFECT_INIT` is registered when an effect `POST_ENTITY_DATA_LOAD` listener is added, effect data is found in a loaded save, or save data is retrieved for an effect
   - Once registered, callbacks stay active for the rest of the session

2. **Detect entity load listeners**
`SaveManager.Init` wraps `modReference.AddCallback` and `AddPriorityCallback` to detect `POST_ENTITY_DATA_LOAD` listeners. This ensures `onEntityInit` still runs when another mod needs entity load data

3. **Skip unnecessary entity initialization checks**
When no `POST_ENTITY_DATA_LOAD` listeners are registered, non-player entities that don't pass `ShouldSaveType` now return immediately from `onEntityInit`

4. **Skip unnecessary entity removal checks**
Tears, projectiles, lasers, and knives now return immediately from `postEntityRemove`, avoiding `ShouldSaveType` and unnecessary reads of `Variant`, `SubType`, and `SpawnerType`

## Profiling
Combat room, no `POST_ENTITY_DATA_LOAD` listener: a mod registering both callbacks went from about 0.69ms to 0.17ms per frame, mostly `MC_POST_EFFECT_INIT` (0.58ms to 0.10ms). Mods that don't use entity save features incur no performance cost from these callbacks

author: quantumnightmare
body:
## Summary

PyPDF2's final release has an unpatched infinite-loop vulnerability during PDF text extraction. Replace it with maintained `pypdf==6.21.4`, pin the reviewed data/document libraries, and raise the SDK minimum to `~=2.0.1`. The final pypdf pin also fixes CVE-2026-119203, CVE-2026-119204, and CVE-2026-119205 discovered during the pre-PR audit.

Pin `python-dateutil==2.9.0.post0` to satisfy the Lambda image's bundled botocore requirement. Update the advertised libraries, dependency documentation, test commands, and packaging guidance, and add a PDF generation/read/write/text-extraction regression test.

## Breaking change

Bump the integration from 2.0.0 to 3.0.0. Existing scripts must replace `PyPDF2` imports with `pypdf`; legacy merging code must use `PdfWriter.append()` instead of `PdfMerger`. Action inputs and outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

- Structure validation and comprehensive code checks passed, including lint, formatting, Bandit, dependency audit, and config/code sync.
- All 8 unit tests passed.
- Built the deployment ZIP using HiveUp's packaging library with dependencies staged in the AWS Lambda Python 3.13 base image. Verified the extracted bundle with `pip check`, all 8 tests, and smoke checks for all nine analysis libraries.
- The packaged dependency inventory was audited separately: zero known vulnerabilities.
- No external service API or credentials are required; the runtime smoke checks exercise local file generation and reading.

## Packaging limitation

HiveUp's hardcoded `manylinux2014_x86_64` wheel target cannot resolve the pinned NumPy/Pillow releases. Stage dependencies inside `public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.13` and assemble with HiveUp's `write_package_zip` function, as documented in the README. Downgrading Pillow to the last wheel for the older target reintroduces known vulnerabilities. The generated ZIP is a local build artifact and is not committed.

## Author commitment

- [x] I understand the third-party API areas I implemented (local library APIs; no external service endpoints).
- [x] I can explain every action, endpoint, permission, dependency, and important helper.
- [x] I used the documented Autohive SDK process and repository conventions.
- [x] I reviewed the generated or written code myself and completed an independent code review.
- [x] I removed dead code, generic boilerplate, hallucinated endpoints, and unnecessary abstractions.
- [x] I tested the integration with meaningful mocked tests.
- [x] I included real runtime checks where safe and practical; external API tests are inapplicable.
- [x] I ran local validation and fixed issues before requesting review.
- [x] I documented the integration clearly for users and future maintainers.

## Review standard

Reviewed against the Integration Engineering Charter. The main review points are the breaking PDF-library migration, the Lambda dependency constraint, and the documented packaging target limitation.

author: ooonea
body:
### Motivation and Context

Positive temporary mount options can leave `zfs get` reporting the stored `off` value. Linux also needs to expose the superblock atime state when a property callback changes it on a mounted dataset. On FreeBSD, cached mount entries use `suid` and `nosuid`, which property reporting must recognize.

### Description

Report positive temporary options and the current Linux atime flag, and recognize the FreeBSD option aliases and mount flags. Extend the native mount test to cover plain remounts and inherited atime changes on a mounted child. Run the mount-cache test with both stored setuid values.

### How Has This Been Tested?

Built debug modules and userspace and ran `zfs_mount_007_pos`, `libzfs_mnttab_cache`, and `mountpoint_003_pos`, including their setup and cleanup, on Linux 7.0.0-38 and FreeBSD 16.0-CURRENT. All passed on this revision. The new inherited-atime assertion failed on the previous PR head; the FreeBSD cache checks failed with both stored setuid values before the correction.

The full ZFS Test Suite has not been run on this revision.

author: dwalker-va
body:
Card: AS-446

Every reward-tier weapon's damage now follows the item-level rule. A Gauntlet or Champion one-hander, bow, crossbow or wand deals its starting-kit anchor's DPS × `ilvl / anchor ilvl`. A reward two-hander deals its one-hander's DPS × Classic's two-hander premium. Each weapon keeps its Classic stand-in's spread and speed. No default loadout wears these items.

**The anchor** is the starting weapon held the same way, of the same role (spell power means caster) and the same weapon type. Where none of its type starts, any weapon of that hand and role qualifies. When several qualify, the anchor is the one with the most DPS per item level, so no wearer's reward scales below the weapon it starts with. Two wands start, so wands anchor on Staff of Dominance rather than Wand of Shadows. This also moves the Champion Doomfinger.

| Weapon | Tier | Anchor | DPS before | DPS after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stormblade Edge | Gauntlet | Frostbite Blade | 16.50 | 17.98 |
| Fang of the Viper | Gauntlet | Serpent Fang Dagger | 19.50 | 20.43 |
| Mace of the Redeemer | Gauntlet | Hammer of the Righteous | 15.00 | 17.03 |
| Claw of Chromaggus | Gauntlet | Witchblade | 17.25 | 18.39 |
| Azuresong Mageblade | Gauntlet | Witchblade | 15.40 | 18.39 |
| Wand of the Invoker | Gauntlet | Staff of Dominance | 9.10 | 11.84 |
| Eaglestrike Bow | Gauntlet | Ashwood Bow | 11.20 | 18.80 |
| Deadeye Crossbow | Gauntlet | Sniper Scope | 10.50 | 11.67 |
| Bloodlord's Battleaxe | Gauntlet | Stormblade Edge × 1.32 | 21.78 | 23.74 |
| Runestaff of Elements | Gauntlet | Claw of Chromaggus × 1.35 | 23.26 | 24.79 |
| Doomfinger | Champion | Staff of Dominance (was Wand of Shadows) | 11.50 | 13.96 |

The rule is stated once, in the `items.ron` header. The test is now `reward_weapon_dps_scales_its_starting_weapon_by_item_level`. It derives each anchor by the rule, pins the result in its table, and names every Gauntlet and Champion non-two-hander by set equality. The encyclopedia's Eaglestrike Bow snapshot is re-blessed.

**Human testing:** Nothing needs human testing

body:
## Summary

A Maths instructor created an assignment template for a quiz, but it never appeared on the semester's Assignments page, because it was not in the semester schedule. The wizard's prompt to add it to the schedule only showed after an extra "Save the marking settings" click, so in practice nobody saw it.

- **Semester Assignments page:** a "Not in this semester yet" section lists course templates the semester schedule does not use, each with an **Add to the schedule** button.
- **New assignment button** on that page keeps the semester, so the wizard's last step picks it by default.
- **New assignment done step:**
  - re-checks the template every 10 s until it is complete;
  - saves the marking settings by itself;
  - shows "Course template created." (green), "Nothing reaches students until you add it to a semester instance." (yellow) and an **Add to a semester** button.

`console/README.md` updated: the Assignments page and the `?cohort=` wizard route. No public doc filenames changed.

- `npm test` (1079), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` pass.
- Inspected locally against the demo orgs by the maintainer: approved.

author: teorth
body:
Further updates to the paper and referee response. Relative to `main`, this:

- **End-to-end theorem:** replaces the stale claim that the extension to the full implication graph is external to Lean. `foundations.tex` now describes `end_to_end1` (#1506), and notes that the finite implication graph still relies on external programs.
- **What is formalized (R1.9):** adds a paragraph to `foundations.tex` stating which material is and is not formalized.
- **Timings and line counts:** updated to commit `3f68407`, using summed per-file build times from CI.
- **Versions (R1.10):** the paper now refers to repository tag `paper-v3`, Lean 4.29.1 and Mathlib `v4.29.1`. **The `paper-v3` tag still has to be created** once the final paper changes are merged.
- **Consistency result (R2.3):** corrects the statement of Carneiro's result. It is now given as consistency relative to ZFC plus $n$ inaccessible cardinals for each natural number $n$, and it notes that the proof does not directly apply to Lean 4.
- **Higman-Neumann data (R2.12):** adds `data/Higman-Neumann.md` describing the data file, and links to it from the footnote. The link resolves once this is merged.
- **Equational laws:** adds a figure showing the three forms of the commutative law in the codebase, with the `lean` listing and Unicode support this needs in `main.tex`, and describes `LawX` more precisely.
- **Blueprint citation:** adds "Version of November 1, 2026" to the `ETP_blueprint` entry.
- **Referee response:** updates the corresponding `response.tex` items, with related wording changes in `conclusions.tex`, `constructions.tex` and `metatheorems.tex`.
- **Cleanup:** removes the obsolete `response-todo-zulip.md` checklist.

R1.1–R1.6 and R2.4 are not addressed here. The new `foundations.tex` text on the end-to-end theorem overlaps with them, so it should be coordinated with that work.

Makes `codeassembly-run-core`, the package that contains the domain model and parsers for CodeAssembly's development runs, publishable to npm so that projects outside this monorepo can depend on it.

## Claim

The cheap Dancer2 activation gate that decides whether a request pays filesystem module resolution now opens on the earliest 1.x **or** 2.x `use Dancer2` site, and `file_activations` still mints 2.x facts for a resolved 2.x module even when the 1.x extractor lists nothing. `canonical_file_facts` assembles those 2.x comparison facts without a 1.x detection result.

## Controlling issue

Governing issue or accepted claim: #14989

Advances #14989. Parent: #13616 (L3 prerequisite).

This slice is the residual activation-gate parity left after #15006. It does **not** complete #14989: the `Shadow → Production` disposition decision and route-family / consumer-rendering leaves remain on the issue.

## Governing contract

Accepted residual of #14989: `file_activations` already arbitrates 2.x facts (`two_x_packages` / `two_x_detection`, landed in #15006 / `ae795a276`). The still-1.x-only cheap gate was `first_activation_site_offset` / `has_activation_site`, consumed by `perl-lsp-rs` `dancer2_request_context` (untouched here; owned by PR #16775).

## Changed production path

`textDocument/*` Dancer2 request → `dancer2_request_context` → `first_activation_site_offset(ast)` → (on `Some`) filesystem `Dancer2` resolution anchored at that offset → `file_activations` → `canonical_file_facts` → 1.x and/or 2.x facts.

The gate now mins AST spans from both extractors. `file_activations` no longer returns before dual-adapter arbitration when the 1.x site list is empty. `canonical_file_facts` no longer returns empty solely because 1.x `detection` is `None`.

Today's extractor predicates are identical, so a 2.x-shaped `use Dancer2` already opened the 1.x gate. The live assembler delta is 2.x comparison facts without a 1.x detection result. The dual-min gate is structural so a future 2.x-only form cannot skip module resolution.

## Proof

- `bash scripts/cargo-admitted test -p perl-lsp-rs-core --lib --locked dancer2` — **86 passed**, 0 failed (includes the new gate tests and the simulated extractor-split assembler assertion).
- `cargo fmt -p perl-lsp-rs-core -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p perl-lsp-rs-core --lib --locked -- -D warnings` — clean for the lib target.
- `bash scripts/cargo-admitted clippy -p perl-lsp-rs-core --all-targets --profile agent --locked -- -D warnings` — **not claimed here**: pre-existing `clippy::panic` / `doc_lazy_continuation` on unrelated files (`postfix.rs`, `launcher/mod.rs`, `facade_surface_tests.rs`), identical class to current `main`, not introduced by this diff.

## Hosted proof

- [ ] Hosted-only: no local Rust toolchain; named hosted checks are the first-class proof
- Named hosted checks: Compile All Targets (bit-rot guard), Conflict marker check, validate-title, Perl LSP Rust Small Result, ripr+ New Gap Gate
- Commit SHA evaluated: `c0a571a43abcceb7a7daedfe2ca2d3b968caadea`
- Check run URL(s):
  - Compile All Targets (bit-rot guard): https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/actions/runs/41355038200/job/124993588555 (pass)
  - Conflict marker check: https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/actions/runs/41355038200/job/124993588578 (pass)
  - validate-title: https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/actions/runs/41355358265/job/124994124691 (pass)
  - Perl LSP Rust Small Result: https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/perl-lsp-swarm/actions/runs/41355038344/job/124997290900 (pass)
  - ripr+ New Gap Gate: pending (`ripr` workflow run 41355038256 has not started a job)
- Result per check: 4 of 5 named required producers green on this head; ripr still queued
- Why local proof was not run (hosted-only only): N/A — local focused proof ran as recorded above

## Test hardening

Wrong implementations challenged:

- A 1.x-only `min` that ignores an earlier 2.x offset (`dancer2_earliest_activation_site_offset_takes_the_minimum_across_both_extractors`). This is the pre-PR falsifier for the gate.
- A 2.x-only versioned document (`use Dancer2 2.0.1`) whose gate must be true at the 2.x site (live-seam pin; extractors currently agree).
- A 1.x versioned document whose offset is unchanged.
- Mixed 1.x + 2.x sites: offset is the minimum.
- Dancer2-free / `use Dancer2::Core` documents: `None` / false (no FS resolution).
- Provider-seam e2e: `file_activations` for a resolved 2.x module emits 2.x facts, and `canonical_file_facts` still assembles them after `detection` is cleared (`dancer2_file_activations_emits_two_x_facts_for_a_resolved_two_x_module`).

## Simplification

`earliest_activation_site_offset` is the single min over both extractors. `file_activations` no longer couples 2.x arbitration to a non-empty 1.x site list. `canonical_file_facts` no longer couples 2.x minting to 1.x detection.

## Deviations

No 2.x-only activation **form** currently exists that `extract_dancer2_activation_sites` misses (identical module-name predicates and the same `Use` walk). The gate still consults both extractors so a future 2.x-only site cannot skip module resolution. The production signature stays `first_activation_site_offset(ast)` — the runtime consumer is owned by PR #16775 — so the 2.x walk uses AST spans only (empty source; source-dependent 2.x evidence is unused for offsets).

## Claim Boundary

Provably true: the in-memory gate's offset is `min(1.x spans, 2.x spans)`; Dancer2-free documents still skip FS resolution; a resolved 2.x module still mints 2.x facts through `file_activations`; `canonical_file_facts` assembles those 2.x comparison facts without 1.x detection.

Not proven here: installed-client / exact-process Dancer2 2.x UX; Shadow→Production disposition; diagnostics/hover/symbol rendering of 2.x route-handler scope (other claims). The 2.x extractor is still `Shadow`. Today's 2.x-shaped documents already opened the 1.x gate; the dual-min is structural for future extractor divergence.

## Non-goals

- No change to `crates/perl-lsp-rs/src/runtime/language/dancer2.rs`.
- No change to analyzer extractors, diagnostics, hover, or UX scenarios.
- No Shadow→Production promotion.

## Risk and rollback

The gate does one extra in-memory 2.x site walk before any filesystem resolution. Dancer2-free documents still return `None` and skip I/O. Rollback: revert the squash commit.

## Review index

- `first_activation_site_offset` / `earliest_activation_site_offset` / `has_activation_site`

- `canonical_file_facts` assembles 2.x facts without 1.x detection

author: micoo79
body:
## Cél

Érintőkijelző nélküli gépen a felhasználó **QR-kódot** kap. Telefonnal beolvasva megnyílik az aláíró oldal, ott aláír, és az aláírás **magától visszakerül a gép böngészőjébe**, ahol elkészül a PDF.

## Hogyan működik

1. A gépen kitöltöd az űrlapot → **„Aláírás telefonon (QR)"**. (Érintő nélküli gépen ez a kiemelt gomb.)
2. QR-kód jelenik meg egy véletlen, 128 bites tokennel. A telefon beolvassa → megnyílik `…/megbizolevel.html?sign=TOKEN`.
3. A telefon fekvőbe fordítva aláír (a korábbi, minden böngészőn pontos aláírópad), majd a PNG feltöltődik a relay-re a tokennel.
4. A gép 2 másodpercenként lekérdezi a relay-t; amint megérkezik, beteszi az aláírást és felkínálja a PDF-et. A relay a lekérés után azonnal törli az adatot.

## Saját relay — adatvédelem

- `docs/relay/sign-relay.php`: **egyetlen PHP fájl, adatbázis nélkül**, a saját tárhelyedre. Feltölt / egyszer lekér / töröl; TTL 10 perc; max ~3 MB; csak PNG data URL; CORS.
- **Semmi nem megy harmadik félhez** — az aláírás csak a te szervereden halad át, és rövid ideig él.
- A token kitalálhatatlan (`crypto.randomUUID`), a tároló (`_sigstore`) gitignore-ban, direkt elérése tiltva.

## Beállítás (egyszeri)

1. Töltsd fel a `docs/relay/sign-relay.php`-t a tárhelyedre (pl. `https://sajat-domain.hu/vitel/sign-relay.php`). PHP 7+ kell, adatbázis nem.
2. A `docs/config.js`-ben állítsd be ugyanerre: `window.VITEL_SIGN_RELAY = "https://sajat-domain.hu/vitel/sign-relay.php";`
3. Ha üresen hagyod, a QR-opció rejtve marad; az azonos eszközös (érintős/egeres) aláírás továbbra is működik.

## Teszt (Playwright + valódi PHP relay)

Asztali (nincs touch) → QR megjelenik → telefon (fekvő) aláír → **az aláírás megérkezik a gépre, a PDF gomb megjelenik.** Minden lépés zöld.

Vendorolt lib: `docs/vendor/qrcode.min.js` (qrcode-generator, MIT).

- Three columns from `lg` (`lg:grid-cols-3`) instead of CSS auto-fit, as Joan asked. At 1024 each column is 293px, and the longest label and chip fit.

body:
## What

Developer ID signing and Apple notarization for the release DMG, so the published build opens on any Mac without Gatekeeper warnings.

**Signed path (all five secrets set):**
1. Imports the `.p12` into a temporary keychain and decodes the notary `.p8` into `$RUNNER_TEMP`.
2. `scripts/build-app.sh` signs `MacOptimized.app` with `Developer ID Application`, `--options runtime --timestamp`. The bundle has a single Mach-O.
3. Zips the app, notarizes it (`xcrun notarytool submit --key/--key-id/--issuer --wait`, via the new `scripts/notarize.sh`), then staples it.
4. `scripts/make-dmg.sh` (with `SKIP_APP_BUILD=1`) packs the stapled app and signs the DMG. The DMG is then notarized and stapled.
5. Verifies with `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, checks TeamIdentifier `RQTYDUV329`, the hardened runtime flag and the timestamp, and runs `spctl --assess` on the app, the DMG and the app inside the mounted DMG.
6. Publishes the release with "signed and notarized" notes. The keychain and key are removed in an `always()` step.

`notarize.sh` fails the run and prints Apple's notary log unless the status is `Accepted`. `notarytool --wait` alone doesn't guarantee that.

**Unsigned path (no secrets: forks, or until they're configured):** same ad-hoc build and release as today, same release notes, plus a `::warning::` saying the macOS build is unsigned. If only some of the secrets are set, the run fails so an unsigned build can't ship by accident.

**Entitlements:** none. Nothing in the app needs a hardened-runtime exception. There's no JIT, `dlopen` only loads Apple frameworks, and the `osascript` `do shell script … with administrator privileges` call sends no Apple Events to other apps.

**Docs:** new `docs/RELEASING.md` covering each secret, how to create it, how to cut a release, and local signing. `.gitignore` ignored the whole `docs/` folder, so it now ignores `docs/*` except `docs/RELEASING.md`. README now points to it.

## Validation
- `swift test`: 8 tests pass.
- `./scripts/make-dmg.sh` without an identity: ad-hoc signed app and DMG, same as before.
- Signed path run locally with an Apple Development identity (no Developer ID cert on this machine). The app gets `flags=0x10000(runtime)`, a secure timestamp and TeamIdentifier `RQTYDUV329`. It passes `codesign --verify --deep --strict` and launches under the hardened runtime. The DMG signs and verifies.
- `actionlint` (with shellcheck) and `shellcheck scripts/*.sh`: clean.
- **Not tested:** notarization, stapling and `spctl` with a real Developer ID. They need the secrets and Apple's service. Once the secrets exist, do a **dry run** of the workflow before tagging.

## Owner to-do
- Add the five secrets (`DEVELOPER_ID_P12_BASE64`, `DEVELOPER_ID_P12_PASSWORD`, `NOTARY_KEY_P8_BASE64`, `NOTARY_KEY_ID`, `NOTARY_ISSUER_ID`) as described in `docs/RELEASING.md`.
- Run Actions › release › Run workflow with **dry run** ticked to confirm signing and notarization.

Pages move from `/steps.html` to `/steps`, the way most docs sites address them. The Markdown version stays at `/steps.md`.

## How

- **Build:** unchanged. It still writes `build/<id>.html`.
- **Publish:** `publish.py — key_for` uploads each page's HTML under its bare id. `index.html` and `404.html` keep their names, because CloudFront asks for them by name. Every upload already sets its content type from the file's suffix, so a key with no extension still goes up as `text/html; charset=utf-8`.

- **Links:** `href()`, render's `.md`→HTML link rewrite, the canonical tag, `sitemap.xml`, `search.json` and the Overview's diagram all use `/<id>`. A link to `/index.md` becomes `/`.

- **Local preview:** new `scripts/serve.py`, because a plain `http.server` returns 404 for every page link.

  - `/<id>.html` returns 404, as it will in prod.

The orphan sweep deletes the old `<id>.html` keys, so those addresses return 404, as the `/use/...` ones did after #179. They have only been live since #179.

Follow-up after publish: the popcorn-cli `docs/TEMPLATE_AUTHORING.md` pointer still links `/template-authoring.html`.

author: usehoplite[bot]
body:
## Summary

Implements #409: an optional, evidence-grounded visual-understanding stage for audio description. The default remains the deterministic acoustic narration; enabling a vision provider adds descriptions of visible events without inventing identities, dialogue, emotions or causes.

## What changed

- **Bounded frame sampling** (`narrate/visual/frames.rs`): ffmpeg decodes only the candidate gap window, prefers scene-change timestamps and fills the budget evenly. `max_frames_per_window` and `max_total_frames` cap work; repeated windows are served from cache instead of re-decoding.
- **Provider-agnostic vision** (`narrate/visual/provider.rs`): `VisionProvider` trait, OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` and local Ollama `/api/chat` implementations, and strict JSON parsing that requires every observation to reference a supplied frame/timestamp and takes timestamps from the frame, not the model.
- **Grounding** (`narrate/visual/grounding.rs`): drops dialogue attribution, emotion, causality, unsupported identities, "we see"/"camera" wording and low-confidence frames; records rejected claims and uncertainty per window.
- **Narration + fallback** (`narrate/visual/mod.rs`): confident grounded sentences are fitted to the existing whole-clause word budget, so they stay inside the speech-free window. Every `NarrationScript` now carries `NarrationEvidence` (`visual` or `audio_only` with a reason); failures fall back to the acoustic description, labelled.
- **Cache/review**: analysis cache keyed by movie identity, window, sampling policy, language and provider/model; `<output>.visual-review.json` lists each window's source, sampled frame paths/timestamps, confidence, uncertainty, rejected claims, narration and fallback reason, and is committed as a `plan_narration` artifact.
- **Config/wiring**: `narrator.visual` config (default `provider = "none"`), validation, `MRPLAY_VISION_PROVIDER`/`MRPLAY_VISION_MODEL` env overrides, config schema, default TOML, both `radio-play` and `produce` entry points, `plan_narration` input/version update, ADR-129 and changelog.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/quality_gate.sh` passes (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, workspace tests, doc tests, secret scan, LOC limit, benchmarks).
- New tests cover: grounded fixture description, ambiguous/obstructed frame → uncertainty + audio fallback, unsupported identity, no provider → audio-only path, malformed provider output, provider timeout, empty frames, scene-change/budget sampling, language forwarding, cache reuse and key sensitivity, prompt constraints, real ffmpeg extraction, and the action-level audio-only default.
- `NarrationScript` evidence defaults keep older `scripts.json` artifacts deserializable.

Closes #409.

author: jiribenes
body:
After looking more into Chez' documentation and source for a different project, I notice that we are using very strange representations, silently converting from one to another.

Here are the changes:

1. monotonic clock (slightly faster geomean)
2. `Double`s now use exclusively floating number operations (flonums), making sure that we keep them unboxed (geomean ~0.869-0.909)
3. `Int`, `Char`, and `Byte` are fixnums, `i61` with ~~wrapping arithmetic~~ undefined arithmetic on over-/under-flow, again making sure they're unboxed (geomean 0.806)

Altogether, the geomean is 0.700 on Chez CPS, 0.747 on CallCC, and 0.758 on Monadic.

превью: /styleguide/chertezhi/

## Что меняется
Цвета вынесены в токены чертежей (`styles/tokens.css`, темы листов `lib/sheet/theme.css`):

| Токен | Цвет | Контраст на белом |
|---|---|---|
| `--chertezh-vershina` — вершины и точки | синий `#1F5FD0` | 5,8 : 1 |
| `--chertezh-velichina` — числа и первая переменная (x, a) | терракота `#E07A2F` | **3,0 : 1** |
| `--chertezh-velichina-2` — вторая переменная (y, b) | янтарь `--amber-700` `#A85F06` | 4,9 : 1 |

В ч/б и строгой темах листа все три токена чёрные.

- **Вершины и точки** — синие. Подписи вершин — полужирный курсив, на 12 % крупнее. Невидимые вершины в стереометрии — тот же синий, светлее (0,55).
- **Величины** — тёплые, обычное начертание. Угол: дуга, сектор и подпись одного цвета. Контуры — navy.
- **Печать:** вершины — чёрный полужирный, величины — чёрный обычный. В «Цветных чертежах» — как на экране.

## Правила цвета (решения автора, коммит 580ef57)
1. **Отрезок с конкретным числом** (AB = 15, хорда) — линия navy, цветная только подпись. Цвет линии — только у смысловых связей: части через x и y и равные отрезки. В 9 шаблонах тренажёра снята роль part-x / part-y у отрезков с числами.
2. **mediana** — все стороны и медиана navy, подписи 5, 7, √21 терракотой.
3. **Равные отрезки** (одинаковые засечки) — всегда одного цвета и вида. Равный отрезок на стороне — сторона разбита в точке:
   - bis-par: AC = CM + AM, участок AM оформлен как ML;
   - mediana: MD оформлен как AM (пунктир сохранён).

   Без переменной равные отрезки остаются navy (так выходит и в mediana по п. 2).
4. **Площади.**
   - Данная (`region`) — терракота ~18 % и число.
   - Искомая (новая роль `region-sought`) — голубая заливка ~8 %, пунктирный контур внутри фигуры и подпись «S… = ?». Пунктир — препятствие для подписей.
   - Где применено: menelay-pl (APC, подпись под AC — треугольник узкий), trap-seredina (ABCD), obshchiy-ugol (MBCN), ravnobok-perp (ABCD).
   - Голубая заливка основной фигуры убрана: голубой теперь только у искомой площади.
5. **Ч/б (печать, листы по умолчанию)** — без заливок вообще:
   - ни фигур, ни площадей, ни секторов углов; углы — только дуги, равенства — засечки;
   - данная и искомая площадь различаются подписью «S = 18» / «S = ?»;
   - то же в ч/б темах листа для №1 (штриховка областей, секторы углов) и №3 (закрашенные грани и сечения): `lib/sheet/theme.css`.

**Автотест** (`verify_schemes/geometriya.mjs`, входит в `test:skhemy-18`):
- part-x / part-y — только у частей с записью через переменную;
- отрезки с одинаковыми засечками — одного цвета и роли;
- если б) ищет площадь — на чертеже есть искомая фигура и «S = ?»;
- данная площадь — роль `region`.

Эталон записей обновлён у четырёх шаблонов с искомой площадью.

## Где применено
- **Движок схем** (№18: генератор, тренажёр, ключевые схемы, опорные задачи, теория, карточки): тема включена у всех чертежей движка. Кегль подписей вершин 17 → 19 px, раскладка подписей идёт с новым размером.
- **Планиметрия №1** (теория, банк, листы):
  - буквы и точки — цветом вершин, полужирные, 16 → 18 px;
  - величины и искомое — терракотой; подсказки и построения учителя — янтарём (раньше искомое было синим, а синий теперь только у вершин);
  - дуга угла с подписью — цветом подписи.
- **Стереометрия №3** (банк, листы, разборы): имена вершин синим полужирным ×1,12 — и на экране (HTML-подписи KaTeX, замер с тем же начертанием), и на листе; величины — терракотой.
- **Куб с √3/2.** Дробь оценивалась одной строкой «√3/2», а KaTeX рисует её в два этажа, поэтому она упиралась в рёбра. Теперь `\frac`, `\dfrac`, `\tfrac` и корень в числителе получают рамку на оба этажа и черту корня.

## Решить
- **Контраст терракоты.** Терракота величин `#E07A2F` задана явно и даёт 3,0 : 1 — для текста это ниже 4,5. Если нужен проходной контраст, есть тёмный оттенок того же тона `#B4541A` (5,0 : 1): одна строка в токене `--chertezh-velichina`.
- **Цвета №1.** Синий был цветом «искомого». Сейчас искомое — терракота, подсказки — янтарь.

## Проверки
- Локально проходят:
  - `test:skhemy-18` (с новыми проверками цвета и площадей), `test:opornye-18`, `test:kartochki`, `test:trenazher-filtry`;
  - `test:point-labels --seeds 12` — 0 ошибок (до коммита 580ef57);
  - `test:spravochnik-1`, `test:seriya-1`, `test:planimetria`, `test:zadanie3`, `test:stereo-engine`, `test:stereo-kachestvo`, `test:stereo-vydelenie`, `test:stereo-metodika`;
  - `test:math-markup --src`, `test:drawing-labels`, `typecheck`, `lint`.
- `test:stereo-kachestvo` теперь требует, чтобы вершины были полужирными, а величины — обычными.
- Эталон геометрии №18: точки и записи данных на месте; подписи вершин сместились из-за нового кегля.
- Стильгайд `/styleguide/chertezhi`:
  - правила и роль `region-sought`;
  - образцы трёх движков (30-60-90, P03-47, P03-02 и проверка дроби, mediana, bis-par, menelay-pl, obshchiy-ugol, trap-seredina) — цветная и ч/б версии рядом;
  - снимки — в переписке с автором.

author: karnigen
body:
I originally wanted to try writing a small Python program that followed the description of Mortran and translated Mortran input into modern Fortran 2018.

I quickly discovered that Mortran is far more subtle than it first appears. I then made an experimental C/C++ version to better understand how it works. That experience gave me an even greater appreciation for the thought and effort behind the original translator.

Rather than replace the translator with either prototype, I decided to modernize its Fortran implementation gradually. I replaced many old-style control-flow patterns with clearer constructs and added documentation to explain how the translator works.

The aim is to make the code easier to read and study while preserving its behavior. The regression tests compare generated Fortran and listings with saved reference files; all 35 reference comparisons pass.

I am sharing this work for anyone interested in learning how Mortran works. I have great respect for the people who created it. Building and debugging such a capable tool while working within fixed-size limits and tables must have required exceptional care and planning.

### Main changes

- Added a standalone, modernized Fortran implementation of the Mortran 3 translator under `HEN_HOUSE/mortran3_inc`.
- Refactored the legacy Fortran code gradually, replacing many old control-flow patterns with clearer structured constructs.
- Introduced named constants for buffer indices, making the translator’s internal tables easier to follow.
- Added a standalone build setup and documentation explaining the translator’s structure, Mortran operators, and expression tables.
- Compared generated Fortran and listings against 35 saved reference cases.

### Test results

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Build check | Translator was already up to date; no rebuild was needed. |
| `test_appended_file_read_error` | Passed |
| `test_configuration_read_error` | Passed |
| `test_configuration_translation_matches_reference` | Passed; generated Fortran matched the `cavity` reference exactly. |
| `test_generated_fortran_and_listing_match_references` | Passed for all 29 `egs_home` cases listed below. |
| `test_hen_house_mortjobs_match_references` | Passed for all 6 HEN_HOUSE cases listed below. |

**egs_home cases (29):** `cavity`, `cavrznrc`, `cavsphnrc`, `dosrznrc`, `dosxyznrc`, `edknrc`, `egs_app`, `egs_cbct`, `egs_chamber`, `egs_fac`, `egs_gammaspec`, `egs_kerma`, `egs_phd`, `examin`, `flurznrc`, `g`, `ranlux_test`, `ranmar_test`, `sprrznrc`, `tutor1`, `tutor2`, `tutor2pp`, `tutor3`, `tutor4`, `tutor4pp`, `tutor5`, `tutor6`, `tutor7`, `tutor7pp`.

**HEN_HOUSE cases (6):** `pegs4`, `omega-addphsp`, `omega-beamdp`, `omega-ctcreate`, `omega-readphsp`, `omega-statdose`.

For all 35 cases, generated Fortran matched the reference exactly, and listings matched after timestamp normalization. All 5 regression tests passed in 26.020 seconds.

author: doriancollier
body:
## What changes

A new table, `member_reports`, for reporting a person when there's no one message to point at. No routes or UI: nothing reads it yet. Part of DOR-3624.

Stacked on #3402. It lands after #3402.

## What the table enforces

- No self-reports: `member_reports_not_self`.
- Same space only: `member_reports_subject_tenant_fk`, `member_reports_reporter_tenant_fk`, `member_reports_resolver_tenant_fk`.
- One open report per reporter and person: `member_reports_open_once`.
- Null reporter only on import: `member_reports_reporter_shape`.
- A resolved row is always complete: `member_reports_status_shape`.

## Deletion and erasure

- The deletion worker removes these rows before the members and the space.
- Erasing a person clears the note on reports by or about them, and keeps the record.
- If this table ever enters an export, the person a report is about never learns who filed it.

Additive, so the compatibility floor doesn't move. Backout: revert the code and leave the table.

## Proof

Local Postgres: `member-reports-migration`, `moderation`, every `export-` suite, `administration`, `member-erasure`, `migrate`, `index-coverage`, `tenant-relations`, `invite-sign-up-mail`. Server typecheck, lint, `check:max-lines`.

Opens on `hold` for @security-auditor.

author: msff
body:
Stacked on #1. Its base is `fix/job-marker-enqueue-day`, so the diff here is only this PR's two commits; GitHub retargets it to `main` when #1 merges and that branch is deleted.

## Problem

A Bot API URL carries the bot token: `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage`. `requests` repeats that URL in its connection errors. While the network was down, a failed owner alert logged the exception text as is (`turn_runner: owner alert failed: {exc}`), so every such line wrote the token into a plain-text job log. Observed live: 29 lines across five job logs of two instances.

## Fix

Two layers, because each catches what the other misses:

- `send.bot_api_sender` re-raises a network failure as `SendError` with the token redacted, `from None`, so neither the message nor a traceback of the chained original carries it. `send.py`'s CLI, which caught only `SendError`, now reports the failure instead of dying on a traceback.
- `estate_client.log` and `poller.log`, the two sinks every gateway line goes through, pass each line through a shared `redact_secrets()`.

## CI's secret scan

The `telegram-bot-token` rule anchored the token with `\b`. There is no word boundary between `bot` and the digits after it, so a token inside its URL, the shape it actually leaks in, matched neither this rule nor gitleaks' built-in ones. The rule now matches the edges explicitly and takes the token as the secret group (RE2 has no lookarounds). Checked with a random fake token: a log line and a bare URL go from undetected to detected, a bare token is still caught, a chat id is not flagged, and the full-history scan stays clean.

## Tests

Three regression tests, all failing on the old code:

- The sender's error and the CLI's output carry no token.
- The owner-alert path that leaked logs none.
- Both log sinks redact a token wherever it sits and leave ordinary numbers alone.

The fake token is assembled at runtime, so the test files don't trip the secret scan. Full suite locally: 620 passed, 6 skipped, under both `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=Europe/Berlin`.

author: creatorinstant548
body:
## Summary

T10 (V0-10, "Python reads the state"): a minimal `ts_py` crate (pyo3 + numpy, built by maturin) that loads the toy world of `ts_toy` with a public test seed, advances it, and reads copies of its state, plus `cargo xtask py` and the revised F3 check of `cargo xtask check`.

- **`crates/ts_py`** (tool crate, outside `default-members`): `ts_py.ToyWorld(seed, threads=1)`, `advance_ticks(n)`, `advance_to(millis)`, `positions()` (owned `int64` array `(1000, 5)`: id, place, parcel, x, y, by increasing `StableId`), `state_hash()`, `rules_fingerprint()`, `now`, `tick_millis`; constants `MILLIS_PER_DAY`, `MAX_DAYS`, `POSITION_COLUMNS`, `PLACES`. No game rule, no file, no state write besides advancing.
- **Lints (AS-18)**: no `lints.workspace`; local `[lints.rust]` and `[lints.clippy]` equal to `[workspace.lints.*]` except `unsafe_code = "deny"`; `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` at the crate root, **no local `allow(unsafe_code)`**: the pyo3 macros need none.
- **F3 revised** (`tools/xtask/src/manifests.rs`, `steps.rs`): `ts_py`'s local tables are compared key by key with the workspace tables (fail closed: extra or missing table, duplicate key, unreadable line, `[lints]` or root `lints…` key next to the tables, quoted names such as `["lints".rust]` read as Cargo reads them, multi-line strings and escapes refused). Quoted names are also unquoted in the check of every other crate. Any other local `[lints]` is still refused. **The anticipated exemption of `ts_client_native` is removed** from `crate_roots` (PY1): it must `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` like any crate until archi-sec decides otherwise.
- **`cargo xtask py`** (`tools/xtask/src/py.rs`): `uv` found on `PATH`, SHA-256 and version checked against `tools/dev/tools.lock`; then in `python/`: `uv sync --locked`, `uv run --no-sync maturin develop --uv --locked`, `uv run --no-sync pytest -p no:cacheprovider`. Children get no `UV_*`, `PIP_*`, `PYTHON*`, `PYO3_*`, `MATURIN_*`, `VIRTUAL_ENV*`, `CONDA*` variable, and `UV_NO_CONFIG=1` (no user or system `uv.toml`, also for the `uv pip` of maturin); the settings that matter are therefore passed to `uv sync` on the command line (`--no-build --no-python-downloads --python-preference only-system --exclude-newer <from uv.lock>`). Error messages name `uv.exe`, never its path.
- **`python/`**: `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version` (3.14.0), `uv.lock` (with hashes), `tests/test_toy_world.py`.
- **`tools/dev/tools.lock`**: `uv.version`, `uv.source`, `uv.archive_sha256`, `uv.sha256` (PY5); the reserved `maturin.*` placeholder is removed (maturin is pinned in `uv.lock`). **After the merge, `cargo xtask hooks install` must be rerun from the main copy** (the pinned hook set includes `tools.lock`).
- Docs: `docs/dev/xtask.md` (F3 row, new §8 `cargo xtask py`), `docs/dev/espace-travail.md` §5 (exception list).

## Conditions of archi-sec (§9.16)

| | How it holds |
|---|---|
| **PY1** `unsafe` | `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, zero `allow(unsafe_code)` in `crates/ts_py`; `cargo clippy -p ts_py -- -D warnings` is clean, so the pyo3 macro expansions trip no `unsafe_code` lint. F3 admits local lints for `ts_py` only (`manifests::LOCAL_LINTS_CRATE`), `ts_client_native` exemption removed; unit tests `local_lints_follow_the_workspace`, `no_anticipated_unsafe_exception`. |
| **PY2** copies only | `positions()` builds a `Vec<i64>` from the ECS, then `Array2::to_pyarray`, which allocates a numpy array and copies into it: `flags.owndata` is true and `base is None` (tested). No `PyBuffer`, no raw pointer, no view. Rows by increasing `StableId` (`StableIndex` is a `BTreeMap`). Only `ToyWorld` holds the `Sim`; no returned object refers to it, and a copy taken before an advance does not change after it (tested). |
| **PY3** key | The only key is `ts_toy::public_test_key(seed)`; `seed` is a Python `int` in `0..2^64`. No function takes a key, key bytes or a seed path. |
| **PY4** bounded inputs | Every integer goes through `int_arg` (`int` or `__index__` object such as `np.int64`; `bool`, `np.bool_`, `float` → `TypeError`; beyond `i128` → `ValueError`), then checked conversion. `advance_ticks`: negative, `ticks × tick` overflow, or a target after day 3660 (`MAX_DAYS`, the `ts-sim` bound Y4) → `ValueError`. `advance_to`: before the current date, after day 3660, or outside `i64` → `ValueError`. `threads` outside 1..64, or another count than the process pool → `ValueError`. Messages carry no path (tested). |
| **PY5** Python locked | `uv.lock` committed with hashes; `cargo xtask py` runs `uv sync --locked`. `[tool.uv] no-build = true` (wheels only; our crate is built by maturin, never by uv: `package = false`); `exclude-newer = 2026-10-17` (≥ two weeks); `.python-version` 3.14.0, `requires-python ==3.14.*`, `python-downloads = "never"`, `python-preference = "only-system"`; `required-version = "==0.11.33"` and `uv` pinned in `tools.lock` with its SHA-256. Base group: `numpy==2.5.4` (arrays returned by ts_py), `pytest==9.1.1` (tests), `maturin==1.15.0` (builds ts_py), nothing else. |
| **PY6** determinism | pytest checks `state_hash()` after 14 days against `short.world` of `data/golden/ts_toy.json` (and `short.ticks`, `short.skipped`, `short.rules`), in-process and in two **separate interpreters** with 1 and 4 threads (the pool is per process, L6). Two runs give the same hash and positions; cutting the run into 28 calls gives the same hash. The thread count only goes to `SimConfig`; the binding starts no thread, and the GIL is released during `run_until` only while the `ToyWorld` is mutably borrowed, so no other Python thread can touch the world meanwhile. |
| **PY7** scope | `ts_py` is in `manifests::TOOLS`, outside `default-members`, depends on no host and no host depends on it; no `fs`, no environment read, no file written. `[lib] test = false, doctest = false`: `cargo test --workspace` builds nothing for it. |

## New dependencies (SEC0-05)

Direct: `pyo3 =0.30.1` (`default-features = false`, `macros`), `numpy =0.30.0` (`default-features = false`), both in `[workspace.dependencies]`. **12 new crates** in `Cargo.lock` (119 crates in the whole `ts_py` graph, normal + build, with the kernel's):

```
ts_py v0.0.0
├── numpy v0.30.0                      (new)
│   ├── libc, num-integer, num-traits, rustc-hash   (already in the lock)
│   ├── ndarray v0.17.2                (new)
│   │   ├── matrixmultiply v0.3.11     (new)  [build: autocfg]
│   │   │   └── rawpointer v0.2.1      (new)
│   │   ├── num-complex v0.4.6         (new)
│   │   └── portable-atomic(-util), num-*, rawpointer
│   ├── num-complex v0.4.6
│   ├── pyo3 v0.30.1                   (new)
│   │   ├── libc, once_cell
│   │   ├── pyo3-ffi v0.30.1           (new)  [build: pyo3-build-config]
│   │   └── pyo3-macros v0.30.1        (new, proc-macro)
│   │       └── pyo3-macros-backend v0.30.1 (new)
│   │           ├── heck v0.5.0        (new)
│   │           └── proc-macro2, quote, syn
│   │   [build: pyo3-build-config v0.30.1 (new) -> target-lexicon v0.13.5 (new)]
│   [build: pyo3-build-config]
├── pyo3 v0.30.1
├── ts_kernel, ts_toy (workspace)
```

| Crate | Version | Published | License | `build.rs` | `unsafe` (approx. sites) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pyo3` | 0.30.1 | 2026-10-14 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | yes: reads the interpreter config from pyo3-build-config, emits cfgs | yes (Python C API, FFI) |
| `pyo3-ffi` | 0.30.1 | 2026-10-14 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | yes: link arguments for libpython | yes (FFI declarations) |
| `pyo3-macros` | 0.30.1 | 2026-10-14 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | no | no (proc-macro) |
| `pyo3-macros-backend` | 0.30.1 | 2026-10-14 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | yes: sets one cfg | generates code with `unsafe` blocks, none trips `deny(unsafe_code)` in ts_py |
| `pyo3-build-config` | 0.30.1 | 2026-10-14 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | no (library used by build scripts; **runs the Python interpreter**) | ~2 |
| `numpy` | 0.30.0 | 2026-10-15 | BSD-2-Clause | yes: `use_pyo3_cfgs()` only | yes (numpy C API) |
| `ndarray` | 0.17.2 | 2026-01-10 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | no

author: lunaparker
body:
The claude.ai connector for the deployed gateway listed no tools. Tracing what the proxy sends to a real waveapps-mcp server turned up two bugs in `gateway/src/waveapps_gateway/app.py`.

- **Duplicate Authorization header:** FastMCP forwards the caller's lowercase `authorization`, so the transport's `Authorization` went out as a second header. Node kept the first (the gateway's own token) and answered 401. The token now goes in as `auth=`, which replaces every Authorization header at send time.
- **Protocol era:** FastMCP 4 mirrors the caller's era to the backend. claude.ai speaks `2026-07-28` (`server/discover`, no session), and the server only the `initialize` handshake, so it answered "no valid session id". `create_proxy(..., mode="legacy")` pins the backend.
- **Tests:** the header test now checks every Authorization header the upstream receives (FastMCP's `get_http_headers()` keeps the last duplicate, which hid the bug), and a new test checks the upstream sees a handshake-era version. 24 pytest tests pass, Pyright clean.
- **Verified live:** with both fixes hot-patched on the desktop deployment, the claude.ai connector lists all 58 tools.
- **CLAUDE.md:** corrected the header note and documented the protocol pin.
